charles-littlejohn-prosecution.summary: John Kiriakou''s explanation of how a nine-year federal offence becomes a forty-year sentence: the sentencing table''s forty offence levels and seven criminal-history columns, and the enhancements stacked on top of a base level — for terrorism, for hacking, and, in the case he considers most perverse, for having pleaded not guilty and lost.

charles-samuels.title: Administrative remedy process
charles-samuels.summary: The Bureau of Prisons' internal grievance system, which Kiriakou describes as a fig leaf designed to run out the clock on prisoners' complaints rather than resolve them.

charles-samuels.title: Letter from Loretto
charles-samuels.summary: Prison newsletter written by John Kiriakou from FCI Loretto, modeled on Martin Luther King's "Letter from Birmingham Jail," which exposed two crimes committed against him by guards and went viral after being relayed to the Huffington Post, drawing national press to the prison.

charles-samuels.title: Bureau of Prisons
charles-samuels.summary: The federal agency that ran John Kiriakou's incarceration — and one of his most persistent post-prison targets. The BOP overrode his judge's camp recommendation by deeming him "a threat to the public safety," threatened him with "diesel therapy" until 1,600 logged phone calls and letters from a dozen House members and two senators backed it off, and, per Kiriakou, functions as "an employment agency for unemployable semi-literate rural white men" and "a dumping ground for failed medical professionals" — an agency for which a prisoner's death is cheaper than his treatment.

charles-samuels.title: Diesel Therapy
charles-samuels.summary: Per John Kiriakou, a punitive practice within the U.S. Federal Bureau of Prisons in which an inmate is placed into indefinite transit — moved continuously from facility to facility — for up to six months, with no access to phone, email, or pen and paper, and listed on the BOP website only as 'in transit' with no destination. Kiriakou described it as the one threat at FCI Loretto that actually frightened him.

charles-samuels.title: Jim Moran
charles-samuels.summary: Twelve-term Democratic congressman from Northern Virginia and John Kiriakou's own representative, who took the floor of the House to call for his release and a presidential pardon, and wrote twice to the director of the Bureau of Prisons asking that his constituent receive halfway-house time. In Kiriakou's account he was one of only a handful of elected officials willing to help at all.

charles-samuels.title: This desk kills fascism
charles-samuels.summary: The sign Kiriakou taped to the cell desk on which he wrote the letters from Loretto, borrowed from Woody Guthrie's guitar, torn down by a guard within hours and kept by Kiriakou ever since.

charlie-kirk-shooting.title: Jeffrey Epstein
charlie-kirk-shooting.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

charlie-kirk-shooting.title: JFK assassination
charlie-kirk-shooting.summary: November 22, 1963 killing of President John F. Kennedy in Dallas, Texas. John Kiriakou's position, drawn from a Pakistan-station encounter with Bay of Pigs commander Jean Gately, an RFK Jr. account of CIA Director John McCone's same-day exchange with Bobby Kennedy Sr., and a White House contact's confirmation that the remaining classified Kennedy documents all contain the word "Israel," is that elements of the CIA were probably involved and that Israeli intelligence was involved as well.

charlie-kirk-shooting.title: Joe Kent
charlie-kirk-shooting.summary: Kiriakou on the former counterterrorism director he gave an award to, publicly opposed for a nomination, and has never actually spoken to.

charlie-kirk-shooting.title: Washington political culture
charlie-kirk-shooting.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how Washington changed across the forty-four years he has lived in it — from a city where members of opposing parties shared houses, churches and Friday-night poker games to one he calls hideous, angry and backstabbing, in which the polarisation is itself the reason nothing gets done and political violence keeps being waved past.

charlie-kirk-shooting.title: Kiriakou and third parties
charlie-kirk-shooting.summary: John Kiriakou's advocacy for viable third parties, and his 2016 experience touring the West with Libertarian candidate Gary Johnson — including the disorganization that convinced him the party would never break through, epitomized by a colleague who ignored an airport page thinking it was 'NSA tracking my movements.'

charlie-kirk-shooting.title: Turning Point USA
charlie-kirk-shooting.summary: The conservative youth organization founded by Charlie Kirk out of the Tea Party and anti-tax movement to work university campuses for Trump's MAGA message. John Kiriakou treats it as the vehicle that brought first-time young voters into MAGA as a movement, credits its campus events as genuine dialogue despite disagreeing with Kirk on most issues, and judges that it cannot survive its founder's death intact.

charlie-kirk.title: Turning Point USA
charlie-kirk.summary: The conservative youth organization founded by Charlie Kirk out of the Tea Party and anti-tax movement to work university campuses for Trump's MAGA message. John Kiriakou treats it as the vehicle that brought first-time young voters into MAGA as a movement, credits its campus events as genuine dialogue despite disagreeing with Kirk on most issues, and judges that it cannot survive its founder's death intact.

charlie-kirk.title: Charlie Kirk shooting
charlie-kirk.summary: Kiriakou questions the official account: a court filing says the ATF could not match the autopsy bullet to the rifle tied to the suspect.

charlie-kirk.title: Senate Foreign Relations Committee
charlie-kirk.summary: Kiriakou was senior investigator under John Kerry — and still held the post when his own federal prosecution came to a head in January 2012.

charlie-kirk.title: ''An unusually violent society''
charlie-kirk.summary: The judgment the Amir of Bahrain delivered to John Kiriakou in the mid-1990s, shortly after the Oklahoma City bombing — that Americans are accepting of violence 'that would be unacceptable in any other civilized country,' even by Arab standards. Kiriakou says he had no answer, because it was true, and he has since used it as the frame for political shootings in the United States.

charlie-kirk.title: MOSSAD
charlie-kirk.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

charlie-kirk.title: Middle East Forum
charlie-kirk.summary: The publication — 'clearly an Israeli publication,' in John Kiriakou's words, and one he had never heard of before a Google alert surfaced it — that ran a piece by the political adviser to the Israeli foreign minister calling Kiriakou antisemitic and describing his writing as evidence of 'the rot' in the American intellectual left. Kiriakou took the phrase as a compliment and says the episode shows how closely Israel monitors even small independent outlets.

chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.title: Saudi Arabia as an open-air prison
chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.summary: John Kiriakou's verdict on the country he served in — 'the biggest open air prison in the world' — together with his account of what the ambassador's life there is like inside the residence and outside it, the two ambassadors he served under, and the annual migration of the entire Saudi government to Jeddah to escape the heat.

chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.title: Abraham Accords
chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.title: King Abdullah II of Jordan
chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.summary: The Jordanian monarch whom John Kiriakou rates as knowing more about the Middle East than anyone else who leads or studies it, and as almost never wrong across twenty-five years of foreign-policy predictions. Kiriakou recounts the deathbed succession that made him king against his own expectations, and his refusal after October 7 to accept Palestinian refugees on the grounds that doing so would deliver Israel the ethnic cleansing it wanted.

chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.title: The War Department renaming
chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.summary: John Kiriakou's support for restoring the name Department of War — because Truman changed it in 1947 to avoid the United States looking like an aggressor, and the record since does not support the euphemism — together with his point that a president cannot rename a federal department by executive order.

chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.title: The Dublin compensation
chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.summary: The night John Kiriakou spent in Dublin at an airline's expense after a mechanical fault in Madrid cost him his connection — a four-star hotel, an expedited check-in, a shuttle bus and half his fare refunded into his checking account six weeks later — offered as the standard American passengers do not get.

chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.title: The North Korea SEAL Team Six operation
chas-freeman-gaza-plan-1991.summary: The 2018 mission in which American special forces attempted to plant an eavesdropping device on North Korean soil, killed a boatload of fishermen and withdrew without planting it — which John Kiriakou uses to call Donald Trump a liar, because such an operation requires the president's signature on a finding, and to note that Congress was never told.

chelsea-manning.title: Jack Teixeira
chelsea-manning.summary: Massachusetts Air National Guard reservist arrested in April 2023 for leaking classified Pentagon documents to a small Discord server. John Kiriakou, discussing the case the day after Teixeira's arrest, initially suspected a covert action program rather than a genuine leak, ultimately concluded Teixeira was not a whistleblower, and predicted — correctly — that he would be charged under the Espionage Act and take a plea bargain.

chelsea-manning.title: Kiriakou Introduction to WikiLeaks
chelsea-manning.summary: Kiriakou first heard of WikiLeaks as a warning inside the secret spaces it existed to expose: ''Don''t touch that. Don''t go near that.''

chelsea-manning.title: Collateral Murder Video
chelsea-manning.summary: The 2010 WikiLeaks release of gun-camera footage from a 2007 U.S. Apache helicopter attack in Baghdad; part of the trove of Iraq and Afghan war logs, Guantanamo files, and State Department cables leaked by Chelsea Manning, which John Kiriakou credits with corroborating major abuses and helping to touch off the Arab Spring.

chelsea-manning.title: "It''s either him or it''s Manning"
chelsea-manning.summary: John Kiriakou's account of why Barack Obama commuted Chelsea Manning's sentence — that Joe Biden, lobbied by a wealthy Greek-American businessman, argued Kiriakou's clemency case to the president directly, and that Obama cut the discussion off ten minutes in by saying he would do one or the other but not both. Kiriakou's conclusion is that the commutation was an arithmetic judgement about a 35-year sentence rather than an act of conscience.

chelsea-manning.title: The OPCW Douma investigation
chelsea-manning.summary: The chemical weapons inquiry into the alleged 2018 attack in Douma, Syria, which John Kiriakou describes as falsified rather than merely disputed: fifteen investigators objected that their analysis had been taken out of context or fabricated outright, and the false version was then used to reach a political conclusion. He credits WikiLeaks with being the only reason any of it is public — and notes that major American shows carried on repeating the original story anyway.

chelsea-manning.title: Qasem Soleimani
chelsea-manning.summary: The Iranian general killed by an American drone strike in Baghdad in January 2020. John Kiriakou, speaking the following morning, called him arguably the second most important person in Iran and a potential successor to the supreme leader, relayed the Iranian comparison that killing him was worse than killing Petraeus or Mattis — 'this is like killing Pence' — and dismissed talk of de-escalation as a pipe dream.

cheney-airstrip-question.title: Executive assistant to the Deputy Director for Operations
cheney-airstrip-question.summary: The job John Kiriakou held during the Iraq war, and the shape of its day: a 2:45 a.m. alarm, ten thousand overnight cables triaged down to five or ten by dawn, the deputy directors briefed at seven and the director at half past — and only then the actual work of coordinating with the State Department, the Pentagon and the vice president''s office.

cheney-airstrip-question.title: President's Daily Brief
cheney-airstrip-question.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the President's Daily Brief (PDB) is a roughly 16-page, top-secret intelligence document produced daily for the president, written in a uniform CIA house style, briefed each morning, and — in his account — used partly to gauge and flatter incoming presidents.

cheney-airstrip-question.title: AIPAC
cheney-airstrip-question.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

cheney-airstrip-question.title: Bill Clinton
cheney-airstrip-question.summary: 42nd U.S. president whom John Kiriakou describes as wholly disinterested in intelligence — briefed by the CIA only twice in eight years, with Vice President Al Gore taking the daily briefing instead and relaying anything important.

cheney-airstrip-question.title: The CIA as a policy support agency
cheney-airstrip-question.summary: John Kiriakou''s standing correction to the idea that the CIA has a foreign policy of its own: it is not a policy agency but a policy support agency, it serves at the pleasure of the president, and its officers have no civil service protections at all. Career staff can slow-roll an order they dislike until an administration ends — but in a hot war, he says, they do as they are told.

cheney-airstrip-question.title: Greater Israel
cheney-airstrip-question.summary: The territorial project John Kiriakou believes the Israeli government genuinely holds: the expulsion of every Palestinian, beginning in Gaza and continuing into the West Bank, pursued on a hundred- or two-hundred-year horizon in the confidence that the United States will never push back.

chief-of-station.title: George W. Bush
chief-of-station.summary: 43rd President of the United States. In John Kiriakou's telling, Bush signed the August 1, 2002 executive order that authorized the CIA torture program, spent years telling the public "we don't torture," and — days after Kiriakou's 2007 ABC interview — blamed torture on "a rogue CIA officer" while walking from the White House South Portico to Marine One, a moment Kiriakou instantly read as the White House preparing to pin the program on him. Bush also ordered the FBI removed from Abu Zubaydah's black site, flew the bin Laden family out of the country after 9/11, and loosened the assassination ban of Executive Order 12333.

chief-of-station.title: Senior Intelligence Service
chief-of-station.summary: The CIA's executive rank above the General Schedule, entry to which requires a tour outside an officer's own directorate and a tour in the policy community — a box-checking requirement John Kiriakou identifies as the reason an untrained analyst was sent to run a base in Afghanistan. Its officers are career staff rather than political appointees, some with thirty or forty years in place, which is why Kiriakou describes the service as capable of simply waiting a president out — or slow-rolling him. Its officers in the Counterterrorism Center were also the authors of the torture techniques.

chief-of-station.title: CIA language training
chief-of-station.summary: The agency''s language pipeline as John Kiriakou experienced and describes it: a full year of Arabic at nine hours a day, an optional second year at the State Department''s school, and the calculation that made his own career — that it is cheaper to teach a linguist operations than to teach an operations officer Greek and Arabic.

chief-of-station.title: The Directorate of Operations
chief-of-station.summary: The CIA's clandestine service, which John Kiriakou joined from analysis because he spoke both Greek and Arabic — a culture he describes as wildly different from the analytic side, short on institutional memory and organised around the race to become a station chief.

chief-of-station.title: Cover stop
chief-of-station.summary: A routine, innocuous errand run in the middle of a surveillance detection route so that an intelligence officer has a plausible reason to be where he is — the 7-Eleven, the dry cleaner, the wine shop — and, in John Kiriakou's account, also a petty-expense line item that has ended CIA careers.

child-trafficking-misquotation.title: Military Ethics
child-trafficking-misquotation.summary: The hypothetical Kiriakou puts to college audiences — and the line no CIA training class ever teaches an officer where to draw.

child-trafficking-misquotation.title: Publications Review Board
child-trafficking-misquotation.summary: The CIA office that must clear anything a former officer publishes. John Kiriakou says everything he writes goes to it — books, articles, "even a letter to the editor of Home and Garden magazine" — and describes how the turnaround tracked his standing at the agency: his first book took 22 months to clear while the leadership hated him; his most recent six cleared in days.

child-trafficking-misquotation.title: Agent inducements
child-trafficking-misquotation.summary: The non-cash things the CIA can offer a recruited agent — a child's university place anywhere in America, treatment at a top hospital for a sick spouse, or a carefully staged personal gift — and the standing arrangements with universities and large corporations that make them possible.

child-trafficking-misquotation.title: Agent payment mechanics
child-trafficking-misquotation.summary: How the CIA physically pays a recruited agent — cash every month, a receipt signed with any alias the agent chooses, and a polygraph regime built around the assumption that the officer handling the money is the person most likely to steal it.

child-trafficking-misquotation.title: Rick Praau
child-trafficking-misquotation.summary: Career CIA officer, chief of operations at the Counterterrorism Center and previously of the Special Activities Division, whose retirement memoir John Kiriakou reviewed critically in Covert Action Magazine. Kiriakou's objection is not to what the book contains but to what it omits — published reports that before joining the agency its author was investigated by Miami-Dade police over seven contract killings for the Medellín cartel. The surname is given here as the source transcript's auto-captions render it and may be mis-transcribed.

child-trafficking-misquotation.title: The CIA defense
child-trafficking-misquotation.summary: John Kiriakou's account of what happens when a CIA asset is arrested — either the station chief privately asks the host country's intelligence service for the man's release, which he says works ninety-nine times out of a hundred, or the agency declines, leaving the defendant to argue at trial that he was acting on the CIA's behalf while the agency says nothing at all.

chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.title: Thomas Drake
chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.summary: NSA whistleblower; per John Kiriakou, the source for the statement that on the morning of September 11, 2001, NSA Director Mike Hayden told agency personnel NSA had been 'waiting for a 9/11' to implement the mass-electronic-surveillance program that NSA's founding charter forbids.

chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.title: Espionage Act
chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.title: Anthony Fauci
chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.summary: American physician and public-health official whose pardon John Kiriakou condemned as "unacceptable" in a May 2026 Fox News appearance. Kiriakou''s objection is partly personal: his cousin George was, he says, the second person in Ohio to die of COVID, in very early 2020. Kiriakou confined himself to the pardon and to his own family''s loss, and made no claim of his own about the origin of the virus.

chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.title: The 2007 death threats
chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.summary: The immediate personal consequence of John Kiriakou''s December 2007 television appearance confirming CIA waterboarding: hundreds of pieces of hate mail, and three threats against his life that the FBI classified as credible, one of which named his children and gave his home address. On the Bureau''s advice he took his family out of the country for a week; the FBI then interviewed the senders, judged them local cranks, and told him to come home.

chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.title: The counterintelligence exemption
chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.summary: The rule John Kiriakou says makes counterintelligence the darkest corner of American intelligence: such cases are the only category that need not be briefed to the congressional oversight committees, because a mole hunt might implicate a member of those very committees. He argues Mike Pompeo''s description of WikiLeaks as a hostile non-state intelligence service was chosen precisely to move the Assange operation into that exempt category, where a killing in a London street would never have had to be explained.

chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.title: Authorized leaks
chilling-effect-of-whistleblower-prosecu.summary: The distinction John Kiriakou draws between the classified information Washington releases on purpose and the classified information it prosecutes people for releasing. The mechanism is the same and the legal status is identical; what differs is whether the leak flatters the leaker. His worked example is an agency leak claiming the CIA predicted the October 2023 attack on Israel three days out — a story the CIA can then piously report to the FBI, knowing the source will never be found.

china-as-mediator.title: China as economic threat
china-as-mediator.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

china-as-mediator.title: The refusal to talk to adversaries
china-as-mediator.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that the single worst American foreign-policy habit of the past two decades is the refusal to engage diplomatically with governments Washington disagrees with — a practice he dates to the George W. Bush administration, which he says CIA officers complained about at the time, and which has since become bipartisan.

china-as-mediator.title: Ukraine as a proxy war
china-as-mediator.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment, given two months into the 2022 Russian invasion, that the United States was funding a proxy war it knew Ukraine could not win in order to bog Russia down — and that the outcome was already fixed, so peace talks should happen at once.

china-as-mediator.title: The permanent multipolar world
china-as-mediator.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment that the unipolar period following the collapse of the Soviet Union has ended permanently, and that the arrangement was not inevitable — he attributes it to American strategic choices, principally leaving the Iran nuclear agreement and choosing confrontation with China and Russia over the cooperation that was available.

china-as-mediator.title: The pivot to Asia
china-as-mediator.summary: John Kiriakou's criticism of the American realignment toward the Pacific begun under Barack Obama, which he describes as unnecessarily provocative — and his argument that the historical fear in the region runs the other way, since it was China that was invaded by Japan, and Chinese children are taught the occupation as part of their national inheritance.

china-as-mediator.title: The Putin call and the China exception
china-as-mediator.summary: In February 2025 John Kiriakou said he was optimistic that relations with Russia would improve, on the strength of a telephone call being arranged between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin — but drew a sharp exception for China, arguing that nobody in the American government was sincere about improving those relations and that Washington, not Beijing, was instigating talk of war.

china-djibouti-base.title: Djibouti
china-djibouti-base.summary: The small Horn of Africa state a few miles across the water from Yemen that hosts Camp Lemonnier — the American drone base for the Yemen and Somalia wars, inherited from the departing French, and shared with China's only overseas military base behind a fence down the middle, in what John Kiriakou calls the worst kept secret in the world.

china-djibouti-base.title: China as economic threat
china-djibouti-base.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

china-djibouti-base.title: CIA spy tech from Amazon
china-djibouti-base.summary: John Kiriakou's account that roughly 95% of the CIA's spy technology is purchased commercially from Amazon.com rather than custom-built, illustrated by a $10 leather briefcase he had rigged into a listening device in a Pakistani market.

china-djibouti-base.title: The Kite Runner rescue mission
china-djibouti-base.summary: 2007 covert operation in which John Kiriakou, newly departed from the CIA and working as a corporate-intelligence consultant, was hired by Paramount Studios to secretly evacuate the Afghan child actors of the film "The Kite Runner" and their extended families after real death threats over the film's content.

china-djibouti-base.title: Kiriakou's mother's 2008 trip to Israel
china-djibouti-base.summary: John Kiriakou recounts his mother's 2008 church-group trip to Israel and the West Bank, during which she was struck by the contrast between first-world Tel Aviv and a walled, mined Palestinian town, and witnessed an IDF soldier tear apart a Palestinian bus driver's novel as suspected "PLO propaganda." Kiriakou made two trips of his own to Israel in 2022, including one to cover the elections, during which he personally witnessed a fatal stabbing at Jerusalem's Iron Gate.

china-djibouti-base.title: UK secrecy laws
china-djibouti-base.summary: John Kiriakou's view that Britain is even harsher on whistleblowers and dissent than the United States, using the Official Secrets Act and Terrorism Act to stop people at airports and threaten arrest merely for supporting Palestinian rights.

china-economic-threat.title: CIA spy tech from Amazon
china-economic-threat.summary: John Kiriakou's account that roughly 95% of the CIA's spy technology is purchased commercially from Amazon.com rather than custom-built, illustrated by a $10 leather briefcase he had rigged into a listening device in a Pakistani market.

china-economic-threat.title: PricewaterhouseCoopers
china-economic-threat.summary: The Big Four accounting firm that keeps intersecting John Kiriakou's story — as a target of the corporate human-source intelligence he collected after leaving the CIA, as the audience of 140 partners he told his Pakistan recruitment story to ("what I did and what you do really isn't that different"), as the auditor that spent three years trying to find the Pentagon's money before giving up, and as the Greek government's book-cooking auditor in the debt crisis, never prosecuted.

china-economic-threat.title: Souda Bay Vulnerability and Nasser on American Decisions
china-economic-threat.summary: Two observations John Kiriakou has made on U.S. Mediterranean strategy and decision-making — a U.S. military contact's warning that Souda Bay in Crete, the nearest major port able to host a U.S. aircraft carrier like the USS Gerald Ford, is a possible vulnerability; and Kiriakou's favorite quote from Gamal Abdel Nasser, that Americans never make clear-cut stupid decisions, only complicated ones.

china-economic-threat.title: The cyber victimhood complaint
china-economic-threat.summary: John Kiriakou's dismissal of American public complaint about foreign cyber attacks — that everything the United States accuses Iran, North Korea and China of doing, it does itself every day, because disrupting foreign networks is the NSA's job as much as intercepting communications is. Better security is needed, he says, but so is it by everyone else, against the United States.

china-economic-threat.title: Zelensky action figures
china-economic-threat.summary: The detail John Kiriakou reached for in January 2023 to describe how far American war messaging had gone: you can buy Zelensky action figures in stores now. He offered it as the marker of a ridiculousness he thought few Americans recognised, alongside his argument that the war''s real object was to bog Russia down before confronting China.

china-economic-threat.title: The pivot to Asia
china-economic-threat.summary: John Kiriakou's criticism of the American realignment toward the Pacific begun under Barack Obama, which he describes as unnecessarily provocative — and his argument that the historical fear in the region runs the other way, since it was China that was invaded by Japan, and Chinese children are taught the occupation as part of their national inheritance.

china-illegal-fishing.title: Russia-Ukraine war origins
china-illegal-fishing.summary: John Kiriakou's account that the war began in 2014, not 2022 — rooted in broken U.S. promises that NATO would not expand to Russia's borders, the 2014 removal of a pro-Russian Ukrainian leader, and the seizure of Crimea; he says Russia is now winning and has no reason to negotiate.

china-illegal-fishing.title: Bahrain fishing officer demarche
china-illegal-fishing.summary: Kiriakou's account of serving, while stationed in Bahrain, as the embassy's econ officer and by extension its fishing, banking, aviation, and environment officer — including delivering a formal U.S. demarche to Bahrain's deputy foreign minister over a U.S.-Canada dispute about whether clams legally count as fish.

china-illegal-fishing.title: Below World's End
china-illegal-fishing.summary: Film in which John Kiriakou made his acting debut, filmed entirely in Mexico during October 2025; Kiriakou's performance earned him a Screen Actors Guild membership card, and Sean Penn told him after a private screening that he had unknowingly been acting throughout his entire CIA career.

china-illegal-fishing.title: Big Assawoman Bay NASA launch
china-illegal-fishing.summary: John Kiriakou's account of being taken, as a junior CIA analyst, to watch a NASA rocket launch near the village of Big Assawoman on Virginia's Eastern Shore, where he was startled to find foreign space-agency officials present unsupervised.

china-illegal-fishing.title: Contra rebels
china-illegal-fishing.summary: The right-wing Nicaraguan insurgency armed by the Reagan administration against the Sandinista government. In John Kiriakou's account they were conservatives, right-wingers, in some cases fascists, and disgruntled military officers; they were split into a northern group the United States armed and a southern group that financed itself by selling cocaine — a distinction that became the pivot of the Gary Webb affair, and that Kiriakou uses to answer the CIA's standing denial that it had anything to do with the drug trade.

china-illegal-fishing.title: Iran Nuclear Assessment
china-illegal-fishing.summary: Per John Kiriakou's assessment, the US–Israeli military campaign against Iran was a war of choice driven by Israeli political pressure rather than genuine intelligence indicating an Iranian nuclear weapons threat. The CIA produced two National Intelligence Estimates concluding Iran had no nuclear weapons program; Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei issued a fatwa in the 1980s forbidding such a program. The U.S. went to war anyway, in Kiriakou's view, after President Trump replaced the Joint Chiefs of Staff with officers willing to accept Israeli intelligence and proceed.

chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.title: Canada as a bargaining chip
chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.summary: John Kiriakou's reading of Mark Carney's Davos speech as the moment Canada stopped pretending the United States could be trusted as a long-term partner — and his account of what wore the relationship out, including Washington's insistence that Ottawa arrest Huawei's chief financial officer on a computer-hacking charge and hold her for three years to trade.

chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.title: China as mediator
chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the plausible mediator of Middle Eastern and Ukrainian conflicts, grounded in his claim that — Tibet and its border wars aside — China has no history of invading other countries, and his observation of how quickly Beijing accepted an offhand suggestion that it might mediate between Israel and Iran.

chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.title: China as economic threat
chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.title: Ilhan Omar
chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.summary: U.S. Representative whom John Kiriakou credits with sponsoring a rewrite of the Espionage Act in two consecutive Congresses — legislation he says is dead on arrival with a Republican House because of who she is. Kiriakou has also sat at her table — in January 2026 he was one of about twenty guests at a dinner where Omar described the federal operation in Minneapolis and the budget manoeuvre that funded every part of the government except Homeland Security.

chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.title: Macron and the airplane steps
chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.summary: Asked what he thought was behind the French president's bruised appearance at Davos, John Kiriakou gave the blunt answer — "honestly, I think she hits him" — and dated his own change of mind to the footage at the top of the airplane steps.

chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.title: The killing of Alex Pretty
chinas-generals-without-combat-experienc.summary: John Kiriakou''s verdict on the shooting of a man by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January 2026: a Kent State moment for the administration, a cover-up in progress, and — because there is no statute of limitations on murder — a case that will outlive the presidency and put people in prison.

chinese-overseas-police-stations.title: Fusha and the Gulf dialect
chinese-overseas-police-stations.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of his own Arabic training — a first year in fusha, high standard Arabic, followed by a second year in khaleeji, the Gulf dialect — and what he reports of both: that Yemen is the only place pure fusha is spoken, that Saudis asked him why he spoke Arabic like Shakespeare, that the Gulf dialect is marked by a hard J other Arabs dislike, and that the Maghreb defeats him entirely.

chinese-overseas-police-stations.title: Iran under sanctions: daily life
chinese-overseas-police-stations.summary: John Kiriakou's account of being talked out of his own assumptions about Iran by a close friend who travels there once or twice a year and eventually started filming ordinary life — leading him to conclude that a country with no American embassy, diplomatic presence or business presence since 1979 nonetheless lacks for nothing.

chinese-overseas-police-stations.title: The Afghan National Police poisoning
chinese-overseas-police-stations.summary: An incident John Kiriakou recalls from a 2012 New York Times report and treats as the clearest single illustration of why the American project in Afghanistan failed: at a DynCorp-run training facility that had deliberately mixed recruits from every tribe and region, one recruit poisoned the evening stew and then let four Taliban fighters into the dormitory to stab the survivors in their beds.

chinese-overseas-police-stations.title: The Afghan police tribal rotation
chinese-overseas-police-stations.summary: An American anti-corruption scheme in Afghanistan that John Kiriakou describes as achieving the reverse of its purpose: someone in the Pentagon decided that regional chiefs of police should come from other tribes in other parts of the country, so a man from Herat would head the police in Kandahar — which only deepened hatred between tribes and did nothing at all about corruption.

chinese-overseas-police-stations.title: Kandahar
chinese-overseas-police-stations.summary: The southern Afghan city and province that recurs across John Kiriakou's Afghanistan material — site of one of the two al-Qaeda training camps Abu Zubaydah founded, whose commanders were captured in the same March 2002 raids; the town Bill Clinton said he would have had to destroy, killing 300 innocents, to kill bin Laden in the 1990s; and a stop on Kiriakou's Senate-era heroin-poppy investigation, when the military helicoptered him down before refusing to let him walk the poppy fields.

chinese-overseas-police-stations.title: Kiriakou's speaking tours
chinese-overseas-police-stations.summary: The lecture circuit John Kiriakou described in December 2025: a tour of England, Wales, Scotland, Ireland and Northern Ireland in January and February of that year, and a nationwide American tour due to begin the following February — one strand of a workload he said he was not sure he could keep up.

chinese-spy-balloon-incident.title: Thomas Drake
chinese-spy-balloon-incident.summary: NSA whistleblower; per John Kiriakou, the source for the statement that on the morning of September 11, 2001, NSA Director Mike Hayden told agency personnel NSA had been 'waiting for a 9/11' to implement the mass-electronic-surveillance program that NSA's founding charter forbids.

chinese-spy-balloon-incident.title: Agnes von Kurowsky grave story
chinese-spy-balloon-incident.summary: John Kiriakou's account of discovering the Washington, D.C. grave of Agnes von Kurowsky, the World War I Red Cross nurse whose four-month wartime romance with a young ambulance driver, Ernest Hemingway, made her the model for the lead female character in six of his books, including A Farewell to Arms.

chinese-spy-balloon-incident.title: Kiriakou's personal anecdotes
chinese-spy-balloon-incident.summary: Three personal stories John Kiriakou has told in interviews — tracking down and meeting Andy Warhol as a college senior, a Congolese vice president's remark that Americans promise democracy while the Chinese provide food, and Kiriakou's own Zelle account being suspended over Cuba-sanctions compliance after a paid article about his Cuba trip.

chinese-spy-balloon-incident.title: Spies of Arlington National Cemetery
chinese-spy-balloon-incident.summary: On the Walk With History podcast, John Kiriakou — author of Remains of the Day: A Definitive Guide to Washington D.C.''s Historic Cemeteries — toured Arlington National Cemetery and told personal and historical stories about the intelligence figures buried there, including OSS founder William Donovan, deputy CIA director Vernon Walters, codebreakers William and Elizabeth Friedman, slain station chiefs Richard Welch and William Buckley, U-2 pilot Francis Gary Powers, and Mike Spann, the first CIA officer killed after 9/11.

chinese-spy-balloon-incident.title: Bashar al-Assad
chinese-spy-balloon-incident.summary: President of Syria; John Kiriakou recounts warning Senator John Kerry to stop publicly calling Assad 'my dear friend' after a speech enraged Washington's Lebanese community, with Kerry citing motorcycle rides they had taken together to the Golan Heights.

chinese-spy-balloon-incident.title: CIA adultery culture
chinese-spy-balloon-incident.summary: John Kiriakou's recurring characterization of the CIA officer corps as riddled with adultery and casual sex — which he frames not as gossip but as a systemic counterintelligence vulnerability that makes officers easy to recruit.

chomo.title: FCI Loretto
chomo.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

chomo.title: Federal prison security levels
chomo.summary: The ladder of federal custody as John Kiriakou describes it — penitentiary, medium, low and minimum-security camp — the transfer rules that let long-sentence prisoners descend it, and why that placed dangerous men inside the low-security prison where he served his sentence.

chomo.title: Truck
chomo.summary: The convicted serial killer at FCI Loretto who sought John Kiriakou's approval, claimed to have run guns to Angolan rebels in a shrimp boat, and beat a prisoner unconscious after Kiriakou told him the man had called him a pedophile.

chomo.title: The Nation of Islam at Loretto
chomo.summary: The largest Muslim faction at FCI Loretto — African American converts to the Nation of Islam — two of whom walked into John Kiriakou's cell in his first days holding their own newspaper, in which Louis Farrakhan had called him a hero of the Muslim people for opposing torture. They told him he would have no trouble with them; one declined the handshake he offered, on the ground that he does not shake hands with the white devil. The Aryans, meanwhile, had decided he was a CIA assassin who killed Muslims. Kiriakou kept his mouth shut and let both beliefs stand.

chomo.title: The rat and pedophile table
chomo.summary: The cafeteria table at FCI Loretto reserved for cooperating witnesses and sex offenders — a placement that also carried a ban from the television room, and which John Kiriakou describes as an outcome cooperators knew to expect before they agreed to testify.

chomo.title: The Romanian twins
chomo.summary: The adopted children John Kiriakou says his FCI Loretto roommate Robert the Australian abandoned at the gate of the Romanian embassy in Washington — one of the stories Kiriakou judged to be true, in a stream of claims he otherwise treated as invention.

christian-zionism.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
christian-zionism.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

christian-zionism.title: Church of Saint Porphyrios
christian-zionism.summary: The Greek Orthodox church in Gaza that John Kiriakou describes as the oldest continuously operating church in the world; per Kiriakou, Israel bombed it while 24 women and children were sheltering inside.

christian-zionism.title: Tucker Carlson
christian-zionism.summary: American broadcaster and former Fox News host; a personal friend of John Kiriakou's for years, appearing on Kiriakou's radio and podcast work and hosting him roughly a dozen times on his own Fox show. Kiriakou calls him possibly the most brilliant and best-informed person he has ever encountered, and relays Glenn Greenwald's belief that Carlson could win the presidency — an idea Carlson privately dismisses.

christian-zionism.title: John Kiriakou
christian-zionism.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

christian-zionism.title: Antisemitism and anti-Zionism
christian-zionism.summary: The conflation of criticism of the Israeli state with hatred of Jews, which John Kiriakou describes as a worldwide confusion and, according to a young Israeli he spoke to, an explicit lesson of the Israeli school system; a subject Kiriakou says he personally struggles with.

christian-zionism.title: Liberty University
christian-zionism.summary: Evangelical university in Lynchburg, Virginia — the largest in the world — where John Kiriakou taught for several years as an adjunct professor of intelligence studies in the Jesse Helms School of Government. He says he warned the school he disagreed with it on 95% of the issues and was hired anyway, on the dean's reasoning that "torture's not Christian"; he enjoyed the post while clashing constantly with the institution over the treatment of Middle Eastern Christians.

christians-are-suckers.title: Astrology at the CIA
christians-are-suckers.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that astrology played a role in CIA work in the 1950s and early 1960s as part of MK-ULTRA, alongside time travel and teleportation — and his explanation for why: officials with unlimited budgets and no obligation to report to the public reasoned that there was probably nothing to it, but that if there were, it would make them a star.

christians-are-suckers.title: Carrying passports in Washington
christians-are-suckers.summary: John Kiriakou's report in September 2025 that people in Washington had begun carrying their passports for fear of being scooped up by immigration enforcement — alongside the case of an American symphony violinist held for three weeks, and his own belief that ethnic profiling violates the Fourth Amendment.

christians-are-suckers.title: E. Jean Carroll
christians-are-suckers.summary: The plaintiff whose persistence John Kiriakou singled out for deep respect — she kept suing after the political tide turned against her, and won an award he put at eighty-three or eighty-five million dollars on a day when Donald Trump won almost everything else in the federal courts.

christians-are-suckers.title: Special operations officer
christians-are-suckers.summary: The CIA staff category John Kiriakou describes as an assistant to the operations people — abbreviated SOO and pronounced "Sue" — most of whose members, he says, could not get through operational training, and whose duties included assembling surveillance teams for a case officer's dangerous meetings and filing his accounting paperwork at the end of a long night.

christians-are-suckers.title: CIA backdoor banking
christians-are-suckers.summary: John Kiriakou's answer to a question about the intelligence community opening Western capital markets to sanctioned groups — that the CIA's interests frequently diverge from the national interest, that its friends are often hostile to the State Department and the White House, and that it will arrange backdoor banking, investment and loans to keep those outlaws going.

christians-are-suckers.title: The Ramot Junction shooting
christians-are-suckers.summary: The September 2025 bus stop attack in an East Jerusalem settlement in which two Palestinians from the West Bank killed six Israelis, and John Kiriakou's divided answer — that opposition to attacks on civilians has to be unconditional, and that he does not know what he would do if strangers took his house.

christopher-hitchens.title: Waterboarding
christopher-hitchens.summary: Torture technique in which a prisoner is restrained on an inclined board with the head lower than the feet, a cloth placed over the face, and water poured continuously over it to simulate drowning. Per John Kiriakou, waterboarding was treated as a criminal act under U.S. and international law for decades before 2002 — including a post–World War II execution of Japanese soldiers who waterboarded American POWs, and a 1968 court-martial of a U.S. soldier photographed waterboarding a North Vietnamese prisoner — before the CIA reauthorized it after September 11. Abu Zubaydah was waterboarded 83 times; Khalid Sheikh Mohammed 187 times.

christopher-hitchens.title: Barack Obama
christopher-hitchens.summary: 44th U.S. president; in John Kiriakou's account, Obama publicly recounted refusing Benjamin Netanyahu's demand to bomb Iran and calling Israel's threat to use nuclear weapons a bluff — a bluff Kiriakou says Donald Trump later believed.

christopher-hitchens.title: Bill Clinton
christopher-hitchens.summary: 42nd U.S. president whom John Kiriakou describes as wholly disinterested in intelligence — briefed by the CIA only twice in eight years, with Vice President Al Gore taking the daily briefing instead and relaying anything important.

christopher-hitchens.title: British Bases in Cyprus
christopher-hitchens.summary: British sovereign bases in Cyprus host a large American contingent. Kiriakou, a quarter Cypriot, on the bases as evacuation hub, missile target, and suspected nuclear site — and on the 46-year US weapons embargo almost no American knows about.

christopher-hitchens.title: CIA political neutrality tradition
christopher-hitchens.summary: The informal midcentury norm at the Central Intelligence Agency, described by John Kiriakou from his own 1990-era experience, under which employees did not share their partisan affiliations at work, small displays such as a Bob Dole campaign bumper sticker in a cubicle triggered severe internal discipline, and career officers steered clear of political endorsement — a tradition Kiriakou argues collapsed by 2020, when 51 former intelligence officials signed the letter dismissing the Hunter Biden laptop story.

christopher-hitchens.title: Donald Trump
christopher-hitchens.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

christopher-steele-dossier.title: FISA court
christopher-steele-dossier.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the secret Foreign Intelligence Surveillance court — created under Carter, sitting atop the Justice Department, issuing warrants that are never public — which he says was abused against Carter Page as part of what he believes was John Brennan's plan to deny Trump the presidency.

christopher-steele-dossier.title: Russiagate
christopher-steele-dossier.summary: John Kiriakou''s rebuttal of the claim that Russia swung the 2016 U.S. election: the Mueller report found no interference, the DNC emails were leaked in person rather than remotely hacked, and Russia''s roughly $50,000 in Facebook ads — half spent after the election — was trivial against billions in campaign spending.

christopher-steele-dossier.title: Carlos the Jackal
christopher-steele-dossier.summary: Venezuelan-born militant (Ilich Ramírez Sánchez) active in the 1970s and 1980s; per John Kiriakou, 'the Osama bin Laden of the 70s and 80s.' Kiriakou spent his Athens posting trying to identify the middleman linking Carlos to the Greek terrorist group 17 November, then six months working the lead with MI5 in London; Carlos was finally run down by CIA contractor Billy Waugh in a Khartoum vegetable market and captured in 1994.

christopher-steele-dossier.title: Afghan heroin policy
christopher-steele-dossier.summary: The post-2001 U.S. policy in Afghanistan of protecting, and per John Kiriakou actively encouraging, the cultivation of heroin poppy. Under the Taliban in 2000 Afghanistan produced 0% of the world's heroin; by 2009 under American occupation it produced 93%. Per a DEA officer Kiriakou consulted with on the policy paper he was preparing for Senator Kerry, the strategic rationale was that nearly all of the heroin flowed to Iran and Russia, addiction in those countries was considered desirable as a long-run societal weakener, and the same logic now operates in reverse with Chinese fentanyl flowing into the United States.

christopher-steele-dossier.title: William J. Casey
christopher-steele-dossier.summary: Director of Central Intelligence under Reagan; creator of the CIA's domestic collection arm, architect of the purge that installed a businessman with no intelligence experience as deputy director for operations, and — per John Kiriakou — the man whose campaign to cut Congress out ended the only period of real intelligence oversight the United States has ever had.

christopher-steele-dossier.title: Church Committee
christopher-steele-dossier.summary: U.S. Senate investigative committee operating in 1975–1976 that examined domestic intelligence abuses by the CIA, FBI, and NSA; per John Kiriakou, the Church Committee — alongside the concurrent Pike Committee in the House — was the last genuine moment of legislative oversight over the intelligence community, born of a national consensus that government had gone dangerously off course. Its work led to the creation of the permanent Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, which Kiriakou says ceased to function as real oversight roughly seven years after its founding.

chuck-grassley.title: Whistleblower Protection Act
chuck-grassley.summary: United States statute protecting federal employees who disclose government wrongdoing from retaliation; per John Kiriakou, national security employees — including those at the CIA, Pentagon, FBI, NSA, DEA, White House, and Homeland Security — are explicitly exempt from its protections, leaving them with no legally safe avenue to report illegal activity within their agencies.

chuck-grassley.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
chuck-grassley.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

chuck-grassley.title: Gina Haspel
chuck-grassley.summary: Director of the Central Intelligence Agency under President Trump's first term; known to John Kiriakou and others at the CIA as "Bloody Gina"; per Kiriakou, flew out to the secret black site to sit in on one of the enhanced-interrogation torture sessions "just because she could," personally supervised the torture of USS Cole bombing suspect Rahim al-Nashiri, and later fed the CIA's torture tapes into an industrial document grinder after being explicitly told by White House Counsel not to destroy them.

chuck-grassley.title: The Sociopath Next Door
chuck-grassley.summary: The book John Kiriakou reaches for when explaining why the CIA's leadership looks the way it does — sociopaths climbing over the people around them, as in any Fortune 500 company — and the source of his claim that 85 percent of American prisoners have a diagnosable mental illness.

chuck-grassley.title: Presidential call memcons
chuck-grassley.summary: How a call between the president and a foreign leader is staffed and recorded, as John Kiriakou describes it. Four people are usually on the line and rarely five — not the twenty reported during the Ukraine affair — and the write-up, a memorandum of conversation or memcon, is held so tightly inside the National Security Council that a CIA analyst, he says, would never see one.

chuck-grassley.title: The Directorate of Intelligence
chuck-grassley.summary: The CIA's analytic cadre, where John Kiriakou spent the first seven years of his career working on Iraq before switching to operations — a culture he describes as convinced it holds the smartest people in the room, and whose function he says is duplicated across a dozen other agencies.

church-committee.title: Eric Swallwell
church-committee.summary: Kiriakou names Swalwell once — a passing aside contrasting today's partisan Congress with the Church and Pike Committees of 1975.

church-committee.title: Senior Executive Service
church-committee.summary: Highest tier of the U.S. federal civil service, above GS-1 through GS-15 pay grades; per John Kiriakou, members of the SES — and its agency-specific equivalents such as the CIA's Senior Intelligence Service — are the career officials who functionally operate the federal government across presidential administrations, serving thirty to forty years while presidents come and go every four or eight, and are protected from dismissal by the Civil Service Act.

church-committee.title: Steve Kappes
church-committee.summary: Former Deputy Director of the Central Intelligence Agency; encountered by John Kiriakou in the lobby of the Sanaa Marriott during Kiriakou's final Yemen trip as a Senate Foreign Relations Committee investigator.

church-committee.title: The inside-job refusal
church-committee.summary: Pressed on controlled-demolition theories about the World Trade Center, John Kiriakou refuses the premise while conceding the limits of his own expertise — he was inside the CIA''s Counterterrorism Center before the attacks, and says he has never seen any evidence that 9/11 was an inside job.

church-committee.title: Blackmail in agent recruitment
church-committee.summary: What John Kiriakou says CIA career trainees were taught about blackmail: that the agency does not use it, not on moral grounds but because a long-term agent relationship requires mutual trust and coercion cannot produce it. He allows two exceptions — the pre-Church Committee past, and cases where the objective is simply to stop a target doing something, which can also be handed to a friendlier service.

church-committee.title: CIA Gmail account felony case
church-committee.summary: Per John Kiriakou, a CIA colleague working the counterterrorism fusion center night shift was ordered by cable to check a terrorist suspect's Gmail account and password, did so, and was later charged with a felony for illegally accessing a computer — despite having acted only on explicit written instructions from headquarters.

cia-adultery-culture.title: Brett McGurk
cia-adultery-culture.summary: Senior U.S. diplomat; John Kiriakou cites reporting that McGurk was caught in a sexual encounter atop a U.S. embassy while overseeing the campaign against ISIS, offering it as an example of the adultery culture he considers a security risk.

cia-adultery-culture.title: Sofia, Bulgaria Dead Drop
cia-adultery-culture.summary: John Kiriakou's account of a CIA trip to Sofia, Bulgaria, in which he tracked down and debriefed a retired Bulgarian general — a Cold War-era trainee at Fort Polk, Louisiana — about his proximity to the 1975 assassination of CIA station chief Richard Welch in Athens.

cia-adultery-culture.title: The pillow talk leak case
cia-adultery-culture.summary: A 1990s CIA disclosure John Kiriakou witnessed from the next desk: a colleague passed classified information to a retired senior officer she was involved with, who repeated it on CNN as a terrorism consultant. The agency traced it to her within days and punished her administratively — a letter in her file, two weeks without pay, a year without promotion. Kiriakou holds it up as the correct way to handle mishandled classified information.

cia-adultery-culture.title: CIA Democrats (2016)
cia-adultery-culture.summary: John Kiriakou's term for a wave of 2016-era congressional candidates with intelligence or military backgrounds who ran for office opposing Trump from the right on Russia — including former CIA officer Abigail Spanberger, who won a one-term-limited Virginia governorship, and former DIA official Elissa Slotkin, who moved from intelligence into Congress and the Senate — both of whom Kiriakou suggests are positioning for future presidential runs.

cia-adultery-culture.title: "Don''t charge Donald Trump with espionage"
cia-adultery-culture.summary: An opinion piece John Kiriakou wrote for Consortium News after the classified documents were found at Mar-a-Lago, arguing against an Espionage Act prosecution of Trump — and, in its subheading, against Espionage Act prosecutions of anyone else either. He uses it as the frame for his position that the statute should be scrapped and rewritten to reach only those who mean the country harm.

cia-adultery-culture.title: Mike Hayden
cia-adultery-culture.summary: Director of the National Security Agency on September 11, 2001; subsequently Director of the Central Intelligence Agency under President George W. Bush. Per John Kiriakou's relay of NSA whistleblower Tom Drake, on the morning of 9/11 Hayden told NSA personnel the agency had been 'waiting for a 9/11 so that they could implement the bigger program and grab everybody's electronics' — despite the agency's founding charter forbidding it from intercepting the communications of U.S. persons.

cia-and-hollywood.title: American media consolidation
cia-and-hollywood.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of why American news coverage is uniform: the entire national media is owned by six corporations or oligarchs, a number the Warner Brothers sale would reduce to five. He attributes the consolidation to profit rather than politics, and describes the practical consequence as an audience that turns on a cable channel believing it is being educated when it is being propagandised — with independent media the only alternative and almost nobody with the time to find it.

cia-and-hollywood.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
cia-and-hollywood.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

cia-and-hollywood.title: CIA media relations
cia-and-hollywood.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how the CIA shapes press coverage in the 2020s without needing an Operation Mockingbird-style infiltration program — because corporate media now recites CIA messaging willingly, most journalists simply rewrite emailed statements from the agency's Office of Public Affairs, and the CIA allegedly manipulates algorithms and backs podcasts to spread its point of view.

cia-and-hollywood.title: J. Edgar Hoover
cia-and-hollywood.summary: The FBI's founding director — 48 years in the chair — whose opposition nearly strangled the CIA at birth. Per John Kiriakou, Truman lifted Hoover's objection to the National Security Act of 1947 by disingenuously assuring him the CIA would be a division of the FBI; the lie seeded the two agencies' permanent mutual hatred. Kiriakou also credits Hoover with perfecting the annual ritual the CIA later copied — scaring Congress witless and demanding budget increases — and with controlling Hollywood's FBI image so tightly that no film could be made without his approval.

cia-and-hollywood.title: Jeffrey Epstein
cia-and-hollywood.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

cia-and-hollywood.title: John Brennan
cia-and-hollywood.summary: Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President

cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.title: Abu Omar rendition
cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.summary: The CIA's kidnapping of a Milan cleric, Abu Omar, who was sent to Egypt to be tortured; John Kiriakou calls it a case that ought to be taught at the CIA as how not to run a rendition, and it is what ultimately sent him to prison, after he confirmed a former colleague's surname to a journalist claiming to be writing a book about it.

cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.title: Citizens United
cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.summary: The Supreme Court decision John Kiriakou blames for legalizing unlimited corporate political money and for corporations having "taken over" two of the three branches of government — and which he says lets AIPAC pour tens of millions into single congressional races to defeat candidates who cross Israel.

cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.title: Havana Syndrome
cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.summary: Cluster of neurological symptoms — including nausea, ringing in the ears, vertigo, and traumatic brain injury — reported by American diplomatic and intelligence personnel beginning in Havana, Cuba, and subsequently at posts around the world. Per John Kiriakou, his initial skepticism gave way when a friend developed Havana Syndrome with an MRI-confirmed traumatic brain injury after a meeting outside the Russian Foreign Ministry; Kiriakou attributes the syndrome to Russian or Chinese directed-energy weapons and acknowledges the United States used a similar weapon during the operation to capture Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.

cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.title: MK-Ultra
cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.summary: The CIA's mid-twentieth-century umbrella program of mind-control, behavioral-modification, and biological-warfare experimentation, encompassing subprojects such as MK-Chickwit and MK-Seesaw; active 1952–1975; documented practices included LSD dosing of unwitting American citizens in CIA-rented brothels and the aerosolized release of pathogens into the San Francisco fog; 80% of the program's documentation was destroyed by the CIA in defiance of a 1975 preservation order from Senator Frank Church.

cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.title: Overcriminalization
cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that the United States criminalizes too much — locking up 25% of the world's prisoners with 5% of its population, and adding roughly 50 new felonies a year — illustrated by a NOAA employee prosecuted for whistling at a whale.

cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.title: Alec Baldwin
cia-animal-surveillance-experiments.summary: Actor with whom John Kiriakou recounts a bitter falling-out — Baldwin calling him a liar over lunch at a meeting about a play in which Baldwin was to play him, later attaching to a Kiriakou TV pitch that AMC bought the next day, then quitting for HBO and killing the deal without a word.

cia-arabic-hiring-practices.title: Kiriakou's transfer to the Directorate of Operations
cia-arabic-hiring-practices.summary: John Kiriakou's roughly two-month internal campaign to transfer from the CIA's analytic Directorate of Intelligence to the operational Directorate of Operations, overcoming what he calls a "natural bias in operations against the eggheads on the analytic side," followed by an Athens posting secured because he was the only person in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic. Covers his full CIA career arc from 1988/1990 recruitment through analyst years on Iraq, the switch to operations, 9/11, the enhanced-interrogation refusal, executive assistant to the deputy director for operations, and his eventual resignation and post-CIA career.

cia-arabic-hiring-practices.title: Americans and the word socialism
cia-arabic-hiring-practices.summary: Two exchanges John Kiriakou uses to argue that the political vocabulary of the United States has stopped carrying meaning — a Thanksgiving conversation with a woman who denounced socialism and lived on Social Security, and a newspaper comment thread in which a restaurant owner taking his staff's tips was described as socialism.

cia-arabic-hiring-practices.title: Arabic and Greek
cia-arabic-hiring-practices.summary: The qualification John Kiriakou says opened the door to his transfer from CIA analysis to operations: a post in Athens wanted Greek or Arabic, and he had both — by most of his tellings the only officer in the agency who did. The chief who hired him gave the reason in one sentence: it is easier and cheaper to take a linguist and teach him operations than the other way round. The pairing also became a detection tool, since the language nobody speaks in Pakistan is Arabic.

cia-arabic-hiring-practices.title: Aryan Brotherhood
cia-arabic-hiring-practices.summary: The white prison gang that adopted John Kiriakou on his first day at FCI Loretto. Two hours in, two Aryans with swastika neck tattoos walked into his cell to check his paperwork — not a rat, not a "chomo" — and invited him to the Aryan table, which ran from hardcore Nazis at one end to merely white guys at the other. A rumor that he had been a CIA assassin earned him the nickname "the Muslim killer," which he never corrected; asked directly, he answered "we all did stuff we weren't proud of — it was wartime," and the Aryans loved it. He sat with them a year before the Italians took him in.

cia-arabic-hiring-practices.title: Bahrain Posting (1994–1996)
cia-arabic-hiring-practices.summary: John Kiriakou's 1994–1996 assignment to Bahrain under U.S. State Department cover as second secretary for economic affairs — arriving with his wife Joanne and infant son Chris on August 1, 1994, into a tiny Gulf monarchy whose sectarian tensions erupted, two months later, into the first Intifada.

cia-arabic-hiring-practices.title: Candace Owens
cia-arabic-hiring-practices.summary: The commentator whose claims about the killing of Charlie Kirk John Kiriakou has publicly declined to accept. He credits her reach and her intelligence and rejects her method, citing an earlier occasion — a conference call he says he was on — at which she claimed irrefutable proof that the Italian government had stolen the 2020 election and that its release would return Donald Trump to office.

cia-as-policy-support-agency.title: Ukraine as a proxy war
cia-as-policy-support-agency.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment, given two months into the 2022 Russian invasion, that the United States was funding a proxy war it knew Ukraine could not win in order to bog Russia down — and that the outcome was already fixed, so peace talks should happen at once.

cia-as-policy-support-agency.title: Nobel Peace Prize
cia-as-policy-support-agency.summary: The prize a Swedish parliamentarian nominated John Kiriakou for in 2016 — a marker of how far world opinion had swung his way after prison. Kiriakou once believed Obama deserved his; he came to see it as unearned, and he treats Trump's foreign policy as substantially organized around wanting one too — "never underestimate Donald Trump's desire to win a Nobel Peace Prize," a White House friend told him. Netanyahu's nomination of Trump he summarized in a single unprintable phrase.

cia-as-policy-support-agency.title: AIPAC
cia-as-policy-support-agency.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

cia-as-policy-support-agency.title: Bill Clinton
cia-as-policy-support-agency.summary: 42nd U.S. president whom John Kiriakou describes as wholly disinterested in intelligence — briefed by the CIA only twice in eight years, with Vice President Al Gore taking the daily briefing instead and relaying anything important.

cia-as-policy-support-agency.title: Cheney's airstrip question
cia-as-policy-support-agency.summary: A one-line request from Vice President Dick Cheney — what is the longest airstrip in northern Iraq made of? — that nobody in the CIA's operations directorate could answer, and that John Kiriakou eventually resolved by asking the agency librarian. The answer came back within a day, with the exact mix. The purpose was to work out whether the runway would take a transport aircraft carrying two tanks.

cia-as-policy-support-agency.title: Executive assistant to the Deputy Director for Operations
cia-as-policy-support-agency.summary: The job John Kiriakou held during the Iraq war, and the shape of its day: a 2:45 a.m. alarm, ten thousand overnight cables triaged down to five or ten by dawn, the deputy directors briefed at seven and the director at half past — and only then the actual work of coordinating with the State Department, the Pentagon and the vice president''s office.

cia-attention-to-west-africa.title: The NATO expansion promises
cia-attention-to-west-africa.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the assurances American presidents gave Russia that NATO would not expand to its borders or admit Ukraine — promises he says were made repeatedly, broken repeatedly, and, in his blunt formulation, never meant. He couples the account with an equally explicit statement that he opposes the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

cia-attention-to-west-africa.title: The lawfare template
cia-attention-to-west-africa.summary: The assessment of John Kiriakou''s prosecution that he quotes most often and finds most alarming: a former United States attorney for Utah told him the Kiriakou case was the template for the Democratic Party''s policy of lawfare. Kiriakou''s gloss is that if they do not like you they can ruin your life, and there is nothing you can do to protect yourself.

cia-attention-to-west-africa.title: The science fiction writer FOIA request
cia-attention-to-west-africa.summary: The Freedom of Information Act request John Kiriakou filed with the CIA about a 1950s science fiction writer long rumoured to have been an undercover officer — answered only with a letter saying the agency lacked the manpower to meet its statutory ninety-day deadline. Fifteen years later, he says, he is still waiting.

cia-attention-to-west-africa.title: The General Assembly workaround
cia-attention-to-west-africa.summary: A proposal John Kiriakou says a Russian diplomat described to him: letting the United Nations General Assembly take implementable decisions without Security Council permission, so that a supermajority of states could override an American veto. Kiriakou, whose last CIA tour was at the United Nations and who found the institution paralysed, says he thinks it is a good idea.

cia-attention-to-west-africa.title: The minister of Awqaf compliment
cia-attention-to-west-africa.summary: The moment John Kiriakou calls the highlight of his Bahrain tour and freely describes as an ego booster: interpreting for Ambassador David Ransom''s first courtesy call on the only Bahraini cabinet member who did not speak fluent English, and being complimented on his Arabic on the way out — something he says he still thinks about thirty years later.

cia-attention-to-west-africa.title: The tier one walk-up
cia-attention-to-west-africa.summary: The recruitment John Kiriakou calls one of the best operations of his career and credits entirely to his mentor Gust Avrakotos: an approach to an official of a tier one country — one of America''s greatest enemies — made by the simple expedient of walking right up to the man''s house, a technique Avrakotos had used himself in the 1970s.

cia-big-tech-revolving-door.title: CIA feeder schools
cia-big-tech-revolving-door.summary: John Kiriakou's correction to the assumption that Georgetown is the CIA's principal university pipeline — George Washington University, he says, sends more people to the agency than Georgetown does, the first applied intelligence master's programme in the country was at Mercyhurst College in Erie, Pennsylvania, and he himself teaches intelligence studies to a largely American cohort at the University of Salamanca in Spain, many of whom end up at the CIA.

cia-big-tech-revolving-door.title: National security letters
cia-big-tech-revolving-door.summary: The demand letters the FBI began sending internet service providers after 2001, which John Kiriakou describes as one of three mechanisms that between them retired the warrant requirement for obtaining Americans' personal information. The other two are the FISA process and the outright purchase of metadata from social-media companies.

cia-big-tech-revolving-door.title: Panquake
cia-big-tech-revolving-door.summary: Open-source, blockchain-based social platform developed by the Iceland-registered company Talk Liberation, for which John Kiriakou has served as brand ambassador since 2020. Kiriakou describes it as advertising-free, subscription-funded, free of back doors, and run on servers powered by Icelandic geothermal steam — a project he frames as a David-and-Goliath fight against banks, big technology and governments.

cia-big-tech-revolving-door.title: Bahrain Posting (1994–1996)
cia-big-tech-revolving-door.summary: John Kiriakou's 1994–1996 assignment to Bahrain under U.S. State Department cover as second secretary for economic affairs — arriving with his wife Joanne and infant son Chris on August 1, 1994, into a tiny Gulf monarchy whose sectarian tensions erupted, two months later, into the first Intifada.

cia-big-tech-revolving-door.title: Bill Binney
cia-big-tech-revolving-door.summary: Former NSA technical director whom John Kiriakou cites as having debunked the DNC hack.
