dimitris-koufodinas.title: The CIA Insider's Guide to Surveillance and Surveillance Detection
dimitris-koufodinas.summary: Book by John Kiriakou drawing on his experience as a surveillance detection instructor at the CIA and as a private surveillance training consultant. The book covers the techniques used by intelligence professionals to identify whether they are being followed — including the four-phase surveillance detection route, concealment device placement and retrieval, and counter-surveillance strategy — adapted for use by corporate executives, journalists, and others who want to confirm whether they are being followed.

dimitris-koufodinas.title: More money on security in Athens than Beirut
dimitris-koufodinas.summary: John Kiriakou''s measure of how dangerous Athens was for American officials at the turn of the century — that the United States spent more on security there than in Beirut — and the consequence he says followed: no diplomatic plates, because they would make Americans easier to identify and kill.

dimitris-koufodinas.title: John Larson
dimitris-koufodinas.summary: The twenty-eight-year congressman from Connecticut's first district whose primary defeat John Kiriakou reads as a verdict on both the Democratic Party's campaign theory and the age of its incumbents.

directorate-of-intelligence.title: The Directorate of Operations
directorate-of-intelligence.summary: The CIA's clandestine service, which John Kiriakou joined from analysis because he spoke both Greek and Arabic — a culture he describes as wildly different from the analytic side, short on institutional memory and organised around the race to become a station chief.

directorate-of-intelligence.title: The hot dog lady cable
directorate-of-intelligence.summary: A cable John Kiriakou received in response to eight analytic questions about a prominent Middle Eastern women's-rights campaigner, which answered none of them and instead reported that the station called her 'the hot dog lady' and described her preferred condiments. He offers it as the episode that taught him how completely the CIA's operations and analysis directorates had stopped serving each other.

directorate-of-intelligence.title: Chuck Grassley
directorate-of-intelligence.summary: The senior senator from Iowa, and in John Kiriakou's assessment the one member of Congress who has taken whistleblower protection seriously as a legislative project — a count he has variously put at one finger, at two names, and at four out of 535. Grassley wrote the whistleblower protection statutes, speaks every year at the National Whistleblower Day luncheon, and is the name Kiriakou gives prospective whistleblowers as the single friendly ear on Capitol Hill. Kiriakou's personal verdict is colder — Grassley, he has said, never did anything for him.

directorate-of-intelligence.title: JFK assassination
directorate-of-intelligence.summary: November 22, 1963 killing of President John F. Kennedy in Dallas, Texas. John Kiriakou's position, drawn from a Pakistan-station encounter with Bay of Pigs commander Jean Gately, an RFK Jr. account of CIA Director John McCone's same-day exchange with Bobby Kennedy Sr., and a White House contact's confirmation that the remaining classified Kennedy documents all contain the word "Israel," is that elements of the CIA were probably involved and that Israeli intelligence was involved as well.

directorate-of-intelligence.title: John Kiriakou
directorate-of-intelligence.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

directorate-of-intelligence.title: New Castle, Pennsylvania
directorate-of-intelligence.summary: John Kiriakou's home town, an hour north of Pittsburgh on the edge of Amish country — a rust-belt city of roughly 40,000 to 50,000 people when he was growing up and around 18,000 to 20,000 now, whose decline he measures by the arrival of DEA and ATF field offices. It is also where, aged eight or nine and hunting salamanders in Oak Park Cemetery, he found the grave of a Medal of Honor private and acquired the lifelong interest in cemeteries that became a book.

directorate-of-operations.title: The Directorate of Intelligence
directorate-of-operations.summary: The CIA's analytic cadre, where John Kiriakou spent the first seven years of his career working on Iraq before switching to operations — a culture he describes as convinced it holds the smartest people in the room, and whose function he says is duplicated across a dozen other agencies.

directorate-of-operations.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
directorate-of-operations.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

directorate-of-operations.title: The hot dog lady cable
directorate-of-operations.summary: A cable John Kiriakou received in response to eight analytic questions about a prominent Middle Eastern women's-rights campaigner, which answered none of them and instead reported that the station called her 'the hot dog lady' and described her preferred condiments. He offers it as the episode that taught him how completely the CIA's operations and analysis directorates had stopped serving each other.

directorate-of-operations.title: The promotion panel
directorate-of-operations.summary: The CIA board that reviews an officer for advancement, and the one that reviewed John Kiriakou weeks after the Abu Zubaydah capture — where his refusal to be trained in the enhanced interrogation techniques was recorded as *"a shocking lack of commitment to counterterrorism"*, and he was passed over.

directorate-of-operations.title: Arabic and Greek
directorate-of-operations.summary: The qualification John Kiriakou says opened the door to his transfer from CIA analysis to operations: a post in Athens wanted Greek or Arabic, and he had both — by most of his tellings the only officer in the agency who did. The chief who hired him gave the reason in one sentence: it is easier and cheaper to take a linguist and teach him operations than the other way round. The pairing also became a detection tool, since the language nobody speaks in Pakistan is Arabic.

directorate-of-operations.title: Fabricated intelligence reporting
directorate-of-operations.summary: The three things John Kiriakou says CIA case officers are caught doing — inventing intelligence outright, holding real reports back to smooth out a monthly quota, and padding cover-stop expenses — and his argument that the fabrication is driven by production targets set by bad managers.

directorate-of-science-and-technology.title: Mr. Fish
directorate-of-science-and-technology.summary: The cover name the CIA used for Abu Zubaydah in Pakistan in 2002 — invented because the Americans would not tell their Pakistani partners who the target was, and derived from the only thing they would say about him: that he was a big fish.

directorate-of-science-and-technology.title: Magic box
directorate-of-science-and-technology.summary: An improvised cell-phone locator that two CIA tech officers built from parts bought in a Pakistani bazaar during the hunt for Abu Zubaydah. It could point toward a phone while a call was live, and did so exactly once — long enough for John Kiriakou to conclude the device was wasted time and to fly in a targeting analyst instead.

directorate-of-science-and-technology.title: Targeting analyst
directorate-of-science-and-technology.summary: A specialized CIA analyst — distinct from an intelligence analyst — who sifts millions of pieces of data, much of it metadata, to physically locate a person for capture or killing; John Kiriakou credits one with finding Abu Zubaydah down to 14 sites.

directorate-of-science-and-technology.title: Meeting Elon Musk in 2009
directorate-of-science-and-technology.summary: The evening in 2009 when John Kiriakou, waiting to pitch a television idea to an incoming NBC president in a Washington bar, was introduced to a friend the executive had brought along — asked him what he did for a living, and listened to him talk about Mars all night.

directorate-of-science-and-technology.title: The Jordanian intelligence service
directorate-of-science-and-technology.summary: The service John Kiriakou calls one of the best in the world and arguably the best in the Middle East — good, in his account, out of necessity: half of Jordan''s population is Palestinian, Black September once fought on the steps of the palace, and the survival of the monarchy depends on having infiltrated every faction in the country.

djibouti.title: China's base in Djibouti
djibouti.summary: Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti, the abandoned French base the Djiboutians offered to the Americans and the Chinese took a share of — split down the middle by a chain-link fence, the only Chinese military installation outside China, and the centrepiece of John Kiriakou's argument that China is not an expansionist power.

djibouti.title: CIA spy tech from Amazon
djibouti.summary: John Kiriakou's account that roughly 95% of the CIA's spy technology is purchased commercially from Amazon.com rather than custom-built, illustrated by a $10 leather briefcase he had rigged into a listening device in a Pakistani market.

djibouti.title: Saudi-Iran diplomatic rivalry
djibouti.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the roots of Saudi-Iranian hostility — Iran's bloody 1979 infiltration of the Hajj, Saudi Arabia's suppression of its own Shia minority, and the 2023 restoration of diplomatic relations brokered, to Washington's surprise, by China.

djibouti.title: Somaliland
djibouti.summary: Self-declared breakaway state in the Horn of Africa that Israel became the only country in the world to recognize as independent, gaining a military base positioned roughly 30 seconds' flight time from Yemen; John Kiriakou, who visited Somaliland while posted with the Senate Foreign Relations Committee in Djibouti, describes it as a functioning city of about 100,000 unconnected to Mogadishu, al-Shabaab, or piracy.

djibouti.title: The Eritrea prohibition
djibouti.summary: John Kiriakou's account of being forbidden to visit Eritrea on a Senate Foreign Relations Committee trip through the Horn of Africa — not by the Eritrean government but by the State Department, whose only stated reason was that Eritrea is 'the North Korea of Africa.' He notes that he was later free to dine at the Eritrean ambassador's residence in Washington.

djibouti.title: The US overseas basing footprint
djibouti.summary: John Kiriakou''s summary of the one thing he says Democrats and Republicans in Washington genuinely agree on: that the United States needs a military presence in about 110 countries and bases in about 86 of them, along with the newest nuclear weapons, the biggest ships, the best aircraft and the biggest bombs.

dmitry-polyakov.title: Aldrich Ames
dmitry-polyakov.summary: Senior CIA officer — a GS-15 who rose to chief of counterintelligence for the Soviet branch — who spied for the KGB for nine years. Per John Kiriakou, Ames walked into the Soviet embassy in Washington in April 1985 and sold the identities of two CIA-recruited double agents for $50,000 to clear a debt run up by his second marriage; both were executed. He went on to identify more than thirty agents, compromise over a hundred clandestine operations, cause at least twelve deaths and take more than $2 million, while being known throughout the agency as a daily drunk and promoted at every turn. The KGB protected him with a decoy mole hunt; analyst Sandy Grimes caught him by matching his handler meetings to his bank deposits.

dmitry-polyakov.title: Sandy Grimes
dmitry-polyakov.summary: CIA analyst who, per John Kiriakou, was the person who actually broke the Aldrich Ames case. After a 27-year-old security officer sat on an Ames file for eighteen months without action, Grimes independently noticed that Ames made $100,000–$150,000 bank deposits within days of every trip to Mexico City — the pattern that identified him as a spy. After Ames's arrest, she submitted a hot-wash paper recommending 27 reprimands across the chain of command that had promoted a known alcoholic into the most sensitive counterintelligence position in the CIA. Director John Deutch responded with strongly worded letters for seven. Grimes resigned in 1993.

dmitry-polyakov.title: Warrenton Training Center
dmitry-polyakov.summary: A secret CIA communications facility in Warrenton, Virginia, which — per John Kiriakou — the KGB used as a decoy to protect Aldrich Ames. When Ames warned Moscow in 1986 that he feared becoming a suspect, a Soviet case officer told a CIA contact that the mole was posted to Warrenton; agency mole hunters then spent almost a year investigating ninety employees there and produced ten suspects, none of them Ames.

dmitry-polyakov.title: Rosario Ames
dmitry-polyakov.summary: Colombian cultural attaché recruited to work for the CIA, and the second wife of Aldrich Ames. Per John Kiriakou, Ames began an affair with her in Mexico in 1981 in violation of agency regulations; when he brought her and her mother to America his first marriage collapsed, and their taste for high living put him deep enough in debt that he walked into the Soviet embassy to sell it away. She was arrested alongside him at their Arlington home in 1994 and served four years of a 63-month sentence before returning to Colombia.

dmitry-polyakov.title: James Jesus Angleton
dmitry-polyakov.summary: The CIA counterintelligence chief old-timers were 'genuinely afraid' of — and the wall of illegal files on American citizens kept in his office.

dmitry-polyakov.title: John Kiriakou
dmitry-polyakov.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

do-not-contact-me-again.title: The desert sunset photograph
do-not-contact-me-again.summary: The half-hour standoff John Kiriakou describes with Saudi security after photographing a desert sunset that happened to include the Ministry of Interior in the distance — resolved, he says, only when he produced his black diplomatic passport. He also explains that the ban on photographing American embassies from the street is Office of Diplomatic Security policy rather than law, because such pictures can be used to case a building.

do-not-contact-me-again.title: Bigger than the Russian embassy
do-not-contact-me-again.summary: Why American embassies in small, strategically unimportant countries are enormous: the answer John Kiriakou says he was given by a station chief on one of his first CIA trips — that the building had to be bigger than the Soviet one across town. He describes American embassies in Africa as "absolutely gigantic" for that reason alone, and calls the US embassy in Cairo an enormous facility matched by an equally enormous Russian one.

do-not-contact-me-again.title: Declare victory and go home
do-not-contact-me-again.summary: The exit John Kiriakou prescribed for Israel in Gaza: turn the territory back to the United Nations, declare Hamas destroyed, declare victory, then engage the Saudis on the Abraham Accords and negotiate a deal later. His reasoning was that nothing remained to destroy, that killing as many people as possible is not a viable policy, and that Israel had no other way out.

do-not-contact-me-again.title: "Every Israeli I ever knew"
do-not-contact-me-again.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the attitudes he encountered among Israelis he knew professionally and socially — that almost every one of them wanted the Palestinians killed or exiled — together with his description of a sensibility he says is palpable walking around Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, and his immediate self-correction when he overstated the claim.

do-not-contact-me-again.title: The Greek offer for the Bamiyan Buddhas
do-not-contact-me-again.summary: John Kiriakou's account that the Greek government, in the depths of its own economic depression, tried to buy the Bamiyan Buddhas from the Taliban in order to save them — intending to donate the statues back to a post-Taliban Afghan government. The offer was refused and the fifteen-hundred-year-old figures were destroyed.

do-not-contact-me-again.title: The Kerry yacht tax
do-not-contact-me-again.summary: John Kiriakou's account, from his time on John Kerry's Senate staff, of the ocean-going boat Kerry docked in Rhode Island to avoid the Massachusetts yacht tax — the flood of angry calls it produced, and the advice Kiriakou gave the staff director about it.

do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.title: The Berlin conference list
do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.summary: Checking into a Berlin hotel for a conference, John Kiriakou was handed the guest list when the clerk could not find his booking — and discovered that every one of the dozen names on it was a friend of his, and every one of them an outspoken whistleblower.

do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.title: "The least I could do"
do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.summary: Told that he had kept another whistleblower from slipping, John Kiriakou declined the credit and described the work in the plainest possible terms: getting somebody out of the house for three or four hours, or taking them to dinner, because so many people had done exactly that for him when he was at his lowest.

do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.title: National Whistleblower Day
do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.summary: John Kiriakou has called National Whistleblower Day an event no whistleblower or supporter should miss — held every year in the Kennedy Caucus Room, which he describes as not merely the biggest room on Capitol Hill but the most historic single room anywhere on it, having hosted every major Senate hearing from the sinking of the Titanic to Watergate and Iran-Contra.

do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.title: The cousin who stopped speaking
do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.summary: An older first cousin told John Kiriakou after his conviction that he could no longer speak to him because Kiriakou had brought shame on the family; Kiriakou's reply was to point out that the cousin had imported drugs from Colombia, had appeared in the Washington Post as a mayor's cocaine dealer, and had fled to Greece until the statute of limitations expired.

do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.title: "We don''t hire felons"
do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.summary: After his release from prison John Kiriakou could not find work anywhere — turned down, he says, by Target, Safeway, McDonald's and Uber — and the one job he was eventually offered, at a Washington think tank, paid minimum wage on condition that he run a permanent crowdfunding campaign to raise his own salary.

do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.title: The woman escorted from the White House
do-what-is-right-or-what-is-easy.summary: Before John Kiriakou spoke to ABC News, someone else had already blown the whistle on the CIA's secret prisons — a woman at the White House whom he respected deeply, who was escorted out of the building, stripped of her badge and told never to come back, and who has always insisted it was not her.

doctor-zhivago-operation.title: John Paul II and the CIA
doctor-zhivago-operation.summary: John Kiriakou's account that CIA old-timers took credit for helping make the Polish cardinal John Paul II pope — a political move to weaken the Soviet Union — and that his later recognition of the state of Israel was seen as a bonus for the West.

doctor-zhivago-operation.title: Mormons in intelligence
doctor-zhivago-operation.summary: John Kiriakou's observation that Mormons are heavily overrepresented in the CIA and FBI — because their clean-living record lets them pass the polygraph easily, and their missionary years leave them fluent in rare languages the agencies need.

doctor-zhivago-operation.title: Operation Gladio
doctor-zhivago-operation.summary: A CIA, MI6, Vatican and NATO operation to leave 'stay-behind' sleeper networks across Western Europe after World War II in case of a Soviet invasion; John Kiriakou, who learned of it only after leaving the CIA, notes it was made public by Italian PM Andreotti in 1990.

doctor-zhivago-operation.title: Italian election covert action
doctor-zhivago-operation.summary: What John Kiriakou calls the CIA''s very first covert action: bribing Italian journalists in the 1949 election to write in favor of the Christian Democrats, who narrowly beat the Communists — a operation he says amounted to stealing the election.

doctor-zhivago-operation.title: Active measures
doctor-zhivago-operation.summary: The in-house name John Kiriakou gives to the CIA branch responsible for propaganda and for countering hostile propaganda — a division he describes as running twenty-four hours a day, paired with an opposing anti-active-measures branch, and as the ancestor of the political action group that remains the agency's clandestine propaganda arm.

doctor-zhivago-operation.title: Bahrain Posting (1994–1996)
doctor-zhivago-operation.summary: John Kiriakou's 1994–1996 assignment to Bahrain under U.S. State Department cover as second secretary for economic affairs — arriving with his wife Joanne and infant son Chris on August 1, 1994, into a tiny Gulf monarchy whose sectarian tensions erupted, two months later, into the first Intifada.

dog-food-memo.title: Sewer trout
dog-food-memo.summary: The name prisoners at FCI Loretto gave the fish served on Fridays — which John Kiriakou says arrived in boxes stacked illegally behind the serving line, marked Alaskan cod, product of China, and not for human consumption, feed use only.

dog-food-memo.title: FCI Loretto
dog-food-memo.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

dog-food-memo.title: Cell transfers at Loretto
dog-food-memo.summary: How a prisoner at FCI Loretto moved from one cell to another — a process requiring six months in place, the written agreement of the receiving cell and the signature of the counselor, which John Kiriakou describes as a guard assigned to be a designated pain in the ass.

dog-food-memo.title: Cleanliness in prison
dog-food-memo.summary: John Kiriakou's account of hygiene and order at FCI Loretto — where everybody showered daily on pain of a beating, everybody was constantly cleaning, and the rules on possessions and bedmaking left almost no room for clutter.

dog-food-memo.title: Blue
dog-food-memo.summary: The FCI Loretto correctional officer, widely considered the most unpopular in the prison, who covered his own nameplate with masking tape so released prisoners could not find him — and who told a colleague of John Kiriakou's that he would never touch the CIA man because of the press attention.

dog-food-memo.title: Prison nicknames
dog-food-memo.summary: The naming convention John Kiriakou describes at FCI Loretto — where nearly every Black and Hispanic prisoner went by a nickname, most white prisoners did not, and the nickname rather than the legal name was what a man gave when signing up for the basketball tournament.

doing-time-like-a-spy.title: Louis Farrakhan
doing-time-like-a-spy.summary: Leader of the Nation of Islam; per John Kiriakou, issued a perfectly timed statement during Kiriakou's imprisonment at FCI Loretto identifying him as a hero of the Muslim people for standing up for human rights — protecting Kiriakou from the prison's Muslim population at a moment when the Aryans were simultaneously protecting him under the cover story that he was a "Muslim hunter."

doing-time-like-a-spy.title: Mark Lanzotti
doing-time-like-a-spy.summary: John Kiriakou's best friend in prison — an Italian sentenced to triple life without parole for a first-time nonviolent meth conspiracy he was the only man to voluntarily leave; Kiriakou wrote the appeal that won his release, and he is now the top-selling realtor on the Jersey Shore.

doing-time-like-a-spy.title: The prison food economy
doing-time-like-a-spy.summary: The underground kitchen at FCI Loretto, where meals were cooked in bin liners heated by improvised immersion elements, guards stole and resold the food they were meant to be guarding, and Kiriakou stopped going to the cafeteria for the last six to eight months of his sentence.

doing-time-like-a-spy.title: Kiriakou''s recommended reading
doing-time-like-a-spy.summary: Asked in March 2026 what to read about the CIA, John Kiriakou named his own first two books and, beyond them, a 1980s history called The Rise and Fall of the CIA, which he says was his own first real introduction to covert action and its failures.

doing-time-like-a-spy.title: The prison visiting room
doing-time-like-a-spy.summary: The room where a federal prisoner sees his family, reached through a strip-search cell — where John Kiriakou's children came to accept where their father was, where a former CIA boss turned up unannounced, and which is closed entirely to prisoners held under special administrative measures.

doing-time-like-a-spy.title: The Cat in the Hat and Truck
doing-time-like-a-spy.summary: The prison anecdote John Kiriakou uses to illustrate the CIA counter-accusation tradecraft he applied at FCI Loretto, a cellmate applicant called Cat in the Hat named him a rat to a serial killer named Truck within earshot; Kiriakou answered by remarking Cat in the Hat had earlier called Truck a pedophile; Truck beat Cat in the Hat almost to death and had to be lifelighted by helicopter to Pittsburgh.

domingos-television.title: Three square meals and a warm bed
domingos-television.summary: John Kiriakou has said he will never forget a remark he overheard from three men playing cards in an empty television room at FCI Loretto, who counted up the meals, the bed, the clothes, the television and the medical care they were given and concluded that the place was very nearly paradise.

domingos-television.title: The persona in the first week
domingos-television.summary: Five days into a sentence he had expected to serve at a minimum-security camp, John Kiriakou decided to fall back on his CIA training and adopt a deliberately aggressive exterior — reasoning that in a prison where the weak end up checking themselves into solitary for protection, he would rather be the man other people needed protection from.

domingos-television.title: The CIA that never existed
domingos-television.summary: A former senior CIA officer once told John Kiriakou that the agency he spoke about so fondly had never really existed — that it had only existed in his mind, that it had always been troubled and antithetical to American life, and that he had simply been too junior to see what was happening at the top. Kiriakou has come to think the man was right.

domingos-television.title: The Official Secrets Act comparison
domingos-television.summary: John Kiriakou has argued that for whistleblowers the United Kingdom is far worse than the United States, because the Official Secrets Act bars anyone from saying anything touching national security and is used, in his phrase, as an iron fist against whistleblowers and potential whistleblowers alike.

domingos-television.title: The Flynn charges
domingos-television.summary: John Kiriakou supported the appointment of a special counsel in 2017 while rejecting the Russia allegations outright — arguing that the case for an investigation rested not on election interference but on a list of ordinary, provable crimes he believed senior Trump campaign figures, and Michael Flynn in particular, had already committed.

domingos-television.title: The Washington Post editorial on the cover-up
domingos-television.summary: In May 2017 John Kiriakou pointed to an editorial in a newspaper he says he generally hates, which advised Donald Trump to save himself by adopting Ronald Reagan's Iran-Contra posture — on the principle that it is never the crime that brings a president down but the cover-up, a principle Kiriakou illustrated with the conviction of Scooter Libby.

domino-theory.title: Contra rebels
domino-theory.summary: The right-wing Nicaraguan insurgency armed by the Reagan administration against the Sandinista government. In John Kiriakou's account they were conservatives, right-wingers, in some cases fascists, and disgruntled military officers; they were split into a northern group the United States armed and a southern group that financed itself by selling cocaine — a distinction that became the pivot of the Gary Webb affair, and that Kiriakou uses to answer the CIA's standing denial that it had anything to do with the drug trade.

domino-theory.title: Dark Alliance
domino-theory.summary: Gary Webb's seven-part San Jose Mercury News investigation reporting that cocaine reaching Los Angeles and fuelling the crack epidemic had travelled through Nicaragua with the CIA's knowledge. John Kiriakou's account stresses what Webb did and did not claim — that the agency turned a blind eye rather than ran the operation — and that three separate federal investigations later found his reporting correct.

domino-theory.title: Iran-Contra
domino-theory.summary: The mid-1980s scandal in which the Reagan administration secretly sold weapons to Iran and diverted the proceeds — laundered through Cyprus — to fund the Contra rebels in Nicaragua. Per John Kiriakou, Iran-Contra marks the precise end of what he calls the ''golden age'' of congressional intelligence oversight: the roughly 1975–1982 window opened by the Church and Pike Committees, when ''serious people, heavyweights'' actually held the CIA accountable. After Iran-Contra, he says, the oversight committees reverted to being ''cheerleaders'' for the agency — a posture that has held ever since.

domino-theory.title: Adnan Khashoggi
domino-theory.summary: Saudi arms dealer and Iran-Contra middleman whom John Kiriakou says was mentioned 'all the time' at the CIA — in pointed contrast to Jeffrey Epstein, whose name he never once heard there.

domino-theory.title: CIA Drug Facilitation
domino-theory.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the CIA''s reported involvement in facilitating the arrival of cocaine into the United States during the era that became the crack epidemic, and his own firsthand discovery — as a Senate Foreign Relations Committee investigator — that under American military control Afghanistan produced 93% of the world''s heroin. A DEA contact told him the report would never be published because ''we want Iran and Russia to be addicted to heroin. It weakens their societies.'' Kiriakou draws a direct parallel to the current fentanyl crisis: China is doing to the US what the US did to Iran and Russia.

domino-theory.title: Kill the Messenger (Gary Webb)
domino-theory.summary: The 2014 film about journalist Gary Webb, on which John Kiriakou served as script advisor; when Kiriakou was arrested in January 2012, the FBI seized his electronics, including a draft of the unclassified Hollywood script, and stamped every page "top secret" despite Kiriakou having no role in writing it.

donald-rumsfeld.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
donald-rumsfeld.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

donald-rumsfeld.title: Sleep deprivation
donald-rumsfeld.summary: A CIA interrogation technique used against high-value detainees post-9/11; the agency was authorized to deny prisoners sleep for up to 12 days continuously; people died; at least one detainee was rendered permanently clinically insane.

donald-rumsfeld.title: John Kiriakou
donald-rumsfeld.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

donald-rumsfeld.title: Osama bin Laden
donald-rumsfeld.summary: Founder and leader of al-Qaeda and the central target of the manhunt that shaped John Kiriakou's counterterrorism career. Per Kiriakou, bin Laden came from a billionaire Saudi construction family, was never one of the CIA-funded Afghan mujahideen, overruled subordinates who wanted to attack Israel and insisted the 9/11 attacks hit the United States to crash its economy, escaped Tora Bora dressed as a woman, and spent his final years next to Pakistan's equivalent of West Point — where, Kiriakou says, you would have to be a "mental defective" not to know he was there. Kiriakou believes the United States never intended to capture him alive.

donald-rumsfeld.title: Cold cell
donald-rumsfeld.summary: A CIA interrogation technique in which a stripped detainee is chained to a ceiling eyebolt in a cell chilled to 50°F, then doused with a bucket of ice water at hourly intervals; never authorized; documented to have killed at least two prisoners.

donald-rumsfeld.title: Senate Intelligence Committee
donald-rumsfeld.summary: The Senate Select Committee on Intelligence — the CIA's designated overseer, which John Kiriakou credits with the torture report's unimpeachable method (6 million contemporaneous CIA field cables) and simultaneously dismisses, along with its House counterpart, as "little more than cheerleaders for the CIA" since the mid-1980s. It sits in the official whistleblower channel he calls a proven dead end, and its own investigation was famously spied on by the very agency it oversees.

donald-trump.title: Alex Padilla
donald-trump.summary: U.S. Senator from California who was forced to the ground and handcuffed at a June 2025 press event after identifying himself as a sitting senator; per John Kiriakou, DHS Secretary Kristi Noem's claim that he failed to identify himself was false, and the White House's stated interest in prosecuting him was legally baseless because sitting senators have congressional immunity while acting in the course of their duties.

donald-trump.title: Israeli False Flags
donald-trump.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the Mossad has been carrying out false flag operations since the founding of the state of Israel and is "usually very good at it"; he says his first suspicion on hearing of attacks on Saudi oil fields, Azerbaijan, and Cyprus was that they were Israeli false flags, and he fears a false flag against the Al-Aqsa Mosque blamed on Iran or the Arabs.

donald-trump.title: James Fishback
donald-trump.summary: Florida gubernatorial candidate whom Kiriakou says he never personally endorsed, despite viral claims and a since-deleted tweet posted by his assistant; Kiriakou calls Fishback's stance on Israel well-considered but distances himself from Fishback's other stated positions, including a proposed sin tax on OnlyFans creators, an immigration moratorium, and comments Kiriakou calls racist.

donald-trump.title: Roy Cohn
donald-trump.summary: Closeted McCarthy-era prosecutor and fixer, later a mentor, advisor and attorney to Donald Trump from the 1970s onward; per John Kiriakou, one of the darkest, ugliest figures in modern American history, who — while closely allied with a similarly closeted J. Edgar Hoover — was central to ruining the lives of gay men, and who died of AIDS in the 1980s alone and unloved.

donald-trump.title: Saudi-Iran diplomatic rivalry
donald-trump.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the roots of Saudi-Iranian hostility — Iran's bloody 1979 infiltration of the Hajj, Saudi Arabia's suppression of its own Shia minority, and the 2023 restoration of diplomatic relations brokered, to Washington's surprise, by China.

donald-trump.title: "The American war against Iran"
donald-trump.summary: A correction Benjamin Netanyahu issued to an Israeli reporter during the 2026 war — that it was the American war against Iran, and that Israel was merely America's ally. John Kiriakou treats it as the moment Israel walked away from a war it had spent years demanding, leaving the United States to fight it alone.

donnie-reynolds-jr.title: Marty Gottesfeld
donnie-reynolds-jr.summary: American hacktivist and computer security engineer, convicted for a 2014 denial-of-service attack on Boston Children's Hospital in protest of the treatment of patient Justina Pelletier; a fellow federal prisoner of John Kiriakou who has publicly taken up the case of Donnie Reynolds Jr.

donnie-reynolds-jr.title: Operation Fast and Furious
donnie-reynolds-jr.summary: The ATF gun-walking operation John Kiriakou describes as the background to the Donnie Reynolds Jr case — in which agents let 2,000 weapons reach Mexican cartel buyers in the hope of tracing them upward, arrested nobody at the top, and then turned back on the small players when Congress demanded answers.

donnie-reynolds-jr.title: FCI Loretto
donnie-reynolds-jr.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

donnie-reynolds-jr.title: Private prison system
donnie-reynolds-jr.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the U.S. private prison industry as an incentive to keep beds filled and cut costs on food and medicine — illustrated by the 'sewer trout,' dog-food, and dead-rat-in-the-Kool-Aid stories from his own incarceration.

donnie-reynolds-jr.title: Clint Goswick
donnie-reynolds-jr.summary: Fellow federal prisoner of John Kiriakou at FCI Loretto; a devout Christian and Wichita Falls, Texas heating-and-air-conditioning business owner convicted of drug conspiracy and a gun charge despite never having used, possessed, manufactured, or distributed drugs.

donnie-reynolds-jr.title: Communications management unit
donnie-reynolds-jr.summary: The two restricted-contact units inside the American federal prison system, at Terre Haute and Marion; built for "the worst of the worst" but, in John Kiriakou's account, used to silence prisoners whose messages are inconvenient — and a practice he groups with solitary confinement as torture. He served part of his own sentence in a modified one.

dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.title: Espionage Act
dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.title: The pillow talk leak case
dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.summary: A 1990s CIA disclosure John Kiriakou witnessed from the next desk: a colleague passed classified information to a retired senior officer she was involved with, who repeated it on CNN as a terrorism consultant. The agency traced it to her within days and punished her administratively — a letter in her file, two weeks without pay, a year without promotion. Kiriakou holds it up as the correct way to handle mishandled classified information.

dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.title: The Charles Littlejohn prosecution
dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.summary: The five-year sentence handed to an IRS contractor who disclosed Donald Trump's tax returns to the New York Times, which John Kiriakou calls stunning and unjustified — the material was protected but not classified, the Biden campaign made use of it, and the sentencing judge compared the disclosure to the January 6 attack on the Capitol.

dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.title: Chelsea Manning
dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.summary: Former U.S. Army intelligence analyst who provided WikiLeaks its 2010 trove of military and diplomatic documents. Per John Kiriakou, Manning meets the legal definition of whistleblower for exposing war crimes, was a torture victim of prolonged solitary confinement with forced nudity, and was sentenced to 35 years in prison before Barack Obama commuted — not pardoned — her sentence. Kiriakou says Manning later refused a grand jury's offer of immunity and chose renewed jail time rather than testify against Julian Assange.

dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.title: CIA adultery culture
dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.summary: John Kiriakou's recurring characterization of the CIA officer corps as riddled with adultery and casual sex — which he frames not as gossip but as a systemic counterintelligence vulnerability that makes officers easy to recruit.

dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.title: Donald Trump
dont-charge-trump-with-espionage-oped.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.title: Business class after 9/11
dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.summary: John Kiriakou''s illustration of what the post-attack money did to the CIA''s habits: Cofer Black telling him to just do whatever operation he was proposing because there was so much money it could not possibly be spent, and everyone at the agency flying business class from then on, anywhere in the world.

dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.title: Security, medical and finance
dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.summary: The warning John Kiriakou says his first station chief gave him and that he passed on in turn to a first-tour case officer in Pakistan: there are only three offices at the CIA that can wreck your career — security, medical and finance — and only finance can send you to prison.

dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.title: The General Muhammad equipment gift
dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the end of the Abu Zubaydah operation in Pakistan, when headquarters told him to throw away or hand over the truckloads of equipment his station had bought — and of learning weeks later from his day-to-day Pakistani contact that the brigadier general who accepted the gift had simply taken it all himself.

dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.title: Kiriakou on wine
dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.summary: John Kiriakou's long-standing interest in wine — a subscription to Wine Spectator running a quarter of a century, a climate-controlled cellar built into his house, an eye that has twice caught a host passing off a cheap bottle as something better, and a professional life in which wine served in turn as cover story, surveillance-detection errand, recruitment currency and diplomatic catastrophe.

dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.title: No-bid contracts
dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the mechanism he considers the real corruption of American national security: an officer retires on a Friday, returns Monday on a contractor badge at ten times the salary, and is fed no-bid contracts by the friends he left behind — including, in one unnamed case he describes, a tax shelter that became a multi-billion dollar company inside a decade.

dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.title: Prison guard hiring standards
dont-try-to-save-the-government-money.summary: John Kiriakou's account of what it takes to become a federal prison guard — a GED or work towards one, and no felony convictions — and his supporting anecdote that prisoners themselves regularly had to conduct mail call because the officer assigned to it could not read.

double-agent-capture.title: Surveillance detection route
double-agent-capture.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

double-agent-capture.title: Asset acquisition cycle
double-agent-capture.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

double-agent-capture.title: Marriott double-agent trap
double-agent-capture.summary: Operation in which John Kiriakou, posing as a CIA station chief in a Middle East posting, lured a hostile-service-controlled double agent ordered to kill him into a Marriott Hotel room, tackled him out of the bathroom, sedated him with Demerol, and smuggled him out under a sheet on a gurney. A children's-style hand-drawn map with an X led the CIA to the terrorist network's full weapons cache.

double-agent-capture.title: The propane truck ruse
double-agent-capture.summary: The improvised environmental emergency John Kiriakou staged to empty a Middle Eastern cul-de-sac so a CIA lock-picking team could search a captured Hezbollah organiser's house — after his liaison partners rejected a gas leak on the ground that the country had no underground gas lines.

double-agent-capture.title: Training foreign intelligence services
double-agent-capture.summary: The CIA job John Kiriakou took after returning from Athens — travelling the world to teach foreign services how to carry out counterterrorist raids, break down doors, seize people, conduct interrogations and disrupt cells — and why, he says, those countries asked the Americans rather than the Israelis or the British.

double-agent-capture.title: The weapons cache map
double-agent-capture.summary: The single sheet of paper found inside an otherwise empty gun safe in the Middle East — a childlike map marked with an X and written directions past a palm tree and a large rock, which led John Kiriakou's team to a desert bunker packed to the ceiling with Hezbollah's arsenal.

double-agent-marriott-trap.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
double-agent-marriott-trap.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

double-agent-marriott-trap.title: Surveillance detection route
double-agent-marriott-trap.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

double-agent-marriott-trap.title: Billy Waugh
double-agent-marriott-trap.summary: Long-serving CIA paramilitary contractor; U.S. Army Special Forces ("Green Beret") veteran of World War II, Korea, and Vietnam; holder of approximately seventeen Purple Hearts (license plate "17 HITS"); resident of Niceville, Florida; died in his nineties.

double-agent-marriott-trap.title: Counterterrorism Center
double-agent-marriott-trap.summary: The CIA's Counterterrorism Center (CTC) — the unit where John Kiriakou spent the defining years of his operational career. He joined in the late 1990s as the only officer in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic, served as chief of counterintelligence in the bin Laden unit, watched the Center swell from a few hundred employees to nearly 2,000 by September 12, 2001, and it was to CTC that he walked back down in May 2002 to refuse the torture program — the moment, he says, the CIA began to turn on him.

double-agent-marriott-trap.title: Doing Time Like a Spy
double-agent-marriott-trap.summary: Prison memoir by John Kiriakou, full title Doing Time Like a Spy: How the CIA Taught Me to Survive and Thrive in Prison; winner of two literary awards and reissued in a second edition by Simon and Schuster.

double-agent-marriott-trap.title: Mad minute
double-agent-marriott-trap.summary: CIA case-officer procedure for the opening seconds of every meeting with a recruited source — confirm the source is safe, confirm a clean surveillance-detection route, and set the next meeting — so that if the door is kicked in, the operational essentials have already been taken care of.

dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.title: Barrett Brown
dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.summary: American journalist and former Anonymous associate whom John Kiriakou describes as one of the most intelligent writers and analysts he has ever encountered, with long-standing mental health problems and a two-decade heroin addiction he has now been clear of for at least a year, expelled from the United Kingdom and relocated to Mexico.

dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.title: Censorship on the left
dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.summary: John Kiriakou''s observation that he was censored far less by Forbes and Fortune than by The Nation and Mother Jones, which he offers as an instance of a general rule that a writer''s own side censors them hardest — the counterpart to Ted Rall''s account of being made to fit a particular kind of leftism rather than any kind.

dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.title: The Iron Dome
dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.summary: Israel's air-defence system as John Kiriakou reads it — impressive against a wave of slow Iranian drones, but shown by the handful that got through, and later by Iranian ballistic missiles, to be not all it is cracked up to be; each exchange, in his account, buying Iran intelligence about the gaps.

dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.title: James Morris
dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.summary: A close friend of John Kiriakou''s who served seventeen years of a twenty-year sentence for a crime committed at sixteen, found on release that a violent felony conviction closed off employment, made his own way to Turkey and across the border into Syria, spent two years fighting alongside the Kurds against ISIS, and later took his own life.

dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.title: The Afghans in diplomatic limbo
dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.summary: John Kiriakou''s two-sided answer on the Afghan evacuees still held at a base in Qatar years after the fall of Kabul: that anyone who works for an occupation government which then loses will probably end badly, and that the United States nevertheless owes a debt to people who worked for it and should not leave them hanging.

dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.title: Turkey and a safe zone in Iran
dr-oz-and-the-armenian-hospices.summary: John Kiriakou''s response to the Turkish president''s suggestion that, in the event of an attack on Iran, the Turkish army would establish a safe zone inside Iranian territory — that Ankara would love nothing more, having previously taken Iraqi, Cypriot and Syrian territory, and that pan-Turkism is a subject most people are unaware of.

drone-base-balochistan.title: Jason Leopold
drone-base-balochistan.summary: Bloomberg investigative journalist; characterized by John Kiriakou as the leading practitioner of Freedom of Information Act litigation against U.S. [intelligence agencies](/wiki/intelligence-agencies); broke the Hillary Clinton private-email-server story; whose FOIA suit against the CIA Office of Public Affairs produced documentary evidence that NBC's chief national-security correspondent had been sending articles to the CIA for clearance before sending them to his own editor.

drone-base-balochistan.title: John Brennan
drone-base-balochistan.summary: Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President

drone-base-balochistan.title: Alex Karp
drone-base-balochistan.summary: Co-founder and CEO of Palantir Technologies; subject of a biographical assessment commissioned from John Kiriakou by an unnamed interest group; characterized as militarily-industrially conservative despite a Democratic Party registration, religious, extremely patriotic, and "driven by profit."

drone-base-balochistan.title: Arrais Corporation
drone-base-balochistan.summary: Private intelligence firm; companion entity to The Analysis Corporation; originally an LLC pass-through for retired Senior Intelligence Service personnel from the CIA's operations side; subsequently acquired by IBM for over $1 billion.

drone-base-balochistan.title: Asset acquisition cycle
drone-base-balochistan.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

drone-base-balochistan.title: Bluffdale NSA Data Center
drone-base-balochistan.summary: The NSA's purpose-built facility in the Utah desert, characterized by John Kiriakou as having storage capacity for every phone call, text message, and email of every American for the next 500 years.

drunken-border-guards.title: Trump's NATO reversal
drunken-border-guards.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for Donald Trump's turn from hostility to enthusiasm for NATO — that he genuinely expected Vladimir Putin to do as he was told, and embraced the alliance out of anger when Putin would not settle the war in Ukraine, because the alternative was standing alone.

drunken-border-guards.title: The Kosovo objection
drunken-border-guards.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the 1999 NATO bombing of Yugoslavia as seen from the American embassy in Athens — an Orthodox Christian American diplomat serving in an Orthodox country while the United States bombed one, and his view that Kosovo is a rump state invented on land holy to the Serbian Orthodox Church.

drunken-border-guards.title: Ali from Newark
drunken-border-guards.summary: The Black shot caller at FCI Loretto, near the end of a twenty-five-year drug sentence, who came to embrace John Kiriakou at the close of his term and tell him how much he respected him — a friendship possible only because Kiriakou had decided on arrival to ignore the prison's racial divisions.

drunken-border-guards.title: Bezalel Smotrich
drunken-border-guards.summary: Israeli far-right minister whom John Kiriakou, alongside Itamar Ben-Gvir, blames for leaving Israel unprepared on October 7 by insisting any attack would come from the West Bank rather than Gaza.

drunken-border-guards.title: Candace Owens
drunken-border-guards.summary: The commentator whose claims about the killing of Charlie Kirk John Kiriakou has publicly declined to accept. He credits her reach and her intelligence and rejects her method, citing an earlier occasion — a conference call he says he was on — at which she claimed irrefutable proof that the Italian government had stolen the 2020 election and that its release would return Donald Trump to office.

drunken-border-guards.title: Clyde Hall
drunken-border-guards.summary: The imprisoned Ohio congressman John Kiriakou says served at his prison a few years before him, whose remark on release — that he had made some of the best friends of his life inside — Kiriakou thought insane at the time and came to understand after his own sentence.

dubai-as-irans-window.title: Why the UAE was targeted
dubai-as-irans-window.summary: John Kiriakou''s explanation for the disproportionate weight of Iranian fire falling on the United Arab Emirates in 2026: not the American presence but the Emirati role at the forefront of the war against the Houthis — and a wish to bloody Emirati noses despite the thousands of Iranians living in Dubai.

dubai-as-irans-window.title: Bombing the Omanis
dubai-as-irans-window.summary: John Kiriakou's judgement that Iran's strikes on the Gulf states — and above all on Oman, which had been trying to broker peace — made enemies Iran did not need to make, of governments that would otherwise have sat the war out.

dubai-as-irans-window.title: Chaos as the Israeli objective
dubai-as-irans-window.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to whether Netanyahu''s government actually wanted an American invasion of Iran: what the Israelis want in Iran is what they got in Libya — chaos, civil war, and as many dead Iranians as possible.

dubai-as-irans-window.title: Iranian strikes on Gulf hotels
dubai-as-irans-window.summary: John Kiriakou''s reading of the Iranian drone and missile attacks on hotels in Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Muscat during the 2026 war: not targeted killings, but deliberate strikes at the tourist economies of the Gulf states, aimed at hotels famous enough to empty the country of visitors.

dubai-as-irans-window.title: Marco Rubio and Iran policy
dubai-as-irans-window.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to who was actually driving American policy toward Iran in 2026: with the Vice President, the Director of National Intelligence and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs all reported as opposed, and with Marco Rubio holding both the State Department and the National Security Adviser''s job, the policy was Rubio''s.

dubai-as-irans-window.title: The Bridgeton and the tanker escorts
dubai-as-irans-window.summary: John Kiriakou's recollection of the 1980s American naval escort of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, and of seeing the SS Bridgeton — then the largest oil tanker in the world, set ablaze by the Iranians — from a boat in the Persian Gulf.

dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.title: The Scooter Libby deposition
dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.summary: The 2006 or 2007 session at which John Kiriakou, appearing as a witness in the Scooter Libby case, mentioned that the only conversation he had witnessed between two senior CIA officers concerned a covert action programme — and the agency's general counsel jumped up and stopped him mid-sentence, because an officer may not say the words at all.

dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.title: The voice vote on the Epstein files
dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how the Senate passed the Epstein files release without a roll call — a voice vote he says Chuck Schumer requested to save the majority leader, leaving no written record of how anyone voted and allowing every senator but one House holdout to claim they had stood up to the pedophiles.

dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.title: The can of ravioli
dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.summary: John Kiriakou's confession that he eats tinned ravioli cold, straight from the can, and refuses on principle to pay more than ninety-nine cents for it — used, when the price reached $2.49, as his own answer to the polling finding that Americans care about prices more than anything else.

dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.title: The colour-coded badges
dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.summary: The CIA's badge system as John Kiriakou describes it — blue for the top secret compartments everyone in the building holds, green for contractors, yellow for the language instructors cleared only to secret, red for the man in the cafeteria doughnut shop and the woman who vacuums at night — and the lettered suffixes that were dropped once the letters themselves gave the game away.

dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.title: The culture of secrecy and the truth
dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.summary: Asked how he decided what counted as true inside an institution built on secrecy, and whether that changed after he left, John Kiriakou answered no twice — because in his account everyone knows the difference in their gut, and the job is to stop the culture of secrecy from bastardising what you already know.

dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.title: The family that spans the spectrum
dumping-cash-in-a-moscow-bathroom.summary: John Kiriakou''s Greek relations, offered as a political cross-section: his grandmother''s first cousin sat on the politburo of the Communist Party of Greece, a close cousin was elected governor of the Dodecanese for the Conservatives, he has everybody in between — and all of them, to his bafflement, love the American ambassador.

dumping-the-treasury-bonds.title: The rare earth calculation
dumping-the-treasury-bonds.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of how China came to control the world market in rare earth metals — not by holding the only deposits, which exist everywhere including under California's Salton Sea, but by being willing to absorb the economic loss of mining ore that is mostly waste, at a fraction of American defence spending.

dumping-the-treasury-bonds.title: MOSSAD
dumping-the-treasury-bonds.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

dumping-the-treasury-bonds.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
dumping-the-treasury-bonds.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

dumping-the-treasury-bonds.title: "Beyond Your Dreams"
dumping-the-treasury-bonds.summary: The gloss a host gave John Kiriakou on his first trip to China when he asked what the beautiful car with the BYD badge was — and the answer he got when he asked why he had never heard of it, which was that the United States is the only country where they are not sold.

dumping-the-treasury-bonds.title: Lavrov on sanctions
dumping-the-treasury-bonds.summary: The two remarks by Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov that John Kiriakou pairs to summarise the failure of the sanctions weapon — that Russia was surprised by how swiftly the Americans imposed sanctions, and, a year or two later, surprised by how quickly Russia got around them.

dumping-the-treasury-bonds.title: Abu Zubaydah
dumping-the-treasury-bonds.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

e-jean-carroll.title: The Epstein birthday book
e-jean-carroll.summary: The page attributed to Donald Trump in Jeffrey Epstein's 2003 fiftieth-birthday book, released by House Democrats in September 2025, which John Kiriakou read out in full and assessed as a banker who had studied handwriting and as an artist — concluding that whoever signed it probably drew it, and refusing to call it a hoax.

e-jean-carroll.title: The Bloomingdale precedent
e-jean-carroll.summary: The scandal from Ronald Reagan's kitchen cabinet that John Kiriakou holds up as the model Donald Trump should have followed over Jeffrey Epstein — when Reagan's advisers nearly denied the friendship, were talked out of it because the denial would become the story, and issued a statement embracing it instead.

e-jean-carroll.title: Astrology at the CIA
e-jean-carroll.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that astrology played a role in CIA work in the 1950s and early 1960s as part of MK-ULTRA, alongside time travel and teleportation — and his explanation for why: officials with unlimited budgets and no obligation to report to the public reasoned that there was probably nothing to it, but that if there were, it would make them a star.

e-jean-carroll.title: Carrying passports in Washington
e-jean-carroll.summary: John Kiriakou's report in September 2025 that people in Washington had begun carrying their passports for fear of being scooped up by immigration enforcement — alongside the case of an American symphony violinist held for three weeks, and his own belief that ethnic profiling violates the Fourth Amendment.

e-jean-carroll.title: "Christians are suckers"
e-jean-carroll.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for how a president who does not go to church, has no spiritual adviser and could not name a line of scripture can push school prayer without cost — that he thinks most Christians are suckers, an assessment Kiriakou says he hates to make and believes anyway.

e-jean-carroll.title: Find a Grave
e-jean-carroll.summary: The cemetery database John Kiriakou calls literally his favourite website on the internet, which he opens during the ten-minute countdown before broadcasts and uses to decide who goes into his cemetery books — and which supplied him the story of Greta Zimmer Friedman.

eastern-district-of-virginia.title: The 2020 extradition hearing
eastern-district-of-virginia.summary: The London hearing on the United States' request to extradite Julian Assange, described by John Kiriakou two days into it — a proceeding scheduled to run to July with a month-long recess inserted at the American prosecutors' request, held in a courtroom whose microphones did not work, with Assange behind a plastic screen and unable to hear his own case. Kiriakou called it more of a circus sideshow than a legal hearing, and warned that even a defence victory would leave Assange expelled to Australia and open to a fresh American request.

eastern-district-of-virginia.title: The Knight Ridder panel
eastern-district-of-virginia.summary: At an April 2022 Assange benefit in Washington, John Kiriakou described a Zoom panel on which two former Knight Ridder reporters spoke for ninety minutes without once mentioning Julian Assange, and one of them, asked why, said he saw Assange as an activist rather than a journalist.

eastern-district-of-virginia.title: The Toronto transit detention
eastern-district-of-virginia.summary: John Kiriakou's account of being seized at the aircraft door in Toronto by two Royal Canadian Mounted Police officers, told 'you are not welcome in Canada,' and walked by both arms through the airport onto his connecting flight — while transiting home from a trip on which the Greek government had hired him to help write a whistleblower protection law.

eastern-district-of-virginia.title: The business-card espionage charges
eastern-district-of-virginia.summary: Two of the three Espionage Act counts brought against John Kiriakou rested on his having passed a former CIA colleague's business card to two reporters — a man who had left the agency and had never been undercover — and were dropped after an exchange in open court in which the prosecutor's only answer to the judge was that Kiriakou should have been more careful.

eastern-district-of-virginia.title: The New York Times problem
eastern-district-of-virginia.summary: Barack Obama''s reason, as John Kiriakou reports it, for never charging Julian Assange: the Washington Post, the New York Times, the Wall Street Journal and the Associated Press publish classified information every single day, so a publisher charged with espionage cannot be the only one. Kiriakou treats it as the central First Amendment question of the case, and notes that Joe Biden — who was in the room for the original argument — doubled down instead of dropping the charges.

eastern-district-of-virginia.title: The plea-hearing objection
eastern-district-of-virginia.summary: John Kiriakou's account of standing up at his own plea hearing, over his lawyer's objection, to tell the judge that the statement of facts the prosecutors had written into his plea agreement was untrue — and of her reply that it was just window dressing.

eastern-mediterranean-gas.title: The Imia crisis
eastern-mediterranean-gas.summary: The 1996 confrontation between Greece and Turkey over an uninhabited Aegean islet, which John Kiriakou cites as the last time the two came close to exchanging fire — a flag raised, a flag taken down, warships dispatched, and Bill Clinton telephoning both capitals to tell them to stop.

eastern-mediterranean-gas.title: The Arab states and the Gaza war
eastern-mediterranean-gas.summary: John Kiriakou's country-by-country reading of how the Arab governments positioned themselves after October 2023 — the Gulf states ranked by their fear of Iran, Jordan caught between its border and its population, Egypt sealing Rafah to prevent a repeat of earlier refugee flows — and his conclusion that every one of them is calculating damage to itself first and the Palestinians second.

eastern-mediterranean-gas.title: Afghan heroin policy
eastern-mediterranean-gas.summary: The post-2001 U.S. policy in Afghanistan of protecting, and per John Kiriakou actively encouraging, the cultivation of heroin poppy. Under the Taliban in 2000 Afghanistan produced 0% of the world's heroin; by 2009 under American occupation it produced 93%. Per a DEA officer Kiriakou consulted with on the policy paper he was preparing for Senator Kerry, the strategic rationale was that nearly all of the heroin flowed to Iran and Russia, addiction in those countries was considered desirable as a long-run societal weakener, and the same logic now operates in reverse with Chinese fentanyl flowing into the United States.

eastern-mediterranean-gas.title: China as mediator
eastern-mediterranean-gas.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the plausible mediator of Middle Eastern and Ukrainian conflicts, grounded in his claim that — Tibet and its border wars aside — China has no history of invading other countries, and his observation of how quickly Beijing accepted an offhand suggestion that it might mediate between Israel and Iran.

eastern-mediterranean-gas.title: China as economic threat
eastern-mediterranean-gas.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

eastern-mediterranean-gas.title: The Damascus consulate strike
eastern-mediterranean-gas.summary: The April 2024 Israeli attack on Iran's consulate in Damascus, which John Kiriakou describes as an unambiguous violation of the Vienna Convention, and whose official Israeli explanation — that it had not occurred to anyone the world would read it as a provocation — he calls disingenuous and intended purely for domestic audiences.

eastern-state-penitentiary.title: Daniel Duggan
eastern-state-penitentiary.summary: The former US Marine pilot and naturalised Australian citizen held in Australian custody for three years, uncharged in Australia, while the United States sought his extradition over flight training given in China years earlier. John Kiriakou submitted an affidavit in the case on the effects of solitary confinement, has spoken to both his Australian and American legal teams, and argues the selective prosecution "just stinks of politics" — and that extradition would end the case: "if he is extradited to the US, he''s lost."

eastern-state-penitentiary.title: The solitary confinement precedents
eastern-state-penitentiary.summary: The legal argument John Kiriakou made repeatedly between 2020 and 2022 in defence of Julian Assange, and revived in 2025 for the Australian pilot Daniel Duggan — that no extradition to the United States can succeed once a court is asked to find that American solitary confinement is not torture, a proposition already contradicted by the United Nations, by the United States' own federal torture statute, and by a line of British and European rulings blocking extraditions on exactly that ground.

eastern-state-penitentiary.title: Communications management unit
eastern-state-penitentiary.summary: The two restricted-contact units inside the American federal prison system, at Terre Haute and Marion; built for "the worst of the worst" but, in John Kiriakou's account, used to silence prisoners whose messages are inconvenient — and a practice he groups with solitary confinement as torture. He served part of his own sentence in a modified one.

eastern-state-penitentiary.title: Solitary confinement
eastern-state-penitentiary.summary: The prison isolation practice the United Nations calls a form of torture; John Kiriakou, drawing on his own ten days in a six-by-sixteen-foot cell, argues that jailing depressed prisoners like Daniel Hale in solitary 'for their own safety' is precisely what drives them to suicide.

eastern-state-penitentiary.title: Julian Assange
eastern-state-penitentiary.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

eastern-state-penitentiary.title: The fifteen-minute call
eastern-state-penitentiary.summary: How Marty Gottesfeld, held in the communications management unit at Terre Haute, allocated the single fifteen-minute telephone call he was permitted each week: an email to his wife, his two attorneys and John Kiriakou, with the call going to whoever answered first.

economic-roots-of-terrorism.title: Abolish the CIA
economic-roots-of-terrorism.summary: John Kiriakou's position that the CIA should be abolished because its functions are already duplicated by the other 17 U.S. intelligence agencies — analysis by the State Department, human spying by the Pentagon, technology by DARPA, NSA and the private sector.

economic-roots-of-terrorism.title: Syrian sanctions relief
economic-roots-of-terrorism.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that lifting sanctions on Syria was the most effective counter-terrorism measure available — because the recruits he interrogated joined for money, and an economy that offers roads, a working port and wages removes the recruiting pool rather than the recruiters.

economic-roots-of-terrorism.title: Donald Trump
economic-roots-of-terrorism.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

economic-roots-of-terrorism.title: Amnesty International
economic-roots-of-terrorism.summary: The human rights organization whose torture report forms part of John Kiriakou's core defense — the CIA's crimes were already public knowledge before he confirmed them on ABC, and the Justice Department's own declination letter said so — and the organization whose silence during his prosecution he cannot forgive. He begged Amnesty for a one-sentence statement and got a New Yorker subscription instead; it took Ai Weiwei to change their minds, and by then he was walking out of prison.

economic-roots-of-terrorism.title: The French human sources
economic-roots-of-terrorism.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation of what Chris Hedges was told by French intelligence after 9/11 — that the CIA had no human assets inside al-Qaeda at all, while the French thwarted attacks by having recruited people next to the plotters — and the general principle he draws from it: that no amount of money spent on electronics substitutes for a human source.

economic-roots-of-terrorism.title: "Take our word for it"
economic-roots-of-terrorism.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the standing justification given after American strikes kill civilians — that there was a terrorist present, and that the public would agree if it could see the intelligence — set against his statement that he saw that intelligence and it was fabricated, and applied to the 2021 Kabul strike that killed seven children.

ecuador-is-open-for-business.title: Assange and solitary confinement
ecuador-is-open-for-business.summary: John Kiriakou's 2018 argument that Julian Assange's isolation inside the Ecuadorian embassy amounted to solitary confinement — a practice the United Nations classes as torture — and that everybody breaks under it eventually, however strong they are.

ecuador-is-open-for-business.title: Seventy-two denied motions
ecuador-is-open-for-business.summary: The count John Kiriakou gives of the pretrial motions filed in his case and denied by Judge Leonie Brinkema — seventy-two denied and none granted — which he offers as the mechanism by which a national security defendant in the Eastern District of Virginia is prevented from mounting a defence at all.

ecuador-is-open-for-business.title: The Guardian smear series
ecuador-is-open-for-business.summary: The run of articles about Julian Assange that John Kiriakou characterised in 2018 as a pile-on based on anonymous sources leaking intelligence-agency material, and which he read as a formal psychological operation intended to weaken Assange rather than as journalism.

ecuador-is-open-for-business.title: The chain of command argument
ecuador-is-open-for-business.summary: John Kiriakou's standing rejection of the advice given to new intelligence officers — that evidence of waste, fraud, abuse or illegality should be taken up the chain of command — supported by the fates of Thomas Drake, William Binney, Kirk Wiebe and Diane Roark, and by the fact that his own chain of command had created the torture programme.

ecuador-is-open-for-business.title: "Embrace it and keep telling it"
ecuador-is-open-for-business.summary: The advice John Kiriakou says he was given days after his arrest — that he could not hide from the prosecution but had to embrace it, and had to keep telling his side of the story until it became the side of record, because the government would eventually move on to its next target.

ecuador-is-open-for-business.title: Julian Assange
ecuador-is-open-for-business.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

ed-martin.title: The writ of coram nobis
ed-martin.summary: The second route out of his conviction that John Kiriakou describes, besides a pardon: a writ of coram nobis, under which the Justice Department would go to the Eastern District of Virginia and state that it made a mistake in prosecuting him, admits the mistake, and asks that the conviction be overturned. He calls them exceedingly rare, citing one around 2001 and one in 1986.

ed-martin.title: The Crenshaw text messages
ed-martin.summary: John Kiriakou's account of taking his girlfriend's phone at midnight, finding a message from Dan Crenshaw asking what she was wearing, and texting back that he was her boyfriend and Crenshaw should ask his own wife — who had a ten-month-old baby at the time. Kiriakou says the woman showed him other messages that were filthy, and that she had saved them in case she needed to use them.

ed-martin.title: The January 6 pipe bomber report
ed-martin.summary: The story John Kiriakou says he posted to Facebook and nobody else picked up: a report that the FBI had identified the person who placed pipe bombs outside the RNC and DNC as a former Capitol Police officer who had been on rotation to the CIA doing physical security, recognised from a limp caused by a college sports injury, at a stated confidence of 94 per cent. She had not been charged, and Kiriakou lists the questions it would raise if true.

ed-martin.title: The Red Fort bombing
ed-martin.summary: John Kiriakou''s on-air attribution of a car bombing outside the Red Fort in New Delhi to Kashmiri separatist groups — offered with the acknowledgement that saying so brings him death threats from Pakistanis, and with a flat definition: groups that murder civilians for political purposes are terrorist groups, whatever their political point may be.

ed-martin.title: Zaluzhny and the Nordstream prosecution
