ed-martin.summary: John Kiriakou''s reaction to German investigators drawing a bead on the former commander-in-chief of the Ukrainian armed forces over the Nordstream sabotage: that the CIA and the Pentagon now wish the case would go away, that the truth is not supposed to come out in such an operation, that Seymour Hersh probably had the kernel but not the details, and that it was very likely a joint operation. He expects somebody to go to prison.

ed-martin.title: Three Republican congressmen
ed-martin.summary: John Kiriakou''s arithmetic for why the shutdown fight was not over when the Senate cut its deal: the Senate produced its own agreement rather than voting on the House bill, so the House has to be recalled to vote on the Senate version. Republicans needed seven Democratic senators; the House needs only three Republican congressmen to kill it — which is why he thought attention should shift to the House.

ed-schultz.title: The 2022 deplatforming
ed-schultz.summary: The removal of John Kiriakou's radio programme from every major podcast platform after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, on the basis of his work for Sputnik News — preceded, he says, by a Washington Post article and a CSIS paper arguing that his weekly segment on American prison conditions was Russian propaganda weakening American democracy.

ed-schultz.title: Kiriakou's Russian media work
ed-schultz.summary: John Kiriakou's account of hosting a daily Sputnik radio show for seven and a half years with full contractual freedom to criticize anyone, including Putin — which he did on the morning of the Ukraine invasion — offered as a rebuttal to claims that Russian outlets are mere propaganda.

ed-schultz.title: The state-affiliated media labels
ed-schultz.summary: The warning tags applied by social media platforms from 2020 identifying accounts as mouthpieces of foreign governments, which John Kiriakou describes checking his own account for daily. His standing example of how indiscriminate the practice became is the labelling of Ed Schultz, who had been dead for years.

ed-schultz.title: Press TV website seizure
ed-schultz.summary: The FBI's confiscation of the Press TV domain, which John Kiriakou cites alongside the banning of TeleSUR, RT and Sputnik as the point at which American censorship stopped being algorithmic and became straightforwardly physical.

ed-schultz.title: Panquake
ed-schultz.summary: Open-source, blockchain-based social platform developed by the Iceland-registered company Talk Liberation, for which John Kiriakou has served as brand ambassador since 2020. Kiriakou describes it as advertising-free, subscription-funded, free of back doors, and run on servers powered by Icelandic geothermal steam — a project he frames as a David-and-Goliath fight against banks, big technology and governments.

ed-schultz.title: Bahrain Posting (1994–1996)
ed-schultz.summary: John Kiriakou's 1994–1996 assignment to Bahrain under U.S. State Department cover as second secretary for economic affairs — arriving with his wife Joanne and infant son Chris on August 1, 1994, into a tiny Gulf monarchy whose sectarian tensions erupted, two months later, into the first Intifada.

edward-snowden.title: Kiriakou Introduction to WikiLeaks
edward-snowden.summary: Kiriakou first heard of WikiLeaks as a warning inside the secret spaces it existed to expose: ''Don''t touch that. Don''t go near that.''

edward-snowden.title: "I''m a non-person"
edward-snowden.summary: The phrase John Kiriakou uses for his standing after prison: a former colleague was sent to deliver congratulations from a mutual friend who had risen to a senior administration post, together with the message that he could never speak to Kiriakou again. Kiriakou pairs it with the loss of his federal pension after nineteen and a half years of service, and with the fact that in eight years no other CIA officer joined him in speaking publicly.

edward-snowden.title: The night the Snowden story broke
edward-snowden.summary: How John Kiriakou learned about Edward Snowden. Three months into his sentence at FCI Loretto, a cellmate who could not sleep was listening to Coast to Coast AM in the middle of the night and woke him. Kiriakou turned on his own radio and followed the story through the distant stations that reach central Pennsylvania after dark.

edward-snowden.title: Thin Thread
edward-snowden.summary: Competing NSA programs at the center of the post-9/11 mass-surveillance turn. Per John Kiriakou, on September 11, 2001 NSA Director Michael Hayden implemented Operation Thin Thread — which 'vacuums up every phone call, every text message, every email, every bit of metadata from every American' — and reportedly called 9/11 'the greatest possible gift to NSA.' Three NSA officers (Bill Binney, Kirk Wiebe, and Ed Loomis) had built a competing program, Stellar Wind, that could collect the same data while protecting Americans' identities; Hayden chose to grab everything instead. Kiriakou says it was Tom Drake's effort to report the illegality that destroyed Drake.

edward-snowden.title: Assange plea deal
edward-snowden.summary: The 2024 agreement under which Julian Assange pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit espionage, was processed in Saipan, and returned to Australia; John Kiriakou details its odd terms — a Chelsea Manning purge affidavit and a 25-year green-card ban — and the debate over whether it sets a precedent.

edward-snowden.title: Barry Pollock
edward-snowden.summary: Washington defense attorney who represented Julian Assange; John Kiriakou credits Pollock with negotiating the deal that let Assange be processed in Saipan — the U.S. district closest to Australia — rather than be brought to Virginia.

elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.title: Abbas and the three-state problem
elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that no two-state solution is available — because there is already one state, because Mahmoud Abbas is nineteen years into a four-year term and has become a billionaire, and because East Bank, West Bank and Gaza Palestinians are so disconnected that the real arithmetic is three states, which nobody will discuss.

elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.title: Bulldozing the olive orchards
elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.summary: The sequence John Kiriakou describes preceding Israeli seizures of Palestinian land in the West Bank — olive orchards bulldozed and crops burned to make leaving easier, then the house demolished and a prefabricated one built for a settler family — and the different practice he says applies in East Jerusalem.

elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.title: New Castle, Pennsylvania
elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.summary: John Kiriakou's home town, an hour north of Pittsburgh on the edge of Amish country — a rust-belt city of roughly 40,000 to 50,000 people when he was growing up and around 18,000 to 20,000 now, whose decline he measures by the arrival of DEA and ATF field offices. It is also where, aged eight or nine and hunting salamanders in Oak Park Cemetery, he found the grave of a Medal of Honor private and acquired the lifelong interest in cemeteries that became a book.

elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.title: From sixteen employees to twenty thousand
elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.summary: John Kiriakou's support for cutting the staff of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, on the ground that a body created after 9/11 with sixteen employees to coordinate the agencies had grown to twenty thousand.

elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.title: The Las Vegas case
elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.summary: John Kiriakou's scepticism about the Justice Department's claim that it played no role in a Las Vegas child-exploitation case involving an Israeli suspect who left the country — on the ground that electronic images and electronic communications would have made the matter federal.

elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.title: The twenty-thousand-dollar tweet
elbridge-gerry-and-the-salamander.summary: John Kiriakou's account of asking Jeanine Pirro for help with a pardon and being quoted $20,000 by her assistant — for a tweet. He refused, and says he was never invited back on her programme.

eli-cohen.title: Jeffrey Epstein
eli-cohen.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

eli-cohen.title: MOSSAD
eli-cohen.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

eli-cohen.title: Sacha Baron Cohen
eli-cohen.summary: British comedian and actor; per John Kiriakou, "a comedic genius" who hired Kiriakou as a Middle East script advisor for the film Bruno, and whose attempt to film in Jordan without notifying the Jordanian Intelligence Service resulted in King Abdullah II personally greeting him at the Royal Palace.

eli-cohen.title: John Kiriakou
eli-cohen.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

eli-cohen.title: Prince Andrew
eli-cohen.summary: British royal, now Andrew Mountbatten Windsor, named repeatedly by John Kiriakou as one of the un-recruitable principals whose access made Jeffrey Epstein valuable to a foreign intelligence service. Kiriakou has asked why Andrew was never charged over conduct with minors, reads his alleged provision of classified Ministry of Defence documents to Epstein as evidence of espionage rather than vanity — and expects him to face no criminal consequence at all, because the statute of limitations has run.

eli-cohen.title: One-Time Pad
eli-cohen.summary: Cipher system in which a secret, random key — shared between sender and receiver — is used to encode a message and then destroyed so that it can never be used again. In traditional shortwave-radio tradecraft, one-time pads enabled spies to broadcast number sequences over public airwaves that only the intended recipient, holding the matching page, could decode. Per John Kiriakou, his lifelong interest in intelligence began at age nine after he picked up KGB number transmissions on a 50-cent shortwave radio.

elliott-abrams.title: The Baltimore tunnel
elliott-abrams.summary: The rail tunnel built in 1850 just north of Baltimore that John Kiriakou names as the physical reason the American northeast has no high-speed rail — it is too narrow to admit a high-speed train, so every train on the corridor must be built to fit through it.

elliott-abrams.title: The Capitol Hill cocaine ring
elliott-abrams.summary: The 1983 congressional drug scandal John Kiriakou stumbled into at eighteen, when an FBI agent called at his father's house and then asked him whether he had ever seen his congressman trade stamps for cocaine — a question he answered no to, and which turned out to be exactly what the congressman was doing.

elliott-abrams.title: The cocaine in the West Wing
elliott-abrams.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of how a bag of cocaine came to be found in a White House cubby in July 2023 — the phone cubbies outside every vaulted area, the fingerprints that every cleared visitor has already surrendered, and his prediction that despite an investigation requiring only a couple of hours of work, the public would never be told whose it was.

elliott-abrams.title: The nuclear testing legacy
elliott-abrams.summary: John Kiriakou's observation that the United States waited seventy years after the Second World War before offering money and relocation to the South Pacific communities contaminated by its own atmospheric nuclear tests — a delay he called ridiculous, and a measure of how casually the era's tens of thousands of test detonations were treated.

elliott-abrams.title: Rival factions in Libya
elliott-abrams.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the CIA and the State Department backing opposing factions inside Libya — proxies funded by two arms of the same government that end up fighting each other, an arrangement he calls insane and treats as characteristic of American intervention in places nobody is reporting on.

elliott-abrams.title: The Afghan woman's lesson
elliott-abrams.summary: The remark a visiting Afghan intellectual made to the Senate Foreign Relations Committee staff that John Kiriakou says stuck with him for over a decade — that the Taliban did not come down from outer space, that they are Afghanistan's own sons and brothers and husbands, and that if the country had not been secured after ten years of nation-building it was because nobody wanted the Americans there.

elon-musk-2009-meeting.title: Abraxas Corporation
elon-musk-2009-meeting.summary: The private intelligence company founded in the 1990s by retired CIA operations officers as a tax pass-through and a place to smoke cigars and tell stories — which, after 9/11, made its founders, in John Kiriakou's phrase, Mega Millions rich.

elon-musk-2009-meeting.title: The Directorate of Science and Technology
elon-musk-2009-meeting.summary: One of the CIA's four directorates, which in John Kiriakou's time was an afterthought responsible for disguises and briefcases with hidden compartments, and which he says now works with Palantir, Amazon, Nvidia and Elon Musk's companies on work closer to DARPA's than to anything the agency did in the past.

elon-musk-2009-meeting.title: Central Intelligence Agency
elon-musk-2009-meeting.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

elon-musk-2009-meeting.title: Concealment devices
elon-musk-2009-meeting.summary: Hollowed everyday objects — known inside the CIA as CDs — issued to officers to hide documents, equipment and, in the larger sizes, a gun. Per John Kiriakou every CIA officer has access to them, some are simply assigned with no instructions attached, and the way they are found in real life is the way they are found in *The Good Shepherd* — by an anomaly a hand can feel.

elon-musk-2009-meeting.title: Abu Zubaydah
elon-musk-2009-meeting.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

elon-musk-2009-meeting.title: The Brüno shoot in Jordan
elon-musk-2009-meeting.summary: The scene John Kiriakou set up for Sacha Baron Cohen in Amman — four retired Palestinian militants, found in the Damascus telephone book at the Library of Congress, shown hardcore pornography by a character they believed to be an Austrian documentary journalist — which produced no reaction at all and was cut from the film entirely.

elon-musk.title: Donald Trump
elon-musk.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

elon-musk.title: Julian Assange
elon-musk.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

elon-musk.title: Sociopathic Tendencies
elon-musk.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the CIA actively recruits for what its instructors call 'sociopathic tendencies' — not full clinical sociopathy, but the capacity to operate in legal, moral, and ethical gray areas without being paralyzed by regret. Kiriakou describes this as the trait that makes case officers effective at recruitment and adaptable in the field, and offers his own act of whistleblowing as evidence he does not possess the deeper sociopathy that, in his view, characterizes the most institutionally successful intelligence officers.

elon-musk.title: Panquake
elon-musk.summary: Open-source, blockchain-based social platform developed by the Iceland-registered company Talk Liberation, for which John Kiriakou has served as brand ambassador since 2020. Kiriakou describes it as advertising-free, subscription-funded, free of back doors, and run on servers powered by Icelandic geothermal steam — a project he frames as a David-and-Goliath fight against banks, big technology and governments.

elon-musk.title: The arrest of Yves Engler
elon-musk.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the arrest of the Canadian activist Yves Engler in Montreal on a hate-speech charge after he criticised a prominent Canadian Zionist — five days in jail, additional harassment charges filed after he telephoned the arresting officer to request his own police reports, and suspension from Twitter and Facebook.

elon-musk.title: Youngstown Sheet and Tube
elon-musk.summary: The Ohio steel producer whose closure John Kiriakou treats as the moment the economy of his hometown region ended; he remembers the day it shut and classmates weeping in the school hallways because their fathers had lost their jobs, and dates the collapse of New Castle, Pennsylvania to it.

embassy-fortification-after-9-11.title: Iranian intelligence capability
embassy-fortification-after-9-11.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of Iranian intelligence as poor and always having been poor, on the ground that Iranian officers do not receive good training and are essentially on their own, with only marginal help from the Russians and the Chinese.

embassy-fortification-after-9-11.title: Bowe Bergdahl
embassy-fortification-after-9-11.summary: The American soldier who walked off his base in Afghanistan, was captured by the Haqqani network and handed to the Taliban, and was repatriated in a prisoner trade — a man John Kiriakou says was treated as a traitor although he was not one.

embassy-fortification-after-9-11.title: Iranian strikes on Gulf hotels
embassy-fortification-after-9-11.summary: John Kiriakou''s reading of the Iranian drone and missile attacks on hotels in Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Muscat during the 2026 war: not targeted killings, but deliberate strikes at the tourist economies of the Gulf states, aimed at hotels famous enough to empty the country of visitors.

embassy-fortification-after-9-11.title: A Middle East reading list
embassy-fortification-after-9-11.summary: The books and the starting point John Kiriakou recommends to anyone trying to understand the modern Middle East: begin at the end of the Second World War, not five thousand years earlier, and start with The House of Saud, the Sykes-Picot Agreement and From Beirut to Jerusalem.

embassy-fortification-after-9-11.title: Bombing the Omanis
embassy-fortification-after-9-11.summary: John Kiriakou's judgement that Iran's strikes on the Gulf states — and above all on Oman, which had been trying to broker peace — made enemies Iran did not need to make, of governments that would otherwise have sat the war out.

embassy-fortification-after-9-11.title: Chaos as the Israeli objective
embassy-fortification-after-9-11.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to whether Netanyahu''s government actually wanted an American invasion of Iran: what the Israelis want in Iran is what they got in Libya — chaos, civil war, and as many dead Iranians as possible.

embassy-movie-night.title: Lindsey Graham
embassy-movie-night.summary: Republican senator from South Carolina who died in July 2026, and John Kiriakou's standing shorthand for the permanent war caucus — a "show horse" rather than a workhorse, a "chameleon" who "never saw a war that he didn't want to jump into with both feet," and, on posthumously released documentary footage, a man offering the US Air Force to bomb a country America was not at war with.

embassy-movie-night.title: 2026 Iran war
embassy-movie-night.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

embassy-movie-night.title: The Italian schoolchildren
embassy-movie-night.summary: An encounter John Kiriakou described in July 2026 as a measure of how far his late-career fame had spread: walking down Fifth Avenue in New York, a bus pulled up, a boy of about thirteen shouted his name in Italian, and sixty-five Italian middle schoolers ran off the bus. The selfies took half an hour.

embassy-movie-night.title: The McConnell obituary
embassy-movie-night.summary: A Kentucky newspaper's decision, reported by John Kiriakou in July 2026, to run an obituary of the living Senator Mitch McConnell on purpose — a response, in Kiriakou's reading, to the rapid rehabilitation of Lindsey Graham after his death, and an attempt to get the assessment on the record before the whitewashing could begin.

embassy-movie-night.title: The DNC in debt
embassy-movie-night.summary: John Kiriakou''s July 2026 summary of the Democratic National Committee''s finances, drawn from New York Times reporting: two million dollars in debt against Republican reserves of $130 million, vendors asked to hold their invoices until after the elections, the party headquarters pledged as loan collateral, and a chairman who threw his phone at a junior aide.

embassy-movie-night.title: The stapler in the Dirksen building
embassy-movie-night.summary: An incident John Kiriakou witnessed while serving as a senior staff member on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee: a Democratic senator threw a stapler at a staff member in a hallway of the Dirksen Senate Office Building, swore at him, and then looked around to see who had seen it.

embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.title: The underlying sadness
embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.summary: The change several people have independently reported to John Kiriakou about himself since his prosecution — an underlying sadness that was not there before — which he says he does not see in himself, considering himself a happy and well-adjusted person.

embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.title: Whistleblowers and suicide
embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.summary: John Kiriakou's claim, drawn from conversations with some fifty whistleblowers, that every one of them considered suicide in the early stage of their case — and his own account of the family vigil that kept him from the garage.

embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.title: Assange and solitary confinement
embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.summary: John Kiriakou's 2018 argument that Julian Assange's isolation inside the Ecuadorian embassy amounted to solitary confinement — a practice the United Nations classes as torture — and that everybody breaks under it eventually, however strong they are.

embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.title: Seventy-two denied motions
embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.summary: The count John Kiriakou gives of the pretrial motions filed in his case and denied by Judge Leonie Brinkema — seventy-two denied and none granted — which he offers as the mechanism by which a national security defendant in the Eastern District of Virginia is prevented from mounting a defence at all.

embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.title: The chain of command argument
embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.summary: John Kiriakou's standing rejection of the advice given to new intelligence officers — that evidence of waste, fraud, abuse or illegality should be taken up the chain of command — supported by the fates of Thomas Drake, William Binney, Kirk Wiebe and Diane Roark, and by the fact that his own chain of command had created the torture programme.

embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.title: Consulting for royal families
embrace-it-and-keep-telling-it.summary: The work John Kiriakou says he was hired to do by members of two different royal families following the 2026 virality of his interviews — advising on ethics in their own intelligence operations — which he offers as evidence of how far the reversal in his standing had gone.

encryption-backdoor-demands.title: NSA Surveillance
encryption-backdoor-demands.summary: ''It is part of NSA''s founding charter that it is not allowed to spy on Americans'' — Kiriakou on warrantless collection and the Bluffdale warehouse.

encryption-backdoor-demands.title: John Ratcliffe
encryption-backdoor-demands.summary: CIA director under Trump's second term; per John Kiriakou, a "bombthrower" he mostly disagrees with politically but supported as a needed disruptor for the agency — "a good guy, expert in what he does," though "not a visionary thinker" and, on Kiriakou's later assessment, a neocon who has outmanoeuvred Tulsi Gabbard for primacy over U.S. intelligence. Ratcliffe told the White House the CIA had no objection to pardoning Kiriakou.

encryption-backdoor-demands.title: Purchased data as a warrant workaround
encryption-backdoor-demands.summary: John Kiriakou's account of U.S. federal agencies buying Americans' personal data from social-media platforms and data brokers rather than seeking a warrant — a practice he describes as an ethical and legal problem likely to reach the Supreme Court, and one in which no judge is aware a case is being built.

encryption-backdoor-demands.title: Panquake
encryption-backdoor-demands.summary: Open-source, blockchain-based social platform developed by the Iceland-registered company Talk Liberation, for which John Kiriakou has served as brand ambassador since 2020. Kiriakou describes it as advertising-free, subscription-funded, free of back doors, and run on servers powered by Icelandic geothermal steam — a project he frames as a David-and-Goliath fight against banks, big technology and governments.

encryption-backdoor-demands.title: Donald Trump
encryption-backdoor-demands.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

encryption-backdoor-demands.title: The arrest of Yves Engler
encryption-backdoor-demands.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the arrest of the Canadian activist Yves Engler in Montreal on a hate-speech charge after he criticised a prominent Canadian Zionist — five days in jail, additional harassment charges filed after he telephoned the arresting officer to request his own police reports, and suspension from Twitter and Facebook.

encryption-before-the-key.title: The Libertarian Party
encryption-before-the-key.summary: The third party a lifelong Democrat joined on release from prison, after its 2016 presidential nominee had written to him in his cell and to the Attorney General on his behalf — the party John Kiriakou says was the only one talking about whistleblowing and the security-versus-liberty trade-off, and the one whose structural problem, he was told, is that it has no benefactor.

encryption-before-the-key.title: Securedrop
encryption-before-the-key.summary: The encrypted submission tool pioneered by WikiLeaks to let sources hand over documents without exposing themselves.

encryption-before-the-key.title: James Comey
encryption-before-the-key.summary: Former FBI director indicted under the second Trump administration, whose prosecution John Kiriakou reads as a search for charges to fit a man rather than evidence of a crime — and which he expects to collapse, unlike the parallel case against John Brennan.

encryption-before-the-key.title: Espionage Act
encryption-before-the-key.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

encryption-before-the-key.title: Arianna Huffington
encryption-before-the-key.summary: Founder of the Huffington Post and the accidental amplifier who turned John Kiriakou's prison writing into a phenomenon. His first Letter from Loretto went to his attorney, then to a friend running Firedoglake who — unknown to Kiriakou — was close to Huffington; she plastered it as a banner headline and it drew over a million hits, bringing CNN and 60 Minutes to the prison gates. She published his open letter to Snowden, ran the diesel-therapy exposé that triggered the "hands off John Kiriakou" campaign, and came to Loretto herself with two young journalists.

encryption-before-the-key.title: Crypto AG
encryption-before-the-key.summary: The Swiss encryption-machine company revealed in February 2020 to have been secretly owned by the CIA and West German intelligence, which sold riggable ciphers to governments around the world for decades. John Kiriakou, who held senior positions at the agency, says he knew nothing about it — it was held that closely — and refuses to describe it as a scandal: nobody will be prosecuted, several people will probably win medals, and an intelligence operation is not supposed to be honest or fair.

enhanced-interrogation.title: Central American Task Force
enhanced-interrogation.summary: CIA unit that led the agency's early-to-mid-1980s effort to overthrow the Sandinista government and support the Contras in Nicaragua. John Kiriakou describes serving as assistant to the unit's head as one of his first, and most controversial, CIA jobs; he denies the accusation that the CIA trained Contra and Salvadoran insurgents to garrote nuns, saying the agency instead worked to stop such atrocities, while acknowledging it was associated with people who did terrible things.

enhanced-interrogation.title: FBI apologies to Kiriakou
enhanced-interrogation.summary: John Kiriakou says three FBI agents who worked on his prosecution have written to apologize since his conviction — one saying the case was 'directed and driven by seniormost officials' while mid- and street-level personnel objected, but 'we just followed orders.'

enhanced-interrogation.title: Five and a half years on the table
enhanced-interrogation.summary: John Kiriakou''s stated regret about his own whistleblowing — not that he did it, but that he waited: he learned of the torture programme in May 2002, it began on 2 August 2002, and he said nothing until 11 December 2007.

enhanced-interrogation.title: Haroon Yenor trial
enhanced-interrogation.summary: Federal terrorism prosecution in which John Kiriakou testified as a defense expert witness; Yenor, arrested in November 2024 on charges tied to an alleged plot to bomb the New York Stock Exchange and a synagogue, was acquitted on all six charges on June 30; Kiriakou's expert testimony argued the FBI supplied the idea, the bomb, the explosives, the timer, the detonation cord, and the getaway car.

enhanced-interrogation.title: Jane Harman
enhanced-interrogation.summary: Former U.S. Representative from California who served as ranking member and later chair of the House Intelligence Committee. Per John Kiriakou, Harman was present in the room when congressional leadership was briefed on the CIA's enhanced interrogation program; when reporters later asked her about the program, she denied knowing about it. Kiriakou told the New York Times she had been in the room, after which Harman revised her account to say she had left early and that an aide remained as a notetaker.

enhanced-interrogation.title: The 2026 KSM confession ruling
enhanced-interrogation.summary: The Guantanamo military commission ruling, issued by Lieutenant Colonel Michael Shramma in late August 2026 and reported by John Kiriakou as breaking news on September 1, that threw out Khalid Sheikh Mohammed's confession as inadmissible because the CIA had waterboarded him 183 times, and further threw out his 2007 non-torture Guantanamo interrogations because FBI agents *"intentionally failed to explicitly tell KSM that he had a right to remain silent, that he had a right to consult an attorney, and that what he told them could be used against him at trial."* Kiriakou reads it as the moment the American torture programme made the trial of the man who murdered three thousand Americans impossible.

epstein-and-more-than-one-service.title: Jeffrey Epstein
epstein-and-more-than-one-service.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

epstein-and-more-than-one-service.title: The Israelis are free agents
epstein-and-more-than-one-service.summary: John Kiriakou's formulation of Israel as an intelligence partner whose cooperation is conditional rather than allied — friendly when it suits, and equally willing to deal with Russia, China or Germany — offered as the reason an Israeli-run source could end up passing American information to a service hostile to the United States, and given each time with an acknowledgement that saying it brings him threats.

epstein-and-more-than-one-service.title: Access Agent
epstein-and-more-than-one-service.summary: CIA (and foreign intelligence service) term for a recruited asset whose value lies not in the secrets they hold directly but in their regular social access to high-value targets — politicians, executives, heads of state — who cannot themselves be recruited. Per John Kiriakou, the access agent is funded generously to maintain an environment in which the targets feel comfortable and return repeatedly; kompromat — compromising photographs or recordings — may be collected as a secondary tool. Kiriakou identifies Jeffrey Epstein as a textbook access agent, in his assessment working for Israeli intelligence.

epstein-and-more-than-one-service.title: MOSSAD
epstein-and-more-than-one-service.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

epstein-and-more-than-one-service.title: Why he believes Epstein killed himself
epstein-and-more-than-one-service.summary: John Kiriakou's stated conclusion that Jeffrey Epstein died by suicide, reasoned from his own experience of how federal prison guards actually work rather than from any view of the wider Epstein case.

epstein-and-more-than-one-service.title: Why Maxwell took the Fifth
epstein-and-more-than-one-service.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of Ghislaine Maxwell's silence before Congress — not that she was protecting anyone, but that nobody had offered her anything. His precedent is Oliver North, whose congressional immunity made his testimony unusable and kept him out of prison altogether.

epstein-files-beef-jerky-anomaly.title: Prince Andrew
epstein-files-beef-jerky-anomaly.summary: British royal, now Andrew Mountbatten Windsor, named repeatedly by John Kiriakou as one of the un-recruitable principals whose access made Jeffrey Epstein valuable to a foreign intelligence service. Kiriakou has asked why Andrew was never charged over conduct with minors, reads his alleged provision of classified Ministry of Defence documents to Epstein as evidence of espionage rather than vanity — and expects him to face no criminal consequence at all, because the statute of limitations has run.

epstein-files-beef-jerky-anomaly.title: Adnan Khashoggi
epstein-files-beef-jerky-anomaly.summary: Saudi arms dealer and Iran-Contra middleman whom John Kiriakou says was mentioned 'all the time' at the CIA — in pointed contrast to Jeffrey Epstein, whose name he never once heard there.

epstein-files-beef-jerky-anomaly.title: AIPAC
epstein-files-beef-jerky-anomaly.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

epstein-files-transparency-act.title: Jeffrey Epstein

epstein-files-transparency-act.title: Mike Johnson
epstein-files-transparency-act.summary: Speaker of the House during the fight over the Epstein files, whose procedural manoeuvres John Kiriakou reads as a sustained attempt to prevent his own party from ever having to vote — first by blocking the motion in the Rules Committee, then by adjourning the House until September so that nothing at all could be voted on — and whose midterm framing of Democrats as communists Kiriakou dismisses outright.

epstein-files-transparency-act.title: John Kiriakou
epstein-files-transparency-act.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

epstein-files-transparency-act.title: Thomas Massie
epstein-files-transparency-act.summary: Republican U.S. Representative from Kentucky known for a constitutionalist voting record and consistent opposition to foreign military intervention; per John Kiriakou, a principled America-First congressman who votes with the president on the vast majority of issues, and whose opposition to U.S. funding of Israel and foreign wars is the only plausible explanation for the roughly $30 million spent by the Israel lobby to unseat him in a primary.

epstein-files-transparency-act.title: Alexander Acosta and the sweetheart deal
epstein-files-transparency-act.summary: The US attorney who gave Jeffrey Epstein his 2006 non-prosecution agreement and later said he had been ordered to — a chain of command John Kiriakou traces upward to an attorney general famous for his powerlessness, and therefore to somebody above him whom nobody has ever named.

epstein-files-transparency-act.title: Nick Bryant
epstein-files-transparency-act.summary: Investigative journalist, activist and co-founder of Epstein Justice, author of The Franklin Scandal, and a repeat guest on John Kiriakou's programme, where Kiriakou describes him as knowing the Epstein case better than anybody else in America.

epstein-statute-of-limitations.title: Prince Andrew
