Kiriakou also recounts an Egyptian al-Qaeda fighter he later recruited who survived a cruise-missile strike on a Tora Bora cave — one of only two who came out alive, his ears bleeding, describing the explosion as the most hideous sound he had ever heard.

isi.title: The Taliban truck escort origin
isi.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of how the Taliban began: as a Pakistani government scheme under Benazir Bhutto to take madrasa students — talib, plural taliban — out of the religious schools and put them with Kalashnikovs aboard Pakistani trucks crossing Afghanistan to Iran, to stop mujahideen fighters from pirating the cargo.

isi.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
isi.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

isis.title: Al-Julani
isis.summary: The former al-Qaeda commander and, per John Kiriakou, co-founder of ISIS who was installed as president of Syria and received at the White House. Kiriakou''s initial reading was that no one moves from a ten-million-dollar American bounty to a state visit in months without being a long-term CIA asset — until a senior Turkish official told him over dinner that al-Julani was Turkey''s: ''We created him from nothing and we installed him in Syria.'' Kiriakou judged that version more plausible than his own.

isis.title: Kurds
isis.summary: The stateless people John Kiriakou calls generationally pro-American — he escorted visiting Kurdish delegations around Washington as a young analyst and bristled at officials who talked down to them. In his telling the Kurds were the only genuine opposition inside Saddam's Iraq, the only faction of the exile circus that ever amounted to anything (Jalal Talabani ended up president of Iraq), the victims of Saddam's chemical weapons and of a no-fly zone that forgot to ban helicopters — and the common enemy that actually united Turkey and ISIS.

isis.title: Bashar al-Assad
isis.summary: President of Syria; John Kiriakou recounts warning Senator John Kerry to stop publicly calling Assad 'my dear friend' after a speech enraged Washington's Lebanese community, with Kerry citing motorcycle rides they had taken together to the Golan Heights.

isis.title: Osama bin Laden
isis.summary: Founder and leader of al-Qaeda and the central target of the manhunt that shaped John Kiriakou's counterterrorism career. Per Kiriakou, bin Laden came from a billionaire Saudi construction family, was never one of the CIA-funded Afghan mujahideen, overruled subordinates who wanted to attack Israel and insisted the 9/11 attacks hit the United States to crash its economy, escaped Tora Bora dressed as a woman, and spent his final years next to Pakistan's equivalent of West Point — where, Kiriakou says, you would have to be a "mental defective" not to know he was there. Kiriakou believes the United States never intended to capture him alive.

isis.title: Barbara Leaf
isis.summary: American diplomat, assistant secretary of state for the Near East, and — in John Kiriakou's description — an old friend of his. He cites her trip to Damascus, made within days of al-Julani taking power and alongside the special envoy for hostage affairs, as the moment American recognition was traded for the lifting of the ten-million-dollar bounty on the new Syrian leader.

isis.title: Muammar Gaddafi
isis.summary: Libya's ruler and, in John Kiriakou's telling, the cautionary tale that teaches every proliferator never to disarm. In February 2003 the CIA's Steve Kappes secretly visited Gaddafi with an ultimatum — the U.S. was about to overthrow Saddam, and Libya would meet the same fate unless it surrendered its weapons of mass destruction. Gaddafi complied — and was later overthrown and lynched anyway, "at the insistence of the United States." A bad guy, Kiriakou stresses, but one Washington had a healthy working relationship with, who hated al-Qaeda as much as America did; flipping sides to destroy him was "a terrible policy error" that left anarchy.

islam-in-america.title: Jihad means to struggle
islam-in-america.summary: John Kiriakou's insistence, as a graduate in Islamic theology and an Arabic speaker, that jihad does not mean and has never meant holy war. He traces the American usage to media coverage of the 1979 Iranian revolution and the embassy hostage crisis, and points out that one can declare a jihad against poverty or in favour of education.

islam-in-america.title: The Texas Muslim development
islam-in-america.summary: A housing development planned by a group of wealthy Muslim professionals in Texas — twenty-five or thirty large houses on an empty tract with a mosque at the centre, marketed to other Muslim doctors, lawyers and engineers. John Kiriakou cites the alarm it caused, up to and including Governor Greg Abbott, as a case study in unnecessary panic.

islam-in-america.title: CIA sexpionage
islam-in-america.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the CIA''s use of sex in espionage — routine from its founding through the early 1980s, including MK-Ultra and honey-pot operations — and why the agency largely abandoned it: coercion cannot build the trust a long-term source requires. Other services never stopped.

islam-in-america.title: Olof Palme assassination
islam-in-america.summary: The 1986 street murder of the Swedish prime minister, which John Kiriakou revisited step by step in Stockholm with researchers who had spent years on it. His conclusion — drawn from dozens of witness reports of two-man cars with walkie-talkies, some identified as police vehicles — is that much of the surveillance that night was carried out by people who believed they were running a practice exercise, until someone walked up and shot Palme dead.

islam-in-america.title: Syrian minorities and the Israeli strikes
islam-in-america.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of a conflict inside American policy toward post-Assad Syria: Washington wants the country''s Christian, Jewish and Druze communities protected and has recognised the new government and moved to reopen its embassy, while Israel continues to strike Syrian territory despite repeated instructions from Donald Trump to stop.

islam-in-america.title: The CIA and honey-trapping
islam-in-america.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of why the CIA, unlike the Russians, Chinese, Israelis and French, does not run honey-trap recruitment operations. He credits an instructor's story about a 1970s attempt against an Iranian mulla, who reacted to the incriminating photographs by asking for 8×10s and wallets, as the moment the agency concluded coercion produces resentment rather than sources.

islamofascism-term.title: Muslim Brotherhood terrorist designation
islamofascism-term.summary: John Kiriakou''s objection to the designation of the Muslim Brotherhood, or elements of it, as a terrorist organisation: that the group is more than a century old, has never carried out an anti-American terrorist operation, and had never been so designated by any previous administration. He distinguishes fundamentalism and hostility from terrorism, has made the same argument to a former IDF spokesman''s face, and traces the American quarrel with the Brotherhood back to its winning an Egyptian election.

islamofascism-term.title: Deep state
islamofascism-term.summary: John Kiriakou''s position on the deep state — that it is not a right-wing trope but an accurate description of something he served inside for fifteen years at the CIA and two more on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee staff. He is indifferent to the label ("call it the state, call it the federal bureaucracy") and insists on the substance: "It''s there to stay. It''s not going anywhere."

islamofascism-term.title: Americans and the word socialism
islamofascism-term.summary: Two exchanges John Kiriakou uses to argue that the political vocabulary of the United States has stopped carrying meaning — a Thanksgiving conversation with a woman who denounced socialism and lived on Social Security, and a newspaper comment thread in which a restaurant owner taking his staff's tips was described as socialism.

islamofascism-term.title: Permanent wartime economy
islamofascism-term.summary: John Kiriakou's thesis that since 9/11 the United States has run a permanent wartime economy so large that cutting the defense budget would trigger a depression — likening the dependency to crack addiction and warning it makes war almost inevitable.

islamofascism-term.title: Ukraine as a proxy war
islamofascism-term.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment, given two months into the 2022 Russian invasion, that the United States was funding a proxy war it knew Ukraine could not win in order to bog Russia down — and that the outcome was already fixed, so peace talks should happen at once.

islamofascism-term.title: Air India Flight 182
islamofascism-term.summary: The 1985 bombing of a Boeing 747 over the Atlantic, which John Kiriakou has attributed to the government of India in the course of arguing that state sponsorship of terrorism is not confined to the countries formally designated for it.

ismail-haniyeh-assassination.title: Hamas
ismail-haniyeh-assassination.summary: The Palestinian movement behind the October 7, 2023 attack; John Kiriakou argues that a case could be made for calling it a freedom-fighting organization dedicated to the liberation of its people rather than simply a terrorist group, notes it is labeled a terrorist organization by only a small minority of UN member states, and has ruled Gaza since Israel's 2005 withdrawal.

ismail-haniyeh-assassination.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
ismail-haniyeh-assassination.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

ismail-haniyeh-assassination.title: October 7 attack
ismail-haniyeh-assassination.summary: John Kiriakou's analysis of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack as a policy failure, not an intelligence one — Israel was warned repeatedly, but Itamar Ben-Gvir diverted response forces to the West Bank, and Kiriakou believes Israel welcomed a pretext for overwhelming retaliation.

ismail-haniyeh-assassination.title: Afghan heroin policy
ismail-haniyeh-assassination.summary: The post-2001 U.S. policy in Afghanistan of protecting, and per John Kiriakou actively encouraging, the cultivation of heroin poppy. Under the Taliban in 2000 Afghanistan produced 0% of the world's heroin; by 2009 under American occupation it produced 93%. Per a DEA officer Kiriakou consulted with on the policy paper he was preparing for Senator Kerry, the strategic rationale was that nearly all of the heroin flowed to Iran and Russia, addiction in those countries was considered desirable as a long-run societal weakener, and the same logic now operates in reverse with Chinese fentanyl flowing into the United States.

ismail-haniyeh-assassination.title: Andrew Bustamante
ismail-haniyeh-assassination.summary: Former CIA officer who sells CIA-style training online; John Kiriakou identifies him as the lone critic of his work hosting a show on a Russian network, and argues Bustamante's training business — open to anyone who pays — is the more problematic of the two.

ismail-haniyeh-assassination.title: China as economic threat
ismail-haniyeh-assassination.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.title: MOSSAD
israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.title: Israeli intelligence presence in the United States
israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Israeli intelligence activity inside the United States — dozens of undeclared Mossad and Shin Bet officers identified by the FBI, a critical-threat counterintelligence classification alongside Russia, North Korea and Cuba, and a pattern of harassment and intimidation directed at declared CIA officers posted to Israel.

israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.title: "One dead pedophile"
israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of why he believes the American intelligence community will not examine whether Jeffrey Epstein worked for a foreign service — that the accusation points at Israel, that the relationship with Israel is uniquely valuable, and that nobody in Washington will upset it over one dead pedophile when covering it up is easier.

israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.title: Snowden did not defect
israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.summary: John Kiriakou's two corrections to the treatment of Edward Snowden at Tulsi Gabbard's 2025 confirmation hearing — that "traitor" has a constitutional definition Snowden does not meet, there having been no declaration of war since December 1941, and that Snowden did not defect to Russia but was stranded in a Moscow transit lounge en route to Ecuador when John Kerry revoked his passport.

israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.title: The CIA buyout offer
israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.summary: The deferred-resignation offer extended to CIA staff in early 2025 on the same terms given to other federal workers — six to eight months' pay, no requirement to come to work, and then the end of the contract — which John Kiriakou discussed as part of a broader reorientation of the agency towards the Western Hemisphere.

israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.title: Five Eyes
israel-and-the-fear-of-being-held-back.summary: The intelligence-sharing partnership of the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand

israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.title: Remains of the Day (book)
israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.summary: John Kiriakou's book, announced for publication by Simon and Schuster in March 2026, billed as a definitive guide to the historic cemeteries of Washington DC and the first in a planned series; the second installment will cover the Mafia graves of New York City.

israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.title: Israeli intelligence presence in the United States
israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Israeli intelligence activity inside the United States — dozens of undeclared Mossad and Shin Bet officers identified by the FBI, a critical-threat counterintelligence classification alongside Russia, North Korea and Cuba, and a pattern of harassment and intimidation directed at declared CIA officers posted to Israel.

israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.title: Whispers in the Dirt
israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.summary: John Kiriakou's second cemetery book — a guide to the mafia graves of New York City, and the sequel Simon & Schuster commissioned after Remains of the Day. Reporting it produced the moment he realised an inmate who had told him a body was found in a barrel in his storage unit had been telling the truth.

israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.title: Greek death rituals
israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.summary: The five-year grave rental, exhumation and ossuary practice of rural Greece as John Kiriakou describes it — bones washed in red wine, blessed, boxed, and eventually laid beneath the foundations of a new church, with cremation strictly forbidden. He visits the ossuary in his ancestral Rhodes village, where the records stop in the nineteenth century because the Ottomans burned everything earlier.

israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.title: Kiriakou's writing process
israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of how he actually writes — books in waves over roughly nine months, op-eds in forty-five minutes to an hour once an idea has sat for a few days, and a habit of getting up at two in the morning to write one because he cannot sleep. He wrote *Remains of the Day* in six weeks during COVID, losing whole evenings to it: "I look at the clock again, it''s 2:00 in the morning. I''m like, oh my god, what happened?"

israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.title: Abraham Accords
israel-boyd-wonder-bread-story.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.title: MOSSAD
israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.title: F-35 avionics dispute with Israel
israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how Israel demanded F-35 fighters without the deliberately degraded avionics the U.S. installs on export models — and, refused, allegedly worked through American defense contractors to steal the technology instead.

israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.title: Jonathan Pollard
israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.summary: U.S. Navy civilian intelligence analyst convicted in 1985 of spying for Israel; the canonical proven case of Israeli espionage against the United States; cited by John Kiriakou in his 2024 Piers Morgan debate with a former Mossad director who denied any Israeli spying on the U.S.

israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.title: NDAA 2027 US–Israel fusion provisions
israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.summary: Provisions in the proposed National Defense Authorization Act for 2027 and the companion intelligence authorization bill that would create a permanent Pentagon executive agent for US–Israeli military fusion and lock in permanent intelligence sharing tied to Israel's qualitative military edge. John Kiriakou describes the effect as handing over voluntarily the technology Israel previously ran spies to steal.

israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.title: Veterans' benefits for IDF service
israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.summary: A bill sponsored by a Republican congressman from Pennsylvania and one from Ohio that would extend US veterans' benefits to any American who joins the Israel Defense Forces. John Kiriakou calls it an outrage and, as an American, treason.

israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.title: Israeli interception of US secure calls
israel-counterintelligence-threat-rankin.summary: John Kiriakou's account of overhearing evidence, within six months of joining the CIA, that Israeli intelligence was listening to encrypted American government calls — a colleague's secure line dropped mid-conversation and two Israeli voices could be heard on the open channel discussing whether the call had ended. He treats the episode as the concrete basis for assuming that American principals are intercepted as a matter of routine.

israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.title: Iran Nuclear Assessment
israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.summary: Per John Kiriakou's assessment, the US–Israeli military campaign against Iran was a war of choice driven by Israeli political pressure rather than genuine intelligence indicating an Iranian nuclear weapons threat. The CIA produced two National Intelligence Estimates concluding Iran had no nuclear weapons program; Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei issued a fatwa in the 1980s forbidding such a program. The U.S. went to war anyway, in Kiriakou's view, after President Trump replaced the Joint Chiefs of Staff with officers willing to accept Israeli intelligence and proceed.

israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.title: MOSSAD
israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.title: Iran's 2024 drone retaliation
israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Iran's telegraphed 2024 drone strike on Israel — hundreds of slow drones, launched with advance warning to the U.S. and Jordan, nearly all shot down, which he reads as a controlled show of force and an intelligence victory that exposed the Iron Dome.

israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.title: Reza Pahlavi
israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.summary: The exiled Iranian crown prince whom John Kiriakou dismisses as an Israeli-backed fantasy candidate to rule Iran — a man who has not lived there since his teens, supported mainly by Beverly Hills exiles, whom Kiriakou says 'wouldn't survive the walk from the plane to the terminal.'

israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.title: The Russian nuclear umbrella
israel-iran-cell-phone-assassinations.summary: John Kiriakou's report, two days after the Israeli strikes on Iran began in June 2025, that Russia had declared Iran to be under the protection of its nuclear umbrella — and his conclusion that this rules out any Israeli nuclear use against Iran, because it would risk Russian nuclear retaliation against Israel.

israel-non-extradition-of-jews.title: Jeffrey Epstein
israel-non-extradition-of-jews.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

israel-non-extradition-of-jews.title: Truman's regret over Israel
israel-non-extradition-of-jews.summary: John Kiriakou's account that Harry Truman called his role in the creation of the state of Israel the act of 'a damn fool' and the biggest regret of his presidency, because the situation spun out of control almost immediately.

israel-non-extradition-of-jews.title: Nixon's guarantee of Israeli national security
israel-non-extradition-of-jews.summary: John Kiriakou's account that AIPAC, having begun to focus on election fundraising in the late 1960s, succeeded in getting President Nixon to guarantee Israeli national security in 1969 — a commitment he says no American president had made before.

israel-non-extradition-of-jews.title: 2026 Iran war
israel-non-extradition-of-jews.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

israel-non-extradition-of-jews.title: Access Agent
israel-non-extradition-of-jews.summary: CIA (and foreign intelligence service) term for a recruited asset whose value lies not in the secrets they hold directly but in their regular social access to high-value targets — politicians, executives, heads of state — who cannot themselves be recruited. Per John Kiriakou, the access agent is funded generously to maintain an environment in which the targets feel comfortable and return repeatedly; kompromat — compromising photographs or recordings — may be collected as a secondary tool. Kiriakou identifies Jeffrey Epstein as a textbook access agent, in his assessment working for Israeli intelligence.

israel-non-extradition-of-jews.title: Tom Alexandrovich
israel-non-extradition-of-jews.summary: Senior Israeli cyber security official arrested in Las Vegas in August 2025 on multiple counts of child pornography after being caught in an undercover police sting targeting child sex predators, and immediately permitted to board a plane back to Israel — a case John Kiriakou uses as a live illustration of the rule that Israel does not extradite Jews.

israel-turkey-nato-article-5.title: Israeli drone factories in Serbia
israel-turkey-nato-article-5.summary: Five drone factories John Kiriakou was told the Israelis are building in Serbia — a fact relayed to him by members of a Serbian delegation who welcomed it on the grounds that Israel is effective against Islamists, and which Kiriakou treats as the same emotional play he sees used on Greeks and Cypriots.

israel-turkey-nato-article-5.title: Israeli property acquisition in Greece and Cyprus
israel-turkey-nato-article-5.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Israelis buying land in Greece and Cyprus at a scale he considers destabilising — entire villages rather than holiday homes, a Jewish-only village outside Paphos with a casino attached, a rejected bid for an island in the Ionian Sea, and a request to open the first Zionist high school in Cyprus.

israel-turkey-nato-article-5.title: South Caucasus realignment
israel-turkey-nato-article-5.summary: John Kiriakou''s reading of the post-election South Caucasus: Russia has lost Armenia, Georgia has split from Armenia and moved closer to Moscow, and Iran — contrary to the assumption that two Muslim neighbours would be natural partners — keeps far closer relations with Christian Armenia than with Azerbaijan.

israel-turkey-nato-article-5.title: Sports and the Steelers bar
israel-turkey-nato-article-5.summary: Asked whether he enjoys any sport, John Kiriakou named baseball and football, and described walking to a Steelers bar in Clarendon, Arlington, to watch a game he could have watched at home — for the five hundred screaming Pittsburgh fans.

israel-turkey-nato-article-5.title: Trump's Supreme Court appointees
israel-turkey-nato-article-5.summary: An assessment John Kiriakou volunteered in February 2026 and that runs against his politics elsewhere: that Donald Trump''s appointees to the Supreme Court have been surprisingly good, and that the justices he regards as disasters — Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas — were put there by moderate presidents.

israel-turkey-nato-article-5.title: The Vietnam speech
israel-turkey-nato-article-5.summary: A paid speaking engagement John Kiriakou described in February 2026 — booked by a New York speakers bureau for the morning of 10 August, addressing three hundred Australian investment bankers at their annual convention in a country he had never visited and had always wanted to.

israel-united-states-relations.title: AIPAC
israel-united-states-relations.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

israel-united-states-relations.title: MOSSAD
israel-united-states-relations.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

israel-united-states-relations.title: Jeffrey Epstein
israel-united-states-relations.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

israel-united-states-relations.title: Patrick Bet-David
israel-united-states-relations.summary: The podcast host whom John Kiriakou described on another programme as a hardcore Zionist and a total backer of Reza Pahlavi, and who then played the clip back to him on air. Kiriakou withdrew the characterisation on the record, one of the few occasions where he has retracted a public statement about a named individual.

israel-united-states-relations.title: The Truman broadcast
israel-united-states-relations.summary: An address by Harry Truman announcing American recognition of Israel that John Kiriakou says he watched on YouTube — in which Truman took the hatred of both sides as proof of his own success, and said recognition of a Palestinian state would follow further negotiations. Kiriakou''s comment: that was 1948, and we are still waiting.

israel-united-states-relations.title: National Security vs Civil Liberties
israel-united-states-relations.summary: Kiriakou's recurring argument that invoking "national security" is used to excuse the erosion of civil liberties and that the secrecy regime cannot coexist with constitutional democracy.

israeli-art-student-spy-ring.title: Office of Special Plans Israeli leak
israeli-art-student-spy-ring.summary: A major Israeli spy operation John Kiriakou says was uncovered in the 2000s involving a leak from the Pentagon's Office of Special Plans, headed by Paul Wolfowitz and Douglas Feith — both authors, with Richard Perle, of the "Clean Break" report advocating a dual-containment strategy against Iraq and Iran on behalf of Benjamin Netanyahu. Per Kiriakou, Wolfowitz and Feith did not merely fail to take Israeli counterintelligence seriously; he believes they actively helped abet it.

israeli-art-student-spy-ring.title: Operation Mega
israeli-art-student-spy-ring.summary: A 1997 FBI investigation into a senior U.S. government official believed to be passing highly sensitive information to Israel, opened after the NSA intercepted an Israeli intelligence communication referring to a source code-named "Mega." Per John Kiriakou, unlike similar investigations into other countries, the case never resulted in an indictment or public disclosure, and the identity of the American official was never revealed.

israeli-art-student-spy-ring.title: 9/11 attribution of responsibility
israeli-art-student-spy-ring.summary: John Kiriakou's evolving view of who bears ultimate responsibility for the September 11 attacks — that al-Qaeda carried them out but was, in his current view, "allowed" to, amid a distracted Bush administration, an uninvestigated Saudi government, and an Israeli government he believes had a vested interest in the attacks proceeding.

israeli-art-student-spy-ring.title: Alex Station
israeli-art-student-spy-ring.summary: CIA unit that tracked Osama bin Laden beginning in 1995; per John Kiriakou, who served as chief of its counterintelligence branch, the unit kept extremely tight security around its files, limited FBI investigators' access to information about future 9/11 hijackers Khaled al-Mihdhar and Nawaf al-Hazmi, and — under a deliberate policy of non-cooperation with the FBI — failed to watchlist participants in the Malaysia summit where al-Qaeda planned the attacks.

israeli-art-student-spy-ring.title: Ali Mohamed
israeli-art-student-spy-ring.summary: Egyptian-American former U.S. Army sergeant who trained at Fort Bragg while secretly working for Egyptian intelligence, later trained some of the 9/11 hijackers and other al-Qaeda operatives, and was arrested in connection with the 1998 U.S. embassy bombings before disappearing under the George W. Bush administration; John Kiriakou speculates he was actually a double agent working for al-Qaeda — or possibly Israeli intelligence — against his CIA handlers.

israeli-art-student-spy-ring.title: Charlie Kirk shooting
israeli-art-student-spy-ring.summary: Kiriakou questions the official account: a court filing says the ATF could not match the autopsy bullet to the rifle tied to the suspect.

israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.title: Israel, Turkey, and NATO Article 5
israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.summary: John Kiriakou's scenario in which an Israeli attack on Turkey would oblige every NATO member, the United States included, to come to Turkey's defence — and in which the alliance would sooner dissolve than honour that obligation against Israel.

israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.title: Israeli property acquisition in Greece and Cyprus
israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Israelis buying land in Greece and Cyprus at a scale he considers destabilising — entire villages rather than holiday homes, a Jewish-only village outside Paphos with a casino attached, a rejected bid for an island in the Ionian Sea, and a request to open the first Zionist high school in Cyprus.

israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.title: Rhodes Jewish deportation
israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.summary: The 1944 deportation of the Jewish community of Rhodes, John Kiriakou''s ancestral island, which he recounts from his grandmother''s memory: rounded up within twenty-four hours, shipped to Piraeus and taken by train through Thessaloniki to Auschwitz. Of roughly two thousand taken, fourteen survived and seven returned. Kiriakou''s great-grandfather hid the wealthy Jewish Rhodian he chauffeured for three and a half years.

israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.title: South Caucasus realignment
israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.summary: John Kiriakou''s reading of the post-election South Caucasus: Russia has lost Armenia, Georgia has split from Armenia and moved closer to Moscow, and Iran — contrary to the assumption that two Muslim neighbours would be natural partners — keeps far closer relations with Christian Armenia than with Azerbaijan.

israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.title: Antisemitism and anti-Zionism
israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.summary: The conflation of criticism of the Israeli state with hatred of Jews, which John Kiriakou describes as a worldwide confusion and, according to a young Israeli he spoke to, an explicit lesson of the Israeli school system; a subject Kiriakou says he personally struggles with.

israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
israeli-drone-factories-in-serbia.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

israeli-espionage-in-the-united-states.title: Jonathan Pollard
israeli-espionage-in-the-united-states.summary: U.S. Navy civilian intelligence analyst convicted in 1985 of spying for Israel; the canonical proven case of Israeli espionage against the United States; cited by John Kiriakou in his 2024 Piers Morgan debate with a former Mossad director who denied any Israeli spying on the U.S.

israeli-espionage-in-the-united-states.title: NDAA Section 219
israeli-espionage-in-the-united-states.summary: The provision of the National Defense Authorization Act for 2027 that would co-locate Israeli personnel with the Pentagon and open Five Eyes-style intelligence liaison with the CIA, which John Kiriakou opposes as merging with a service ranked a critical counterintelligence threat.

israeli-espionage-in-the-united-states.title: MOSSAD

israels-rightward-shift.summary: The program by which the CIA's predecessor brought Nazi scientists to the United States after World War II; John Kiriakou notes the FBI opposed it, that the Nazis surrendered to the U.S. fearing the Soviets, and that V-2 rocket father Wernher von Braun is buried near his home in Virginia.

israels-rightward-shift.title: Gulf intelligence services
israels-rightward-shift.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of the intelligence services of the Gulf Cooperation Council states, which he worked with closely during his CIA career and rates uniformly excellent — highly trained, multilingual and experienced worldwide — with the Emiratis and Qataris the strongest of them and the Emiratis, in his ranking, the best of all.

italian-election-covert-action.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
italian-election-covert-action.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

italian-election-covert-action.title: Radio and TV Martí
italian-election-covert-action.summary: U.S. government broadcasters beaming anti-communist programming at Cuba; John Kiriakou uses their accidental reach into Florida to explain why the Obama administration made it legal, in 2015, to propagandize the American people.

italian-election-covert-action.title: Operation Mockingbird
italian-election-covert-action.summary: The CIA's mid-twentieth-century program of recruiting and managing American journalists as influence assets; in John Kiriakou's account, no longer operationally necessary in the contemporary period because the U.S. media voluntarily reprints CIA-supplied material, and in at least one documented case sends articles to the agency for clearance before sending them to its own editor.

italian-election-covert-action.title: Active measures
italian-election-covert-action.summary: The in-house name John Kiriakou gives to the CIA branch responsible for propaganda and for countering hostile propaganda — a division he describes as running twenty-four hours a day, paired with an opposing anti-active-measures branch, and as the ancestor of the political action group that remains the agency's clandestine propaganda arm.

italian-election-covert-action.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
italian-election-covert-action.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

italian-election-covert-action.title: John Kiriakou
italian-election-covert-action.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

italian-intelligence-services.title: "Most other countries are more moral than the CIA"
italian-intelligence-services.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to a viewer who asked whether the United States has the most moral intelligence agency: it does not, and a hundred countries could be named whose services behave better — the disqualifying practice being the killing of people who pose no threat to the United States.

italian-intelligence-services.title: Iranian intelligence capability
italian-intelligence-services.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of Iranian intelligence as poor and always having been poor, on the ground that Iranian officers do not receive good training and are essentially on their own, with only marginal help from the Russians and the Chinese.

italian-intelligence-services.title: A Middle East reading list
italian-intelligence-services.summary: The books and the starting point John Kiriakou recommends to anyone trying to understand the modern Middle East: begin at the end of the Second World War, not five thousand years earlier, and start with The House of Saud, the Sykes-Picot Agreement and From Beirut to Jerusalem.

italian-intelligence-services.title: Bombing the Omanis
italian-intelligence-services.summary: John Kiriakou's judgement that Iran's strikes on the Gulf states — and above all on Oman, which had been trying to broker peace — made enemies Iran did not need to make, of governments that would otherwise have sat the war out.

italian-intelligence-services.title: Bowe Bergdahl
italian-intelligence-services.summary: The American soldier who walked off his base in Afghanistan, was captured by the Haqqani network and handed to the Taliban, and was repatriated in a prisoner trade — a man John Kiriakou says was treated as a traitor although he was not one.

italian-intelligence-services.title: Chaos as the Israeli objective
italian-intelligence-services.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to whether Netanyahu''s government actually wanted an American invasion of Iran: what the Israelis want in Iran is what they got in Libya — chaos, civil war, and as many dead Iranians as possible.

italians-at-loretto.title: Aryan Brotherhood
italians-at-loretto.summary: The white prison gang that adopted John Kiriakou on his first day at FCI Loretto. Two hours in, two Aryans with swastika neck tattoos walked into his cell to check his paperwork — not a rat, not a "chomo" — and invited him to the Aryan table, which ran from hardcore Nazis at one end to merely white guys at the other. A rumor that he had been a CIA assassin earned him the nickname "the Muslim killer," which he never corrected; asked directly, he answered "we all did stuff we weren't proud of — it was wartime," and the Aryans loved it. He sat with them a year before the Italians took him in.

italians-at-loretto.title: Doing Time Like a Spy
italians-at-loretto.summary: Prison memoir by John Kiriakou, full title Doing Time Like a Spy: How the CIA Taught Me to Survive and Thrive in Prison; winner of two literary awards and reissued in a second edition by Simon and Schuster.

italians-at-loretto.title: The prison food economy
italians-at-loretto.summary: The underground kitchen at FCI Loretto, where meals were cooked in bin liners heated by improvised immersion elements, guards stole and resold the food they were meant to be guarding, and Kiriakou stopped going to the cafeteria for the last six to eight months of his sentence.

italians-at-loretto.title: Prison tattoos
italians-at-loretto.summary: Tattoos as John Kiriakou encountered them at FCI Loretto — the swastika-necked welcoming committee on his first day, the Lady Justice piece that made him laugh and then think, the constant pressure on him to get one, and his flat refusal to take a souvenir of the place.

italians-at-loretto.title: Truck and Cat in the Hat
italians-at-loretto.summary: An incident at FCI Loretto in which John Kiriakou, told by one prisoner that another had called him a rat, invented a slur he knew would enrage a convicted serial killer — who beat the accuser badly enough to require a helicopter medevac. Kiriakou presents it as a live application of two rules he says he learned at the CIA: let others do your dirty work, and admit nothing, deny everything, make counter-accusations.

italians-at-loretto.title: CIA Training Doctrine
italians-at-loretto.summary: ''Our job is to break the law'' — Kiriakou on what CIA training actually teaches, why it applies only overseas, and the ethics class that never comes.

itamar-ben-gvir.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
itamar-ben-gvir.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

itamar-ben-gvir.title: October 7 attack
itamar-ben-gvir.summary: John Kiriakou's analysis of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack as a policy failure, not an intelligence one — Israel was warned repeatedly, but Itamar Ben-Gvir diverted response forces to the West Bank, and Kiriakou believes Israel welcomed a pretext for overwhelming retaliation.

itamar-ben-gvir.title: The Israeli generals' tour of the West Bank
itamar-ben-gvir.summary: The September 2026 New York Times reporting John Kiriakou aired on his own show, in which retired Israeli generals including Amiram Levin, Ephraim Sneh and Assaf Agmon, men who had fought Israel's wars from 1973 through 2006, publicly named settler violence in the West Bank as a graver threat to Israel than Iran, Gaza or Lebanon. Their tour of Palestinian villages recorded ethnic cleansing, called the erasure effort *"what some Israelis' forebears endured during the Holocaust,"* and produced the line Kiriakou returns to, *"once a society behaves this way, that society is doomed."*

itamar-ben-gvir.title: Netanyahu in hiding
itamar-ben-gvir.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the Israeli prime minister's disappearance from public view during the 2026 Iran war, when reports placed him in Germany and then Cyprus, and of Iran's adoption of Israel's own decapitation tactics — strikes on Netanyahu's house, which killed his brother, and on Itamar Ben-Gvir's.

itamar-ben-gvir.title: The obliteration claim
itamar-ben-gvir.summary: Donald Trump's statement that the Iranian nuclear programme had been "obliterated", and John Kiriakou's reading of it. Kiriakou offers three possibilities — the president lied, was tricked, or did not understand what had been achieved — and notes the claim's incompatibility with the later justification that Iran was days away from a weapon.

itamar-ben-gvir.title: The Knesset death penalty law
itamar-ben-gvir.summary: The Israeli law imposing a mandatory death sentence by hanging on Palestinians convicted of killing during a terrorist act, and John Kiriakou's response to it. He notes that the government defining what counts as terrorism is the same government whose settlers the law exempts, and calls the result a codification of racial discrimination.

j-edgar-hoover.title: National Security Act of 1947
j-edgar-hoover.summary: The law that created the CIA and the National Security Council — passed, in John Kiriakou's telling, only because Harry Truman lied to J. Edgar Hoover. Hoover lobbied Capitol Hill to kill the bill until Truman promised the CIA would be a division of the FBI; the bill passed, Hoover realized he'd been duped, and ordered the FBI not to cooperate with the new agency — a freeze that lasted, incredibly, until after 9/11. Kiriakou's account of how the agency was designed at all runs through a room in New York where MI6 officers sat down with Bill Donovan, Prescott Bush and some pads of paper.

j-edgar-hoover.title: William Donovan
j-edgar-hoover.summary: General William "Wild Bill" Donovan — Medal of Honor recipient, decorated World War I veteran, Wall Street figure, and founder of the wartime Office of Strategic Services (OSS). Per John Kiriakou, Donovan had President Truman's ear and insisted the new agency be independent rather than a division of the FBI; he was among the men who sat down with visiting MI6 officers in New York in 1946–47 and sketched out a centralized intelligence service on pads of paper, and he became — in Kiriakou's telling — the first director of the CIA, over the sustained opposition of J. Edgar Hoover.

j-edgar-hoover.title: Langley
j-edgar-hoover.summary: The Virginia location of CIA headquarters and, in John Kiriakou''s usage, shorthand for the agency''s permanent power. It''s where he worked as the CIA''s lone Iraq-Kuwait analyst — told to start on Iraq "because nothing ever happened there" — where a cafeteria conversation invited him into the torture program, where he walked past the Kryptos sculpture every day for fifteen years without solving it, and the place agencies return to after apologizing to Congress, "where of course nothing ever changes." When a host suggested the real government of America is out in Langley and Washington''s white marble is for show, Kiriakou''s answer was: "that''s about the shape of it."

j-edgar-hoover.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
j-edgar-hoover.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

j-edgar-hoover.title: Julian Assange
j-edgar-hoover.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

j-edgar-hoover.title: Roy Cohn
j-edgar-hoover.summary: Closeted McCarthy-era prosecutor and fixer, later a mentor, advisor and attorney to Donald Trump from the 1970s onward; per John Kiriakou, one of the darkest, ugliest figures in modern American history, who — while closely allied with a similarly closeted J. Edgar Hoover — was central to ruining the lives of gay men, and who died of AIDS in the 1980s alone and unloved.

jack-devine.title: CIA Drug Facilitation
jack-devine.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the CIA''s reported involvement in facilitating the arrival of cocaine into the United States during the era that became the crack epidemic, and his own firsthand discovery — as a Senate Foreign Relations Committee investigator — that under American military control Afghanistan produced 93% of the world''s heroin. A DEA contact told him the report would never be published because ''we want Iran and Russia to be addicted to heroin. It weakens their societies.'' Kiriakou draws a direct parallel to the current fentanyl crisis: China is doing to the US what the US did to Iran and Russia.

jack-devine.title: Dewey Clarridge
jack-devine.summary: The CIA operations officer John Kiriakou calls a legendary figure and a giant of the 1980s — prosecuted over Iran-Contra, and the man who said publicly that Saudi Arabia already had nuclear weapons. Kiriakou believes him, holds that the Saudis financed the Pakistani bomb and were repaid in access to it, and believes Clarridge was also involved in the movement of cocaine into the United States.

jack-devine.title: Contra rebels
jack-devine.summary: The right-wing Nicaraguan insurgency armed by the Reagan administration against the Sandinista government. In John Kiriakou's account they were conservatives, right-wingers, in some cases fascists, and disgruntled military officers; they were split into a northern group the United States armed and a southern group that financed itself by selling cocaine — a distinction that became the pivot of the Gary Webb affair, and that Kiriakou uses to answer the CIA's standing denial that it had anything to do with the drug trade.

jack-devine.title: Extraordinary Rendition
jack-devine.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the CIA practice of seizing terrorism suspects in one country and transporting them to a third country — often a country with no due-process protections — to be held, interrogated, or tortured outside U.S. legal jurisdiction. The program operated alongside the enhanced-interrogation program and was the operational mechanism by which prisoners reached secret CIA facilities and allied torture sites in countries like Bahrain. Kiriakou himself was not in the rendition line of work but became a federal felon under the Intelligence Identities Protection Act for a single confirmation of a colleague's surname to a journalist who claimed to be writing a book on the Abu Omar rendition from Milan.

jack-devine.title: Saudi nuclear program
jack-devine.summary: Saudi Arabia's decades-long pursuit of uranium enrichment, nominally for nuclear power, which John Kiriakou notes was already old news when he arrived at the CIA in 1990 and which conventional wisdom has always read as a weapons programme.

jack-devine.title: Bob Baer
jack-devine.summary: Former CIA case officer; per John Kiriakou, "pretty famous"; the subject of George Clooney's film Syriana; pulled out of northern Iraq by the Clinton White House in the 1990s after [NSA intercepted](/wiki/the-intercept) a communication revealing he was developing a network of sources to assassinate Saddam Hussein — National Security Adviser Sandy Berger called CIA and threatened him with a conspiracy charge.

jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.title: Special Activities Division
jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.summary: The CIA's paramilitary arm; described by John Kiriakou as having two organizationally distinct components — the pre-9/11 SAD, a covert-action division within the Directorate of Operations, and a post-9/11 special activities group within the Counterterrorism Center, staffed largely by personnel on secondment from Delta Force, SEAL Team 6, and other special-operations units.

jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.title: Agnes von Kurowsky grave story
jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.summary: John Kiriakou's account of discovering the Washington, D.C. grave of Agnes von Kurowsky, the World War I Red Cross nurse whose four-month wartime romance with a young ambulance driver, Ernest Hemingway, made her the model for the lead female character in six of his books, including A Farewell to Arms.

jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.title: Kiriakou's personal anecdotes
jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.summary: Three personal stories John Kiriakou has told in interviews — tracking down and meeting Andy Warhol as a college senior, a Congolese vice president's remark that Americans promise democracy while the Chinese provide food, and Kiriakou's own Zelle account being suspended over Cuba-sanctions compliance after a paid article about his Cuba trip.

jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.title: Spies of Arlington National Cemetery
jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.summary: On the Walk With History podcast, John Kiriakou — author of Remains of the Day: A Definitive Guide to Washington D.C.''s Historic Cemeteries — toured Arlington National Cemetery and told personal and historical stories about the intelligence figures buried there, including OSS founder William Donovan, deputy CIA director Vernon Walters, codebreakers William and Elizabeth Friedman, slain station chiefs Richard Welch and William Buckley, U-2 pilot Francis Gary Powers, and Mike Spann, the first CIA officer killed after 9/11.

jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.title: Bashar al-Assad
jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.summary: President of Syria; John Kiriakou recounts warning Senator John Kerry to stop publicly calling Assad 'my dear friend' after a speech enraged Washington's Lebanese community, with Kerry citing motorcycle rides they had taken together to the Golan Heights.

jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.title: Chinese spy balloon incident
jack-murphy-nato-sabotage-story.summary: 2023 controversy over a high-altitude balloon that crossed U.S. airspace, widely labeled in media coverage as a "Chinese spy balloon"; John Kiriakou notes no U.S. government official ever officially confirmed it was conducting espionage, and says he personally believes it was likely a weather balloon, since satellite surveillance already renders such balloons unnecessary for spying.

jack-teixeira.title: Chelsea Manning
jack-teixeira.summary: Former U.S. Army intelligence analyst who provided WikiLeaks its 2010 trove of military and diplomatic documents. Per John Kiriakou, Manning meets the legal definition of whistleblower for exposing war crimes, was a torture victim of prolonged solitary confinement with forced nudity, and was sentenced to 35 years in prison before Barack Obama commuted — not pardoned — her sentence. Kiriakou says Manning later refused a grand jury's offer of immunity and chose renewed jail time rather than testify against Julian Assange.

jack-teixeira.title: Espionage Act
jack-teixeira.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

jack-teixeira.title: Angela Merkel
jack-teixeira.summary: German chancellor whose mobile phone the NSA was intercepting, in what John Kiriakou treats as the cleanest illustration of the two-tier American attitude to surveillance: the interception of one of Washington''s closest allies was big news, Hillary Clinton flew to Germany to apologise, and — per Kiriakou — the United States then did it again. Asked about it in Berlin, his answer was that intercepting her phone is exactly what he wants the CIA to be doing.

jack-teixeira.title: Public-interest defense
jack-teixeira.summary: The affirmative defense the Espionage Act does not allow: John Kiriakou explains that a defendant cannot tell a jury he acted in the public interest, and that Edward Snowden''s willingness to come home hinged on getting that chance — which the Justice Department refused.

jack-teixeira.title: CIA disguise program
jack-teixeira.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the CIA's disguise and forgery specialists — including a master disguise maker recruited from a beauty academy who built him a custom bald-head mask over six weeks, and a master forger recruited off his college newspaper cartoons.

jack-teixeira.title: The sources and methods red herring
jack-teixeira.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that the federal government invokes the exposure of sources and methods in every leak prosecution as a matter of routine, has never produced proof in any of them — not against Julian Assange, Edward Snowden or Chelsea Manning — and that American claims of damage to national security should therefore not be taken seriously.

jake-tapper.title: Arianna Huffington
jake-tapper.summary: Founder of the Huffington Post and the accidental amplifier who turned John Kiriakou's prison writing into a phenomenon. His first Letter from Loretto went to his attorney, then to a friend running Firedoglake who — unknown to Kiriakou — was close to Huffington; she plastered it as a banner headline and it drew over a million hits, bringing CNN and 60 Minutes to the prison gates. She published his open letter to Snowden, ran the diesel-therapy exposé that triggered the "hands off John Kiriakou" campaign, and came to Loretto herself with two young journalists.

jake-tapper.title: Freedom of Information Act
jake-tapper.summary: The U.S. transparency law that runs through John Kiriakou's story from every direction — his plea agreement banned him from ever filing a FOIA request on himself, so he filed one with the Bureau of Prisons anyway and got back pages stamped "FOIA EXEMPT — DO NOT RELEASE TO INMATE"; a FOIA request exposed the prison commissary skim; Jason Leopold's requests revealed that a detainee's eye was removed under sedation without his knowledge and that NBC's Ken Dilanian sent his stories to the CIA before his own editor; and a FOIA request is how Kiriakou learned Gary Johnson had quietly lobbied for his early release.

jake-tapper.title: Letter from Loretto
jake-tapper.summary: Prison newsletter written by John Kiriakou from FCI Loretto, modeled on Martin Luther King's "Letter from Birmingham Jail," which exposed two crimes committed against him by guards and went viral after being relayed to the Huffington Post, drawing national press to the prison.

jake-tapper.title: Jon Stewart
jake-tapper.summary: American broadcaster, on whom John Kiriakou publicly accepted a correction from a viewer, and about whom he tells a single unflattering story from their one meeting.

jake-tapper.title: The Knight Ridder panel
jake-tapper.summary: At an April 2022 Assange benefit in Washington, John Kiriakou described a Zoom panel on which two former Knight Ridder reporters spoke for ninety minutes without once mentioning Julian Assange, and one of them, asked why, said he saw Assange as an activist rather than a journalist.

jake-tapper.title: The filibuster and Harry Reid's lesson
jake-tapper.summary: John Kiriakou's defence of the Senate filibuster, offered as praise for John Thune's refusal to abolish it under pressure from the White House, and grounded in what he regards as Harry Reid's costly mistake over judicial nominations.

jamaal-bowman.title: AIPAC
jamaal-bowman.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

jamaal-bowman.title: Cori Bush
jamaal-bowman.summary: Former U.S. Representative from St. Louis (Missouri's 1st congressional district); cited by John Kiriakou as one of the two named cases of AIPAC successfully primarying an incumbent for delivering a House floor speech describing the Gaza war as a "wholesale massacre of Palestinian civilians."

jamaal-bowman.title: Abdul El-Sayed
jamaal-bowman.summary: Physician and Democratic Socialists of America-backed candidate in Michigan's 2026 Democratic Senate primary. John Kiriakou, who discloses a $100 donation to the campaign, presents him as the test case for whether the electability argument still works for establishment Democrats.

jamaal-bowman.title: AIPAC and foreign-agent registration
jamaal-bowman.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that AIPAC is the only organization of its kind exempt from registering under the Foreign Agents Registration Act — set against his own experience around 2008, when a contract worth five or six thousand dollars to write four op-eds praising the Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce obliged him to register as a foreign agent.

jamaal-bowman.title: BDS movement
jamaal-bowman.summary: The Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement against Israel; John Kiriakou notes that some 40 U.S. states now have anti-BDS laws that can require a speaker at a publicly funded university to sign a pledge of support for Israel — which he refuses to do.

jamaal-bowman.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
jamaal-bowman.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

james-angleton.title: JFK assassination
james-angleton.summary: November 22, 1963 killing of President John F. Kennedy in Dallas, Texas. John Kiriakou's position, drawn from a Pakistan-station encounter with Bay of Pigs commander Jean Gately, an RFK Jr. account of CIA Director John McCone's same-day exchange with Bobby Kennedy Sr., and a White House contact's confirmation that the remaining classified Kennedy documents all contain the word "Israel," is that elements of the CIA were probably involved and that Israeli intelligence was involved as well.

james-angleton.title: MK-Ultra
james-angleton.summary: The CIA's mid-twentieth-century umbrella program of mind-control, behavioral-modification, and biological-warfare experimentation, encompassing subprojects such as MK-Chickwit and MK-Seesaw; active 1952–1975; documented practices included LSD dosing of unwitting American citizens in CIA-rented brothels and the aerosolized release of pathogens into the San Francisco fog; 80% of the program's documentation was destroyed by the CIA in defiance of a 1975 preservation order from Senator Frank Church.

james-angleton.title: Allen Dulles
james-angleton.summary: Long-serving CIA director whom John Kiriakou calls a 'monster' and a 'very dark figure in American history' — a United Fruit board member who ran the agency that overthrew Guatemala's Árbenz, who went to Truman's house to talk him out of criticising the CIA, and who stayed in touch with the men Kiriakou believes killed John F. Kennedy.

james-angleton.title: John Brennan
james-angleton.summary: Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President

james-angleton.title: Abu Zubaydah
james-angleton.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

james-angleton.title: LSD Mind Manipulation
james-angleton.summary: Kiriakou on the CIA dosing unwitting men with LSD in safe houses, using sex workers as bait, to find out whether the drug could unlock secrets.

james-bond.title: John Kiriakou
james-bond.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

james-bond.title: Central Intelligence Agency
james-bond.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

james-bond.title: George Washington University
james-bond.summary: The Washington university where John Kiriakou took a bachelor's degree in Middle Eastern studies and began a master's in legislative affairs, and where a professor who was in fact a CIA spotter recruited him into the agency — an institution that recurs throughout his account as the place his intelligence career began, as the venue of his first CIA tests, and later as a classroom he taught in himself.

james-bond.title: The colleague who went to Microsoft
james-bond.summary: In 2000, John Kiriakou''s supervisor left the CIA for Microsoft to do what he called "some really cool social media stuff" — a phrase that meant nothing to Kiriakou at the time, and which he later read as an early sign of the deliberate placement of intelligence officers inside technology companies.

james-bond.title: The counterfeit dollar trade
james-bond.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of high-quality counterfeit US currency — the Swiss paper that makes it possible, an estimate that five to ten percent of the notes in circulation may be forged, and a quiet policy of buying up caches at thirty cents on the dollar and incinerating them.

james-bond.title: The ask-forgiveness maxim
james-bond.summary: The rule of thumb John Kiriakou says he was taught early in his CIA career — that it is always better to ask forgiveness than to ask permission — and which he offers as the explanation for how the agency runs legally doubtful programmes: it does what it wants, apologises if caught, and that is the end of it.

james-clapper.title: John Brennan
james-clapper.summary: Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President

james-clapper.title: Espionage Act
james-clapper.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

james-clapper.title: Anwar al-Awlaki
james-clapper.summary: American-born al-Qaeda propagandist; in 1993 the imam of the Falls Church, Virginia mosque visited by John Kiriakou's CIA Arabic-language class on a field trip; in 2001 the cleric at whose mosque the 9/11 hijackers prayed the night before the attacks; killed by U.S. drone strike in Yemen in approximately 2011.

james-clapper.title: Ron Wyden
james-clapper.summary: U.S. senator and the lone real challenger of the CIA on the intelligence committees; John Kiriakou faults Wyden for challenging the agency only 'by the agency's rules' — refusing to read the Senate torture report into the record, and admitting at a dinner that fighting harder would cost him his security clearance.

james-clapper.title: Abolish the CIA
james-clapper.summary: John Kiriakou's position that the CIA should be abolished because its functions are already duplicated by the other 17 U.S. intelligence agencies — analysis by the State Department, human spying by the Pentagon, technology by DARPA, NSA and the private sector.

james-clapper.title: Langley
james-clapper.summary: The Virginia location of CIA headquarters and, in John Kiriakou''s usage, shorthand for the agency''s permanent power. It''s where he worked as the CIA''s lone Iraq-Kuwait analyst — told to start on Iraq "because nothing ever happened there" — where a cafeteria conversation invited him into the torture program, where he walked past the Kryptos sculpture every day for fifteen years without solving it, and the place agencies return to after apologizing to Congress, "where of course nothing ever changes." When a host suggested the real government of America is out in Langley and Washington''s white marble is for show, Kiriakou''s answer was: "that''s about the shape of it."

james-comey.title: FISA court
james-comey.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the secret Foreign Intelligence Surveillance court — created under Carter, sitting atop the Justice Department, issuing warrants that are never public — which he says was abused against Carter Page as part of what he believes was John Brennan's plan to deny Trump the presidency.

james-comey.title: John Brennan
james-comey.summary: Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President

james-comey.title: Julian Assange
james-comey.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

james-comey.title: Carter Page
james-comey.summary: Trump campaign adviser against whom, per John Kiriakou, the FBI lied to the FISA court multiple times in order to obtain surveillance warrants. Kiriakou offers the episode as evidence less of a conspiracy than of an assumption — that at that level, with everything classified, officials believe the truth will simply never come out.

james-comey.title: John Durham
james-comey.summary: United States attorney for Connecticut appointed to investigate the origins of the Russia inquiry. Speaking in December 2019, John Kiriakou described Durham as having obtained John Brennan''s call logs, his emails from his time as CIA director, and the contemporaneous notes Brennan took in meetings with other agency heads — and read Durham''s own insistence that this was a criminal investigation rather than an inquiry as pointing at process crimes: false statements and perjury.

james-comey.title: John Kiriakou
james-comey.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

james-fishback.title: AIPAC
james-fishback.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

james-fishback.title: MOSSAD
james-fishback.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

james-fishback.title: Donald Trump
james-fishback.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

james-fishback.title: Jeffrey Epstein
james-fishback.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

james-fishback.title: Ted Rall
james-fishback.summary: American editorial cartoonist and two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist; co-host with John Kiriakou of the daily news-commentary podcast "Deprogram," launched in September 2025 and by late 2025 running every weekday morning.

james-fishback.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
james-fishback.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

james-jesus-angleton.title: Kim Philby
james-jesus-angleton.summary: The British MI6 deputy director secretly working for the KGB — recruited in college and directed to join the service — and, in John Kiriakou's telling, James Angleton's best man and his child's godfather; his decades of betrayal broke Angleton, and he escaped from Beirut through a bathroom window to Moscow. Kiriakou ranks the Cambridge ring as damage at historic levels, above any modern comparison.

james-jesus-angleton.title: Aldrich Ames
james-jesus-angleton.summary: Senior CIA officer — a GS-15 who rose to chief of counterintelligence for the Soviet branch — who spied for the KGB for nine years. Per John Kiriakou, Ames walked into the Soviet embassy in Washington in April 1985 and sold the identities of two CIA-recruited double agents for $50,000 to clear a debt run up by his second marriage; both were executed. He went on to identify more than thirty agents, compromise over a hundred clandestine operations, cause at least twelve deaths and take more than $2 million, while being known throughout the agency as a daily drunk and promoted at every turn. The KGB protected him with a decoy mole hunt; analyst Sandy Grimes caught him by matching his handler meetings to his bank deposits.

james-jesus-angleton.title: James Angleton
james-jesus-angleton.summary: Long-serving chief of CIA counterintelligence; in John Kiriakou's account the man whose wall of files at headquarters were all dossiers on American citizens, who was best man at Kim Philby's wedding and never recovered from learning Philby was the mole, and who — per the declassified JFK files — ordered CIA officers to recruit Lee Harvey Oswald.

james-jesus-angleton.title: Warrenton Training Center
james-jesus-angleton.summary: A secret CIA communications facility in Warrenton, Virginia, which — per John Kiriakou — the KGB used as a decoy to protect Aldrich Ames. When Ames warned Moscow in 1986 that he feared becoming a suspect, a Soviet case officer told a CIA contact that the mole was posted to Warrenton; agency mole hunters then spent almost a year investigating ninety employees there and produced ten suspects, none of them Ames.

james-jesus-angleton.title: Allen Dulles
james-jesus-angleton.summary: Long-serving CIA director whom John Kiriakou calls a 'monster' and a 'very dark figure in American history' — a United Fruit board member who ran the agency that overthrew Guatemala's Árbenz, who went to Truman's house to talk him out of criticising the CIA, and who stayed in touch with the men Kiriakou believes killed John F. Kennedy.

james-jesus-angleton.title: Dmitry Polyakov
james-jesus-angleton.summary: GRU colonel run as a CIA agent by Sandy Grimes, and one of the assets burned by Aldrich Ames. Per John Kiriakou, Polyakov's loss is why Grimes took Ames's treachery personally — the analyst who eventually broke the case had handled one of the men it killed.

james-morris.title: Turkey and a safe zone in Iran
james-morris.summary: John Kiriakou''s response to the Turkish president''s suggestion that, in the event of an attack on Iran, the Turkish army would establish a safe zone inside Iranian territory — that Ankara would love nothing more, having previously taken Iraqi, Cypriot and Syrian territory, and that pan-Turkism is a subject most people are unaware of.

james-morris.title: Barrett Brown
james-morris.summary: American journalist and former Anonymous associate whom John Kiriakou describes as one of the most intelligent writers and analysts he has ever encountered, with long-standing mental health problems and a two-decade heroin addiction he has now been clear of for at least a year, expelled from the United Kingdom and relocated to Mexico.

james-morris.title: Censorship on the left
james-morris.summary: John Kiriakou''s observation that he was censored far less by Forbes and Fortune than by The Nation and Mother Jones, which he offers as an instance of a general rule that a writer''s own side censors them hardest — the counterpart to Ted Rall''s account of being made to fit a particular kind of leftism rather than any kind.

james-morris.title: Dr Oz and the Armenian hospices
james-morris.summary: John Kiriakou''s reaction to a television segment by Mehmet Oz alleging fraud by Armenian-run hospices in Los Angeles — that a man he identifies as a veteran of the Turkish special forces zeroing in on Armenians in California is not a coincidence, and that each of the administration''s appointees appears to arrive with a racial scandal of their own.

james-morris.title: The Iron Dome
