kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: Director of the Central Intelligence Agency under President Trump's first term; known to John Kiriakou and others at the CIA as "Bloody Gina"; per Kiriakou, flew out to the secret black site to sit in on one of the enhanced-interrogation torture sessions "just because she could," personally supervised the torture of USS Cole bombing suspect Rahim al-Nashiri, and later fed the CIA's torture tapes into an industrial document grinder after being explicitly told by White House Counsel not to destroy them.

kiriakou-cuba-trip.title: Kiriakou's Russian media work
kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: John Kiriakou's account of hosting a daily Sputnik radio show for seven and a half years with full contractual freedom to criticize anyone, including Putin — which he did on the morning of the Ukraine invasion — offered as a rebuttal to claims that Russian outlets are mere propaganda.

kiriakou-cuba-trip.title: Kiriakou's daily news diet
kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the wide range of mainstream and alternative outlets he reads each morning to compare competing angles, the two outlets — the Associated Press and ProPublica — he singles out as exceptional, and his broader habits of media consumption, from an admitted addiction to political polling to his distrust of AI chatbots after they repeatedly fabricated his own biography.

kiriakou-cuba-trip.title: The Eritrea prohibition
kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: John Kiriakou's account of being forbidden to visit Eritrea on a Senate Foreign Relations Committee trip through the Horn of Africa — not by the Eritrean government but by the State Department, whose only stated reason was that Eritrea is 'the North Korea of Africa.' He notes that he was later free to dine at the Eritrean ambassador's residence in Washington.

kiriakou-cuba-trip.title: Kiriakou's Iran trips
kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: John Kiriakou's account of his own visits to Iran and his Iranian-American partner's regular travel there — noting Tehran's status as the cosmetic-surgery capital of the Middle East, a warning to Iranian state TV viewers about American fast food rather than American generals, and his own repeated but unfulfilled invitations to visit.

kiriakou-cuba-trip.title: A virtual state of war with Venezuela
kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: John Kiriakou said in February 2025 that he was mystified by the choice of Marco Rubio as Secretary of State, describing him as a neoconservative in the mould of George W. Bush, and predicted that on Venezuela the second Trump administration would simply continue the Biden policy — which had itself continued the first Trump policy — leaving the two countries in what he called a virtual state of war.

kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.title: The Green Line in Nicosia
kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.summary: The division of Nicosia between the Republic of Cyprus and the Turkish-occupied north, which John Kiriakou toured in July 2026 and described as maintained through deliberate humiliation rather than any interest in settlement.

kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.title: Origin of the Kiriakou name
kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.summary: The Kiriakou surname originates in a clerical error at a Rhodes courthouse, where John Kiriakou's great-great-grandfather, arrested for stealing a potato while starving, gave a patronymic that was written down as his family name and never corrected.

kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.title: Kiriakou on Greek and Cypriot food
kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.summary: The verdict John Kiriakou delivered on Cypriot cooking during a 2026 visit to the island — that its cheeses are more sophisticated and more distinct from one another than Greece's, where most are variations on a theme — together with his coffee positions, his conversion from frappé by a cousin in Rhodes, and his complaint about the size of the straw.

kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.title: Kiriakou on travel
kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.summary: John Kiriakou''s own ranking of the countries he has visited: Greece his favourite and, he insists, the best food anywhere; Oman the most beautiful landscape; Syria the most extraordinary civilisation; and Chile the cheapest, illustrated by a bottle of a vineyard''s locked-away reserve that cost $8.50 on his honeymoon.

kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.title: There is no such thing as bad food in Athens
kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.summary: The lesson John Kiriakou says he learned at a lorry drivers' stop outside Corinth, where the food was as good as his grandmother's — reached on the three-and-a-half-hour drives he made to meet a source too sensitive to be met in Athens, with a vineyard tour as his cover story.

kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.title: Operational eating
kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.summary: The two rules John Kiriakou gives about food on operations: that a case officer never orders seafood, and above all never shellfish, because a day spent incapacitated by food poisoning makes him useless to the operation — and that a fourteen-hour surveillance can be run on nothing but a container of mango juice.

kiriakou-daily-news-diet.title: Donald Trump
kiriakou-daily-news-diet.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

kiriakou-daily-news-diet.title: Jeffrey Epstein
kiriakou-daily-news-diet.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

kiriakou-daily-news-diet.title: Kiriakou's Russian media work
kiriakou-daily-news-diet.summary: John Kiriakou's account of hosting a daily Sputnik radio show for seven and a half years with full contractual freedom to criticize anyone, including Putin — which he did on the morning of the Ukraine invasion — offered as a rebuttal to claims that Russian outlets are mere propaganda.

kiriakou-daily-news-diet.title: Djibouti
kiriakou-daily-news-diet.summary: The small Horn of Africa state a few miles across the water from Yemen that hosts Camp Lemonnier — the American drone base for the Yemen and Somalia wars, inherited from the departing French, and shared with China's only overseas military base behind a fence down the middle, in what John Kiriakou calls the worst kept secret in the world.

kiriakou-daily-news-diet.title: China's base in Djibouti
kiriakou-daily-news-diet.summary: Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti, the abandoned French base the Djiboutians offered to the Americans and the Chinese took a share of — split down the middle by a chain-link fence, the only Chinese military installation outside China, and the centrepiece of John Kiriakou's argument that China is not an expansionist power.

kiriakou-daily-news-diet.title: Saudi-Iran diplomatic rivalry
kiriakou-daily-news-diet.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the roots of Saudi-Iranian hostility — Iran's bloody 1979 infiltration of the Hajj, Saudi Arabia's suppression of its own Shia minority, and the 2023 restoration of diplomatic relations brokered, to Washington's surprise, by China.

kiriakou-death-threats.title: Death threats against Kiriakou
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: The threats John Kiriakou has received across two decades — first after going public about the CIA torture program, when FBI advice that at least two were credible sent his family out of the country, and later in waves tied to his opposition to Gina Haspel, his remarks about Pakistan, and his advocacy on Palestine and the Epstein case.

kiriakou-death-threats.title: John Kiriakou's Briefing Room
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: A twice-weekly news and commentary programme launched by John Kiriakou in July 2026, presented as analysis rather than partisan opinion, and distinct from his storytelling podcast Dead Drop.

kiriakou-death-threats.title: Dead Drop (podcast)
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: John Kiriakou''s narrative podcast, launched in late 2025 — a season-long, memoir-style retelling of his life in intelligence, from recruitment ("The New Recruit") through Athens ("Golden Boy") to the post-9/11 hunt ("The Hunt Begins"), with mini-episodes like "A Spy''s Guide to Sofia." Written by Kiriakou with Alan Katz, produced by Costard & Touchstone Productions, with Kiriakou, Katz, and Nick Mechanic as executive producers. Its stated goal: "the deepest possible perspective on the world of spying and what makes any spy tick."

kiriakou-death-threats.title: President's Daily Brief
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the President's Daily Brief (PDB) is a roughly 16-page, top-secret intelligence document produced daily for the president, written in a uniform CIA house style, briefed each morning, and — in his account — used partly to gauge and flatter incoming presidents.

kiriakou-death-threats.title: Situational awareness
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: The discipline John Kiriakou describes as the civilian version of surveillance detection — get out of the kill zone at the first sign of trouble, keep an escape route, and refuse to let the brain rationalise away what it is seeing.

kiriakou-death-threats.title: The Islamabad surveillance incident
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: The episode in which John Kiriakou, then the CIA's chief of counterterrorism operations in Pakistan, detected a motorcyclist following him, resolved to kill the man, and discovered on a passing impulse that the surveillance was friendly.

kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.title: Julian Assange
kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.title: Ed Schultz
kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.summary: American broadcaster, a friend of John Kiriakou''s and later his colleague at RT, whom Kiriakou cites twice over: as a man forbidden by MSNBC to discuss Bernie Sanders during a primary, and as a dead man still being labelled a Russian government mouthpiece four years after his death.

kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.title: Kiriakou's Russian media work
kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.summary: John Kiriakou's account of hosting a daily Sputnik radio show for seven and a half years with full contractual freedom to criticize anyone, including Putin — which he did on the morning of the Ukraine invasion — offered as a rebuttal to claims that Russian outlets are mere propaganda.

kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.title: Press TV website seizure
kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.summary: The FBI's confiscation of the Press TV domain, which John Kiriakou cites alongside the banning of TeleSUR, RT and Sputnik as the point at which American censorship stopped being algorithmic and became straightforwardly physical.

kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.title: Panquake
kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.summary: Open-source, blockchain-based social platform developed by the Iceland-registered company Talk Liberation, for which John Kiriakou has served as brand ambassador since 2020. Kiriakou describes it as advertising-free, subscription-funded, free of back doors, and run on servers powered by Icelandic geothermal steam — a project he frames as a David-and-Goliath fight against banks, big technology and governments.

kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.title: The state-affiliated media labels
kiriakou-deplatforming-2022.summary: The warning tags applied by social media platforms from 2020 identifying accounts as mouthpieces of foreign governments, which John Kiriakou describes checking his own account for daily. His standing example of how indiscriminate the practice became is the labelling of Ed Schultz, who had been dead for years.

kiriakou-family-name.title: Kiriakou's Cypriot ancestry
kiriakou-family-name.summary: The DNA result showing John Kiriakou to be 24 per cent Cypriot — his largest single ancestry — which corrected a family belief that the line came from Crete and coincided with an invitation to address a Cypriot diaspora conference.

kiriakou-family-name.title: The Green Line in Nicosia
kiriakou-family-name.summary: The division of Nicosia between the Republic of Cyprus and the Turkish-occupied north, which John Kiriakou toured in July 2026 and described as maintained through deliberate humiliation rather than any interest in settlement.

kiriakou-family-name.title: Abu Zubaydah
kiriakou-family-name.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

kiriakou-family-name.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kiriakou-family-name.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kiriakou-family-name.title: Bureau of Prisons advisory board
kiriakou-family-name.summary: The advisory board John Kiriakou joined at the personal invitation of the Director of the Bureau of Prisons, who told him the president had tasked him with tearing the Bureau down and rebuilding it.

kiriakou-family-name.title: Cameo
kiriakou-family-name.summary: The personalised-video app John Kiriakou joined in February 2026 and turned into an unexpected second career — around 2,600 videos, roughly 900 of them in his first month alone. Half are birthday messages and most of the rest are requests for CIA stories, but about two hundred have been appeals for advice or a pep talk, and three of those people later told him he had talked them out of suicide.

kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.title: Barry Eisler
kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.summary: Former CIA officer turned bestselling novelist, and a recurring guest of John Kiriakou's, who describes him as one of the very few former intelligence officers to have succeeded at storytelling outside the secret world as thoroughly as he did inside it.

kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.title: Beirut
kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.summary: The Lebanese capital John Kiriakou confirms was a genuine espionage playground — though he dates the peak to the 1950s through the mid-1970s, when Beirut was the Paris and the banking centre of the Middle East, and when, beneath the CIA, KGB and Israeli presence, "more secretly the French ran the place." He also explains why the enormous new American embassy there is about fortification rather than a regional CIA headquarters.

kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.title: Bruce Fein
kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.summary: John Kiriakou's longtime attorney and one of his closest friends; a Harvard Law-trained constitutional scholar, former Deputy Attorney General under President Reagan and former General Counsel of the Federal Communications Commission. Fein took the call from Jared Kushner's attorney that opened Kiriakou's first pardon track, sat beside him at the 2018 Trump International Hotel meeting at which Rudy Giuliani's aide solicited $2 million for a presidential pardon, and is his co-author on a long-planned book about the CIA's record of failure.

kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.title: Dead Drop (podcast)
kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.summary: John Kiriakou''s narrative podcast, launched in late 2025 — a season-long, memoir-style retelling of his life in intelligence, from recruitment ("The New Recruit") through Athens ("Golden Boy") to the post-9/11 hunt ("The Hunt Begins"), with mini-episodes like "A Spy''s Guide to Sofia." Written by Kiriakou with Alan Katz, produced by Costard & Touchstone Productions, with Kiriakou, Katz, and Nick Mechanic as executive producers. Its stated goal: "the deepest possible perspective on the world of spying and what makes any spy tick."

kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.title: The Directorate of Operations
kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.summary: The CIA's clandestine service, which John Kiriakou joined from analysis because he spoke both Greek and Arabic — a culture he describes as wildly different from the analytic side, short on institutional memory and organised around the race to become a station chief.

kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.title: The twenty-seven cousins
kiriakou-father-and-grandfather.summary: John Kiriakou has said Daniel Ellsberg was a hero in his family before he was six years old — because seven of his twenty-seven first cousins on his mother's side fought in Vietnam believing what they had been told, and it was Ellsberg who showed the family that all of it had been a lie.

kiriakou-gastrectomy.title: Kiriakou's type 2 diabetes
kiriakou-gastrectomy.summary: The disease John Kiriakou was diagnosed with after leaving the CIA for a desk job, which he first fought down with a nutritionist's diet and a 70-pound weight loss, then lost ground to when insulin slowed his metabolism to a halt — reaching an A1C of 12.1 before he had his stomach removed to end it.

kiriakou-gastrectomy.title: Kiriakou on diet and nutrition
kiriakou-gastrectomy.summary: John Kiriakou''s views on eating, given to a Cypriot nutrition interviewer who challenged several of them: that the worst dietary advice he ever heard was to cut fat and cholesterol, that the American sugar lobby spent decades persuading the public that fat was the enemy, and that at his age carbohydrates are the enemy instead.

kiriakou-gastrectomy.title: Kiriakou's post-gastrectomy complications
kiriakou-gastrectomy.summary: The aftermath of John Kiriakou''s stomach removal: eighteen months of daily vomiting that turned out to be scar tissue, a diagnosis of malnutrition, and a night on his kitchen floor with a blood pressure of 80 over 52, caused by a blood clot sitting on an ulcer at the surgical site — one hour, his surgeon told him, from being too late.

kiriakou-gastrectomy.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-gastrectomy.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-gastrectomy.title: The glyburide incident
kiriakou-gastrectomy.summary: The episode John Kiriakou described in a Letter from Loretto of 12 September 2014: handed a bottle of glyburide by the prison pharmacy without explanation, he crashed twice and passed out on the floor — and his physician father-in-law told him the drug could have put him into heart failure.

kiriakou-gastrectomy.title: Kiriakou on Greek and Cypriot food
kiriakou-gastrectomy.summary: The verdict John Kiriakou delivered on Cypriot cooking during a 2026 visit to the island — that its cheeses are more sophisticated and more distinct from one another than Greece's, where most are variations on a theme — together with his coffee positions, his conversion from frappé by a cousin in Rhodes, and his complaint about the size of the straw.

kiriakou-greek-citizenship.title: Kiriakou Greek whistleblower law
kiriakou-greek-citizenship.summary: A whistleblower protection law John Kiriakou says he was hired by the Greek government to write in 2015, at the invitation of Greece, after which it was passed by both the European Parliament and the Greek Parliament and became law across the European Union. Per Kiriakou, the law's first courtroom use involved a whistleblower who exposed Greece's defense minister for taking bribes from Siemens; the resulting press coverage led a consortium of Greece's four wealthiest families to ask Kiriakou to run a private equity fund for them.

kiriakou-greek-citizenship.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
kiriakou-greek-citizenship.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

kiriakou-greek-citizenship.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
kiriakou-greek-citizenship.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

kiriakou-greek-citizenship.title: J. Edgar Hoover
kiriakou-greek-citizenship.summary: The FBI's founding director — 48 years in the chair — whose opposition nearly strangled the CIA at birth. Per John Kiriakou, Truman lifted Hoover's objection to the National Security Act of 1947 by disingenuously assuring him the CIA would be a division of the FBI; the lie seeded the two agencies' permanent mutual hatred. Kiriakou also credits Hoover with perfecting the annual ritual the CIA later copied — scaring Congress witless and demanding budget increases — and with controlling Hollywood's FBI image so tightly that no film could be made without his approval.

kiriakou-greek-citizenship.title: Kyriakos Mitsotakis
kiriakou-greek-citizenship.summary: The Greek prime minister John Kiriakou names when asked which world leader he would put in Donald Trump's place — a choice he qualifies by admitting he did not vote for the man the first time and has since been pleasantly surprised.

kiriakou-greek-citizenship.title: The Greek health care system
kiriakou-greek-citizenship.summary: John Kiriakou's description of Greek health care as a two-tier system in which the private sector buys nothing but position in the queue — a procedure that takes eleven or twelve months on the public system takes one or two privately, and the care itself is the same.

kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.title: Blueprint for Free Speech
kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.summary: The Australian non-governmental organisation that drafts whistleblower protection legislation and markets it to governments around the world, and which hired John Kiriakou in 2015 to help write Greece's law. Its board is mostly academics and transparency activists; Kiriakou credits it with successes in Canada, Zambia, Jamaica and Ukraine, and names its founder and director as Suelette Dreyfus, whom he describes as a co-founder of WikiLeaks with Julian Assange.

kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.title: Julian Assange
kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.title: Kiriakou's Greek citizenship
kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.summary: The Greek nationality John Kiriakou acquired in 2010, after his CIA career and before his prosecution — offered, he says, by the Greek ambassador who asked what could be done to help when his troubles began, and granted when he answered "you could give me Greek citizenship." Held by his children too, it made him a Greek national at the moment he became, in Greece, a national hero; it brought him the commission to write the country's whistleblower protection law, and the Athens job that turned out to be a money laundering operation.

kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.title: The EU whistleblower directive
kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.summary: The European Union whistleblower protection directive, which John Kiriakou describes as a watered-down descendant of the Greek law he helped write in 2015. His objection is to its exemption: the directive does not apply to Brussels itself. He treats that as an instance of a general legislative habit rather than a European failing — Congress, he notes, routinely exempts itself from the laws it passes, including the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.title: J. Edgar Hoover
kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.summary: The FBI's founding director — 48 years in the chair — whose opposition nearly strangled the CIA at birth. Per John Kiriakou, Truman lifted Hoover's objection to the National Security Act of 1947 by disingenuously assuring him the CIA would be a division of the FBI; the lie seeded the two agencies' permanent mutual hatred. Kiriakou also credits Hoover with perfecting the annual ritual the CIA later copied — scaring Congress witless and demanding budget increases — and with controlling Hollywood's FBI image so tightly that no film could be made without his approval.

kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.title: The Toronto transit detention
kiriakou-greek-whistleblower-law.summary: John Kiriakou's account of being seized at the aircraft door in Toronto by two Royal Canadian Mounted Police officers, told 'you are not welcome in Canada,' and walked by both arms through the airport onto his connecting flight — while transiting home from a trip on which the Greek government had hired him to help write a whistleblower protection law.

kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.title: United Fruit and the Arbenz coup
kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the 1954 CIA overthrow of Guatemala's President Arbenz after he nationalized the banana crop — engineered by the Dulles brothers, who sat on the board of the United Fruit Company, and followed by half a century of dictatorship.

kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.title: Allen Dulles
kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.summary: Long-serving CIA director whom John Kiriakou calls a 'monster' and a 'very dark figure in American history' — a United Fruit board member who ran the agency that overthrew Guatemala's Árbenz, who went to Truman's house to talk him out of criticising the CIA, and who stayed in touch with the men Kiriakou believes killed John F. Kennedy.

kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.title: Agent payment mechanics
kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.summary: How the CIA physically pays a recruited agent — cash every month, a receipt signed with any alias the agent chooses, and a polygraph regime built around the assumption that the officer handling the money is the person most likely to steal it.

kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.title: Church Committee
kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.summary: U.S. Senate investigative committee operating in 1975–1976 that examined domestic intelligence abuses by the CIA, FBI, and NSA; per John Kiriakou, the Church Committee — alongside the concurrent Pike Committee in the House — was the last genuine moment of legislative oversight over the intelligence community, born of a national consensus that government had gone dangerously off course. Its work led to the creation of the permanent Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, which Kiriakou says ceased to function as real oversight roughly seven years after its founding.

kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.title: The CIA's internal social culture
kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.summary: John Kiriakou's one-word characterisation of the agency's internal culture — "incestuous" — describing a club for every conceivable interest, actively encouraged officer-to-officer romances, and a design intent that officers should have no need of friends or activities outside the building.

kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.title: Congressional intelligence oversight
kiriakou-guatemala-orphanage-trip.summary: John Kiriakou''s standing criticism of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Permanent Select Committee — that unlike the armed services and foreign relations committees, they do not perform oversight at all: "They''re just cheerleaders." His illustration is a sitting committee chairman who summoned him privately, then asked whether Kiriakou would write the criticism publicly on his behalf.

kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.title: Mark Warner
kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.summary: Vice chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee and former governor of Virginia. John Kiriakou reports being told, by a congressman who had campaigned for his release, that Warner had said in a room he should be hanging from a tree; he counts Warner among the Democrats who switched at the last minute to confirm Gina Haspel, and cites him as evidence that congressional oversight of the CIA is a joke — and then, asked to grade him, puts him at the top of the scale anyway.

kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.title: Jon Ossoff
kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.summary: United States senator from Georgia, whom John Kiriakou places among the rare honest figures on Capitol Hill and grades at the top of his case-officer rankings. Kiriakou also notes a family connection to the wartime liberation of Greece.

kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.title: Kiriakou's case-officer rankings
kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.summary: A recurring segment in which John Kiriakou grades serving and former American politicians on how good a CIA case officer each would make, using an S-to-F scale. The criterion is character and the ability to attract confidence rather than politics, and he repeatedly grades allies low and opponents high.

kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.title: Abu Omar rendition
kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.summary: The CIA's kidnapping of a Milan cleric, Abu Omar, who was sent to Egypt to be tortured; John Kiriakou calls it a case that ought to be taught at the CIA as how not to run a rendition, and it is what ultimately sent him to prison, after he confirmed a former colleague's surname to a journalist claiming to be writing a book about it.

kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.title: Brian Ross
kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.summary: American investigative journalist and seven-time Emmy Award winner who was a prominent reporter at ABC News when, in December 2007, he conducted the on-camera interview with John Kiriakou that produced the first public confirmation by a U.S. official that the CIA waterboarded prisoners. Per Kiriakou, Ross called him out of the blue with the assertion that a source said Kiriakou had personally tortured Abu Zubaydah; Kiriakou's decision to give the interview anyway — driven by the conclusion that 'Brian Ross's source is at the White House and they're going to pin this on me' — became the pivot point of his entire post-CIA life.

kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.title: Gavin Newsom
kiriakou-gun-rights-appeal.summary: The California governor John Kiriakou described in 2023 as the consummate Democratic Party insider waiting his turn — a Pelosi relative who married into the Brown family, doing everything the Biden operation asked of him, including a pointless surrogate trip to Idaho, on the calculation that Joe Biden would not reach the nominating convention.

kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.title: Julian Assange
kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.title: Chelsea Manning
kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.summary: Former U.S. Army intelligence analyst who provided WikiLeaks its 2010 trove of military and diplomatic documents. Per John Kiriakou, Manning meets the legal definition of whistleblower for exposing war crimes, was a torture victim of prolonged solitary confinement with forced nudity, and was sentenced to 35 years in prison before Barack Obama commuted — not pardoned — her sentence. Kiriakou says Manning later refused a grand jury's offer of immunity and chose renewed jail time rather than testify against Julian Assange.

kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.title: Edward Snowden
kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.title: CIA Car Hacking
kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.summary: Kiriakou on the Vault 7 disclosure that the CIA can seize control of a moving car and stage the crash as a suicide or an accident — a capability he says is not limited to electric vehicles, whose only counter is the emergency brake, and which he treats as the clearest example of a leak that is a matter of life and death rather than embarrassment.

kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.title: Espionage Act
kiriakou-introduction-to-wikileaks.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

kiriakou-iran-trips.title: Kiriakou's Cuba trip
kiriakou-iran-trips.summary: John Kiriakou's account of his first visit to Cuba, where his books sit in the national library and officials treated him warmly — and a Cuban vice president told him every U.S. president is 'the same,' blaming Cuba while it cannot keep the lights on. He was invited as a guest of the Havana international book fair after his first two books were translated into Spanish, and later wrote about how the U.S. embargo shapes daily life there, from a dengue-fever hospital bill he had to pay in euros to a diet dominated by squash.

kiriakou-iran-trips.title: Aafia Siddiqui
kiriakou-iran-trips.summary: Pakistani-American neuroscientist arrested in Afghanistan and convicted in the United States of attempting to shoot FBI agents; per John Kiriakou, who covered the arrest as a terrorism consultant for ABC News and has followed the case since, she never had a gun and never fired, the bullet holes offered as proof predated her capture, and the CIA took her three children — two later recovered, the youngest never found.

kiriakou-iran-trips.title: The CIA divorce rate
kiriakou-iran-trips.summary: John Kiriakou's account of why marriages fail at the CIA at a rate he says exceeds that of any other part of the U.S. government — the impossibility of explaining a midnight departure to a spouse without a clearance, and the difficulty officers have switching off a professional habit of deception. He gives the figure variously as over 75 percent and upwards of 80 percent, says he was determined not to become a statistic and became one anyway, and dates the end of his first marriage to a sentence spoken in an armoured car on the way to Athens airport. Both his divorces have been costly; of the second he says the agency played an active role he is barred by court order from explaining.

kiriakou-iran-trips.title: Juan Guaidó
kiriakou-iran-trips.summary: Venezuelan opposition figure whom the United States recognized as interim president starting in 2019; John Kiriakou dismisses him as having been, in substance, nothing more than a George Washington University grad student, and says the U.S. attempt to install him — followed later by María Corina Machado — failed because Venezuelan support for Nicolás Maduro rests on loyalty to Chavista revolutionary ideology rather than to Maduro personally.

kiriakou-iran-trips.title: Kuwait Liberation Day
kiriakou-iran-trips.summary: February 1991 expulsion of Iraqi forces from Kuwait by the U.S.-led coalition; John Kiriakou entered the country with U.S. Marines on the day of liberation; the small American flags waved by the crowds — and the post-liberation arrival of Democratic and Republican National Committee personnel ostensibly to assist the country's transition to democracy — were, per Kiriakou, the work of professional propagandist John Rendon.

kiriakou-iran-trips.title: Sanctions Effectiveness
kiriakou-iran-trips.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment that U.S. sanctions have been so overused against disfavored countries that nations like China now route around them entirely, and that sanctions work only when reserved for the worst actors and imposed in concert with other countries — citing apartheid South Africa as a success and Cuba/Venezuela as failures that instead entrench nationalist narratives.

kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.title: Situational awareness
kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.summary: The discipline John Kiriakou describes as the civilian version of surveillance detection — get out of the kill zone at the first sign of trouble, keep an escape route, and refuse to let the brain rationalise away what it is seeing.

kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.title: The CIA Insider's Guide to Surveillance and Surveillance Detection
kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.summary: Book by John Kiriakou drawing on his experience as a surveillance detection instructor at the CIA and as a private surveillance training consultant. The book covers the techniques used by intelligence professionals to identify whether they are being followed — including the four-phase surveillance detection route, concealment device placement and retrieval, and counter-surveillance strategy — adapted for use by corporate executives, journalists, and others who want to confirm whether they are being followed.

kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.title: Surveillance detection route
kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.title: Commercial off-the-shelf tradecraft
kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of how much CIA field equipment is simply bought rather than built. He describes the pen recorder arriving while he was in Pakistan and early GPS units in Athens being repurposed to map surveillance detection routes, and states the underlying economics: buying existing technology is far cheaper than developing it from scratch.

kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.title: Threats against John Kiriakou
kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.summary: The stalkers and death threats John Kiriakou has received since going public in 2007 — including a woman who believed he had proposed to her in code on C-SPAN and arrived at his office armed, and a caller who recited his son's home address.

kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.title: Kiriakou's television pilots
kiriakou-islamabad-surveillance-incident.summary: The eight television pilots John Kiriakou has sold since 2007 as a hobby, beginning with Bomb Squad, a procedural about the New York City bomb squad built around a statistic that almost no bomb threat has anything to do with terrorism — alongside a parallel career as a script adviser on The Bourne Ultimatum, Kill the Messenger and CBS's True Lies, an MGM pilot conceived in prison, and a History Channel series developed with Oliver Stone from one chapter of his first book.

kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.title: Consulting job entrapment offers
kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.summary: John Kiriakou's claim that he receives a steady stream of emails and telephone calls offering him work — always consulting — that he reads as attempts to bait him into violating federal law, and which he says happens all the time.

kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.title: Phone microphone ad targeting
kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.summary: John Kiriakou's account of a spoken telephone conversation about concealed carry permits being followed, five minutes later, by a Facebook feed in which every single advertisement was for a concealed carry class — offered as evidence for his claim that the platforms go further than they admit and listen when the phone is turned off.

kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.title: Generals in national security posts
kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.summary: John Kiriakou''s blanket objection to putting retired generals in charge of the CIA, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the Defense Department or the National Security Council, resting on a single argument about how officers reach flag rank: generals became generals by saying ''yes sir'', and what a president needs is somebody who can tell him why an idea is terrible.

kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.title: Kamala Harris
kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.summary: Vice President under Joe Biden and 2024 Democratic presidential nominee; per John Kiriakou, installed as the party's nominee without a competitive primary despite having failed to reach the 2020 Iowa caucus, and closed out her 2024 campaign courting the Cheney family as a symbol of American values. Kiriakou, a lifelong progressive, says her pursuit of Dick Cheney's endorsement is what decided him against voting for her.

kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.title: Kiriakou's Greek citizenship
kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.summary: The Greek nationality John Kiriakou acquired in 2010, after his CIA career and before his prosecution — offered, he says, by the Greek ambassador who asked what could be done to help when his troubles began, and granted when he answered "you could give me Greek citizenship." Held by his children too, it made him a Greek national at the moment he became, in Greece, a national hero; it brought him the commission to write the country's whistleblower protection law, and the Athens job that turned out to be a money laundering operation.

kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.title: The Backstory
kiriakou-legal-counteroffensive.summary: The daily Radio Sputnik programme John Kiriakou co-hosted with Lee Stranahan, carried on terrestrial radio in the Washington area as well as online. It was the successor to his earlier show Loud and Clear with Brian Becker, and he described its format as two men with a beer talking about the day.

kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.title: Kiriakou's Abraham Lincoln collection
kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.summary: John Kiriakou''s private collection of Abraham Lincoln relics, assembled at auction over many years and governed by a strict standard of provenance: a blood-soaked fragment of the pillowcase Lincoln died on, wallpaper from the Petersen House death room, a swatch of Mary Todd Lincoln''s funeral dress, and wood from the gallows on which the conspirators were hanged.

kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.title: Lincoln's last turd
kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.summary: A purported piece of human waste attributed by a Pennsylvania circus-freak-show museum to Abraham Lincoln on the night of his assassination; auctioned for $5,000; subsequent DNA analysis disproved the attribution. John Kiriakou's failed bid for the artifact is the anecdote that, recirculated in early 2026, made him an internet meme figure.

kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.title: 1953 Iran coup
kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.summary: The U.S.- and UK-backed overthrow of Iran's democratically elected prime minister, Mohammad Mossadegh; per John Kiriakou, the coup served British national interests rather than American ones, and the subsequent outlawing of secular political opposition under the Shah forced dissent into the mosques — producing a religious rather than secular revolution in 1979.

kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.title: AIPAC
kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.title: Aldrich Ames
kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.summary: Senior CIA officer — a GS-15 who rose to chief of counterintelligence for the Soviet branch — who spied for the KGB for nine years. Per John Kiriakou, Ames walked into the Soviet embassy in Washington in April 1985 and sold the identities of two CIA-recruited double agents for $50,000 to clear a debt run up by his second marriage; both were executed. He went on to identify more than thirty agents, compromise over a hundred clandestine operations, cause at least twelve deaths and take more than $2 million, while being known throughout the agency as a daily drunk and promoted at every turn. The KGB protected him with a decoy mole hunt; analyst Sandy Grimes caught him by matching his handler meetings to his bank deposits.

kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.title: Amaryllis Fox Kennedy
kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip.summary: Former CIA non-official-cover officer who worked under commercial cover as an international art consultant, later a Trump campaign manager and nominee for deputy CIA director. Per John Kiriakou, Senator Tom Cotton threatened to filibuster her appointment; the president responded by naming her deputy national security adviser instead — a job Kiriakou considers more powerful, since the CIA director reports to the national security adviser.

kiriakou-morning-reading-list.title: Consortium News
kiriakou-morning-reading-list.summary: Independent investigative news outlet John Kiriakou has written for since at least 2017, founded by Polk Award-winning journalist Robert Parry, who broke major stories on Iran-Contra. Kiriakou's columns there have covered John Bolton's exit, the entrapment of Maria Butina, his own first tour in Saudi Arabia and the 2019 Ukraine-call whistleblower. He says PayPal permanently shuttered the outlet's account and briefly seized its funds before backing down under public pressure, while still refusing to reinstate it.

kiriakou-morning-reading-list.title: CovertAction Magazine
kiriakou-morning-reading-list.summary: The muckraking outlet "exposing covert action since 1978" — and one of John Kiriakou's three long-running syndicated column homes, alongside Consortium News and ScheerPost. Kiriakou joined its podcast arm, the CovertAction Bulletin, appearing on panels with Peter Dale Scott and Pepe Escobar, and jokes that the Pentagon's browser-plugin credibility warnings — red check marks against outlets like CovertAction — are the surest sign it's worth reading.

kiriakou-morning-reading-list.title: The Cat in the Hat and Truck
kiriakou-morning-reading-list.summary: The prison anecdote John Kiriakou uses to illustrate the CIA counter-accusation tradecraft he applied at FCI Loretto, a cellmate applicant called Cat in the Hat named him a rat to a serial killer named Truck within earshot; Kiriakou answered by remarking Cat in the Hat had earlier called Truck a pedophile; Truck beat Cat in the Hat almost to death and had to be lifelighted by helicopter to Pittsburgh.

kiriakou-morning-reading-list.title: Kiriakou's writing process
kiriakou-morning-reading-list.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of how he actually writes — books in waves over roughly nine months, op-eds in forty-five minutes to an hour once an idea has sat for a few days, and a habit of getting up at two in the morning to write one because he cannot sleep. He wrote *Remains of the Day* in six weeks during COVID, losing whole evenings to it: "I look at the clock again, it''s 2:00 in the morning. I''m like, oh my god, what happened?"

kiriakou-morning-reading-list.title: Active measures
kiriakou-morning-reading-list.summary: The in-house name John Kiriakou gives to the CIA branch responsible for propaganda and for countering hostile propaganda — a division he describes as running twenty-four hours a day, paired with an opposing anti-active-measures branch, and as the ancestor of the political action group that remains the agency's clandestine propaganda arm.

kiriakou-morning-reading-list.title: Advice to the next generation
kiriakou-morning-reading-list.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to a Gen Z viewer who said he felt helpless — that helplessness is not new, that 1968 and 1969 were worse, and that the remedy is four concrete things: run for any office at all, starting with the local water board; demonstrate; ride your elected officials and vote them out if they will not do what they are told; and write.

kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.title: MOSSAD
kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.title: October 7 attack
kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.summary: John Kiriakou's analysis of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack as a policy failure, not an intelligence one — Israel was warned repeatedly, but Itamar Ben-Gvir diverted response forces to the West Bank, and Kiriakou believes Israel welcomed a pretext for overwhelming retaliation.

kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.title: Abraham Accords
kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.title: Israeli torture of Palestinian prisoners
kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.summary: John Kiriakou's account of systematic abuse in Israeli detention after October 7 — thousands held, whistleblower reports of forced amputations, and a prison-wide rule that Palestinian inmates must crawl rather than walk, on pain of being beaten with rebar.

kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.title: AIPAC
kiriakou-mother-israel-trip.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

kiriakou-non-person.title: Edward Snowden
kiriakou-non-person.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

kiriakou-non-person.title: Espionage Act
kiriakou-non-person.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

kiriakou-non-person.title: Abu Zubaydah
kiriakou-non-person.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

kiriakou-non-person.title: Ali Soufan
kiriakou-non-person.summary: FBI special agent who handled Abu Zubaydah immediately after his March 2002 capture; through patient, respectful interrogation produced the only actionable intelligence ever obtained from the detainee, including the first identification of "Mukhtar" as Khalid Sheikh Mohammed.

kiriakou-non-person.title: Deuce Martinez
kiriakou-non-person.summary: The former CIA analyst whose business card was the basis of two of the three Espionage Act charges brought against John Kiriakou. Kiriakou scanned and emailed the card — which showed Martinez had gone to work for Mitchell and Jessen, the firm of the torture programme's architects — to a New York Times reporter and later to an ABC News reporter. The judge threw the espionage counts out.

kiriakou-non-person.title: Eric Holder
kiriakou-non-person.summary: Attorney General of the United States under Barack Obama, and the head of the Justice Department that reopened and then brought the 2012 prosecution of John Kiriakou. In Kiriakou's account Holder personally doubted that the espionage charge was sound, told John Brennan so in writing, and signed off on it anyway.

kiriakou-omega-seamaster.title: Abu Omar rendition
kiriakou-omega-seamaster.summary: The CIA's kidnapping of a Milan cleric, Abu Omar, who was sent to Egypt to be tortured; John Kiriakou calls it a case that ought to be taught at the CIA as how not to run a rendition, and it is what ultimately sent him to prison, after he confirmed a former colleague's surname to a journalist claiming to be writing a book about it.

kiriakou-omega-seamaster.title: Brian Ross
kiriakou-omega-seamaster.summary: American investigative journalist and seven-time Emmy Award winner who was a prominent reporter at ABC News when, in December 2007, he conducted the on-camera interview with John Kiriakou that produced the first public confirmation by a U.S. official that the CIA waterboarded prisoners. Per Kiriakou, Ross called him out of the blue with the assertion that a source said Kiriakou had personally tortured Abu Zubaydah; Kiriakou's decision to give the interview anyway — driven by the conclusion that 'Brian Ross's source is at the White House and they're going to pin this on me' — became the pivot point of his entire post-CIA life.

kiriakou-omega-seamaster.title: Gavin Newsom
kiriakou-omega-seamaster.summary: The California governor John Kiriakou described in 2023 as the consummate Democratic Party insider waiting his turn — a Pelosi relative who married into the Brown family, doing everything the Biden operation asked of him, including a pointless surrogate trip to Idaho, on the calculation that Joe Biden would not reach the nominating convention.

kiriakou-omega-seamaster.title: Human Rights Watch
kiriakou-omega-seamaster.summary: The organization whose 2005 report that the CIA was torturing its prisoners — two years before John Kiriakou''s ABC interview — anchors his defense that he confirmed rather than revealed the program. It is also the middle link in the chain that ended in his arrest: working with the John Adams Project, Human Rights Watch employed the investigator who carried a classified name from journalist Matthew Cole to the Guantánamo defense attorneys, and when the FBI walked that chain backwards it arrived at Kiriakou''s door.

kiriakou-omega-seamaster.title: Jim Jordan
kiriakou-omega-seamaster.summary: Republican congressman from Ohio and chairman of the House Judiciary Committee. John Kiriakou describes a genuinely divided view of him: one of only four members of Congress he names as a friend of whistleblowers, and simultaneously the chairman whose Weaponization subcommittee he says is a partisan counterfeit of the Church Committee — with the whole question settled against Jordan by the Ohio State wrestlers who told him their team doctor was abusing them.

kiriakou-omega-seamaster.title: Jon Ossoff
kiriakou-omega-seamaster.summary: United States senator from Georgia, whom John Kiriakou places among the rare honest figures on Capitol Hill and grades at the top of his case-officer rankings. Kiriakou also notes a family connection to the wartime liberation of Greece.

kiriakou-on-animated-television.title: Ali from Newark
kiriakou-on-animated-television.summary: The Black shot caller at FCI Loretto, near the end of a twenty-five-year drug sentence, who came to embrace John Kiriakou at the close of his term and tell him how much he respected him — a friendship possible only because Kiriakou had decided on arrival to ignore the prison's racial divisions.

kiriakou-on-animated-television.title: Bezalel Smotrich
kiriakou-on-animated-television.summary: Israeli far-right minister whom John Kiriakou, alongside Itamar Ben-Gvir, blames for leaving Israel unprepared on October 7 by insisting any attack would come from the West Bank rather than Gaza.

kiriakou-on-animated-television.title: Candace Owens
kiriakou-on-animated-television.summary: The commentator whose claims about the killing of Charlie Kirk John Kiriakou has publicly declined to accept. He credits her reach and her intelligence and rejects her method, citing an earlier occasion — a conference call he says he was on — at which she claimed irrefutable proof that the Italian government had stolen the 2020 election and that its release would return Donald Trump to office.

kiriakou-on-animated-television.title: Clyde Hall
kiriakou-on-animated-television.summary: The imprisoned Ohio congressman John Kiriakou says served at his prison a few years before him, whose remark on release — that he had made some of the best friends of his life inside — Kiriakou thought insane at the time and came to understand after his own sentence.

kiriakou-on-animated-television.title: Drunken border guards
kiriakou-on-animated-television.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for how quiet frontiers become shooting wars — bored, drinking troops with nothing to do and no supervision — which he applies to the Thailand-Cambodia clashes, to the India-China line, and to why Vladimir Putin objects to a NATO country on his border.

kiriakou-on-animated-television.title: France recognises Palestine
kiriakou-on-animated-television.summary: Emmanuel Macron's decision in July 2025 to extend formal recognition to the Republic of Palestine and exchange ambassadors, which John Kiriakou called a turning point that could not be overstated — the first serious crack in Western support for Israel, and significant precisely because France is a historic colonial power in the Middle East with a Security Council veto.

kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.title: Mass Surveillance
kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.summary: Kiriakou says the NSA has dropped any pretext of protecting civil liberties, warehousing every call, text and email in the Utah desert.

kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.title: Purchased data as a warrant workaround
kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.summary: John Kiriakou's account of U.S. federal agencies buying Americans' personal data from social-media platforms and data brokers rather than seeking a warrant — a practice he describes as an ethical and legal problem likely to reach the Supreme Court, and one in which no judge is aware a case is being built.

kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.title: Panquake
kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.summary: Open-source, blockchain-based social platform developed by the Iceland-registered company Talk Liberation, for which John Kiriakou has served as brand ambassador since 2020. Kiriakou describes it as advertising-free, subscription-funded, free of back doors, and run on servers powered by Icelandic geothermal steam — a project he frames as a David-and-Goliath fight against banks, big technology and governments.

kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.title: WLDragnet
kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.summary: Free search tool documenting U.S. defense contractors' monitoring of social-media users by political affiliation. John Kiriakou says a search of his own name in the tool's beta showed Northrop Grumman had queried him hundreds of times, and that his attorneys used the data in separate litigation against the company.

kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.title: Clock Tower X
kiriakou-on-artificial-intelligence.summary: The American firm John Kiriakou described as being paid $6 million by the Israeli government to make ChatGPT more pro-Israeli by generating content, gaming algorithms and managing AI frameworks.

kiriakou-on-christmas.title: Kiriakou's Abraham Lincoln collection
kiriakou-on-christmas.summary: John Kiriakou''s private collection of Abraham Lincoln relics, assembled at auction over many years and governed by a strict standard of provenance: a blood-soaked fragment of the pillowcase Lincoln died on, wallpaper from the Petersen House death room, a swatch of Mary Todd Lincoln''s funeral dress, and wood from the gallows on which the conspirators were hanged.

kiriakou-on-christmas.title: Bahrain Posting (1994–1996)
kiriakou-on-christmas.summary: John Kiriakou's 1994–1996 assignment to Bahrain under U.S. State Department cover as second secretary for economic affairs — arriving with his wife Joanne and infant son Chris on August 1, 1994, into a tiny Gulf monarchy whose sectarian tensions erupted, two months later, into the first Intifada.

kiriakou-on-christmas.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kiriakou-on-christmas.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kiriakou-on-christmas.title: David Ransom
kiriakou-on-christmas.summary: U.S. Ambassador to Bahrain during the period of John Kiriakou's posting there; characterized by Kiriakou as one of the finest people he worked for in his CIA career

kiriakou-on-christmas.title: Donald Trump
kiriakou-on-christmas.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

kiriakou-on-christmas.title: Ed Schultz
kiriakou-on-christmas.summary: American broadcaster, a friend of John Kiriakou''s and later his colleague at RT, whom Kiriakou cites twice over: as a man forbidden by MSNBC to discuss Bernie Sanders during a primary, and as a dead man still being labelled a Russian government mouthpiece four years after his death.

kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.title: Kiriakou's gastrectomy
kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.summary: The experimental operation John Kiriakou paid for with a bank loan in September 2022, in which his stomach was removed to reverse an uncontrolled type 2 diabetes — a procedure he had found in a Lancet paper by a Scottish surgeon, and which cost him 55 kilos and, he says, the disease itself.

kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.title: Operational eating
kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.summary: The two rules John Kiriakou gives about food on operations: that a case officer never orders seafood, and above all never shellfish, because a day spent incapacitated by food poisoning makes him useless to the operation — and that a fourteen-hour surveillance can be run on nothing but a container of mango juice.

kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.title: Kiriakou's type 2 diabetes
kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.summary: The disease John Kiriakou was diagnosed with after leaving the CIA for a desk job, which he first fought down with a nutritionist's diet and a 70-pound weight loss, then lost ground to when insulin slowed his metabolism to a halt — reaching an A1C of 12.1 before he had his stomach removed to end it.

kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.title: Kiriakou on Greek and Cypriot food
kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.summary: The verdict John Kiriakou delivered on Cypriot cooking during a 2026 visit to the island — that its cheeses are more sophisticated and more distinct from one another than Greece's, where most are variations on a theme — together with his coffee positions, his conversion from frappé by a cousin in Rhodes, and his complaint about the size of the straw.

kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.title: The glyburide incident
kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.summary: The episode John Kiriakou described in a Letter from Loretto of 12 September 2014: handed a bottle of glyburide by the prison pharmacy without explanation, he crashed twice and passed out on the floor — and his physician father-in-law told him the drug could have put him into heart failure.

kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-on-diet-and-nutrition.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.title: Kiriakou on travel
kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.summary: John Kiriakou''s own ranking of the countries he has visited: Greece his favourite and, he insists, the best food anywhere; Oman the most beautiful landscape; Syria the most extraordinary civilisation; and Chile the cheapest, illustrated by a bottle of a vineyard''s locked-away reserve that cost $8.50 on his honeymoon.

kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.title: There is no such thing as bad food in Athens
kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.summary: The lesson John Kiriakou says he learned at a lorry drivers' stop outside Corinth, where the food was as good as his grandmother's — reached on the three-and-a-half-hour drives he made to meet a source too sensitive to be met in Athens, with a vineyard tour as his cover story.

kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.title: Kiriakou's Cypriot ancestry
kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.summary: The DNA result showing John Kiriakou to be 24 per cent Cypriot — his largest single ancestry — which corrected a family belief that the line came from Crete and coincided with an invitation to address a Cypriot diaspora conference.

kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.title: Kiriakou on diet and nutrition
kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.summary: John Kiriakou''s views on eating, given to a Cypriot nutrition interviewer who challenged several of them: that the worst dietary advice he ever heard was to cut fat and cholesterol, that the American sugar lobby spent decades persuading the public that fat was the enemy, and that at his age carbohydrates are the enemy instead.

kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.title: Operational eating
kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.summary: The two rules John Kiriakou gives about food on operations: that a case officer never orders seafood, and above all never shellfish, because a day spent incapacitated by food poisoning makes him useless to the operation — and that a fourteen-hour surveillance can be run on nothing but a container of mango juice.

kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.title: Kiriakou's gastrectomy
kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.summary: The experimental operation John Kiriakou paid for with a bank loan in September 2022, in which his stomach was removed to reverse an uncontrolled type 2 diabetes — a procedure he had found in a Lancet paper by a Scottish surgeon, and which cost him 55 kilos and, he says, the disease itself.

kiriakou-on-soccer.title: The 2026 World Cup final
kiriakou-on-soccer.summary: Spain''s victory over Argentina in a final John Kiriakou described as dirty on the losers'' part and notable for a red card, and the awkwardness that followed: Donald Trump, who had exerted considerable influence over FIFA and whose country was hosting, had to present the trophy to a nation whose leadership he had spent weeks publicly attacking. The Spanish press cropped him out of the celebration photographs.

kiriakou-on-soccer.title: Acts of Service
kiriakou-on-soccer.summary: The Doja Cat song that John Kiriakou discovered, through a Cameo request, had become the soundtrack to a genre of montage about him. The clips set to it use footage from before his weight loss — he lost 77 pounds by 2007 and 115 pounds from 2022 — and he says he cannot watch them.

kiriakou-on-soccer.title: 2026 Iran war
kiriakou-on-soccer.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

kiriakou-on-soccer.title: Strait of Hormuz
kiriakou-on-soccer.summary: The shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Persian Gulf, and the centre of gravity of the 2026 Iran war in John Kiriakou''s account — a strait whose only navigable deep water lies on the Iranian side of the maritime border, closed not by Iran''s aggression but, as he insists, by the American and Israeli attack that provoked it: "The Strait of Hormuz was open. We''re the ones that forced the closure."

kiriakou-on-soccer.title: The General Assembly circus
kiriakou-on-soccer.summary: John Kiriakou's view of the annual United Nations General Assembly, which he calls the Super Bowl for global politics and which he disliked more than almost anything else in his CIA career. His last tour was at the United Nations in New York, where the September session brings the city to a halt and makes the American mission almost unreachable.

kiriakou-on-soccer.title: The Pentagon injury figures
kiriakou-on-soccer.summary: John Kiriakou''s explanation of why the Pentagon was able to withhold news of dozens of American casualties in the Iran war: not secrecy law, but the absence of any statute requiring disclosure. In his framing Congress is asleep at the switch, having never passed such a law, so the department reports nothing it is not obliged to report.

kiriakou-on-travel.title: Kiriakou on Greek and Cypriot food
kiriakou-on-travel.summary: The verdict John Kiriakou delivered on Cypriot cooking during a 2026 visit to the island — that its cheeses are more sophisticated and more distinct from one another than Greece's, where most are variations on a theme — together with his coffee positions, his conversion from frappé by a cousin in Rhodes, and his complaint about the size of the straw.

kiriakou-on-travel.title: Oman
kiriakou-on-travel.summary: The Gulf sultanate John Kiriakou singles out as America's most durable friend in the region and its most useful channel to Iran — a country that has acted as go-between for Washington and Tehran many times, and which he argues should be approached again in place of carrier deployments and public threats.

kiriakou-on-travel.title: The Dublin compensation
kiriakou-on-travel.summary: The night John Kiriakou spent in Dublin at an airline's expense after a mechanical fault in Madrid cost him his connection — a four-star hotel, an expedited check-in, a shuttle bus and half his fare refunded into his checking account six weeks later — offered as the standard American passengers do not get.

kiriakou-on-travel.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-on-wine.title: John Kerry
kiriakou-on-wine.summary: U.S. Senator from Massachusetts; chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee during John Kiriakou's 2009 service as the committee's senior investigator; subsequently U.S. Secretary of State; characterized by Kiriakou as a coward who buckled under CIA pressure on the Dasht-i-Leili reopening and as personally fixated on his perceived theft of the Secretary of State position by Hillary Clinton; the famously thrown medals were duplicates purchased at the post exchange.

kiriakou-on-wine.title: Central Intelligence Agency
kiriakou-on-wine.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

kiriakou-on-wine.title: Dick Cheney
kiriakou-on-wine.summary: U.S. Vice President under George W. Bush. Per John Kiriakou — recounting CIA Director George Tenet's memoir — Cheney intercepted the presidential finding authorizing the CIA's enhanced interrogation program in the Oval Office anteroom and took it from Tenet before Bush could sign it. Tenet later concluded the president probably never actually signed the finding and probably told the truth when he said he had no idea the program was taking place. Kiriakou characterizes Cheney as the one who actually ran foreign policy, intelligence policy, and defense policy during the Bush years.

kiriakou-on-wine.title: Intelligence peddlers
kiriakou-on-wine.summary: John Kiriakou''s breakdown of who actually walks into an American embassy offering information: the overwhelming majority are fabricators or probes, a few per cent are peddlers selling the same nugget to five embassies in a month, and about one per cent are the real thing.

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: Mar-a-Lago pardon pitch
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: The lunch at which John Kiriakou put his pardon request directly to Donald Trump. Flown to Palm Beach by a wealthy friend who also wanted a pardon, Kiriakou delivered a prepared line as the president worked the dining room, was told to take it to Pam Bondi, and was afterwards vouched for on a speakerphone call to Trump by a political fixer who then asked him for $25,000 a month until the pardon came through.

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: The hundred-and-fifty-foot limousine
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: A detail John Kiriakou recalls from his years as a congressional staffer — that Mitch McConnell lived in a townhouse four doors from the Hart Senate Office Building, roughly a hundred and fifty feet away, and took a limousine to work every morning anyway, to be booed by staff as he passed.

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: Josh Shapiro
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: Governor of Pennsylvania; veteran of the Israel Defense Forces, in which he served during his late-teen kibbutz year before returning to U.S. citizenship; cited by John Kiriakou as the principal example of the loyalty question raised by American elected officials who have served the Israeli state — a disqualification Kiriakou states in absolute terms, and one he judges to have ended Shapiro's national prospects.

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: Mossad networks in Iran
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: The Israeli human-intelligence penetration of Iran that John Kiriakou calls larger than anyone suspected — thousands of clandestine reporters, many of them undocumented Afghan refugees paid the equivalent of fifty or a hundred dollars a month, run in person by spymasters inside the country and compartmentalized so that rolling up one network yields nothing about the others.

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: "It''s either him or it''s Manning"
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: John Kiriakou's account of why Barack Obama commuted Chelsea Manning's sentence — that Joe Biden, lobbied by a wealthy Greek-American businessman, argued Kiriakou's clemency case to the president directly, and that Obama cut the discussion off ten minutes in by saying he would do one or the other but not both. Kiriakou's conclusion is that the commutation was an arithmetic judgement about a 35-year sentence rather than an act of conscience.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: The TikTok fan edits
kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: The short-form videos made by a University of Texas sophomore, giving John Kiriakou a chipmunk voice and laser eyes, which reached Gen Z at scale and led within weeks to representation by a major talent agency and meetings about film and television.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: Abu Zubaydah
kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: Bureau of Prisons advisory board
kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: The advisory board John Kiriakou joined at the personal invitation of the Director of the Bureau of Prisons, who told him the president had tasked him with tearing the Bureau down and rebuilding it.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: The Green Line in Nicosia
