kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: The division of Nicosia between the Republic of Cyprus and the Turkish-occupied north, which John Kiriakou toured in July 2026 and described as maintained through deliberate humiliation rather than any interest in settlement.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: Diary of a CEO — January 2026 Kiriakou interview
kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: The January 2026 long-form appearance by John Kiriakou on Steven Bartlett's Diary of a CEO podcast that a University of Texas at Austin sophomore then cut into TikTok shorts — sped and slowed, with lasers added — kicking off the Gen Z discovery of Kiriakou that pushed his cameo requests past 1,900 and drew a 2:30 a.m. representation call in Dubai from the Creative Artists Agency; Kiriakou treats it as the pivot after which stories he had been telling for nineteen years finally landed.

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: Kiriakou's gastrectomy
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: The experimental operation John Kiriakou paid for with a bank loan in September 2022, in which his stomach was removed to reverse an uncontrolled type 2 diabetes — a procedure he had found in a Lancet paper by a Scottish surgeon, and which cost him 55 kilos and, he says, the disease itself.

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: Kiriakou's type 2 diabetes
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: The disease John Kiriakou was diagnosed with after leaving the CIA for a desk job, which he first fought down with a nutritionist's diet and a 70-pound weight loss, then lost ground to when insulin slowed his metabolism to a halt — reaching an A1C of 12.1 before he had his stomach removed to end it.

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: The glyburide incident
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: The episode John Kiriakou described in a Letter from Loretto of 12 September 2014: handed a bottle of glyburide by the prison pharmacy without explanation, he crashed twice and passed out on the floor — and his physician father-in-law told him the drug could have put him into heart failure.

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: Kiriakou on diet and nutrition
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: John Kiriakou''s views on eating, given to a Cypriot nutrition interviewer who challenged several of them: that the worst dietary advice he ever heard was to cut fat and cholesterol, that the American sugar lobby spent decades persuading the public that fat was the enemy, and that at his age carbohydrates are the enemy instead.

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: Cofer Black
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: Former head of the CIA Counterterrorism Center during and immediately after the September 11 attacks; principal architect of the agency's paramilitary turn on September 12, 2001; later Vice President of Blackwater under Erik Prince.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: Bureau of Prisons
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: The federal agency that ran John Kiriakou's incarceration — and one of his most persistent post-prison targets. The BOP overrode his judge's camp recommendation by deeming him "a threat to the public safety," threatened him with "diesel therapy" until 1,600 logged phone calls and letters from a dozen House members and two senators backed it off, and, per Kiriakou, functions as "an employment agency for unemployable semi-literate rural white men" and "a dumping ground for failed medical professionals" — an agency for which a prisoner's death is cheaper than his treatment.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: FCI Loretto
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: Ghislaine Maxwell
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: British socialite and convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, her father Robert Maxwell was a prolific Mossad spy, and she is the likely conduit through whom Jeffrey Epstein was introduced to and recruited by Mossad.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: Julian Assange
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: Jeffrey Epstein
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: Brad Birkenfeld
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: The UBS banking whistleblower, who was prosecuted and imprisoned before winning a $104 million settlement from the Treasury Department and spending it on the legal defence of other whistleblowers. John Kiriakou uses him as the measure of the gap between financial and national-security whistleblowing, and names him among the visitors whose devices he believes were copied at the Ecuadorian embassy in London.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Prison racial segregation
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the rigid racial and ethnic division of American prisons — a cafeteria split like the 1950s South — and his argument that segregating and hardening inmates for years, then releasing them with no skills, makes society less safe.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Abraham Accords
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Alan Dershowitz
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: American attorney and Harvard Law professor; John Kiriakou describes debating him on Piers Morgan's show over Jeffrey Epstein, telling Dershowitz he would have wanted to see him "hanging from a tree" had he sought leniency for Epstein as an Israeli spy — and cites attorney David Boies's on-air statement that Dershowitz was far more than Epstein's lawyer, also serving as his publicist, friend, and a guest on Epstein's island.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Arabic and Greek
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: The qualification John Kiriakou says opened the door to his transfer from CIA analysis to operations: a post in Athens wanted Greek or Arabic, and he had both — by most of his tellings the only officer in the agency who did. The chief who hired him gave the reason in one sentence: it is easier and cheaper to take a linguist and teach him operations than the other way round. The pairing also became a detection tool, since the language nobody speaks in Pakistan is Arabic.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Arianna Huffington
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: Founder of the Huffington Post and the accidental amplifier who turned John Kiriakou's prison writing into a phenomenon. His first Letter from Loretto went to his attorney, then to a friend running Firedoglake who — unknown to Kiriakou — was close to Huffington; she plastered it as a banner headline and it drew over a million hits, bringing CNN and 60 Minutes to the prison gates. She published his open letter to Snowden, ran the diesel-therapy exposé that triggered the "hands off John Kiriakou" campaign, and came to Loretto herself with two young journalists.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Arrais Corporation
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: Private intelligence firm; companion entity to The Analysis Corporation; originally an LLC pass-through for retired Senior Intelligence Service personnel from the CIA's operations side; subsequently acquired by IBM for over $1 billion.

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: Kiriakou's writing process
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of how he actually writes — books in waves over roughly nine months, op-eds in forty-five minutes to an hour once an idea has sat for a few days, and a habit of getting up at two in the morning to write one because he cannot sleep. He wrote *Remains of the Day* in six weeks during COVID, losing whole evenings to it: "I look at the clock again, it''s 2:00 in the morning. I''m like, oh my god, what happened?"

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: Admiral William Crowe
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: Former Chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff and former CENTCOM commander who had lived in Bahrain, author of the "pound for pound" formula every Bahraini and every American ambassador quotes, and the visiting dignitary John Kiriakou was assigned to escort — a week that ended with the Bahraini Prime Minister refusing to let go of Kiriakou's hand.

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: Bahrain Posting (1994–1996)
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: John Kiriakou's 1994–1996 assignment to Bahrain under U.S. State Department cover as second secretary for economic affairs — arriving with his wife Joanne and infant son Chris on August 1, 1994, into a tiny Gulf monarchy whose sectarian tensions erupted, two months later, into the first Intifada.

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: Global Response Staff
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: The CIA's protective-security program for case officers operating in high-threat environments; run for the agency by Blackwater; especially active in Baghdad's Green Zone during the Iraq War, where movement between fixed locations was treated as life-threatening.

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: Hawala system
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: Informal, ledger-based money-transfer network used across the Middle East, South Asia, and their diasporas to move funds without involving banks; per John Kiriakou's first-person account of testing one in the UAE — handing $50 to a grocer for a 16-digit number to redeem at an Arabic bakery in Bethesda, Maryland — completely untraceable; identified by Kiriakou (later, as Chief Investigator on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee) as one of the principal channels through which al-Qaeda moved operational money in the post-9/11 period, along with DHL.

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: John Walker Lindh
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: American citizen captured while fighting alongside the Taliban in late 2001, present at the Qala-i-Jangi fortress at the start of the prisoner uprising that killed CIA officer Mike Spann. In John Kiriakou's account his case matters less for what Lindh did than for what was done around him — the false claim that he had been read his rights, the destruction of the career of the Justice Department lawyer who said so, and his place on the docket of the one judge who reserves national-security cases for herself.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: Julian Assange
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: Maria Butina
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: Russian gun-rights activist convicted in the United States of failing to register as a foreign agent; John Kiriakou cites her case as an example of the "process crime" of FARA violations, contrasting the severity of her 18-month solitary-confinement sentence with federal guidelines calling for 0-6 months.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: NewsGuard
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: A media-rating organization, founded by the former head of Court TV and a former Wall Street Journal publisher, that scores news outlets 0-100 for reliability. Per John Kiriakou, NewsGuard docks any outlet that takes a position on Ukraine or Syria contrary to its preferred line, is subscribed to mostly by government entities (chiefly the Pentagon), and singled out Consortium News, the Grayzone, Antiwar.com, and ScheerPost over their criticism of U.S. policy — prompting a First Amendment lawsuit.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: McCain-Feinstein Amendment
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: 2015 amendment, sponsored by Senator John McCain, that formally and permanently banned torture by U.S. government personnel, codifying the Army Field Manual as the single interrogation standard for all agencies. Per John Kiriakou, it restored the original language of the 1946 Federal Torture Act after U.S. policy had drifted from it through post-9/11 reinterpretation — and passed, he says, in part because of his own 2007 whistleblowing.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: Abolish the CIA
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: John Kiriakou's position that the CIA should be abolished because its functions are already duplicated by the other 17 U.S. intelligence agencies — analysis by the State Department, human spying by the Pentagon, technology by DARPA, NSA and the private sector.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: The CIA Insider's Guide to Surveillance and Surveillance Detection
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: Book by John Kiriakou drawing on his experience as a surveillance detection instructor at the CIA and as a private surveillance training consultant. The book covers the techniques used by intelligence professionals to identify whether they are being followed — including the four-phase surveillance detection route, concealment device placement and retrieval, and counter-surveillance strategy — adapted for use by corporate executives, journalists, and others who want to confirm whether they are being followed.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: FCI Loretto
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: Hunter Biden Laptop
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of the Hunter Biden laptop controversy — he saw nothing related to child sex abuse in the material but says the Biden family, particularly Hunter, has serious documented substance-abuse problems; and that the 2020 open letter in which 51 former intelligence officials called the story a Russian/KGB-style operation used deliberately hedged, CIA-trained language and was later shown (per Michael Morell's testimony) to have been solicited by the Biden campaign.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: Imran Khan
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: Former Prime Minister of Pakistan; subsequently deposed and imprisoned; his political party, the PTI (Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf), sent John Kiriakou a formal demand for apology after a November 2025 Indian-media interview in which Kiriakou observed that India would prevail over Pakistan in a conventional conflict; Kiriakou's reply has not been transcribed in polite company.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: J. Edgar Hoover
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: The FBI's founding director — 48 years in the chair — whose opposition nearly strangled the CIA at birth. Per John Kiriakou, Truman lifted Hoover's objection to the National Security Act of 1947 by disingenuously assuring him the CIA would be a division of the FBI; the lie seeded the two agencies' permanent mutual hatred. Kiriakou also credits Hoover with perfecting the annual ritual the CIA later copied — scaring Congress witless and demanding budget increases — and with controlling Hollywood's FBI image so tightly that no film could be made without his approval.

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: One-Time Pad
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: Cipher system in which a secret, random key — shared between sender and receiver — is used to encode a message and then destroyed so that it can never be used again. In traditional shortwave-radio tradecraft, one-time pads enabled spies to broadcast number sequences over public airwaves that only the intended recipient, holding the matching page, could decode. Per John Kiriakou, his lifelong interest in intelligence began at age nine after he picked up KGB number transmissions on a 50-cent shortwave radio.

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: Abu Zubaydah
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: Ali Soufan
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: FBI special agent who handled Abu Zubaydah immediately after his March 2002 capture; through patient, respectful interrogation produced the only actionable intelligence ever obtained from the detainee, including the first identification of "Mukhtar" as Khalid Sheikh Mohammed.

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: Barack Obama
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: 44th U.S. president; in John Kiriakou's account, Obama publicly recounted refusing Benjamin Netanyahu's demand to bomb Iran and calling Israel's threat to use nuclear weapons a bluff — a bluff Kiriakou says Donald Trump later believed.

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: The scholar-in-residence pipeline
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: John Kiriakou's description of retired CIA operations officers taking scholar-in-residence posts at universities and teaching literature courses that function, by their own account, as a recruitment funnel — students enrol knowing the instructor is a former officer and hoping for help getting in.

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: The Islamabad surveillance incident
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: The episode in which John Kiriakou, then the CIA's chief of counterterrorism operations in Pakistan, detected a motorcyclist following him, resolved to kill the man, and discovered on a passing impulse that the surveillance was friendly.

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: The CIA Insider's Guide to Surveillance and Surveillance Detection
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: Book by John Kiriakou drawing on his experience as a surveillance detection instructor at the CIA and as a private surveillance training consultant. The book covers the techniques used by intelligence professionals to identify whether they are being followed — including the four-phase surveillance detection route, concealment device placement and retrieval, and counter-surveillance strategy — adapted for use by corporate executives, journalists, and others who want to confirm whether they are being followed.

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: Surveillance detection route
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: Threats against John Kiriakou
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: The stalkers and death threats John Kiriakou has received since going public in 2007 — including a woman who believed he had proposed to her in code on C-SPAN and arrived at his office armed, and a caller who recited his son's home address.

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: Kiriakou's television pilots
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: The eight television pilots John Kiriakou has sold since 2007 as a hobby, beginning with Bomb Squad, a procedural about the New York City bomb squad built around a statistic that almost no bomb threat has anything to do with terrorism — alongside a parallel career as a script adviser on The Bourne Ultimatum, Kill the Messenger and CBS's True Lies, an MGM pilot conceived in prison, and a History Channel series developed with Oliver Stone from one chapter of his first book.

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: Dead Drop (podcast)
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: John Kiriakou''s narrative podcast, launched in late 2025 — a season-long, memoir-style retelling of his life in intelligence, from recruitment ("The New Recruit") through Athens ("Golden Boy") to the post-9/11 hunt ("The Hunt Begins"), with mini-episodes like "A Spy''s Guide to Sofia." Written by Kiriakou with Alan Katz, produced by Costard & Touchstone Productions, with Kiriakou, Katz, and Nick Mechanic as executive producers. Its stated goal: "the deepest possible perspective on the world of spying and what makes any spy tick."

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: The shooting house
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The live-fire decision course at the Farm where a trainee has about three quarters of a second to decide whether the figure at the window is a gunman or a woman holding a baby — and where John Kiriakou says he never missed, which he connects to his own account of the temperament the CIA selects for.

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: The Farm
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The CIA's clandestine training facility in Virginia; site of approximately 80% of all CIA operational training

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: Counterterrorist driving
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The vehicle training at the Farm — the PIT manoeuvre and how to avoid one, when to ram a roadblock and where to hit it, reversing at sixty miles an hour — conducted in a fleet of junkyard beaters the CIA bought expressly to be wrecked.

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: The hostile border crossing exercise
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The training exercise run before dawn at a closed Dulles Airport in which CIA trainees crossed into the fictional Republic of Victoria — where John Kiriakou talked his way past a US-government-branded pen in his pocket, and the class clown ended up stripped to his underwear.

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: The operations course graduation
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The end of CIA field training: a graduation ceremony at which the whole class wore full disguises for the photograph, and a certificate that is itself classified and therefore cannot be displayed — it stays in the officer''s personnel file.

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: The bomb course
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The week-long CIA explosives course at a facility in another state, where John Kiriakou learned to build a Molotov cocktail, then a detonator rig, then an ammonium nitrate bomb — his final exam, which put a van's transmission three hundred yards into the woods.

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: Edward Snowden
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: Pike Committee
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: U.S. House investigative committee operating in 1975–1976 in parallel with the Senate's Church Committee; per John Kiriakou, the two committees together were the apex — and the last genuine exercise — of congressional oversight of the CIA, staffed by heavyweights and followed by a golden age that lasted only until Iran-Contra. Their work created the permanent House and Senate intelligence committees, which Kiriakou says degraded within a decade into cheerleaders for the agency.

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: Surveillance detection route
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: Situational awareness
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: The discipline John Kiriakou describes as the civilian version of surveillance detection — get out of the kill zone at the first sign of trouble, keep an escape route, and refuse to let the brain rationalise away what it is seeing.

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: Oliver Stone
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: American film director with whom John Kiriakou struck up a friendship after his release from prison. Stone optioned the rights to one chapter of Kiriakou's first book, co-developed an unmade History Channel series with him, blurbed his book on Abu Zubaydah, and was among the public figures who campaigned against the Bureau of Prisons' attempt to shut down Kiriakou's prison blog. The two disagree sharply over whether the CIA killed John F. Kennedy.

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: JFK assassination
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: November 22, 1963 killing of President John F. Kennedy in Dallas, Texas. John Kiriakou's position, drawn from a Pakistan-station encounter with Bay of Pigs commander Jean Gately, an RFK Jr. account of CIA Director John McCone's same-day exchange with Bobby Kennedy Sr., and a White House contact's confirmation that the remaining classified Kennedy documents all contain the word "Israel," is that elements of the CIA were probably involved and that Israeli intelligence was involved as well.

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: Kiriakou's podcast breakthrough
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: The sequence by which John Kiriakou went from saying yes to every podcast request, including from teenagers, to appearances with the largest hosts in the world — a rise he attributes to three friends' shows triggering an algorithm in October 2024.

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: John Kiriakou's Briefing Room
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: A twice-weekly news and commentary programme launched by John Kiriakou in July 2026, presented as analysis rather than partisan opinion, and distinct from his storytelling podcast Dead Drop.

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: 2026 Iran war
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: Abraham Accords
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

kiriakou-titanium-knee.title: Counterterrorist driving
kiriakou-titanium-knee.summary: The vehicle training at the Farm — the PIT manoeuvre and how to avoid one, when to ram a roadblock and where to hit it, reversing at sixty miles an hour — conducted in a fleet of junkyard beaters the CIA bought expressly to be wrecked.

kiriakou-titanium-knee.title: The operations course graduation
kiriakou-titanium-knee.summary: The end of CIA field training: a graduation ceremony at which the whole class wore full disguises for the photograph, and a certificate that is itself classified and therefore cannot be displayed — it stays in the officer''s personnel file.

kiriakou-titanium-knee.title: The Farm
kiriakou-titanium-knee.summary: The CIA's clandestine training facility in Virginia; site of approximately 80% of all CIA operational training

kiriakou-titanium-knee.title: The Advanced Counterterrorism Operations course
kiriakou-titanium-knee.summary: The six-week CIA course for which John Kiriakou says he was one of only about a dozen officers in the entire agency selected — and which he finished, as he puts it, just in time for 9/11.

kiriakou-titanium-knee.title: The shooting house
kiriakou-titanium-knee.summary: The live-fire decision course at the Farm where a trainee has about three quarters of a second to decide whether the figure at the window is a gunman or a woman holding a baby — and where John Kiriakou says he never missed, which he connects to his own account of the temperament the CIA selects for.

kiriakou-titanium-knee.title: The bomb course
kiriakou-titanium-knee.summary: The week-long CIA explosives course at a facility in another state, where John Kiriakou learned to build a Molotov cocktail, then a detonator rig, then an ammonium nitrate bomb — his final exam, which put a van's transmission three hundred yards into the woods.

kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.title: FBI apologies to Kiriakou
kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.summary: John Kiriakou says three FBI agents who worked on his prosecution have written to apologize since his conviction — one saying the case was 'directed and driven by seniormost officials' while mid- and street-level personnel objected, but 'we just followed orders.'

kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.title: PricewaterhouseCoopers
kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.summary: The Big Four accounting firm that keeps intersecting John Kiriakou's story — as a target of the corporate human-source intelligence he collected after leaving the CIA, as the audience of 140 partners he told his Pakistan recruitment story to ("what I did and what you do really isn't that different"), as the auditor that spent three years trying to find the Pentagon's money before giving up, and as the Greek government's book-cooking auditor in the debt crisis, never prosecuted.

kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.title: CIA Arabic hiring practices
kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how few CIA officers historically spoke Arabic — he was one of only two people in the entire agency fluent in both Greek and Arabic — and of how the agency's more recent pool of Arabic speakers, dominated by Arab Christian hires who clear background checks easily, often carries an innate anti-Muslim bias that limits their operational usefulness.

kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.title: World Trade Center
kiriakou-transfer-to-operations.summary: The twin towers whose burning image reached John Kiriakou on the little TV of Cofer Black's secretary — he compared it aloud to the 1930s Empire State Building accident, protested that the day was too clear not to see the tower, and watched the second plane hit as the words left his mouth. Kiriakou ties the towers' story back to the neglected files of the 1990 Kahane assassination and the 1993 bombing, whose captured plotters said they had meant to kill 200,000 by collapsing the buildings into each other — and to John O'Neill, the al-Qaeda-obsessed FBI man who became WTC security chief and died there on his first days at work.

kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.title: Kiriakou's gastrectomy
kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.summary: The experimental operation John Kiriakou paid for with a bank loan in September 2022, in which his stomach was removed to reverse an uncontrolled type 2 diabetes — a procedure he had found in a Lancet paper by a Scottish surgeon, and which cost him 55 kilos and, he says, the disease itself.

kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.title: The glyburide incident
kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.summary: The episode John Kiriakou described in a Letter from Loretto of 12 September 2014: handed a bottle of glyburide by the prison pharmacy without explanation, he crashed twice and passed out on the floor — and his physician father-in-law told him the drug could have put him into heart failure.

kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.title: Kiriakou on diet and nutrition
kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.summary: John Kiriakou''s views on eating, given to a Cypriot nutrition interviewer who challenged several of them: that the worst dietary advice he ever heard was to cut fat and cholesterol, that the American sugar lobby spent decades persuading the public that fat was the enemy, and that at his age carbohydrates are the enemy instead.

kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.title: Kiriakou's post-gastrectomy complications
kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.summary: The aftermath of John Kiriakou''s stomach removal: eighteen months of daily vomiting that turned out to be scar tissue, a diagnosis of malnutrition, and a night on his kitchen floor with a blood pressure of 80 over 52, caused by a blood clot sitting on an ulcer at the surgical site — one hour, his surgeon told him, from being too late.

kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.title: Kiriakou on Greek and Cypriot food
kiriakou-type-2-diabetes.summary: The verdict John Kiriakou delivered on Cypriot cooking during a 2026 visit to the island — that its cheeses are more sophisticated and more distinct from one another than Greece's, where most are variations on a theme — together with his coffee positions, his conversion from frappé by a cousin in Rhodes, and his complaint about the size of the straw.

kiriakou-ufo-sighting.title: New Castle, Pennsylvania
kiriakou-ufo-sighting.summary: John Kiriakou's home town, an hour north of Pittsburgh on the edge of Amish country — a rust-belt city of roughly 40,000 to 50,000 people when he was growing up and around 18,000 to 20,000 now, whose decline he measures by the arrival of DEA and ATF field offices. It is also where, aged eight or nine and hunting salamanders in Oak Park Cemetery, he found the grave of a Medal of Honor private and acquired the lifelong interest in cemeteries that became a book.

kiriakou-ufo-sighting.title: CIA and the UFO question
kiriakou-ufo-sighting.summary: John Kiriakou's consistent answer that UFOs and alien technology are a Pentagon matter, not a CIA one — though he says nearly every former fighter-pilot friend of his has seen something inexplicable, sometimes emerging from the ocean.

kiriakou-ufo-sighting.title: China's base in Djibouti
kiriakou-ufo-sighting.summary: Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti, the abandoned French base the Djiboutians offered to the Americans and the Chinese took a share of — split down the middle by a chain-link fence, the only Chinese military installation outside China, and the centrepiece of John Kiriakou's argument that China is not an expansionist power.

kiriakou-ufo-sighting.title: The Lake Michigan sightings
kiriakou-ufo-sighting.summary: The Netflix-documented Lake Michigan case John Kiriakou raised with a UFO podcaster: National Weather Service employees who watched objects for hours on radar and by eye, the objects avoiding the frozen part of the lake, and the principal witness quitting his job.

kiriakou-ufo-sighting.title: The orb off Yemen
kiriakou-ufo-sighting.summary: A leaked video John Kiriakou describes as the most dramatic UFO material he has seen: two F-18s following a silver orb off the coast of Yemen, given permission to fire, and a missile that hits the object and bounces off before the orb turns ninety degrees and flies on.

kiriakou-ufo-sighting.title: The pilot who saw it drink
kiriakou-ufo-sighting.summary: The F-14 pilot John Kiriakou met at his godfather's Alexandria restaurant in the late 1970s, who described following a cigar-shaped object that submerged, stayed under and came back up — and being told by other pilots that they had all seen the same thing.

kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.title: The Afghan National Police poisoning
kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.summary: An incident John Kiriakou recalls from a 2012 New York Times report and treats as the clearest single illustration of why the American project in Afghanistan failed: at a DynCorp-run training facility that had deliberately mixed recruits from every tribe and region, one recruit poisoned the evening stew and then let four Taliban fighters into the dormitory to stab the survivors in their beds.

kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.title: The Afghan police tribal rotation
kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.summary: An American anti-corruption scheme in Afghanistan that John Kiriakou describes as achieving the reverse of its purpose: someone in the Pentagon decided that regional chiefs of police should come from other tribes in other parts of the country, so a man from Herat would head the police in Kandahar — which only deepened hatred between tribes and did nothing at all about corruption.

kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.title: Chinese overseas police stations
kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.summary: John Kiriakou's account of a New York Times revelation about Chinese nationals with apparent ties to the Chinese police operating out of storefronts around Manhattan and travelling around the United States to threaten Chinese people with reprisals against relatives in Beijing — and his puzzlement that the FBI missed it.

kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.title: Fusha and the Gulf dialect
kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of his own Arabic training — a first year in fusha, high standard Arabic, followed by a second year in khaleeji, the Gulf dialect — and what he reports of both: that Yemen is the only place pure fusha is spoken, that Saudis asked him why he spoke Arabic like Shakespeare, that the Gulf dialect is marked by a hard J other Arabs dislike, and that the Maghreb defeats him entirely.

kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.title: Iran under sanctions: daily life
kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.summary: John Kiriakou's account of being talked out of his own assumptions about Iran by a close friend who travels there once or twice a year and eventually started filming ordinary life — leading him to conclude that a country with no American embassy, diplomatic presence or business presence since 1979 nonetheless lacks for nothing.

kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.title: Kandahar
kiriakou-uk-speaking-tour.summary: The southern Afghan city and province that recurs across John Kiriakou's Afghanistan material — site of one of the two al-Qaeda training camps Abu Zubaydah founded, whose commanders were captured in the same March 2002 raids; the town Bill Clinton said he would have had to destroy, killing 300 innocents, to kill bin Laden in the 1990s; and a stop on Kiriakou's Senate-era heroin-poppy investigation, when the military helicoptered him down before refusing to let him walk the poppy fields.

kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.title: The Saigon CIA station photograph
kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.summary: The Pulitzer-winning image of evacuees climbing a ladder to a helicopter during the fall of Saigon in 1975. John Kiriakou, who talked his way onto the roof in 2026, points out that the building most Americans take for the embassy was in fact an apartment block that secretly housed the CIA's Saigon station.

kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.title: Củ Chi tunnels
kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.summary: The 250-kilometre tunnel network dug by the Viet Cong outside Saigon, which John Kiriakou visited in 2026 and could not physically enter. He attributes the tunnels' viability to the malnutrition of the people who dug them.

kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.title: The McDonald's theory of regime change
kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.summary: John Kiriakou''s argument, drawn from Vietnam and Cuba, that commerce accomplishes what force cannot: to turn a country pro-Western, open a McDonald''s rather than bomb it.

kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.title: Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz
kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.summary: The six demands issued by Iran's Supreme National Security Council in August 2026 as the price of reopening the Strait of Hormuz. John Kiriakou's observation is that they are the old nuclear-deal conditions transposed onto a new lever, and that the transposition is both smart and very difficult for Washington.

kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.title: 2026 Iran war
kiriakou-vietnam-visit-2026.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

kiriakou-weapons-carry.title: The Athens carjacking
kiriakou-weapons-carry.summary: The motorcyclist who followed John Kiriakou''s car through Athens two months into his posting — leading to a gun drawn on a ten-lane intersection, a shot fired, a disabled motorcycle, and a question asked back in Washington: *is John a hothead?*

kiriakou-weapons-carry.title: The Nordeen house
kiriakou-weapons-carry.summary: The embassy housing on Deliyani Street in Athens that John Kiriakou refused on arrival in 1998 — the house outside which the American defence attaché had been blown to pieces by 17 November, his head landing on the neighbouring roof.

kiriakou-weapons-carry.title: Beirut
kiriakou-weapons-carry.summary: The Lebanese capital John Kiriakou confirms was a genuine espionage playground — though he dates the peak to the 1950s through the mid-1970s, when Beirut was the Paris and the banking centre of the Middle East, and when, beneath the CIA, KGB and Israeli presence, "more secretly the French ran the place." He also explains why the enormous new American embassy there is about fortification rather than a regional CIA headquarters.

kiriakou-weapons-carry.title: The El Salvador hotel drill
kiriakou-weapons-carry.summary: A night exercise at the Farm in which trainees sat alone in a mock flea-bag hotel room in El Salvador, were visited by two men announcing housekeeping, and were shot with paint pellets. All eight failed, and the lesson John Kiriakou drew from it he says he never forgot.

kiriakou-weapons-carry.title: Psychiatric evacuation
kiriakou-weapons-carry.summary: The CIA's practice of pulling an officer out of a posting and flying him home when he breaks down — known inside the agency as being psychovac'd — and the desk-bound evaluation period that follows before he is allowed to travel again.

kiriakou-weapons-carry.title: The Clinton asset purge
kiriakou-weapons-carry.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the human-rights screening ordered in the first days of the Clinton administration, under which the CIA fired fully one third of its recruited assets — the informants whose reporting depended on their proximity to right-wing death squads in Latin America.

kiriakou-writing-process.title: Remains of the Day (book)
kiriakou-writing-process.summary: John Kiriakou's book, announced for publication by Simon and Schuster in March 2026, billed as a definitive guide to the historic cemeteries of Washington DC and the first in a planned series; the second installment will cover the Mafia graves of New York City.

kiriakou-writing-process.title: Whispers in the Dirt
kiriakou-writing-process.summary: John Kiriakou's second cemetery book — a guide to the mafia graves of New York City, and the sequel Simon & Schuster commissioned after Remains of the Day. Reporting it produced the moment he realised an inmate who had told him a body was found in a barrel in his storage unit had been telling the truth.

kiriakou-writing-process.title: Kiriakou's public-speaking training
kiriakou-writing-process.summary: The origin John Kiriakou gives for his manner as a speaker: a tenth-grade speech and debate class taught by Dr. Scarvel, his father''s childhood best friend, who drilled his students out of verbal fillers and pushed Kiriakou into competitive extemporaneous debate. Kiriakou credits the class with teaching him to let silence do the work of ''um''.

kiriakou-writing-process.title: Greek death rituals
kiriakou-writing-process.summary: The five-year grave rental, exhumation and ossuary practice of rural Greece as John Kiriakou describes it — bones washed in red wine, blessed, boxed, and eventually laid beneath the foundations of a new church, with cremation strictly forbidden. He visits the ossuary in his ancestral Rhodes village, where the records stop in the nineteenth century because the Ottomans burned everything earlier.

kiriakou-writing-process.title: Israel Boyd and the Wonder Bread story
kiriakou-writing-process.summary: John Kiriakou's account of finding the grave of Israel Boyd, one of two brothers forced by their parents into the family bakery business, who went on to invent the first industrial dough mixer and dough-cutting machine, pioneer adding milk to bread dough, and build the largest bakery in America before World War I — before selling the business, whose flagship "Mrs. McGill's Delicious Bread" was renamed Wonder Bread by its buyer.

kiriakou-writing-process.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-writing-process.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakous-recommended-reading.title: Doing Time Like a Spy
kiriakous-recommended-reading.summary: Prison memoir by John Kiriakou, full title Doing Time Like a Spy: How the CIA Taught Me to Survive and Thrive in Prison; winner of two literary awards and reissued in a second edition by Simon and Schuster.

kiriakous-recommended-reading.title: The Fifth Fleet in Bahrain
kiriakous-recommended-reading.summary: The United States naval presence based in Bahrain since 1976 — the naval component of Central Command, headquartered at Manama. For John Kiriakou as a young diplomat it was mainly a social resource: the officers'' club for its salad bar, the enlisted club for football and cheap beer. It was also, he came to understand, the reason his reporting on Bahraini extrajudicial killings went nowhere. The ambassador''s summary of the alliance was four words long. In 2026 the headquarters was itself hit by Iranian missiles — an outcome that, in Kiriakou''s reading, inverts the entire purpose of the Gulf basing architecture.

kiriakous-recommended-reading.title: Mike Johnson
kiriakous-recommended-reading.summary: Speaker of the House during the fight over the Epstein files, whose procedural manoeuvres John Kiriakou reads as a sustained attempt to prevent his own party from ever having to vote — first by blocking the motion in the Rules Committee, then by adjourning the House until September so that nothing at all could be voted on — and whose midterm framing of Democrats as communists Kiriakou dismisses outright.

kiriakous-recommended-reading.title: The Reluctant Spy
kiriakous-recommended-reading.summary: John Kiriakou''s 2009 memoir, The Reluctant Spy: My Secret Life in the CIA''s War on Terror, begun in secret months before he blew the whistle and reaching number five on the New York Times bestseller list.

kiriakous-recommended-reading.title: The lapsed film rights
kiriakous-recommended-reading.summary: John Kiriakou has sold the rights to his life story three separate times — to Universal, 20th Century Fox and Paramount — and all three studios let the option lapse, telling him there was too much detail and too many stories to fit into two hours.

kiriakous-recommended-reading.title: A Middle East reading list
kiriakous-recommended-reading.summary: The books and the starting point John Kiriakou recommends to anyone trying to understand the modern Middle East: begin at the end of the Second World War, not five thousand years earlier, and start with The House of Saud, the Sykes-Picot Agreement and From Beirut to Jerusalem.

kite-runner-rescue-mission.title: Deloitte Consulting Career
kite-runner-rescue-mission.summary: John Kiriakou's post-CIA career at Deloitte Consulting (2004–2008), covering two corporate acquisitions he says he drove — India Tiger Analysis and, in effect, Bering Point — and ending in his effective firing weeks before his ABC News whistleblower interview aired.

kite-runner-rescue-mission.title: Abu Zubaydah
kite-runner-rescue-mission.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

kite-runner-rescue-mission.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kite-runner-rescue-mission.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kite-runner-rescue-mission.title: China's base in Djibouti
kite-runner-rescue-mission.summary: Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti, the abandoned French base the Djiboutians offered to the Americans and the Chinese took a share of — split down the middle by a chain-link fence, the only Chinese military installation outside China, and the centrepiece of John Kiriakou's argument that China is not an expansionist power.

kite-runner-rescue-mission.title: China as economic threat
kite-runner-rescue-mission.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

kite-runner-rescue-mission.title: The CIA Insider's Guide to Surveillance and Surveillance Detection
kite-runner-rescue-mission.summary: Book by John Kiriakou drawing on his experience as a surveillance detection instructor at the CIA and as a private surveillance training consultant. The book covers the techniques used by intelligence professionals to identify whether they are being followed — including the four-phase surveillance detection route, concealment device placement and retrieval, and counter-surveillance strategy — adapted for use by corporate executives, journalists, and others who want to confirm whether they are being followed.

kompromat.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
kompromat.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

kompromat.title: Jeffrey Epstein
kompromat.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

kompromat.title: Gay Diplomat Operation
kompromat.summary: Per John Kiriakou, a CIA recruitment operation he ran against a foreign diplomat who was closeted and gay. After months of cultivation under cover as a gay man, Kiriakou attempted to kiss the diplomat at his apartment and was deflated by the response: ''I am gay. I''m just not into hairy guys.'' The romantic gambit failed — but the recruitment ultimately succeeded anyway, because the diplomat had been passed over for a promotion and was angry enough at his own government to cooperate. Kiriakou cites the operation as evidence that financial motivation and personal grievance, not coercion, are the reliable drivers of recruitment.

kompromat.title: Cuban double agents
kompromat.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of Cuban intelligence as one of the best services on the planet, defensive in nature and trained by the KGB, and his flat claim — repeated across several tellings — that the CIA has never recruited a Cuban who did not turn out to be working for Havana all along.

kompromat.title: John Kiriakou
kompromat.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kompromat.title: Prince Andrew
kompromat.summary: British royal, now Andrew Mountbatten Windsor, named repeatedly by John Kiriakou as one of the un-recruitable principals whose access made Jeffrey Epstein valuable to a foreign intelligence service. Kiriakou has asked why Andrew was never charged over conduct with minors, reads his alleged provision of classified Ministry of Defence documents to Epstein as evidence of espionage rather than vanity — and expects him to face no criminal consequence at all, because the statute of limitations has run.

ksm-confession-ruling-2026.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
ksm-confession-ruling-2026.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

ksm-confession-ruling-2026.title: Cofer Black
ksm-confession-ruling-2026.summary: Former head of the CIA Counterterrorism Center during and immediately after the September 11 attacks; principal architect of the agency's paramilitary turn on September 12, 2001; later Vice President of Blackwater under Erik Prince.

ksm-confession-ruling-2026.title: Jose Rodriguez
ksm-confession-ruling-2026.summary: Senior CIA officer of the post-9/11 era; identified by John Kiriakou as among those responsible for crimes committed in the name of national security; described as believing himself to be a good guy.

ksm-confession-ruling-2026.title: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed
ksm-confession-ruling-2026.summary: Mastermind of the September 11, 2001 attacks; identified to the CIA by Abu Zubaydah, in the course of FBI interrogator Ali Soufan's rapport-based debriefing at the black site, as the man behind the kunya "Mukhtar" the agency had been hunting since at least 1996 for the Bojinka plot; per Kiriakou's relay of his self-account, radicalized by news video of an Israeli soldier with his boot on the neck of a Palestinian woman.

ksm-confession-ruling-2026.title: Waterboarding
ksm-confession-ruling-2026.summary: Torture technique in which a prisoner is restrained on an inclined board with the head lower than the feet, a cloth placed over the face, and water poured continuously over it to simulate drowning. Per John Kiriakou, waterboarding was treated as a criminal act under U.S. and international law for decades before 2002 — including a post–World War II execution of Japanese soldiers who waterboarded American POWs, and a 1968 court-martial of a U.S. soldier photographed waterboarding a North Vietnamese prisoner — before the CIA reauthorized it after September 11. Abu Zubaydah was waterboarded 83 times; Khalid Sheikh Mohammed 187 times.

ksm-confession-ruling-2026.title: Central Intelligence Agency
ksm-confession-ruling-2026.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

kurds.title: ISIS
kurds.summary: The Islamic State, in John Kiriakou''s account, is an American policy failure made flesh — created because a faction decided al-Qaeda was not radical or violent enough, founded by Baghdadi while he sat in a U.S. military prison in Iraq, armed with hardware captured from the U.S.-supplied Iraqi army, and — per an email he cites from Hillary Clinton to John Podesta — funded by the governments of Saudi Arabia and Qatar. Kiriakou repeatedly punctured the anti-ISIS coalition''s logic: ISIS operated in seven countries while the U.S. bombed two, and Turkey had no real quarrel with ISIS at all — their common enemy was the Kurds.

kurds.title: Saddam Hussein
kurds.summary: President of Iraq from 1979 until the 2003 U.S. invasion; subject of John Kiriakou's CIA portfolio from January 1990 onward, in which capacity Kiriakou became, at age 25, "Saddam Hussein's intelligence community biographer" and the analyst who briefed President George H. W. Bush in the Oval Office on the morning of the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

kurds.title: Iraq WMD intelligence
kurds.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of how the case for Iraqi weapons of mass destruction was fabricated: the intelligence community''s consensus was that Iraq had no WMD, but the White House had already decided to invade and sought analysis to fit the policy.

kurds.title: Ted Rall
kurds.summary: American editorial cartoonist and two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist; co-host with John Kiriakou of the daily news-commentary podcast "Deprogram," launched in September 2025 and by late 2025 running every weekday morning.

kurds.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kurds.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kurds.title: The BBC and the sanctions coverage
kurds.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of the BBC — that it has a long history of offering both sides, which American broadcasters do not — set against his memory of watching it from inside the CIA in the run-up to the liberation of Kuwait, when its reporting on starving Iraqi children under sanctions drove him mad, because food was not sanctioned and Saddam Hussein was refusing to distribute it.

kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.title: Shia populations and the oil fields
kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.summary: John Kiriakou's observation that the oil-bearing areas of the Middle East are largely populated by Shia Muslims, and his account of the effort by Saudi Arabia and by Saddam Hussein's Iraq to ensure that those populations neither controlled the oil industry nor received any of the money it generated.

kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.title: Democratic change in the Middle East
kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.summary: John Kiriakou's answer to what it would take for Middle Eastern populations to free themselves of both Western influence and Saudi ambition — decades, a democratic rather than violent revolution on the early Tunisian model, and, in a conclusion he reaches reluctantly, blood in the streets, because he does not believe a bloodless model exists.

kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.title: Hezbollah
kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.summary: Lebanese Shia militant organization and political party. Per John Kiriakou, Israel''s strategic goal regarding Hezbollah is not to defeat it outright but to keep Lebanon in a state of chaos that serves Israeli interests. He cites two Israeli operations: the simultaneous pager-detonation attack that decapitated Hezbollah''s leadership, which he called ''the most incredible operation I''ve ever seen,'' and the strike that killed former leader Hassan Nasrallah by leveling an entire complex and killing roughly 300 people — which he characterized as a war crime.

kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.title: Iraqi invasion of Kuwait
kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.summary: John Kiriakou''s most detailed account of the intelligence process around the 1990 Iraqi invasion of Kuwait and its 1991 liberation. As a first-year CIA analyst on a ''training account'' covering Iraq, Kiriakou produced the June 30, 1990 warning paper for the White House; suggested calling the US Defense Attaché in Baghdad to drive to the border and report what he saw (the answer: ''Literally the entire Iraqi military is heading south''); briefed the August 2 Oval Office meeting with Bush; and later took a single phone call from General Colin Powell that led, eight hours later, to 47 cruise missiles striking the Iraqi Intelligence Service headquarters in Baghdad.

kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.title: Bahrain's naturalisation policy
kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how the Bahraini royal family changed the sectarian arithmetic of the country over thirty years — importing Syrians and naturalising Indian and Pakistani Sunni Muslims until a population that had been two-thirds to three-quarters Shia was closer to half and half.

kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.title: Saudi influence in Egypt
kuwait-as-a-sectarian-model.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Saudi Arabia's role in Egypt — not merely supporting the government that displaced the Muslim Brotherhood but bankrolling it and ensuring its survival — which he places within a history of Saudi interference in Egyptian internal affairs reaching back to the nationalist revolution of 1958.

kuwait-invasion-intelligence.title: Asel al-Ghabandi
kuwait-invasion-intelligence.summary: Kuwaiti resistance figure during the 1990–91 Iraqi occupation; per John Kiriakou, a "bona fide hero" whose telephone reporting on Iraqi troop movements, roadblocks, atrocities, and the location of inspections reached the CIA every single day via NSA [call interception](/wiki/the-intercept) — Kiriakou's account of the resistance figure who best understood how to weaponize the certainty that the Americans were listening to everything.

kuwait-invasion-intelligence.title: Collateral Murder Video
kuwait-invasion-intelligence.summary: The 2010 WikiLeaks release of gun-camera footage from a 2007 U.S. Apache helicopter attack in Baghdad; part of the trove of Iraq and Afghan war logs, Guantanamo files, and State Department cables leaked by Chelsea Manning, which John Kiriakou credits with corroborating major abuses and helping to touch off the Arab Spring.

kuwait-invasion-intelligence.title: Kuwait oil fires
kuwait-invasion-intelligence.summary: The February 1991 sabotage by retreating Iraqi forces of an estimated 600–800 Kuwaiti oil wells; per John Kiriakou's first-person account, the fires blackened the desert and blotted out the sun as far away as Riyadh, vaporized two French journalists who drove onto a sheet of melted-sand glass, and were extinguished only by an international team led by American specialist Red Adair using a Rolls-Royce jet engine to blow the flames out.

kuwait-invasion-intelligence.title: Yellowcake Niger forgery
kuwait-invasion-intelligence.summary: The fabricated intelligence document claiming Iraq had attempted to buy yellowcake uranium from Niger; passed to the U.S. via the British (originally from the Italians); identified by CIA analysts including John Kiriakou as a forgery on sight ("it's not even in the right font"); pulled from President George W. Bush's State of the Union draft by Colin Powell; reinserted by Vice President Dick Cheney; pulled out by the CIA again; delivered in the 2003 State of the Union address anyway.

kuwait-invasion-intelligence.title: Saud Nasir Al-Sabah
kuwait-invasion-intelligence.summary: Kuwaiti Ambassador to the United States in the run-up to the 1990 Iraqi invasion; per John Kiriakou, "just a lovely, lovely man, very generous with his time"; the diplomatic channel through which the CIA, working from the Kuwaiti embassy in Washington, communicated its escalating June–July 1990 warnings that Iraq was preparing to invade.

kuwait-invasion-intelligence.title: The SIGINT–HUMINT balance
kuwait-invasion-intelligence.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to what he calls the most important question facing any incoming CIA director: how to divide investment between signals intelligence and human intelligence. His position is that signals collection cannot supply the one thing policy requires — a person in the room when a decision is taken — and that every new director says so on arrival and then drifts back toward the technology.

kuwait-liberation-day.title: Iraqi invasion of Kuwait
kuwait-liberation-day.summary: John Kiriakou''s most detailed account of the intelligence process around the 1990 Iraqi invasion of Kuwait and its 1991 liberation. As a first-year CIA analyst on a ''training account'' covering Iraq, Kiriakou produced the June 30, 1990 warning paper for the White House; suggested calling the US Defense Attaché in Baghdad to drive to the border and report what he saw (the answer: ''Literally the entire Iraqi military is heading south''); briefed the August 2 Oval Office meeting with Bush; and later took a single phone call from General Colin Powell that led, eight hours later, to 47 cruise missiles striking the Iraqi Intelligence Service headquarters in Baghdad.

kuwait-liberation-day.title: Saddam Hussein
kuwait-liberation-day.summary: President of Iraq from 1979 until the 2003 U.S. invasion; subject of John Kiriakou's CIA portfolio from January 1990 onward, in which capacity Kiriakou became, at age 25, "Saddam Hussein's intelligence community biographer" and the analyst who briefed President George H. W. Bush in the Oval Office on the morning of the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

kuwait-liberation-day.title: Bahrain Posting (1994–1996)
kuwait-liberation-day.summary: John Kiriakou's 1994–1996 assignment to Bahrain under U.S. State Department cover as second secretary for economic affairs — arriving with his wife Joanne and infant son Chris on August 1, 1994, into a tiny Gulf monarchy whose sectarian tensions erupted, two months later, into the first Intifada.

kuwait-liberation-day.title: Ahmed Khatib
kuwait-liberation-day.summary: Iraqi-installed occupation governor of Kuwait announced on August 2, 1990, hours after the invasion; medical doctor trained at the American University of Beirut whose mother had been a Sudanese slave in the Kuwaiti royal household; college roommate of George Habash and co-founder of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine.

kuwait-liberation-day.title: Joko Widodo
kuwait-liberation-day.summary: Indonesian general; former Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff of Indonesia; banned from the United States on human-rights grounds for personally killing six pro-democracy college student protesters by stabbing each in the heart in front of the others; subsequently elected Vice President of Indonesia; subject of an unsuccessful 2008 reputation-rehabilitation campaign conducted by John Rendon's firm with Karl Rove and John Kiriakou.

kuwait-liberation-day.title: National Endowment for Democracy
kuwait-liberation-day.summary: U.S. federally chartered organization characterized by John Kiriakou as a proxy for CIA propaganda — the funding vehicle by which the agency promotes pro-U.S. political leaders in foreign countries; explicitly not an operational entity in the boots-on-the-ground sense.

kuwait-oil-fires.title: Saddam Hussein
kuwait-oil-fires.summary: President of Iraq from 1979 until the 2003 U.S. invasion; subject of John Kiriakou's CIA portfolio from January 1990 onward, in which capacity Kiriakou became, at age 25, "Saddam Hussein's intelligence community biographer" and the analyst who briefed President George H. W. Bush in the Oval Office on the morning of the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

kuwait-oil-fires.title: Iraqi invasion of Kuwait
kuwait-oil-fires.summary: John Kiriakou''s most detailed account of the intelligence process around the 1990 Iraqi invasion of Kuwait and its 1991 liberation. As a first-year CIA analyst on a ''training account'' covering Iraq, Kiriakou produced the June 30, 1990 warning paper for the White House; suggested calling the US Defense Attaché in Baghdad to drive to the border and report what he saw (the answer: ''Literally the entire Iraqi military is heading south''); briefed the August 2 Oval Office meeting with Bush; and later took a single phone call from General Colin Powell that led, eight hours later, to 47 cruise missiles striking the Iraqi Intelligence Service headquarters in Baghdad.

kuwait-oil-fires.title: Yellowcake Niger forgery
kuwait-oil-fires.summary: The fabricated intelligence document claiming Iraq had attempted to buy yellowcake uranium from Niger; passed to the U.S. via the British (originally from the Italians); identified by CIA analysts including John Kiriakou as a forgery on sight ("it's not even in the right font"); pulled from President George W. Bush's State of the Union draft by Colin Powell; reinserted by Vice President Dick Cheney; pulled out by the CIA again; delivered in the 2003 State of the Union address anyway.

kuwait-oil-fires.title: 1993 Bush Kuwait assassination plot
kuwait-oil-fires.summary: Iraqi intelligence plot, foiled by Kuwaiti authorities, to assassinate former President George H. W. Bush during his post-liberation "victory lap" visit to Kuwait; the U.S. response, per John Kiriakou's first-person account of his telephone call with Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Colin Powell, was 47 cruise missiles fired into the Iraqi Intelligence Service headquarters in Baghdad eight hours later.

kuwait-oil-fires.title: Ahmed Chalabi
kuwait-oil-fires.summary: Iraqi exile and founder of the Iraqi National Congress; per John Kiriakou, a Shia-Kurdish con man who looted Petra Bank in Jordan of $36 million in the 1980s, was sentenced to death in absentia, was pardoned at CIA request, then pocketed $6 million in CIA seed funding for the INC and bought a Mayfair house in cash; later resurrected by Dick Cheney to feed the Pentagon fabricated WMD intelligence used to justify the 2003 invasion of Iraq.

kuwait-oil-fires.title: Ali Hassan al-Majid
kuwait-oil-fires.summary: Saddam Hussein cousin known as "Chemical Ali" and "the Butcher of Kurdistan"; per John Kiriakou, also briefly served as the Iraqi-installed governor of occupied Kuwait — "the Butcher of Kuwait" — and was engaged in the wholesale slaughter of Kurds in the north, Shia in the south, and Kuwaitis under occupation.

kyriakos-mitsotakis.title: Kiriakou's Greek citizenship
kyriakos-mitsotakis.summary: The Greek nationality John Kiriakou acquired in 2010, after his CIA career and before his prosecution — offered, he says, by the Greek ambassador who asked what could be done to help when his troubles began, and granted when he answered "you could give me Greek citizenship." Held by his children too, it made him a Greek national at the moment he became, in Greece, a national hero; it brought him the commission to write the country's whistleblower protection law, and the Athens job that turned out to be a money laundering operation.

kyriakos-mitsotakis.title: Frank Snepp
kyriakos-mitsotakis.summary: The CIA analyst who wrote Decent Interval, and whom John Kiriakou calls a giant — one of the great analysts of his generation, practically the first to say publicly that the United States was losing in Vietnam and committing atrocities there, who paid for it with his career and spent most of the rest of his life fighting the agency's publications review board.

kyriakos-mitsotakis.title: Hot bunking
kyriakos-mitsotakis.summary: John Kiriakou''s description of living conditions aboard the overcrowded American warships and submarines he has visited: three men to a bed on eight-hour rotations, a shared pillow, decks raised several inches by the canned food stacked underfoot, and nuclear submarines that surface not because they must but to keep the crew sane.

kyriakos-mitsotakis.title: Israel, Turkey, and NATO Article 5
kyriakos-mitsotakis.summary: John Kiriakou's scenario in which an Israeli attack on Turkey would oblige every NATO member, the United States included, to come to Turkey's defence — and in which the alliance would sooner dissolve than honour that obligation against Israel.

kyriakos-mitsotakis.title: John Kiriakou
kyriakos-mitsotakis.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kyriakos-mitsotakis.title: John McCain
kyriakos-mitsotakis.summary: Late U.S. Senator from Arizona who gave the most consequential Senate-floor defense of John Kiriakou — declaring that 'if it weren't for John Kiriakou, the American people would never have had any idea what the CIA was doing in their name' — and sponsored the McCain–Feinstein amendment banning torture.

lahore-safe-house.title: Colonel Khaled
lahore-safe-house.summary: The ISI chief in Lahore who worked alongside John Kiriakou through the Abu Zubaydah operation — a man who had never wanted to be a soldier, who spent their first meeting drawing Kiriakou's portrait instead of taking notes, and who explained the spliced telephone wires that nearly derailed the hunt.

lahore-safe-house.title: Navigating Pakistan without maps
lahore-safe-house.summary: The logistical problem John Kiriakou says nearly undid the Abu Zubaydah operation: in 2002 Pakistan had no maps to buy, no street signs and no addresses, so the CIA team navigated a city of twelve million by shoe advertisement, traffic policeman, British school and McDonald''s — rehearsing the route twice in the small hours before the raids.

lahore-safe-house.title: Amir
lahore-safe-house.summary: The pseudonym John Kiriakou gives the Muslim, ethnically Arab domestic officer sent on temporary duty to Pakistan to help with the Abu Zubaydah hunt — the colleague who drove them into India by GPS, drank the roadside tea and had diarrhoea for six weeks, and invented the textile-baron cover story on the spot.

lahore-safe-house.title: Faisalabad
lahore-safe-house.summary: The Pakistani textile city of some seven or eight million people where Abu Zubaydah was captured in March 2002 — concrete, mud and corrugated tin in John Kiriakou's description, with a brand-new glass-and-steel McDonald's standing in the middle of it.

lahore-safe-house.title: The Punjab Elite Force
lahore-safe-house.summary: The Pakistani provincial counterterrorism unit that supplied part of the assault manpower for the Abu Zubaydah raids of March 2002 — black trousers, black t-shirts stencilled with a pistol, and, in John Kiriakou's telling, a refusal to wear body armour on the grounds that if God called them that night they would go.

lahore-safe-house.title: Mr. Fish
lahore-safe-house.summary: The cover name the CIA used for Abu Zubaydah in Pakistan in 2002 — invented because the Americans would not tell their Pakistani partners who the target was, and derived from the only thing they would say about him: that he was a big fish.

langley.title: J. Edgar Hoover
langley.summary: The FBI's founding director — 48 years in the chair — whose opposition nearly strangled the CIA at birth. Per John Kiriakou, Truman lifted Hoover's objection to the National Security Act of 1947 by disingenuously assuring him the CIA would be a division of the FBI; the lie seeded the two agencies' permanent mutual hatred. Kiriakou also credits Hoover with perfecting the annual ritual the CIA later copied — scaring Congress witless and demanding budget increases — and with controlling Hollywood's FBI image so tightly that no film could be made without his approval.

langley.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
langley.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

langley.title: John Kiriakou
langley.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

langley.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
