It is also where, aged eight or nine and hunting salamanders in Oak Park Cemetery, he found the grave of a Medal of Honor private and acquired the lifelong interest in cemeteries that became a book.

sixteen-employees-to-twenty-thousand.title: The coffee with the Jordanian intern
sixteen-employees-to-twenty-thousand.summary: A morning meeting John Kiriakou took with a young intern from the Jordanian embassy who had found him on LinkedIn — and which he credits with reminding him that Palestinians are not a monolith, a point he says pro-Palestinian Westerners in particular tend to get wrong.

sixteen-employees-to-twenty-thousand.title: The Las Vegas case
sixteen-employees-to-twenty-thousand.summary: John Kiriakou's scepticism about the Justice Department's claim that it played no role in a Las Vegas child-exploitation case involving an Israeli suspect who left the country — on the ground that electronic images and electronic communications would have made the matter federal.

sixteen-people-knew.title: Hire a lawyer first
sixteen-people-knew.summary: The single piece of practical advice John Kiriakou gives to anyone considering blowing the whistle: retain a lawyer before saying anything, and have that lawyer sitting beside you when you do.

sixteen-people-knew.title: CIA and the UFO question
sixteen-people-knew.summary: John Kiriakou's consistent answer that UFOs and alien technology are a Pentagon matter, not a CIA one — though he says nearly every former fighter-pilot friend of his has seen something inexplicable, sometimes emerging from the ocean.

sixteen-people-knew.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
sixteen-people-knew.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

sixteen-people-knew.title: Area 58
sixteen-people-knew.summary: The claim John Kiriakou says was put to him by a man who presents as entirely serious and is writing a book about it: that beyond Area 51 there is an Area 58 — seven more, and that much more secret — containing an underground bunker where alien craft land, known to those involved as the embassy because it is where the United States liaises with the aliens.

sixteen-people-knew.title: John Kiriakou
sixteen-people-knew.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

sixteen-people-knew.title: Kiriakou's UFO sighting
sixteen-people-knew.summary: The object John Kiriakou and his father watched from the side of Route 60 in Amish country, western Pennsylvania, on a Friday night in 1981 — three flashes of white light, then a silent orange trapezoid hanging a couple of thousand feet up, which left at a speed he had never seen before or since.

skip-gnehm.title: Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad
skip-gnehm.summary: Amir of Kuwait during the 1990 Iraqi invasion and the 1991 liberation; per John Kiriakou, "a very kind and decent man and a leader who genuinely loved and cared for his people"; the subject of a CIA cable Kiriakou wrote from Taif which led President George H. W. Bush to invite the Amir to Washington for "the red carpet treatment" — after which the Amir returned with renewed focus on driving the Iraqis out.

skip-gnehm.title: Saud Nasir Al-Sabah
skip-gnehm.summary: Kuwaiti Ambassador to the United States in the run-up to the 1990 Iraqi invasion; per John Kiriakou, "just a lovely, lovely man, very generous with his time"; the diplomatic channel through which the CIA, working from the Kuwaiti embassy in Washington, communicated its escalating June–July 1990 warnings that Iraq was preparing to invade.

skip-gnehm.title: Sheikh Saad al-Abdullah
skip-gnehm.summary: Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Kuwait during the 1990–91 Iraqi occupation; per John Kiriakou, the day-to-day leader of the Kuwaiti government-in-exile in Taif — "very military," "hands-on," "the best leader Kuwait had for that situation," meeting twenty hours a day with everyone who needed to be met and simultaneously managing the Kuwaiti resistance on the ground.

skip-gnehm.title: 1993 Bush Kuwait assassination plot
skip-gnehm.summary: Iraqi intelligence plot, foiled by Kuwaiti authorities, to assassinate former President George H. W. Bush during his post-liberation "victory lap" visit to Kuwait; the U.S. response, per John Kiriakou's first-person account of his telephone call with Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Colin Powell, was 47 cruise missiles fired into the Iraqi Intelligence Service headquarters in Baghdad eight hours later.

skip-gnehm.title: Abolish the CIA
skip-gnehm.summary: John Kiriakou's position that the CIA should be abolished because its functions are already duplicated by the other 17 U.S. intelligence agencies — analysis by the State Department, human spying by the Pentagon, technology by DARPA, NSA and the private sector.

skip-gnehm.title: Ahmed Chalabi
skip-gnehm.summary: Iraqi exile and founder of the Iraqi National Congress; per John Kiriakou, a Shia-Kurdish con man who looted Petra Bank in Jordan of $36 million in the 1980s, was sentenced to death in absentia, was pardoned at CIA request, then pocketed $6 million in CIA seed funding for the INC and bought a Mayfair house in cash; later resurrected by Dick Cheney to feed the Pentagon fabricated WMD intelligence used to justify the 2003 invasion of Iraq.

sleep-deprivation.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
sleep-deprivation.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

sleep-deprivation.title: Cold cell
sleep-deprivation.summary: A CIA interrogation technique in which a stripped detainee is chained to a ceiling eyebolt in a cell chilled to 50°F, then doused with a bucket of ice water at hourly intervals; never authorized; documented to have killed at least two prisoners.

sleep-deprivation.title: John Kiriakou
sleep-deprivation.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

sleep-deprivation.title: Donald Rumsfeld
sleep-deprivation.summary: U.S. Secretary of Defense during the post-9/11 torture program and, per John Kiriakou, joined at the hip with Dick Cheney in pushing the Iraq war from inside the Office of the Secretary of Defense. Kiriakou recounts Rumsfeld dismissing sleep deprivation as a real technique by pointing to his own standup desk, and names him among the war criminals who would be prosecuted in any other country.

sleep-deprivation.title: Music as torture
sleep-deprivation.summary: The use of recorded music played on indefinite loop as a coercive interrogation technique. Per John Kiriakou, the CIA's post-9/11 rotation ran to the Bee Gees and the SpongeBob SquarePants theme song, and the practice was not an invention of the war on terror — he places its use throughout the Vietnam War.

sleep-deprivation.title: Walling
sleep-deprivation.summary: A CIA interrogation technique in which a detainee is slammed against a wall; designed on paper to use a padded fiberboard surface and a rolled towel around the neck, but applied in practice against bare concrete-block walls without protective measures, producing in at least one case permanent brain damage.

sleeper-agent.title: John Kiriakou
sleeper-agent.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

sleeper-agent.title: MOSSAD
sleeper-agent.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

sleeper-agent.title: MK-Ultra
sleeper-agent.summary: The CIA's mid-twentieth-century umbrella program of mind-control, behavioral-modification, and biological-warfare experimentation, encompassing subprojects such as MK-Chickwit and MK-Seesaw; active 1952–1975; documented practices included LSD dosing of unwitting American citizens in CIA-rented brothels and the aerosolized release of pathogens into the San Francisco fog; 80% of the program's documentation was destroyed by the CIA in defiance of a 1975 preservation order from Senator Frank Church.

sleeper-agent.title: Asset acquisition cycle
sleeper-agent.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

sleeper-agent.title: Joe Weisberg
sleeper-agent.summary: Former CIA Counterterrorism Center officer and colleague of John Kiriakou who resigned abruptly, saying he did not have it in him to convince people to commit treason, then moved to Hollywood, wrote a well-regarded novel that sold poorly, and created the television series The Americans — which Kiriakou calls the best intelligence show ever made and one hundred per cent true to life, and every script of which the CIA redacted.

sleeper-agent.title: Surveillance detection route
sleeper-agent.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

slow-rolling-the-president.title: Donald Trump
slow-rolling-the-president.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

slow-rolling-the-president.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
slow-rolling-the-president.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

slow-rolling-the-president.title: David Petraeus
slow-rolling-the-president.summary: Retired U.S. Army general and director of the CIA who, per John Kiriakou, confirmed the names of ten covert CIA operatives to his biographer and girlfriend and was never criminally charged — a contrast Kiriakou cites repeatedly as proof that his own prosecution under the Intelligence Identities Protection Act was selective. Kiriakou''s explanation for the disparity: Petraeus had not blown the whistle on the torture program and embarrassed the agency.

slow-rolling-the-president.title: Declassifying for a foreign government
slow-rolling-the-president.summary: The CIA procedure John Kiriakou describes for passing classified intelligence to a foreign service — the originating office extracts the substance onto a fresh sheet marked releasable to that country, so that no source or method travels with it — set out in 2017 as the thing Donald Trump did not do when he spoke to the Russian foreign minister and ambassador in the Oval Office.

slow-rolling-the-president.title: Deep state
slow-rolling-the-president.summary: John Kiriakou''s position on the deep state — that it is not a right-wing trope but an accurate description of something he served inside for fifteen years at the CIA and two more on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee staff. He is indifferent to the label ("call it the state, call it the federal bureaucracy") and insists on the substance: "It''s there to stay. It''s not going anywhere."

slow-rolling-the-president.title: H. R. McMaster
slow-rolling-the-president.summary: National Security Adviser during the May 2017 controversy over Donald Trump's disclosure of intelligence to Russian officials, whose public defence — that the president had not been briefed on the source of the information — John Kiriakou treated as a fork in which either answer reflects badly on McMaster himself.

small-country-intelligence-services.title: Irish intelligence services
small-country-intelligence-services.summary: Ireland's intelligence and law-enforcement services, which John Kiriakou toured and met with during a speaking trip to Belfast, Cork, Dublin, and Waterford. Per Kiriakou, Irish intelligence and the Garda are especially strong at anti-money-laundering investigation and counterterrorism — the latter traced, he says, to the large number of Irish militants trained by Carlos the Jackal in Libya and Lebanon during the 1970s.

small-country-intelligence-services.title: 2026 Iran war
small-country-intelligence-services.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

small-country-intelligence-services.title: Advice to the next generation
small-country-intelligence-services.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to a Gen Z viewer who said he felt helpless — that helplessness is not new, that 1968 and 1969 were worse, and that the remedy is four concrete things: run for any office at all, starting with the local water board; demonstrate; ride your elected officials and vote them out if they will not do what they are told; and write.

small-country-intelligence-services.title: Al-Qaeda training manual interrogation-resistance tactics
small-country-intelligence-services.summary: A captured al-Qaeda training manual instructing operatives on how to resist interrogation, including feigning illness — a technique John Kiriakou says he saw a detainee use, and recognized, during a capture and interrogation in Pakistan.

small-country-intelligence-services.title: China's base in Djibouti
small-country-intelligence-services.summary: Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti, the abandoned French base the Djiboutians offered to the Americans and the Chinese took a share of — split down the middle by a chain-link fence, the only Chinese military installation outside China, and the centrepiece of John Kiriakou's argument that China is not an expansionist power.

small-country-intelligence-services.title: The death of investigative journalism
small-country-intelligence-services.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the collapse of investigative reporting inside the American mainstream press — Joby Warrick's resignation from the *Washington Post*, the paper that brought down a president, and the 80 per cent of its staff Kiriakou says have gone since Jeff Bezos bought it — together with the outlets he says are doing the work instead, and his advice to a student who wants to do it anyway.

snowden-did-not-defect.title: Espionage Act
snowden-did-not-defect.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

snowden-did-not-defect.title: Israel and the fear of being held back
snowden-did-not-defect.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of why an ally that receives almost everything it asks for still spies on the United States — that the Israelis are always afraid something is being withheld, and, having nowhere to be pushed except the Mediterranean, will do anything to be certain about their own security.

snowden-did-not-defect.title: No declaration of war since 1941
snowden-did-not-defect.summary: John Kiriakou's answer to whether Congress will assert its authority over military action against Venezuela — an unqualified no, resting on the fact that the last declaration of war was on 8 December 1941 and that even the Gulf War was fought on an authorisation to use force rather than a declaration.

snowden-did-not-defect.title: The CIA buyout offer
snowden-did-not-defect.summary: The deferred-resignation offer extended to CIA staff in early 2025 on the same terms given to other federal workers — six to eight months' pay, no requirement to come to work, and then the end of the contract — which John Kiriakou discussed as part of a broader reorientation of the agency towards the Western Hemisphere.

snowden-did-not-defect.title: The open letter to Edward Snowden
snowden-did-not-defect.summary: The letter John Kiriakou wrote from prison in 2013 to Edward Snowden, sent privately through a shared attorney and carrying three pieces of advice — hire the best national-security lawyers available, cultivate a base of support on Capitol Hill, and never under any circumstances talk to the FBI — which went viral and reached its addressee only because Arianna Huffington published it.

snowden-did-not-defect.title: Edward Snowden
snowden-did-not-defect.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

sociopathic-tendencies.title: John Kiriakou
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

sociopathic-tendencies.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

sociopathic-tendencies.title: Jeffrey Epstein
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

sociopathic-tendencies.title: Kiriakou's transfer to the Directorate of Operations
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: John Kiriakou's roughly two-month internal campaign to transfer from the CIA's analytic Directorate of Intelligence to the operational Directorate of Operations, overcoming what he calls a "natural bias in operations against the eggheads on the analytic side," followed by an Athens posting secured because he was the only person in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic. Covers his full CIA career arc from 1988/1990 recruitment through analyst years on Iraq, the switch to operations, 9/11, the enhanced-interrogation refusal, executive assistant to the deputy director for operations, and his eventual resignation and post-CIA career.

sociopathic-tendencies.title: Groupthink at the CIA
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the institutional conformity he says has made the CIA wrong about nearly every major international development since its creation — a failure he attributes to analysts agreeing with one another around a conference table while invoking red-team and outside-the-box vocabulary that changes nothing. He and his attorney Bruce Fein discussed writing a book about it.

sociopathic-tendencies.title: Gay Diplomat Operation
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: Per John Kiriakou, a CIA recruitment operation he ran against a foreign diplomat who was closeted and gay. After months of cultivation under cover as a gay man, Kiriakou attempted to kiss the diplomat at his apartment and was deflated by the response: ''I am gay. I''m just not into hairy guys.'' The romantic gambit failed — but the recruitment ultimately succeeded anyway, because the diplomat had been passed over for a promotion and was angry enough at his own government to cooperate. Kiriakou cites the operation as evidence that financial motivation and personal grievance, not coercion, are the reliable drivers of recruitment.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: 1953 Iran coup
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: The U.S.- and UK-backed overthrow of Iran's democratically elected prime minister, Mohammad Mossadegh; per John Kiriakou, the coup served British national interests rather than American ones, and the subsequent outlawing of secular political opposition under the Shah forced dissent into the mosques — producing a religious rather than secular revolution in 1979.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: AIPAC
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: Barack Obama
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: 44th U.S. president; in John Kiriakou's account, Obama publicly recounted refusing Benjamin Netanyahu's demand to bomb Iran and calling Israel's threat to use nuclear weapons a bluff — a bluff Kiriakou says Donald Trump later believed.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: CIA adultery culture
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: John Kiriakou's recurring characterization of the CIA officer corps as riddled with adultery and casual sex — which he frames not as gossip but as a systemic counterintelligence vulnerability that makes officers easy to recruit.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: CIA cable priority levels
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: The five levels of immediacy assigned to U.S. government cable traffic, as described by John Kiriakou. From lowest to highest: Routine, Priority, Immediate, Flash, CRITIC. Most career officers will never see a CRITIC; during the Gulf War, Kiriakou''s desk was receiving multiple CRITICs a day, each one announcing a hostile missile launch.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: CIA Democrats (2016)
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: John Kiriakou's term for a wave of 2016-era congressional candidates with intelligence or military backgrounds who ran for office opposing Trump from the right on Russia — including former CIA officer Abigail Spanberger, who won a one-term-limited Virginia governorship, and former DIA official Elissa Slotkin, who moved from intelligence into Congress and the Senate — both of whom Kiriakou suggests are positioning for future presidential runs.

solitary-confinement.title: Julian Assange
solitary-confinement.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

solitary-confinement.title: Espionage Act
solitary-confinement.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

solitary-confinement.title: Daniel Hale
solitary-confinement.summary: Per John Kiriakou, drone whistleblower Daniel Hale — an NSA contractor and drone targeting analyst who exposed an 80% civilian death rate in the U.S. drone program, was ordered to fire on two young girls his superior called "goats," and was sentenced to 45 months (of which Kiriakou says he actually served about 18) despite prosecutors seeking nine to eleven years.

solitary-confinement.title: RDAP program
solitary-confinement.summary: The Bureau of Prisons' Residential Drug and Alcohol Program, which can shave 12 to 18 months off a federal sentence; John Kiriakou repeatedly advises fellow whistleblowers that, combined with good behavior and a halfway house, it can turn a five-year sentence into as little as two and a half years.

solitary-confinement.title: The 2020 extradition hearing
solitary-confinement.summary: The London hearing on the United States' request to extradite Julian Assange, described by John Kiriakou two days into it — a proceeding scheduled to run to July with a month-long recess inserted at the American prosecutors' request, held in a courtroom whose microphones did not work, with Assange behind a plastic screen and unable to hear his own case. Kiriakou called it more of a circus sideshow than a legal hearing, and warned that even a defence victory would leave Assange expelled to Australia and open to a fresh American request.

solitary-confinement.title: Prison phone monitoring
solitary-confinement.summary: Kiriakou treated the recording of his prison telephone calls as an intelligence channel rather than a constraint, planting messages for staff he knew were listening — a practice that produced a confrontation with a lieutenant over the word 'Nimrod'.

somali-land.title: Djibouti
somali-land.summary: The small Horn of Africa state a few miles across the water from Yemen that hosts Camp Lemonnier — the American drone base for the Yemen and Somalia wars, inherited from the departing French, and shared with China's only overseas military base behind a fence down the middle, in what John Kiriakou calls the worst kept secret in the world.

somali-land.title: Greenland
somali-land.summary: The Danish territory the United States has spent years talking about acquiring; John Kiriakou reports two flatly contradictory readings from his own contacts — a White House friend who says Washington is serious and will lean on a Cold War treaty to claim it is already de facto American, and a Republican friend who says the whole thing is a grenade thrown to distract the press — and warns that taking it by force would end NATO.

somali-land.title: Hillary Clinton
somali-land.summary: Former U.S. Secretary of State and 2016 presidential candidate; John Kiriakou describes her as arguably the most neoconservative candidate Democrats could have nominated, more militarist even than her husband, and credits her — separately — with correctly describing Iran as a military dictatorship run by the IRGC rather than a genuine theocracy.

somali-land.title: Israel's cell-phone assassinations in Iran
somali-land.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how Israel wiped out Iran's military leadership by tracking cell phones — recruiting destitute Afghan refugees as $100-a-month spotters, and, when the generals stopped carrying phones, targeting their bodyguards' phones instead.

somali-land.title: Jeffrey Epstein
somali-land.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

somali-land.title: Kiriakou's daily news diet
somali-land.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the wide range of mainstream and alternative outlets he reads each morning to compare competing angles, the two outlets — the Associated Press and ProPublica — he singles out as exceptional, and his broader habits of media consumption, from an admitted addiction to political polling to his distrust of AI chatbots after they repeatedly fabricated his own biography.

somaliland-israel-recognition.title: Mecca Agreement
somaliland-israel-recognition.summary: A trilateral mutual-defence pact between Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia signed in Mecca in August 2026. John Kiriakou treats it as the most consequential development in the region and one the American media largely ignored, because it makes three separate bilateral enmities collectively enforceable and leaves the United States out of the arrangement entirely.

somaliland-israel-recognition.title: Houthis
somaliland-israel-recognition.summary: The Iran-aligned movement that controls the most important parts of Yemen, described by John Kiriakou as fierce fighters who beat the Saudi military over a decade of war and who in July 2026 declared a naval blockade of Saudi shipping.

somaliland-israel-recognition.title: A Turkey–Israel confrontation
somaliland-israel-recognition.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of what two senior Turkish foreign ministry officials told him over dinner in March 2026 about the prospect of war with Israel: that it will not happen, that Turkey would win if it did, and that Turkey would not ask NATO for help.

somaliland-israel-recognition.title: Abraham Accords
somaliland-israel-recognition.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

somaliland-israel-recognition.title: Dewey Clarridge
somaliland-israel-recognition.summary: The CIA operations officer John Kiriakou calls a legendary figure and a giant of the 1980s — prosecuted over Iran-Contra, and the man who said publicly that Saudi Arabia already had nuclear weapons. Kiriakou believes him, holds that the Saudis financed the Pakistani bomb and were repaid in access to it, and believes Clarridge was also involved in the movement of cocaine into the United States.

somaliland-israel-recognition.title: 2026 Iran war
somaliland-israel-recognition.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: Bashar al-Assad
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: President of Syria; John Kiriakou recounts warning Senator John Kerry to stop publicly calling Assad 'my dear friend' after a speech enraged Washington's Lebanese community, with Kerry citing motorcycle rides they had taken together to the Golan Heights.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: Bob Baer
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: Former CIA case officer; per John Kiriakou, "pretty famous"; the subject of George Clooney's film Syriana; pulled out of northern Iraq by the Clinton White House in the 1990s after [NSA intercepted](/wiki/the-intercept) a communication revealing he was developing a network of sources to assassinate Saddam Hussein — National Security Adviser Sandy Berger called CIA and threatened him with a conspiracy charge.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: China as economic threat
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: Donald Trump
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: The Fifth Fleet in Bahrain
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: The United States naval presence based in Bahrain since 1976 — the naval component of Central Command, headquartered at Manama. For John Kiriakou as a young diplomat it was mainly a social resource: the officers'' club for its salad bar, the enlisted club for football and cheap beer. It was also, he came to understand, the reason his reporting on Bahraini extrajudicial killings went nowhere. The ambassador''s summary of the alliance was four words long. In 2026 the headquarters was itself hit by Iranian missiles — an outcome that, in Kiriakou''s reading, inverts the entire purpose of the Gulf basing architecture.

sources-are-not-traitors.title: Running into former sources
sources-are-not-traitors.summary: John Kiriakou has twice met people he once ran as agents by accident, years after leaving the CIA — once at an airport and once in the street — and both times they came to him with a bear hug. One of them was astonished to discover he spoke English.

sources-are-not-traitors.title: The operational test
sources-are-not-traitors.summary: The vetting procedure John Kiriakou describes for moving a trusted source onto normal handling: put a full surveillance team on him without telling him, watch how he gets to the meeting, and then ask him to describe what he did.

sources-are-not-traitors.title: The density of spies in Washington
sources-are-not-traitors.summary: John Kiriakou's claim that there are more spies in Washington DC than anywhere else in the world, that the FBI's counterintelligence division does nothing but try to root them out, and that the job cannot be finished short of becoming North Korea.

sources-are-not-traitors.title: The Greek colonel and China
sources-are-not-traitors.summary: The arrest of a Greek colonel assigned to NATO on charges of spying for China — a case John Kiriakou calls highly unusual not because espionage arrests are rare in Greece, but because they are almost always for Russia, and which he says shows the Chinese have begun caring about NATO communications.

sources-are-not-traitors.title: Prince Andrew
sources-are-not-traitors.summary: British royal, now Andrew Mountbatten Windsor, named repeatedly by John Kiriakou as one of the un-recruitable principals whose access made Jeffrey Epstein valuable to a foreign intelligence service. Kiriakou has asked why Andrew was never charged over conduct with minors, reads his alleged provision of classified Ministry of Defence documents to Epstein as evidence of espionage rather than vanity — and expects him to face no criminal consequence at all, because the statute of limitations has run.

sources-are-not-traitors.title: The anti-semite smear
sources-are-not-traitors.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the professional cost of saying publicly that Israel spies on the United States: Alan Dershowitz calls him names, and the political director of the Israeli foreign minister called him a noted anti-semite.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Iran regional war (2026)
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: The widening of the 2026 Iran conflict from a war between Iran on one side and the United States and Israel on the other into a regional war — Iranian missiles striking a US base in Jordan, Iranian strikes across the Gulf states, Houthi attacks on Saudi shipping and oil, and Saudi forces striking pro-Iranian militias in Iraq. John Kiriakou notes he had forecast the expansion a week earlier.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Israel, Turkey, and NATO Article 5
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: John Kiriakou's scenario in which an Israeli attack on Turkey would oblige every NATO member, the United States included, to come to Turkey's defence — and in which the alliance would sooner dissolve than honour that obligation against Israel.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Israeli drone factories in Serbia
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: Five drone factories John Kiriakou was told the Israelis are building in Serbia — a fact relayed to him by members of a Serbian delegation who welcomed it on the grounds that Israel is effective against Islamists, and which Kiriakou treats as the same emotional play he sees used on Greeks and Cypriots.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Israeli property acquisition in Greece and Cyprus
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Israelis buying land in Greece and Cyprus at a scale he considers destabilising — entire villages rather than holiday homes, a Jewish-only village outside Paphos with a casino attached, a rejected bid for an island in the Ionian Sea, and a request to open the first Zionist high school in Cyprus.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Antisemitism and anti-Zionism
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: The conflation of criticism of the Israeli state with hatred of Jews, which John Kiriakou describes as a worldwide confusion and, according to a young Israeli he spoke to, an explicit lesson of the Israeli school system; a subject Kiriakou says he personally struggles with.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

south-lebanon-displacement-2026.title: Hezbollah
south-lebanon-displacement-2026.summary: Lebanese Shia militant organization and political party. Per John Kiriakou, Israel''s strategic goal regarding Hezbollah is not to defeat it outright but to keep Lebanon in a state of chaos that serves Israeli interests. He cites two Israeli operations: the simultaneous pager-detonation attack that decapitated Hezbollah''s leadership, which he called ''the most incredible operation I''ve ever seen,'' and the strike that killed former leader Hassan Nasrallah by leveling an entire complex and killing roughly 300 people — which he characterized as a war crime.

south-lebanon-displacement-2026.title: Lebanon-Israeli Conflict
south-lebanon-displacement-2026.summary: Per John Kiriakou, no Israeli government will allow Lebanon to flourish as a nation; he expects continued Israeli attacks and forced displacement of civilians, citing a statistic of up to 700,000 Lebanese internally displaced, and links the war to the "Greater Israel" rhetoric of US ambassador Mike Huckabee.

south-lebanon-displacement-2026.title: Greater Israel
south-lebanon-displacement-2026.summary: The territorial project John Kiriakou believes the Israeli government genuinely holds: the expulsion of every Palestinian, beginning in Gaza and continuing into the West Bank, pursued on a hundred- or two-hundred-year horizon in the confidence that the United States will never push back.

south-lebanon-displacement-2026.title: Air wars are overrated
south-lebanon-displacement-2026.summary: John Kiriakou''s summary judgement on the 2026 Iran and Lebanon campaigns, delivered as the meta-headline of the whole war: air power flattened Gaza without destroying Hamas, is bogging down against Hezbollah, and cannot produce the outcome the war requires.

south-lebanon-displacement-2026.title: Mike Huckabee
south-lebanon-displacement-2026.summary: The United States ambassador to Israel under Donald Trump, and the subject of a public call for resignation from John Kiriakou after Huckabee received Jonathan Pollard at the American embassy. Kiriakou''s assessment separates two charges: Huckabee is not a traitor but an idiot who did not think the meeting was a big deal, and a former governor of a small state who still behaves as though he can set policy without the State Department or the National Security Council.

south-lebanon-displacement-2026.title: "The American war against Iran"
south-lebanon-displacement-2026.summary: A correction Benjamin Netanyahu issued to an Israeli reporter during the 2026 war — that it was the American war against Iran, and that Israel was merely America's ally. John Kiriakou treats it as the moment Israel walked away from a war it had spent years demanding, leaving the United States to fight it alone.

south-pars-and-the-north-dome.title: The Ras Laffan strike
south-pars-and-the-north-dome.summary: The Iranian attack on Qatar's Ras Laffan liquefied natural gas facilities during the 2026 war, which John Kiriakou discussed as taking seventeen per cent of Qatari export capacity offline for an estimated three to five years — one of the strikes that drove oil past a hundred dollars a barrel.

south-pars-and-the-north-dome.title: Why Iran targets the Gulf states
south-pars-and-the-north-dome.summary: John Kiriakou''s explanation of why Iranian missiles fell more heavily on Gulf Arab states than on Israel during the 2026 war: the Gulf has no Iron Dome, a finite missile stock has to be spent where it counts, and hosting American forces converted an uneasy coexistence into open enmity.

south-pars-and-the-north-dome.title: Donald Trump
south-pars-and-the-north-dome.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

south-pars-and-the-north-dome.title: Hamas
south-pars-and-the-north-dome.summary: The Palestinian movement behind the October 7, 2023 attack; John Kiriakou argues that a case could be made for calling it a freedom-fighting organization dedicated to the liberation of its people rather than simply a terrorist group, notes it is labeled a terrorist organization by only a small minority of UN member states, and has ruled Gaza since Israel's 2005 withdrawal.

south-pars-and-the-north-dome.title: Air wars are overrated
south-pars-and-the-north-dome.summary: John Kiriakou''s summary judgement on the 2026 Iran and Lebanon campaigns, delivered as the meta-headline of the whole war: air power flattened Gaza without destroying Hamas, is bogging down against Hezbollah, and cannot produce the outcome the war requires.

south-pars-and-the-north-dome.title: October 7 attack
south-pars-and-the-north-dome.summary: John Kiriakou's analysis of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack as a policy failure, not an intelligence one — Israel was warned repeatedly, but Itamar Ben-Gvir diverted response forces to the West Bank, and Kiriakou believes Israel welcomed a pretext for overwhelming retaliation.

soviet-union.title: Cold War
soviet-union.summary: The U.S.–Soviet confrontation that built the CIA John Kiriakou joined. Kiriakou argues the Cold War was real "but also at a certain level desired" — America has always needed an ism to oppose — and that its habits never died: "The Russians thought the Cold War was over, but no one told the US." From its memoirs he draws a standing tradecraft lesson (the CIA''s best recruits were always walk-ins), and in the new Russia and China confrontations he sees a Cold War 2.0 rebuilt on the old exaggerations.

soviet-union.title: The land-bridge precedents
soviet-union.summary: John Kiriakou''s argument, made during the August 2025 Washington summit on Ukraine, that the Russian demand for a land bridge to Crimea is a solved problem in diplomatic history — the corridor that connected West Germany to West Berlin being the obvious model — and that no American network was discussing what he considered the likely linchpin of any agreement.

soviet-union.title: The water''s-edge doctrine
soviet-union.summary: The old American convention that partisan disagreement stops at the border, which John Kiriakou says was destroyed by Newt Gingrich in 1995 — and whose collapse he offers as the reason the United States has spent thirty years unable to sustain a foreign policy across a change of administration.

soviet-union.title: Tom Alexandrovich
soviet-union.summary: Senior Israeli cyber security official arrested in Las Vegas in August 2025 on multiple counts of child pornography after being caught in an undercover police sting targeting child sex predators, and immediately permitted to board a plane back to Israel — a case John Kiriakou uses as a live illustration of the rule that Israel does not extradite Jews.

soviet-union.title: The hundred-dollar informants
soviet-union.summary: John Kiriakou''s explanation of Iran''s mass detention of some 20,000 suspected Israeli spies after the 2026 twelve-day war: that most of those rounded up were undocumented Afghan refugees, targeted by Israeli intelligence precisely because Iran had spent two years expelling them, and recruited for about $100 a month to report troop movements and the addresses of nuclear scientists and utility headquarters.

soviet-union.title: Thomas Dewey
soviet-union.summary: New York prosecutor, governor and twice-defeated Republican presidential candidate, discussed by John Kiriakou for two reasons: the explanation he encountered for Dewey''s 1948 loss to Harry Truman — that Dewey''s short-cropped moustache reminded an intensely anti-fascist American public of Adolf Hitler — and Dewey''s refusal, at sixty-seven, of Richard Nixon''s 1969 offer to make him Chief Justice of the United States.

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: Central Intelligence Agency
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: 2026 Iran war
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: Abu Zubaydah
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: Adnan Khashoggi
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: Saudi arms dealer and Iran-Contra middleman whom John Kiriakou says was mentioned 'all the time' at the CIA — in pointed contrast to Jeffrey Epstein, whose name he never once heard there.

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: AIPAC
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: Asset acquisition cycle
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.title: Ceuta migrant crossings (2026)
spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.summary: The mass crossing of roughly 60,000 people from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in early August 2026. John Kiriakou reads the episode not as a spontaneous migration but as a deliberate act of Moroccan statecraft aimed at Spain, triggered by the Spanish prime minister's visit to Algeria, and rejects the widely circulated theory that Israel organised it.

spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.title: Morocco–Algeria rivalry
spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.summary: The long enmity between Morocco and Algeria over primacy in North Africa, which John Kiriakou identifies as the actual cause of the 2026 mass crossing into Ceuta after Spain's prime minister paid an official visit to Algiers.

spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.title: Thomas Massie
spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.summary: Republican U.S. Representative from Kentucky known for a constitutionalist voting record and consistent opposition to foreign military intervention; per John Kiriakou, a principled America-First congressman who votes with the president on the vast majority of issues, and whose opposition to U.S. funding of Israel and foreign wars is the only plausible explanation for the roughly $30 million spent by the Israel lobby to unseat him in a primary.

spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.title: AIPAC
spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.title: Temporary protected status
spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.summary: The American immigration category for people who cannot safely return home because of armed conflict, natural disaster or other temporary catastrophe. John Kiriakou treats it as a policy with no exit: when conditions in the home country never improve — often, he argues, because of American action — revoking the status amounts to a death sentence.

spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.title: Abdul El-Sayed
spanish-enclaves-in-north-africa.summary: Physician and Democratic Socialists of America-backed candidate in Michigan's 2026 Democratic Senate primary. John Kiriakou, who discloses a $100 donation to the campaign, presents him as the test case for whether the electability argument still works for establishment Democrats.

speakers-office-gatekeeping.title: Lobbyists writing legislation
speakers-office-gatekeeping.summary: John Kiriakou''s first-hand account from the Senate Foreign Relations Committee: told that the committee would take part in the carbon offsets debate and protesting that he knew nothing about carbon offsets, he was told not to worry — and the next day strangers came into the office, took over most of the desks, logged on and began writing the bill.

speakers-office-gatekeeping.title: Think tank financing
speakers-office-gatekeeping.summary: John Kiriakou's warning that Washington's think tanks — more than 1,200 of them by a Washington Post count — must be read through their funding, illustrated with the case of someone close to him who controlled about $200,000 a year in donations for a Fortune 100 defence contractor and moved the money when a household-name institute proved insufficiently pro-contractor.

speakers-office-gatekeeping.title: The Trumpcare confusion
speakers-office-gatekeeping.summary: A television interview John Kiriakou says he watched, in which a woman from Arkansas wept with gratitude to President Trump because a website had insured her son's cancer treatment — and, told by the reporter that this was in fact the Affordable Care Act, insisted that Obamacare had been repealed and replaced and that what she had was Trumpcare.

speakers-office-gatekeeping.title: Progressive taxation
speakers-office-gatekeeping.summary: John Kiriakou''s argument that the United States abandoned a system it was once proud of: taxation based, in Theodore Roosevelt''s formulation, on a person''s ability to pay. It fell apart under Ronald Reagan, he says, and the regressive substitutes now proposed — a higher gas tax among them — hit the people least able to absorb them.

speakers-office-gatekeeping.title: The Iron Dome
speakers-office-gatekeeping.summary: Israel's air-defence system as John Kiriakou reads it — impressive against a wave of slow Iranian drones, but shown by the handful that got through, and later by Iranian ballistic missiles, to be not all it is cracked up to be; each exchange, in his account, buying Iran intelligence about the gaps.

speakers-office-gatekeeping.title: Congressional intelligence oversight
speakers-office-gatekeeping.summary: John Kiriakou''s standing criticism of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Permanent Select Committee — that unlike the armed services and foreign relations committees, they do not perform oversight at all: "They''re just cheerleaders." His illustration is a sitting committee chairman who summoned him privately, then asked whether Kiriakou would write the criticism publicly on his behalf.

special-activities-division.title: Tuesday morning kill list
special-activities-division.summary: Weekly CIA targeting meeting instituted by John Brennan in 2009 during his service as Deputy National Security Advisor for Counterterrorism in the Obama administration; produced a written list of individuals to be killed in the following week; per John Kiriakou, the program was a source of pride within the Obama administration and was made operationally possible by the targeting-software sophistication of the period.

special-activities-division.title: Executive Order 12333
special-activities-division.summary: The U.S. presidential directive — in its post-9/11 amended form — that grants the CIA the legal authority to kill any individual anywhere in the world deemed by the agency to pose a "clear and present danger" to the United States; the legal foundation underlying both CIA paramilitary operations and the agency's contractor relationships including with Blackwater.

special-activities-division.title: Ground Branch
special-activities-division.summary: The land-operating component of the CIA's Special Activities Division, staffed almost entirely by former Delta Force and SEAL Team 6 operators rather than career officers; per John Kiriakou its job is to kill or kidnap anyone judged a threat to the United States, and its work is so secret that everyone in the office knew what they did and nobody mentioned it.

special-activities-division.title: MOSSAD
special-activities-division.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

special-activities-division.title: Global Services
special-activities-division.summary: The name John Kiriakou gives to the cadre now carrying out the Tuesday-morning White House kill-list meetings, a paramilitary team he says was trained after 9/11 by the head of the Special Activities Division, a former Cali Cartel hitman recruited into the CIA precisely because the agency needed people who knew how to kill without being caught.

special-activities-division.title: Jack Murphy NATO Sabotage Story
special-activities-division.summary: John Kiriakou's account of a story reported by podcaster Jack Murphy — over a year in the making, drawing on CIA and Army intelligence sources — alleging the CIA worked through a NATO partner to conduct sabotage inside Russia, including munitions-warehouse fires and rail explosions; killed before publication after the CIA deputy director denied it on a call with the editor and blamed "rogue Ukrainians."

special-operations-officer.title: Arabic and Greek
special-operations-officer.summary: The qualification John Kiriakou says opened the door to his transfer from CIA analysis to operations: a post in Athens wanted Greek or Arabic, and he had both — by most of his tellings the only officer in the agency who did. The chief who hired him gave the reason in one sentence: it is easier and cheaper to take a linguist and teach him operations than the other way round. The pairing also became a detection tool, since the language nobody speaks in Pakistan is Arabic.

special-operations-officer.title: Astrology at the CIA
special-operations-officer.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that astrology played a role in CIA work in the 1950s and early 1960s as part of MK-ULTRA, alongside time travel and teleportation — and his explanation for why: officials with unlimited budgets and no obligation to report to the public reasoned that there was probably nothing to it, but that if there were, it would make them a star.

special-operations-officer.title: Carrying passports in Washington
special-operations-officer.summary: John Kiriakou's report in September 2025 that people in Washington had begun carrying their passports for fear of being scooped up by immigration enforcement — alongside the case of an American symphony violinist held for three weeks, and his own belief that ethnic profiling violates the Fourth Amendment.

special-operations-officer.title: "Christians are suckers"
special-operations-officer.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for how a president who does not go to church, has no spiritual adviser and could not name a line of scripture can push school prayer without cost — that he thinks most Christians are suckers, an assessment Kiriakou says he hates to make and believes anyway.

special-operations-officer.title: CIA language training
special-operations-officer.summary: The agency''s language pipeline as John Kiriakou experienced and describes it: a full year of Arabic at nine hours a day, an optional second year at the State Department''s school, and the calculation that made his own career — that it is cheaper to teach a linguist operations than to teach an operations officer Greek and Arabic.

special-operations-officer.title: E. Jean Carroll
special-operations-officer.summary: The plaintiff whose persistence John Kiriakou singled out for deep respect — she kept suing after the political tide turned against her, and won an award he put at eighty-three or eighty-five million dollars on a day when Donald Trump won almost everything else in the federal courts.

spies-traded-home.title: Bowe Bergdahl
spies-traded-home.summary: The American soldier who walked off his base in Afghanistan, was captured by the Haqqani network and handed to the Taliban, and was repatriated in a prisoner trade — a man John Kiriakou says was treated as a traitor although he was not one.

spies-traded-home.title: Qat in Yemen
spies-traded-home.summary: The afternoon shrub-chewing habit of Yemen, and the special dispensation the CIA had to issue so that its officers could take part in it. John Kiriakou explains that no source could be developed in a qat-chewing country by an officer who would not chew.

spies-traded-home.title: Narcotics under cover
spies-traded-home.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to whether a CIA officer under cover may take drugs when an asset offers them: yes. The rule he describes begins with qat in Yemen and extends to cocaine in Latin America, on the ground that refusing can be a matter of life and death.

spies-traded-home.title: The Islamabad guest house
spies-traded-home.summary: The sixteen-room guest house in Islamabad that CIA officers took over entirely during the post-9/11 deployments — a place John Kiriakou says the agency still will not let him name, which came with breakfast, dinner and laundry for about thirty-five dollars a day against a per diem of five hundred.

spies-traded-home.title: A Middle East reading list
spies-traded-home.summary: The books and the starting point John Kiriakou recommends to anyone trying to understand the modern Middle East: begin at the end of the Second World War, not five thousand years earlier, and start with The House of Saud, the Sykes-Picot Agreement and From Beirut to Jerusalem.

spies-traded-home.title: Bombing the Omanis
spies-traded-home.summary: John Kiriakou's judgement that Iran's strikes on the Gulf states — and above all on Oman, which had been trying to broker peace — made enemies Iran did not need to make, of governments that would otherwise have sat the war out.

splc-2025-indictment.title: Hillary Clinton
splc-2025-indictment.summary: Former U.S. Secretary of State and 2016 presidential candidate; John Kiriakou describes her as arguably the most neoconservative candidate Democrats could have nominated, more militarist even than her husband, and credits her — separately — with correctly describing Iran as a military dictatorship run by the IRGC rather than a genuine theocracy.

splc-2025-indictment.title: John Kerry
splc-2025-indictment.summary: U.S. Senator from Massachusetts; chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee during John Kiriakou's 2009 service as the committee's senior investigator; subsequently U.S. Secretary of State; characterized by Kiriakou as a coward who buckled under CIA pressure on the Dasht-i-Leili reopening and as personally fixated on his perceived theft of the Secretary of State position by Hillary Clinton; the famously thrown medals were duplicates purchased at the post exchange.

splc-2025-indictment.title: Barack Obama
splc-2025-indictment.summary: 44th U.S. president; in John Kiriakou's account, Obama publicly recounted refusing Benjamin Netanyahu's demand to bomb Iran and calling Israel's threat to use nuclear weapons a bluff — a bluff Kiriakou says Donald Trump later believed.

splc-2025-indictment.title: Bill Clinton
splc-2025-indictment.summary: 42nd U.S. president whom John Kiriakou describes as wholly disinterested in intelligence — briefed by the CIA only twice in eight years, with Vice President Al Gore taking the daily briefing instead and relaying anything important.

splc-2025-indictment.title: Christopher Hitchens
splc-2025-indictment.summary: British-American journalist and author who, at John Kiriakou's telling, argued that CIA waterboarding was 'nothing … not a big deal,' underwent a filmed waterboarding in 2008, tapped out after roughly seventeen seconds, and suffered panic attacks thereafter. Kiriakou knew him and corresponded with him — the experiment happened because Hitchens thought Kiriakou was exaggerating — and remained an admirer of the writer and an opponent of his politics on Iraq.

splc-2025-indictment.title: CIA political neutrality tradition
splc-2025-indictment.summary: The informal midcentury norm at the Central Intelligence Agency, described by John Kiriakou from his own 1990-era experience, under which employees did not share their partisan affiliations at work, small displays such as a Bob Dole campaign bumper sticker in a cubicle triggered severe internal discipline, and career officers steered clear of political endorsement — a tradition Kiriakou argues collapsed by 2020, when 51 former intelligence officials signed the letter dismissing the Hunter Biden laptop story.

spongebob-shirt.title: The two Abu Zubaydahs
spongebob-shirt.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the first cousin who shared Abu Zubaydah's name, whose activities were folded into a single intelligence picture of a man Kiriakou called a terrorist Superman — and who vanished as soon as the capture reached the newspapers.

spongebob-shirt.title: Abu Zubaydah's diary
spongebob-shirt.summary: The notebook captured with Abu Zubaydah, containing drawings and poetry, over which the CIA and the FBI came to deep disagreement — an FBI psychologist calling it the rantings of a crazy person and John Kiriakou insisting it showed creativity in a man who was not crazy at all.

spongebob-shirt.title: The Syrian bodyguard
spongebob-shirt.summary: The 330-pound guard captured alongside Abu Zubaydah, whose gunshot wound John Kiriakou examined and found ringed by a dinner-plate powder burn — evidence that contradicted the official account and left Kiriakou with a question about Pakistani intentions he says he will never be able to answer.

spongebob-shirt.title: Abu Zubaydah
spongebob-shirt.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

spongebob-shirt.title: Buzzy Krongard
spongebob-shirt.summary: The executive director of the CIA — the agency's third-ranking officer — who sat on the board of Johns Hopkins Medical Center and, on learning that Abu Zubaydah had been captured wounded, had the hospital's top trauma surgeon flown to Pakistan on a CIA jet.

spongebob-shirt.title: "Beyond Your Dreams"
spongebob-shirt.summary: The gloss a host gave John Kiriakou on his first trip to China when he asked what the beautiful car with the BYD badge was — and the answer he got when he asked why he had never heard of it, which was that the United States is the only country where they are not sold.

sports-and-the-steelers-bar.title: Frank Snepp
sports-and-the-steelers-bar.summary: The CIA analyst who wrote Decent Interval, and whom John Kiriakou calls a giant — one of the great analysts of his generation, practically the first to say publicly that the United States was losing in Vietnam and committing atrocities there, who paid for it with his career and spent most of the rest of his life fighting the agency's publications review board.

sports-and-the-steelers-bar.title: Hot bunking
sports-and-the-steelers-bar.summary: John Kiriakou''s description of living conditions aboard the overcrowded American warships and submarines he has visited: three men to a bed on eight-hour rotations, a shared pillow, decks raised several inches by the canned food stacked underfoot, and nuclear submarines that surface not because they must but to keep the crew sane.

sports-and-the-steelers-bar.title: Israel, Turkey, and NATO Article 5
sports-and-the-steelers-bar.summary: John Kiriakou's scenario in which an Israeli attack on Turkey would oblige every NATO member, the United States included, to come to Turkey's defence — and in which the alliance would sooner dissolve than honour that obligation against Israel.

sports-and-the-steelers-bar.title: John Kiriakou
sports-and-the-steelers-bar.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

sports-and-the-steelers-bar.title: John McCain
sports-and-the-steelers-bar.summary: Late U.S. Senator from Arizona who gave the most consequential Senate-floor defense of John Kiriakou — declaring that 'if it weren't for John Kiriakou, the American people would never have had any idea what the CIA was doing in their name' — and sponsored the McCain–Feinstein amendment banning torture.

sports-and-the-steelers-bar.title: Kiriakou's Greek citizenship
sports-and-the-steelers-bar.summary: The Greek nationality John Kiriakou acquired in 2010, after his CIA career and before his prosecution — offered, he says, by the Greek ambassador who asked what could be done to help when his troubles began, and granted when he answered "you could give me Greek citizenship." Held by his children too, it made him a Greek national at the moment he became, in Greece, a national hero; it brought him the commission to write the country's whistleblower protection law, and the Athens job that turned out to be a money laundering operation.

spotting-a-cia-impostor.title: Dave Phillips
spotting-a-cia-impostor.summary: The FCI Loretto prisoner who claimed to have been a CIA operations officer and whom John Kiriakou exposed as a fake by testing him on agency vocabulary — a possessive, risk-taking companion who planted shanks on a pedophile, was caught, and was shipped to another prison.

spotting-a-cia-impostor.title: FCI Loretto
spotting-a-cia-impostor.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

spotting-a-cia-impostor.title: Mark Lanzalotti
spotting-a-cia-impostor.summary: The prisoner John Kiriakou describes as his closest friend at FCI Loretto and one of the finest human beings he has known — a first-time non-violent drug defendant sentenced to triple life without parole for refusing to inform, the prison's foremost cook and bookie, and the man whose release Kiriakou secured by writing his Second Chance Act petition.

spotting-a-cia-impostor.title: Cell transfers at Loretto
spotting-a-cia-impostor.summary: How a prisoner at FCI Loretto moved from one cell to another — a process requiring six months in place, the written agreement of the receiving cell and the signature of the counselor, which John Kiriakou describes as a guard assigned to be a designated pain in the ass.

spotting-a-cia-impostor.title: The shank planting incident
spotting-a-cia-impostor.summary: The episode at FCI Loretto in which Dave Phillips made two homemade weapons, planted them on a pedophile the group was feuding with and informed on him anonymously — a plan John Kiriakou refused to join, and which cost Phillips a transfer while leaving Kiriakou untouched.

spotting-a-cia-impostor.title: Blue
spotting-a-cia-impostor.summary: The FCI Loretto correctional officer, widely considered the most unpopular in the prison, who covered his own nameplate with masking tape so released prisoners could not find him — and who told a colleague of John Kiriakou's that he would never touch the CIA man because of the press attention.

spy-films-accuracy.title: The spy shop
spy-films-accuracy.summary: A London shop, with branches in New York and briefly Washington, where John Kiriakou says the CIA bought a good deal of the equipment it needed — on the reasoning that a thousand-dollar purchase beat a million-dollar development programme. Any member of the public could walk in and buy the same things; much of the rest, he says, came from Radio Shack. In six months in Pakistan he used more gadgets than in the whole of the rest of his career, and all but one of them were bought online.

spy-films-accuracy.title: Surveillance detection route
spy-films-accuracy.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

spy-films-accuracy.title: Abu Zubaydah
spy-films-accuracy.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

spy-films-accuracy.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
spy-films-accuracy.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

spy-films-accuracy.title: Bureau of Prisons advisory board
spy-films-accuracy.summary: The advisory board John Kiriakou joined at the personal invitation of the Director of the Bureau of Prisons, who told him the president had tasked him with tearing the Bureau down and rebuilding it.

spy-films-accuracy.title: The Green Line in Nicosia
spy-films-accuracy.summary: The division of Nicosia between the Republic of Cyprus and the Turkish-occupied north, which John Kiriakou toured in July 2026 and described as maintained through deliberate humiliation rather than any interest in settlement.

spy-films-on-screen.title: Bill Buckley
spy-films-on-screen.summary: CIA station chief in Beirut kidnapped by Palestinian Islamic Jihad in March 1984; tortured at length over fifteen months; killed in captivity; the case from which the agency derived a generation of operational-security lessons including the abandonment of single-point tracking devices in CIA officers' personal kit.

spy-films-on-screen.title: Zero Dark Thirty
spy-films-on-screen.summary: 2012 film dramatizing the CIA hunt for Osama bin Laden, criticized on release for suggesting torture produced the intelligence that led to his capture. John Kiriakou surveys the mixed critical reception — praise from Time and the New Yorker for its craft, condemnation from journalist Michael Wolff and director Kathryn Bigelow's critics for what they called pro-torture propaganda — and notes his friend Senator John McCain said the film left him "sick... because it is wrong."

spy-films-on-screen.title: Burn Notice
spy-films-on-screen.summary: Both a piece of real CIA tradecraft — a worldwide cable forbidding every officer from speaking to a named person — and the USA Network spy series named after it, which John Kiriakou watched as a fan before he became its script adviser — a job he obtained by sitting next to its creator, Matt Nix, on a flight from Washington to Los Angeles, having previously run the show's credits in slow motion to find out who was advising it. Nobody was. By the time the plane landed Kiriakou had the job for season six.

spy-films-on-screen.title: Exchange of bona fides
spy-films-on-screen.summary: The challenge-and-response protocol taught on the first day of CIA operational training, by which two intelligence officers who have never met establish that they are on the same side — a fixed nonsense phrase answered by a fixed nonsense phrase. Per John Kiriakou it is drilled hard enough that forgetting it under pressure, a staple of spy films, does not happen; if one side does not have the bona fides, "anything goes."

spy-films-on-screen.title: The Russian illegals program
spy-films-on-screen.summary: The Russian practice, described by John Kiriakou, of recruiting people — sometimes as children — training them abroad and inserting them into Western countries as sleepers who live ordinary lives for decades until they are activated. Kiriakou says a group of illegals was broken up by the FBI in his own Arlington, Virginia neighbourhood and traded for American spies, and that he knows a former KGB sleeper in Brooklyn who refused activation after the birth of his daughter.

spy-films-on-screen.title: Tony Mendez
spy-films-on-screen.summary: The CIA exfiltration specialist who got the American diplomats sheltering in the Canadian embassy out of revolutionary Tehran in 1979 by inventing a fake science-fiction film production — the operation dramatised in *Argo*. John Kiriakou calls him "a giant in the history of the CIA", says the same of his wife, and rates the operation among the greatest the agency has ever carried out.

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: Greek Intelligence Service
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: Greece's intelligence service, with which John Kiriakou worked closely during his Athens posting; its head of surveillance called off surveillance on him after watching him make a large offering at Saint Nectarios's tomb on the island of Aegina.

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: John Kiriakou
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: Church of Saint Porphyrios
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: The Greek Orthodox church in Gaza that John Kiriakou describes as the oldest continuously operating church in the world; per Kiriakou, Israel bombed it while 24 women and children were sheltering inside.

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: Seyyed Hossein Nasr
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: The scholar of Islamic philosophy under whom John Kiriakou studied Shiism as an undergraduate. Kiriakou calls him probably the most important Shia Muslim scholar in the world, notes that he is the father of Vali Nasr, and remarks that at ninety-eight he is still teaching.

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

st-porphyrios-church-gaza.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
st-porphyrios-church-gaza.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

st-porphyrios-church-gaza.title: John Kiriakou
st-porphyrios-church-gaza.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

st-porphyrios-church-gaza.title: Shireen Abu Akleh
