the-ai-weiwei-lego-portrait.summary: What John Kiriakou says he shouted at John Fetterman from ten rows back at an Ohio State football game — and his explanation, as a Pennsylvanian furious about the senator, of why Fetterman keeps his seat anyway.

the-ai-weiwei-lego-portrait.title: Ian Henderson
the-ai-weiwei-lego-portrait.summary: The British colonial police officer who ran Bahrain's intelligence service during John Kiriakou's posting there — a man Kiriakou says even the heir presumptive to the throne was afraid to name aloud, and whom Kiriakou, seated at the crown prince's table at a dinner for George H. W. Bush, mistook for a corpse.

the-ai-weiwei-lego-portrait.title: Ibrahim Traoré
the-ai-weiwei-lego-portrait.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of the military ruler of Burkina Faso — a young officer who took power promising a return to democracy, and who in Kiriakou's account has grown increasingly irrational, criminalising homosexuality, abolishing the electoral commission and moving to expel foreigners.

the-ai-weiwei-lego-portrait.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle in Athens
the-ai-weiwei-lego-portrait.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of Kimberly Guilfoyle's appointment as American ambassador to Greece — that she got it because Donald Trump Jr. wanted her out of the way, a manoeuvre he compares to Saddam Hussein's habit of exiling successful generals as ambassadors — and his reluctant conclusion that Greece could have done worse.

the-ai-weiwei-lego-portrait.title: Max Blumenthal
the-ai-weiwei-lego-portrait.summary: American investigative journalist and a personal friend of John Kiriakou, whom Kiriakou calls one of the most brilliant people he has ever encountered and singles out for an ability to assemble scattered fragments into a picture 'in a way that almost no one else I know is able to do.' Kiriakou also recounts Blumenthal's arrest outside the Venezuelan embassy, where he says video showed Blumenthal was the one assaulted, and counts him among the independent journalists under the same official pressure he is.

the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.title: Senate Foreign Relations Committee
the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.summary: Kiriakou was senior investigator under John Kerry — and still held the post when his own federal prosecution came to a head in January 2012.

the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.title: AIPAC
the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.title: MOSSAD
the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.title: Democratic silence on the Iran war
the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.summary: John Kiriakou's observation that the only front-facing critics of the 2026 Iran war came from the isolationist right, while Democrats said nothing. He attributes the silence to fear of an AIPAC-funded primary challenge, and singles out Senator Cory Booker as the illustration.

the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.title: Brian Ross
the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.summary: American investigative journalist and seven-time Emmy Award winner who was a prominent reporter at ABC News when, in December 2007, he conducted the on-camera interview with John Kiriakou that produced the first public confirmation by a U.S. official that the CIA waterboarded prisoners. Per Kiriakou, Ross called him out of the blue with the assertion that a source said Kiriakou had personally tortured Abu Zubaydah; Kiriakou's decision to give the interview anyway — driven by the conclusion that 'Brian Ross's source is at the White House and they're going to pin this on me' — became the pivot point of his entire post-CIA life.

the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.title: Central Intelligence Agency
the-aipac-holy-land-trip-offer.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.title: Bill Clinton
the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.summary: 42nd U.S. president whom John Kiriakou describes as wholly disinterested in intelligence — briefed by the CIA only twice in eight years, with Vice President Al Gore taking the daily briefing instead and relaying anything important.

the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.title: Nicholas Burns
the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.summary: The United States ambassador to Greece during John Kiriakou''s Athens tour — an envoy Kiriakou says he has always disliked and disrespected, whose unpopularity extended to his own staff, and whom he credits with exactly one good decision: drawing the assignments for a presidential visit out of a hat.

the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.title: The catering truck transfer
the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.summary: The covert removal of Donald Trump from Air Force One at the end of a NATO summit in Turkey — boarded in front of the television cameras, driven across the tarmac inside an airport catering truck, and flown on to Britain aboard a smaller jet while the White House press corps travelled on the aircraft everyone believed he was on.

the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.title: The Clinton Pakistan plane switch
the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.summary: Bill Clinton''s secret transfer to an unmarked aircraft for the 2000 flight into Pakistan — the closest precedent John Kiriakou finds for the catering truck transfer, and the one that differs in the detail he thinks matters: the White House told the reporters while it was happening.

the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.title: Fidel Castro
the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.summary: The Cuban leader John Kiriakou uses as his standing example of a relationship the United States could have had and chose not to — a rebel who liked America and had pitched in its minor leagues, written off because Washington had already committed itself to Batista. Castro also recurs across Kiriakou's account of the CIA as the agency's most-attempted assassination target, as the man who never cashed the rent cheques for Guantánamo, and as the figure American policy is still fighting years after his death.

the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.title: The Baltimore plot
the-air-force-one-bomb-threat.summary: The 1861 conspiracy to assassinate president-elect Abraham Lincoln as his train passed through Baltimore, uncovered by Pinkerton detectives — and the overnight passage in a soft felt hat and shawl that got him to his inauguration and made the press call him a coward.

the-airbridge.title: Declare victory and go home
the-airbridge.summary: The exit John Kiriakou prescribed for Israel in Gaza: turn the territory back to the United Nations, declare Hamas destroyed, declare victory, then engage the Saudis on the Abraham Accords and negotiate a deal later. His reasoning was that nothing remained to destroy, that killing as many people as possible is not a viable policy, and that Israel had no other way out.

the-airbridge.title: Bigger than the Russian embassy
the-airbridge.summary: Why American embassies in small, strategically unimportant countries are enormous: the answer John Kiriakou says he was given by a station chief on one of his first CIA trips — that the building had to be bigger than the Soviet one across town. He describes American embassies in Africa as "absolutely gigantic" for that reason alone, and calls the US embassy in Cairo an enormous facility matched by an equally enormous Russian one.

the-airbridge.title: "Every Israeli I ever knew"
the-airbridge.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the attitudes he encountered among Israelis he knew professionally and socially — that almost every one of them wanted the Palestinians killed or exiled — together with his description of a sensibility he says is palpable walking around Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, and his immediate self-correction when he overstated the claim.

the-airbridge.title: The desert sunset photograph
the-airbridge.summary: The half-hour standoff John Kiriakou describes with Saudi security after photographing a desert sunset that happened to include the Ministry of Interior in the distance — resolved, he says, only when he produced his black diplomatic passport. He also explains that the ban on photographing American embassies from the street is Office of Diplomatic Security policy rather than law, because such pictures can be used to case a building.

the-airbridge.title: "Do not ever attempt to contact me again"
the-airbridge.summary: The reply John Kiriakou says he received from John Kerry, then Secretary of State, after emailing him privately in the days before reporting to prison to beg that his sentence be commuted. Kiriakou had worked closely with Kerry for two and a half years; the one-line answer, sent after two or three days, was the last he ever heard from him.

the-airbridge.title: Palestine House
the-airbridge.summary: The Washington, DC meeting space and gallery for pro-Palestinian human rights groups, artists and musicians that John Kiriakou describes as newly opened on Capitol Hill — housed in a building donated by a Lebanese-American property developer, running programming several nights a week, and headed by Miko Peled.

the-al-mayadeen-debate.title: 2026 Iran war
the-al-mayadeen-debate.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-al-mayadeen-debate.title: The JCPOA
the-al-mayadeen-debate.summary: The Iran nuclear agreement, which John Kiriakou describes as having worked for the two or three years it was in force under an inspection regime identical to the one the United Nations had used in Iraq. He treats the American withdrawal as a strategic error that also exposed a contradiction in American law, since sanctioning every country doing business with Iran would have meant sanctioning Britain, France, Germany and Japan.

the-al-mayadeen-debate.title: The war powers resolution vote
the-al-mayadeen-debate.summary: John Kiriakou''s assessment of the congressional attempt to take back war powers over the 2026 Iran conflict: a sense-of-the-Congress resolution would have no teeth or authority, and a bill with legal force would simply be vetoed.

the-al-mayadeen-debate.title: "A policy support organization"
the-al-mayadeen-debate.summary: Asked how the CIA workforce would be reacting to the war on Iran, John Kiriakou answered from the Iraq war: people put their heads down and did as they were told, after a boss told an assembled group — all of whom opposed the invasion — that the agency is not a policy organization but a policy support organization, and would do what the White House told it to do.

the-al-mayadeen-debate.title: Akrotiri Village Evacuation
the-al-mayadeen-debate.summary: Kiriakou says the drone that hit Britain's Akrotiri base in Cyprus was likely an Israeli operation, staged and then falsely blamed on Iran.

the-al-mayadeen-debate.title: Al Jazeera blocked in the United States
the-al-mayadeen-debate.summary: Within hours of the first strikes on Iran, John Kiriakou reported that American cable carriers had pulled Al Jazeera — a friend in Florida texted him that Dish Network had blocked it, and viewers reported the same of Comcast Xfinity in Boston. His reading was blunt: they do not want Americans to see what is happening in the Middle East.

the-al-udeid-strike.title: The Saudi-administered Gaza proposal
the-al-udeid-strike.summary: An arrangement reported in the Israeli left-wing press and repeated by John Kiriakou as a possible basis for future talks: a disarmed, semi-independent Gaza policed and rebuilt by Saudi Arabia, with a port, an airport, a power grid and a sewage system.

the-al-udeid-strike.title: Bill Clinton
the-al-udeid-strike.summary: 42nd U.S. president whom John Kiriakou describes as wholly disinterested in intelligence — briefed by the CIA only twice in eight years, with Vice President Al Gore taking the daily briefing instead and relaying anything important.

the-al-udeid-strike.title: Church Committee
the-al-udeid-strike.summary: U.S. Senate investigative committee operating in 1975–1976 that examined domestic intelligence abuses by the CIA, FBI, and NSA; per John Kiriakou, the Church Committee — alongside the concurrent Pike Committee in the House — was the last genuine moment of legislative oversight over the intelligence community, born of a national consensus that government had gone dangerously off course. Its work led to the creation of the permanent Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, which Kiriakou says ceased to function as real oversight roughly seven years after its founding.

the-al-udeid-strike.title: Fifty new crimes a year
the-al-udeid-strike.summary: John Kiriakou''s argument that the United States has become a carceral country by legislative accretion — fifty newly created federal crimes every year for two decades, on top of five per cent of the world''s population holding twenty-five per cent of its prisoners.

the-al-udeid-strike.title: How Kiriakou went armed in Athens
the-al-udeid-strike.summary: The load John Kiriakou carried every day during his Athens tour — a 9mm in a tear-away waist pack with three magazines, a snub-nosed .38 on his ankle, about 47 rounds in total, and a buck knife his boss handed him on his first day *"just in case things go to shit"*.

the-al-udeid-strike.title: Presidential appetite for intelligence
the-al-udeid-strike.summary: John Kiriakou''s ranking of the presidents he served under by how much intelligence they actually wanted — from George H. W. Bush, who asked for special analytic products constantly, to Bill Clinton, who he says was briefed twice in eight years.

the-alaska-glacier.title: Phil Donahue
the-alaska-glacier.summary: American talk-show host who, John Kiriakou discovered seven years after the fact, had been secretly paying his weekly newspaper column fee — $400 a week for nine years, routed through Reader Supported News — because Donahue had learned that Kiriakou came out of prison broke and did not want him sleeping in his car.

the-alaska-glacier.title: Soviet Union
the-alaska-glacier.summary: The superpower whose collapse framed the start of John Kiriakou's CIA career — it was "literally in the process of collapsing" when he joined in January 1990, ushering in a brief "peace dividend" era when the agency's new threats were environmental degradation and AIDS. Kiriakou cites Brzezinski's "Afghan trap" that lured the Soviets into Afghanistan, argues the U.S. abandoned the radicalized mujahideen the moment the Soviets were beaten, notes America then took "a vacation from history," and recalls that Jonathan Pollard's stolen documents were traded by Israel to the Soviets in exchange for Russian Jews.

the-alaska-glacier.title: The armour at Union Station
the-alaska-glacier.summary: John Kiriakou''s eyewitness account of stepping off an Amtrak train at Washington''s Union Station in August 2025 to find two armoured personnel carriers and a .50 calibre machine gun trained on the entrance — and of tourists posing for photographs with the National Guardsmen deployed in the parts of the city where, he says, there is no crime.

the-alaska-glacier.title: The land-bridge precedents
the-alaska-glacier.summary: John Kiriakou''s argument, made during the August 2025 Washington summit on Ukraine, that the Russian demand for a land bridge to Crimea is a solved problem in diplomatic history — the corridor that connected West Germany to West Berlin being the obvious model — and that no American network was discussing what he considered the likely linchpin of any agreement.

the-alaska-glacier.title: The water''s-edge doctrine
the-alaska-glacier.summary: The old American convention that partisan disagreement stops at the border, which John Kiriakou says was destroyed by Newt Gingrich in 1995 — and whose collapse he offers as the reason the United States has spent thirty years unable to sustain a foreign policy across a change of administration.

the-alaska-glacier.title: Thomas Dewey
the-alaska-glacier.summary: New York prosecutor, governor and twice-defeated Republican presidential candidate, discussed by John Kiriakou for two reasons: the explanation he encountered for Dewey''s 1948 loss to Harry Truman — that Dewey''s short-cropped moustache reminded an intensely anti-fascist American public of Adolf Hitler — and Dewey''s refusal, at sixty-seven, of Richard Nixon''s 1969 offer to make him Chief Justice of the United States.

the-alcatraz-walkthrough.title: The Ai Weiwei encounter in Berlin
the-alcatraz-walkthrough.summary: John Kiriakou met the artist Ai Weiwei by pure chance on a Berlin street while dragging a suitcase to the airport after a board meeting — an encounter that led to a tour of Ai Weiwei's studio and a signed iPhone case bearing the Lego portrait the artist had made of him for an exhibition at Alcatraz.

the-alcatraz-walkthrough.title: Domingo's television
the-alcatraz-walkthrough.summary: John Kiriakou has used the television rooms at FCI Loretto as his sharpest illustration of prison segregation: sets owned by racial blocs since a riot in the 1990s, a seat in front of one costing fourteen dollars, and one set left tuned to Law & Order every morning because a man named Domingo had paid four hundred dollars for it and had been gone for years.

the-alcatraz-walkthrough.title: Mental health as a disciplinary problem
the-alcatraz-walkthrough.summary: John Kiriakou has said that before his own prosecution he never gave five seconds of thought to the American prison system, and that living inside it showed him a broken one — in particular a system in which mental health is treated as a disciplinary problem rather than a medical one.

the-alcatraz-walkthrough.title: The 2017 European tour
the-alcatraz-walkthrough.summary: In May 2017 John Kiriakou spent a week speaking about national security whistleblowing in Iceland, Germany, Luxembourg, Belgium and Ireland, addressing the German Parliament and sharing panels with serving European ministers — an audience he contrasted sharply with his reception in the United States, and one he found newly willing to break with Washington because it was, in his word, panic-stricken about Donald Trump.

the-alcatraz-walkthrough.title: The attribution problem in the DNC hack
the-alcatraz-walkthrough.summary: Asked in 2017 whether he had any confidence in the intelligence community's assessments of Russian interference, John Kiriakou said he had none — objecting that no one had ever defined what was meant by hacking, that the published evidence told the public nothing, and that an agency asking to be taken at its word should not be.

the-alcatraz-walkthrough.title: The case against work camps
the-alcatraz-walkthrough.summary: John Kiriakou, who asked to serve his own sentence at a minimum-security work camp and was sent to the prison across the street instead, came out of prison arguing that the camps should not exist at all — and, in the same breath, that some prisoners are dangerous enough that prisons certainly should.

the-alternative-obituaries.title: The 9/11 truth honorarium
the-alternative-obituaries.summary: How John Kiriakou came to headline a 9/11 truth event he had not realised was one: a $500 speaking fee from a PR man he had known through better days, a poster that revealed the sponsor, a sister telling him to withdraw, and his decision to honour the commitment anyway — while telling the audience to their faces that he would never believe Building 7 was a controlled demolition or that explosive thermite paint exists.

the-alternative-obituaries.title: The unswept roof
the-alternative-obituaries.summary: John Kiriakou''s two security observations after the killing of Charlie Kirk: that drone surveillance of outdoor events is cheap, easy and has no reason not to be used; and that the building the shooter is said to have fired from had been closed for renovation since April and supposedly locked up tight, yet nobody in the campus police department appears to have walked up to the roof to check.

the-alternative-obituaries.title: Area 58
the-alternative-obituaries.summary: The claim John Kiriakou says was put to him by a man who presents as entirely serious and is writing a book about it: that beyond Area 51 there is an Area 58 — seven more, and that much more secret — containing an underground bunker where alien craft land, known to those involved as the embassy because it is where the United States liaises with the aliens.

the-alternative-obituaries.title: Leaks come from the Pentagon
the-alternative-obituaries.summary: John Kiriakou''s rule of attribution for national security leaks, drawn from his own CIA experience: ninety-nine times out of a hundred the leak came from the Pentagon — which he says leaks constantly, is so gigantic that the source cannot be traced, and does not polygraph anybody. He adds the motive: somebody who opposed the operation and was overruled.

the-alternative-obituaries.title: Luis Elizondo
the-alternative-obituaries.summary: Why John Kiriakou never booked the best-known public advocate for unidentified aerial phenomena on his RT programme: viewers kept insisting Elizondo was an expert, so Kiriakou researched him and found chiefly Elizondo saying he was an expert. He says he does not know what the man is an expert on, and that it was not a fit for the show.

the-alternative-obituaries.title: The Australian pilot
the-alternative-obituaries.summary: The disappearance John Kiriakou recounts as an argument for declassification rather than as proof of anything: a pilot in his early twenties flying on 10 September 1978 who radioed that a silver cylinder was above his aircraft matching his speed exactly, said it was not an aircraft, was cut off by a loud sound of electronic interference, and was never seen again — along with the plane.

the-american-war-against-iran-correction.title: Donald Trump
the-american-war-against-iran-correction.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

the-american-war-against-iran-correction.title: Hezbollah
the-american-war-against-iran-correction.summary: Lebanese Shia militant organization and political party. Per John Kiriakou, Israel''s strategic goal regarding Hezbollah is not to defeat it outright but to keep Lebanon in a state of chaos that serves Israeli interests. He cites two Israeli operations: the simultaneous pager-detonation attack that decapitated Hezbollah''s leadership, which he called ''the most incredible operation I''ve ever seen,'' and the strike that killed former leader Hassan Nasrallah by leveling an entire complex and killing roughly 300 people — which he characterized as a war crime.

the-american-war-against-iran-correction.title: South Lebanon displacement, 2026
the-american-war-against-iran-correction.summary: John Kiriakou''s assessment of the Israeli campaign in southern Lebanon running alongside the 2026 Iran war: mass evacuation orders, hundreds of thousands internally displaced, and his conclusion that Israel has guaranteed Lebanon will be a failed state. He notes the world is not watching because it is watching Iran.

the-american-war-against-iran-correction.title: 2026 Iran war economic shock
the-american-war-against-iran-correction.summary: John Kiriakou''s running assessment of the economic damage from the 2026 Iran war — an oil shock he says already exceeds both 1970s shocks combined, a natural-gas shock worse than the Nord Stream destruction, and a chokepoint problem that runs through fertilizer as much as fuel, since 65% of the world''s supply must transit the Strait of Hormuz. His summary: "This is an economic slowdown of choice."

the-american-war-against-iran-correction.title: Advice to an aspiring intelligence analyst
the-american-war-against-iran-correction.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to a 21-year-old student asking what to study and what to read: pick a geographic area, become the go-to person on it, and consume everything published in the field — including the journals written by people who have never made policy.

the-american-war-against-iran-correction.title: AIPAC
the-american-war-against-iran-correction.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

the-anne-coulter-dinner.title: Presidents asleep in meetings
the-anne-coulter-dinner.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to who is the highest-profile person he ever saw fall asleep in a meeting — George H. W. Bush — together with his explanation that presidents do it all the time because the demands on their time leave too few hours in the day, and his father''s account of Ronald Reagan doing it constantly.

the-anne-coulter-dinner.title: Barrett Brown
the-anne-coulter-dinner.summary: American journalist and former Anonymous associate whom John Kiriakou describes as one of the most intelligent writers and analysts he has ever encountered, with long-standing mental health problems and a two-decade heroin addiction he has now been clear of for at least a year, expelled from the United Kingdom and relocated to Mexico.

the-anne-coulter-dinner.title: Censorship on the left
the-anne-coulter-dinner.summary: John Kiriakou''s observation that he was censored far less by Forbes and Fortune than by The Nation and Mother Jones, which he offers as an instance of a general rule that a writer''s own side censors them hardest — the counterpart to Ted Rall''s account of being made to fit a particular kind of leftism rather than any kind.

the-anne-coulter-dinner.title: Dr Oz and the Armenian hospices
the-anne-coulter-dinner.summary: John Kiriakou''s reaction to a television segment by Mehmet Oz alleging fraud by Armenian-run hospices in Los Angeles — that a man he identifies as a veteran of the Turkish special forces zeroing in on Armenians in California is not a coincidence, and that each of the administration''s appointees appears to arrive with a racial scandal of their own.

the-anne-coulter-dinner.title: The Iron Dome
the-anne-coulter-dinner.summary: Israel's air-defence system as John Kiriakou reads it — impressive against a wave of slow Iranian drones, but shown by the handful that got through, and later by Iranian ballistic missiles, to be not all it is cracked up to be; each exchange, in his account, buying Iran intelligence about the gaps.

the-anne-coulter-dinner.title: James Morris
the-anne-coulter-dinner.summary: A close friend of John Kiriakou''s who served seventeen years of a twenty-year sentence for a crime committed at sixteen, found on release that a violent felony conviction closed off employment, made his own way to Turkey and across the border into Syria, spent two years fighting alongside the Kurds against ISIS, and later took his own life.

the-anti-semite-smear.title: The Epstein files and the Starmer government
the-anti-semite-smear.summary: John Kiriakou's prediction that the Epstein disclosures could bring down Keir Starmer's government, on the strength of evidence that Prince Andrew and Peter Mandelson gave Epstein classified British Ministry of Defence documents — an Official Secrets Act matter that in America would fall under the Espionage Act.

the-anti-semite-smear.title: The Piers Morgan panel
the-anti-semite-smear.summary: The televised debate John Kiriakou returns to most often — two against two, with Scott Horton and himself on one side and Alan Dershowitz and a senior former Israeli official on the other. Kiriakou set out his position on Hamas, October 7th and Gaza, and Piers Morgan told him at the end that he had come around and agreed. On a second appearance from the same panel he argued that Jeffrey Epstein was an Israeli access agent, provoked Dershowitz — Epstein's own attorney — into an interruption Kiriakou considers self-defeating, and got an unbothered "who knows?" from the Israeli.

the-anti-semite-smear.title: Prince Andrew
the-anti-semite-smear.summary: British royal, now Andrew Mountbatten Windsor, named repeatedly by John Kiriakou as one of the un-recruitable principals whose access made Jeffrey Epstein valuable to a foreign intelligence service. Kiriakou has asked why Andrew was never charged over conduct with minors, reads his alleged provision of classified Ministry of Defence documents to Epstein as evidence of espionage rather than vanity — and expects him to face no criminal consequence at all, because the statute of limitations has run.

the-anti-semite-smear.title: Alan Dershowitz
the-anti-semite-smear.summary: American attorney and Harvard Law professor; John Kiriakou describes debating him on Piers Morgan's show over Jeffrey Epstein, telling Dershowitz he would have wanted to see him "hanging from a tree" had he sought leniency for Epstein as an Israeli spy — and cites attorney David Boies's on-air statement that Dershowitz was far more than Epstein's lawyer, also serving as his publicist, friend, and a guest on Epstein's island.

the-anti-semite-smear.title: Bahrain's naturalisation policy
the-anti-semite-smear.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how the Bahraini royal family changed the sectarian arithmetic of the country over thirty years — importing Syrians and naturalising Indian and Pakistani Sunni Muslims until a population that had been two-thirds to three-quarters Shia was closer to half and half.

the-anti-semite-smear.title: Bombing the Omanis
the-anti-semite-smear.summary: John Kiriakou's judgement that Iran's strikes on the Gulf states — and above all on Oman, which had been trying to broker peace — made enemies Iran did not need to make, of governments that would otherwise have sat the war out.

the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.title: The Fox News military analyst
the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.summary: The cable-news commentator John Kiriakou says he identified as a fraud within a single green-room conversation, because the man used movie vocabulary — black ops, wet work — where a real officer would have named a directorate. The man had obtained a Defense Department clearance on the strength of his claimed CIA service, advised generals in Afghanistan, and was later arrested and imprisoned for fraud.

the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.title: George W. Bush
the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.summary: 43rd President of the United States. In John Kiriakou's telling, Bush signed the August 1, 2002 executive order that authorized the CIA torture program, spent years telling the public "we don't torture," and — days after Kiriakou's 2007 ABC interview — blamed torture on "a rogue CIA officer" while walking from the White House South Portico to Marine One, a moment Kiriakou instantly read as the White House preparing to pin the program on him. Bush also ordered the FBI removed from Abu Zubaydah's black site, flew the bin Laden family out of the country after 9/11, and loosened the assassination ban of Executive Order 12333.

the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.title: Spotting a CIA impostor
the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.summary: John Kiriakou's method for exposing people who falsely claim to have served in the CIA — a short sequence of questions about directorate, division and leadership whose correct answers, he says, cannot be guessed by anyone who was never inside.

the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.title: The seventh Espionage Act defendant
the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.summary: The case John Kiriakou cited two days before his own sentencing to correct the count of Espionage Act prosecutions brought under Barack Obama — a translator at the American naval base in Bahrain who had just been charged, making seven, against three in the whole history of the United States before 2009.

the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.title: The whiskers rule
the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.summary: John Kiriakou's description of the cultural practice he says American personnel encountered with some regularity in Afghanistan — that a boy who has not yet reached puberty is treated as available for sexual abuse — and his account of what he understood to have happened, and not happened, at Abu Ghraib.

the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.title: CIA directorates
the-applicant-who-invented-a-cia-career.summary: The four-part internal division of the CIA as John Kiriakou describes it to lay audiences — the Directorate of Intelligence that analyses, the Directorate of Operations that recruits spies and steals secrets, the administrative arm that makes the trains run on time, and the Directorate of Science and Technology that supplies the scientists, forgers and disguise makers — the structure that determines which training a new officer receives.

the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.title: Julian Assange
the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.title: Congressional intelligence oversight
the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.summary: John Kiriakou''s standing criticism of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Permanent Select Committee — that unlike the armed services and foreign relations committees, they do not perform oversight at all: "They''re just cheerleaders." His illustration is a sitting committee chairman who summoned him privately, then asked whether Kiriakou would write the criticism publicly on his behalf.

the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.title: Five Eyes
the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.summary: The intelligence-sharing partnership of the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand

the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.title: Vault 7
the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.summary: The 2017 WikiLeaks disclosure of thousands of pages of CIA Directorate of Science and Technology documents — leaked by agency engineer Joshua Schulte — revealing CIA technical capabilities including remote takeover of internet-connected cars, conversion of smart-TV speakers into covert microphones, and the planting of Russian or Persian language fragments in foreign systems to mislead attribution.

the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.title: MI6
the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.summary: The United Kingdom''s Secret Intelligence Service, the foreign-intelligence service of the British government and the closest CIA liaison partner under the Five Eyes framework. Per John Kiriakou, MI6 was the parent organization that asked Truman after WWII to set up a ''central intelligence agency'' on the model of its own service — making the CIA in effect MI6''s little brother. Kiriakou''s stated view of the historical relationship: MI6 saw the CIA as its little brother, then after the empire fell apart as its big brother, and then after 9/11 as ''strangers'' because U.S. policy became ''simply to kill everybody.''

the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.title: Palantir Technologies
the-approvals-required-to-kill-assange.summary: U.S. data-analytics and intelligence-software company; received its first $1.5 million in seed funding from the CIA's In-Q-Tel venture-capital arm around 2002; characterized by John Kiriakou as functionally inseparable from the CIA in 2025, drawing the majority of its revenue from agency contracts and operating across DARPA, NSA, and the broader U.S. national-security apparatus.

the-arlington-house.title: Abigail Spanberger
the-arlington-house.summary: Governor of Virginia from 2025 and, before Congress, a CIA officer alongside John Kiriakou in the Counterterrorism Center — whom he calls a perfectly nice person who would have been a middle-of-the-road Republican in the 1970s and 1980s, and whose victory speech, to his surprise, said all the right things.

the-arlington-house.title: Canada as a bargaining chip
the-arlington-house.summary: John Kiriakou's reading of Mark Carney's Davos speech as the moment Canada stopped pretending the United States could be trusted as a long-term partner — and his account of what wore the relationship out, including Washington's insistence that Ottawa arrest Huawei's chief financial officer on a computer-hacking charge and hold her for three years to trade.

the-arlington-house.title: China's generals without combat experience
the-arlington-house.summary: Presented with the observation that China's purged and reshuffled top brass are now too young to have fought in any war, John Kiriakou agreed it mattered little in the near term and a great deal in the long term — because American military planning will have to account for an adversary whose senior commanders have never been in combat.

the-arlington-house.title: Ilhan Omar
the-arlington-house.summary: U.S. Representative whom John Kiriakou credits with sponsoring a rewrite of the Espionage Act in two consecutive Congresses — legislation he says is dead on arrival with a Republican House because of who she is. Kiriakou has also sat at her table — in January 2026 he was one of about twenty guests at a dinner where Omar described the federal operation in Minneapolis and the budget manoeuvre that funded every part of the government except Homeland Security.

the-arlington-house.title: Jason Miyares
the-arlington-house.summary: The Cuban-born Republican attorney general of Virginia whom John Kiriakou expected to be a right-wing disaster and found instead to be excellent — a judgement he says is hard for him to make about a conservative Republican, and which he repeated on the night Miyares was unceremoniously thrown out of office.

the-arlington-house.title: The Perplexity subscription
the-arlington-house.summary: The free lifetime account John Kiriakou says the chief executive of Perplexity emailed him at ten o'clock at night, days after he told Joe Rogan's audience that ChatGPT had invented a University of Maryland degree and a Belgian graduate school for him — and that when he corrected it, the machine argued back.

the-armenian-podcasters.title: Clock Tower X
the-armenian-podcasters.summary: The American firm John Kiriakou described as being paid $6 million by the Israeli government to make ChatGPT more pro-Israeli by generating content, gaming algorithms and managing AI frameworks.

the-armenian-podcasters.title: The October 2025 poll of American Jews
the-armenian-podcasters.summary: The Washington Post poll John Kiriakou cited, released on 5 October 2025, which he said found for the first time that a majority of American Jews believed Israel was committing genocide in Gaza — and the question he built on it.

the-armenian-podcasters.title: AIPAC
the-armenian-podcasters.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

the-armenian-podcasters.title: AIPAC and foreign-agent registration
the-armenian-podcasters.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that AIPAC is the only organization of its kind exempt from registering under the Foreign Agents Registration Act — set against his own experience around 2008, when a contract worth five or six thousand dollars to write four op-eds praising the Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce obliged him to register as a foreign agent.

the-armenian-podcasters.title: Dr Oz and the Armenian hospices
the-armenian-podcasters.summary: John Kiriakou''s reaction to a television segment by Mehmet Oz alleging fraud by Armenian-run hospices in Los Angeles — that a man he identifies as a veteran of the Turkish special forces zeroing in on Armenians in California is not a coincidence, and that each of the administration''s appointees appears to arrive with a racial scandal of their own.

the-armenian-podcasters.title: Nixon's guarantee of Israeli national security
the-armenian-podcasters.summary: John Kiriakou's account that AIPAC, having begun to focus on election fundraising in the late 1960s, succeeded in getting President Nixon to guarantee Israeli national security in 1969 — a commitment he says no American president had made before.

the-armitage-leak.title: The thirty-seven analysts
the-armitage-leak.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Tulsi Gabbard firing thirty-seven CIA analysts connected to the national intelligence estimate on Russian election interference, publishing their names, and thereby — because one of them was undercover — violating the same Intelligence Identities Protection Act of 1981 under which he was himself prosecuted. He says she will not be charged, and argues nobody should be.

the-armitage-leak.title: Suing the CIA
the-armitage-leak.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to whether anyone has ever successfully sued the CIA in civil court: not that he knows of. He allows only what he calls small, picky victories — chiefly suing for the right to sue — and applies the same pessimism to the burned officer whose case prompted the question.

the-armitage-leak.title: Mark Polymeropoulos
the-armitage-leak.summary: The CIA officer John Kiriakou describes as a friend who was in his first tour when Aldrich Ames blew his identity, was brought in from the cold, and later became station chief in Moscow — an appointment Kiriakou characterises as a deliberate thumb in the Russians'' eye: the officer their spy had burned, put in charge of operations against them.

the-armitage-leak.title: How the CIA kills
the-armitage-leak.summary: John Kiriakou''s description of the methods used when the CIA is ordered to kill someone outside a war zone: a team parachuting in miles away, stealing a car, a locks-and-picks specialist opening the door and suppressed weapons inside; a snatch into a van bound for an airport or a boat; or a brush past in a market with something poisoned — a technique he says the Russians used often and taught the Bulgarians into the early 1980s.

the-armitage-leak.title: Nine recruitments in twenty-five years
the-armitage-leak.summary: The conversation in which John Kiriakou''s Athens station chief, a twenty-five-year operations officer who had reached senior intelligence service level four with nine recruitments to his name, pointed out that Kiriakou had recruited five in two years — and Kiriakou''s explanation of the knack: that he could hide his disdain for a man completely while talking about whatever interested him.

the-armitage-leak.title: SEALs on loan to the CIA
the-armitage-leak.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to why the CIA did not use its own paramilitary team against Osama bin Laden: it did. The raid was a CIA operation directed by the Counterterrorism Center, and every Navy SEAL involved was temporarily a CIA contractor, on loan to the agency for the duration.

the-armour-at-union-station.title: Thomas Dewey
the-armour-at-union-station.summary: New York prosecutor, governor and twice-defeated Republican presidential candidate, discussed by John Kiriakou for two reasons: the explanation he encountered for Dewey''s 1948 loss to Harry Truman — that Dewey''s short-cropped moustache reminded an intensely anti-fascist American public of Adolf Hitler — and Dewey''s refusal, at sixty-seven, of Richard Nixon''s 1969 offer to make him Chief Justice of the United States.

the-armour-at-union-station.title: Phil Donahue
the-armour-at-union-station.summary: American talk-show host who, John Kiriakou discovered seven years after the fact, had been secretly paying his weekly newspaper column fee — $400 a week for nine years, routed through Reader Supported News — because Donahue had learned that Kiriakou came out of prison broke and did not want him sleeping in his car.

the-armour-at-union-station.title: Soviet Union
the-armour-at-union-station.summary: The superpower whose collapse framed the start of John Kiriakou's CIA career — it was "literally in the process of collapsing" when he joined in January 1990, ushering in a brief "peace dividend" era when the agency's new threats were environmental degradation and AIDS. Kiriakou cites Brzezinski's "Afghan trap" that lured the Soviets into Afghanistan, argues the U.S. abandoned the radicalized mujahideen the moment the Soviets were beaten, notes America then took "a vacation from history," and recalls that Jonathan Pollard's stolen documents were traded by Israel to the Soviets in exchange for Russian Jews.

the-armour-at-union-station.title: The Alaska glacier
the-armour-at-union-station.summary: The visitor centre John Kiriakou saw on a 2016 trip to Alaska with Gary Johnson, built at the foot of a glacier close enough to touch from the observation deck and by then a quarter of a mile away from it — an image he uses as the plainest available demonstration of climate change, and one he refuses to let pass as a joke.

the-armour-at-union-station.title: The CIA and Iridium
the-armour-at-union-station.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the Central Intelligence Agency buying the satellite telephone company Iridium when it was unprofitable and about to go out of business, because the agency needed the network — a purchase he places alongside its acquisition of Intelsat, and which he encountered personally when he had to rent the phones for Afghanistan.

the-armour-at-union-station.title: The diplomatic stool collection
the-armour-at-union-station.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that visiting heads of state routinely carry their own faeces home rather than leave them in an American hotel — because, in his account, entities within the United States government will gladly collect the material for its DNA and health information, and the hotel employee who retrieves it is a CIA officer under cover.

the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.title: The Gang of Four and Gang of Eight
the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.summary: John Kiriakou''s description of how the CIA restricts notification of its most sensitive covert operations to four or eight congressional leaders, and his verdict on the practice: because a member of an intelligence committee can be an overseer without being cleared for what is being overseen, the arrangement is not oversight but, in his word, gangsterism.

the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.title: The CIA as a paramilitary organization
the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.summary: John Kiriakou''s periodisation of the CIA''s mission — spying and analysis until Vietnam, restored after the Church and Pike hearings of 1975, and converted immediately after September 11 into a paramilitary body that he says it has remained ever since. His objection is stated without hedging: drawing up a kill list every Tuesday and dispatching officers to carry it out is not intelligence, it is murder.

the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.title: Abolish the CIA
the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.summary: John Kiriakou's position that the CIA should be abolished because its functions are already duplicated by the other 17 U.S. intelligence agencies — analysis by the State Department, human spying by the Pentagon, technology by DARPA, NSA and the private sector.

the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.title: James Bond
the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.summary: The fictional spy who got John Kiriakou — and, he says, half the Directorate of Operations — into the business. He asked for walkie-talkies at nine and told his father at sixteen that he wanted to be a spy in the Middle East; he concedes "literally none of it is true to life", but vouches for one scene: Bond always runs into the CIA officer at the party. The figure follows him to the end, too — a personality paper titled "Who is James Bond?" describes the officer type in terms he finds harsh, and federal prosecutors, he says, argued for his detention by talking about him "like I was 007."

the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.title: CIA attention to West Africa
the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer on whether the CIA is likely to be operating in Burkina Faso: for all the years he was at the agency it cared very little about Africa and especially West Africa, but the presence of al-Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates plus the drug trade makes CIA and special forces involvement probable — and, he adds, the American public will not hear about it.

the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.title: CIA–FBI incompatible computer systems
the-ask-forgiveness-maxim.summary: John Kiriakou's claim that from the CIA's founding in 1947 until 2009 the computer systems of the CIA and the FBI were not compatible with one another — no message could be sent from one to the other and no intelligence shared — which he offers both as the material substrate of the interagency hatred that helped make September 11 possible, and as the gap through which James Mitchell and Bruce Jessen were able to pass Ali Soufan's FBI debriefings of Abu Zubaydah off as the fruits of torture.

the-asset-recruitment-cycle.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
the-asset-recruitment-cycle.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

the-asset-recruitment-cycle.title: Asset acquisition cycle
the-asset-recruitment-cycle.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

the-asset-recruitment-cycle.title: The polygraph
the-asset-recruitment-cycle.summary: The lie-detector examination that gates entry to the CIA, described by John Kiriakou from the inside: the twenty-minute wiring-up, the psychiatrist''s advice to stare at a speck on the wall, the deliberately planted false accusation used to test a candidate''s reaction, and his contention that the machine screens out exactly the wrong people.

the-asset-recruitment-cycle.title: The Farm
the-asset-recruitment-cycle.summary: The CIA's clandestine training facility in Virginia; site of approximately 80% of all CIA operational training

the-asset-recruitment-cycle.title: Counterterrorism Center
the-asset-recruitment-cycle.summary: The CIA's Counterterrorism Center (CTC) — the unit where John Kiriakou spent the defining years of his operational career. He joined in the late 1990s as the only officer in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic, served as chief of counterintelligence in the bin Laden unit, watched the Center swell from a few hundred employees to nearly 2,000 by September 12, 2001, and it was to CTC that he walked back down in May 2002 to refuse the torture program — the moment, he says, the CIA began to turn on him.

the-asset-recruitment-cycle.title: The tier one walk-up
the-asset-recruitment-cycle.summary: The recruitment John Kiriakou calls one of the best operations of his career and credits entirely to his mentor Gust Avrakotos: an approach to an official of a tier one country — one of America''s greatest enemies — made by the simple expedient of walking right up to the man''s house, a technique Avrakotos had used himself in the 1970s.

the-atf-funding-rider.title: The Guantanamo airfare catch
the-atf-funding-rider.summary: The pair of legal traps John Kiriakou describes around the detainees at Guantanamo Bay who have been cleared for release: no country will take them and Congress defunded the ability to pay for their flights, while a separate 2009 statute forbids any of them from setting foot on United States soil — so that even a conviction could not be served in an American prison.

the-atf-funding-rider.title: Barrett Brown
the-atf-funding-rider.summary: American journalist and former Anonymous associate whom John Kiriakou describes as one of the most intelligent writers and analysts he has ever encountered, with long-standing mental health problems and a two-decade heroin addiction he has now been clear of for at least a year, expelled from the United Kingdom and relocated to Mexico.

the-atf-funding-rider.title: Censorship on the left
the-atf-funding-rider.summary: John Kiriakou''s observation that he was censored far less by Forbes and Fortune than by The Nation and Mother Jones, which he offers as an instance of a general rule that a writer''s own side censors them hardest — the counterpart to Ted Rall''s account of being made to fit a particular kind of leftism rather than any kind.

the-atf-funding-rider.title: Dr Oz and the Armenian hospices
the-atf-funding-rider.summary: John Kiriakou''s reaction to a television segment by Mehmet Oz alleging fraud by Armenian-run hospices in Los Angeles — that a man he identifies as a veteran of the Turkish special forces zeroing in on Armenians in California is not a coincidence, and that each of the administration''s appointees appears to arrive with a racial scandal of their own.

the-atf-funding-rider.title: The Iron Dome
the-atf-funding-rider.summary: Israel's air-defence system as John Kiriakou reads it — impressive against a wave of slow Iranian drones, but shown by the handful that got through, and later by Iranian ballistic missiles, to be not all it is cracked up to be; each exchange, in his account, buying Iran intelligence about the gaps.

the-atf-funding-rider.title: James Morris
the-atf-funding-rider.summary: A close friend of John Kiriakou''s who served seventeen years of a twenty-year sentence for a crime committed at sixteen, found on release that a violent felony conviction closed off employment, made his own way to Turkey and across the border into Syria, spent two years fighting alongside the Kurds against ISIS, and later took his own life.

the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.title: The Flynn charges
the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.summary: John Kiriakou supported the appointment of a special counsel in 2017 while rejecting the Russia allegations outright — arguing that the case for an investigation rested not on election interference but on a list of ordinary, provable crimes he believed senior Trump campaign figures, and Michael Flynn in particular, had already committed.

the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.title: The Washington Post editorial on the cover-up
the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.summary: In May 2017 John Kiriakou pointed to an editorial in a newspaper he says he generally hates, which advised Donald Trump to save himself by adopting Ronald Reagan's Iran-Contra posture — on the principle that it is never the crime that brings a president down but the cover-up, a principle Kiriakou illustrated with the conviction of Scooter Libby.

the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.title: Domingo's television
the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.summary: John Kiriakou has used the television rooms at FCI Loretto as his sharpest illustration of prison segregation: sets owned by racial blocs since a riot in the 1990s, a seat in front of one costing fourteen dollars, and one set left tuned to Law & Order every morning because a man named Domingo had paid four hundred dollars for it and had been gone for years.

the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.title: Mental health as a disciplinary problem
the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.summary: John Kiriakou has said that before his own prosecution he never gave five seconds of thought to the American prison system, and that living inside it showed him a broken one — in particular a system in which mental health is treated as a disciplinary problem rather than a medical one.

the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.title: The 2017 European tour
the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.summary: In May 2017 John Kiriakou spent a week speaking about national security whistleblowing in Iceland, Germany, Luxembourg, Belgium and Ireland, addressing the German Parliament and sharing panels with serving European ministers — an audience he contrasted sharply with his reception in the United States, and one he found newly willing to break with Washington because it was, in his word, panic-stricken about Donald Trump.

the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.title: The Ai Weiwei encounter in Berlin
the-attribution-problem-in-the-dnc-hack.summary: John Kiriakou met the artist Ai Weiwei by pure chance on a Berlin street while dragging a suitcase to the airport after a board meeting — an encounter that led to a tour of Ai Weiwei's studio and a signed iPhone case bearing the Lego portrait the artist had made of him for an exhibition at Alcatraz.

the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.title: Olof Palme assassination
the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.summary: The 1986 street murder of the Swedish prime minister, which John Kiriakou revisited step by step in Stockholm with researchers who had spent years on it. His conclusion — drawn from dozens of witness reports of two-man cars with walkie-talkies, some identified as police vehicles — is that much of the surveillance that night was carried out by people who believed they were running a practice exercise, until someone walked up and shot Palme dead.

the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.title: A spy's guide to a city
the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.summary: The premise of the third season of John Kiriakou''s Dead Drop podcast: that a CIA officer reads a city in a wholly different way from a tourist. The tourist looks for the Parthenon or the Eiffel Tower; the officer is thinking about surveillance, counter-surveillance and surveillance detection, and about not being shot from behind a building.

the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.title: CIA sexpionage
the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the CIA''s use of sex in espionage — routine from its founding through the early 1980s, including MK-Ultra and honey-pot operations — and why the agency largely abandoned it: coercion cannot build the trust a long-term source requires. Other services never stopped.

the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.title: Islam in America
the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.summary: John Kiriakou's response to a widely circulated clip of thousands of American Muslims at prayer, captioned as evidence that Islam is the fastest-growing religion in the United States. He notes that nothing in the clip establishes where or what the event was, and that most new American Muslims are African Americans converting — often, in his experience, in the prison system.

the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.title: Jihad means to struggle
the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.summary: John Kiriakou's insistence, as a graduate in Islamic theology and an Arabic speaker, that jihad does not mean and has never meant holy war. He traces the American usage to media coverage of the 1979 Iranian revolution and the embassy hostage crisis, and points out that one can declare a jihad against poverty or in favour of education.

the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.title: Ro Khanna
the-au-pair-who-became-a-stockholm-polic.summary: Democratic congressman from California, whom John Kiriakou describes as one of the very few selfless people in Congress and grades highly in his case-officer rankings.

the-australian-pilot.title: Area 58
the-australian-pilot.summary: The claim John Kiriakou says was put to him by a man who presents as entirely serious and is writing a book about it: that beyond Area 51 there is an Area 58 — seven more, and that much more secret — containing an underground bunker where alien craft land, known to those involved as the embassy because it is where the United States liaises with the aliens.

the-australian-pilot.title: Luis Elizondo
the-australian-pilot.summary: Why John Kiriakou never booked the best-known public advocate for unidentified aerial phenomena on his RT programme: viewers kept insisting Elizondo was an expert, so Kiriakou researched him and found chiefly Elizondo saying he was an expert. He says he does not know what the man is an expert on, and that it was not a fit for the show.

the-australian-pilot.title: Kiriakou's UFO sighting
the-australian-pilot.summary: The object John Kiriakou and his father watched from the side of Route 60 in Amish country, western Pennsylvania, on a Friday night in 1981 — three flashes of white light, then a silent orange trapezoid hanging a couple of thousand feet up, which left at a speed he had never seen before or since.

the-australian-pilot.title: Leaks come from the Pentagon
the-australian-pilot.summary: John Kiriakou''s rule of attribution for national security leaks, drawn from his own CIA experience: ninety-nine times out of a hundred the leak came from the Pentagon — which he says leaks constantly, is so gigantic that the source cannot be traced, and does not polygraph anybody. He adds the motive: somebody who opposed the operation and was overruled.

the-australian-pilot.title: The alternative obituaries
the-australian-pilot.summary: The obituaries John Kiriakou writes for CovertAction Magazine whenever someone associated with the CIA's torture program dies — deliberately mean-spirited pieces arguing the world is better off without them — and the phone call he took from one subject's daughter, who called him a monster, and what he said back to her.

the-australian-pilot.title: The 9/11 truth honorarium
the-australian-pilot.summary: How John Kiriakou came to headline a 9/11 truth event he had not realised was one: a $500 speaking fee from a PR man he had known through better days, a poster that revealed the sponsor, a sister telling him to withdraw, and his decision to honour the commitment anyway — while telling the audience to their faces that he would never believe Building 7 was a controlled demolition or that explosive thermite paint exists.

the-autographed-basketball.title: College tuition as an inducement
the-autographed-basketball.summary: The recruitment inducement John Kiriakou describes as among the CIA's most effective — enrolling a source's child at any American university and paying for it — and the arrangements with universities and corporations he says make it possible.

the-autographed-basketball.title: "You were the first person that ever asked me about my children"
the-autographed-basketball.summary: The answer John Kiriakou says he received when he asked a mid-level al-Qaeda member he had recruited in Pakistan why he had allowed the recruitment to happen: that in five years of detention Kiriakou had been the first person to ask about his children.

the-autographed-basketball.title: Arabic and Greek
the-autographed-basketball.summary: The qualification John Kiriakou says opened the door to his transfer from CIA analysis to operations: a post in Athens wanted Greek or Arabic, and he had both — by most of his tellings the only officer in the agency who did. The chief who hired him gave the reason in one sentence: it is easier and cheaper to take a linguist and teach him operations than the other way round. The pairing also became a detection tool, since the language nobody speaks in Pakistan is Arabic.

the-autographed-basketball.title: The Indonesian recruitment question
the-autographed-basketball.summary: A hypothetical put to John Kiriakou and other CIA applicants during the interview process — what to do when a foreign official you have cultivated for a year turns out not to be recruitable — and the answer that Kiriakou later understood had been the point of the exercise: break into the embassy and steal the information.

the-autographed-basketball.title: Bankruptcy and the dropped charges
the-autographed-basketball.summary: The sequence John Kiriakou places at the centre of his case: that the espionage counts against him were dropped only after his legal fees had bankrupted him, which he presents as evidence that the government''s aim was attrition rather than conviction.

the-autographed-basketball.title: Curtailment cables
the-autographed-basketball.summary: The career-ending requests John Kiriakou says he read coming back from the CIA's black sites — officers, doctors, psychologists and nurses asking to end their tours early rather than continue to take part in the interrogation programme — and his conclusion that if that many people were objecting in classified channels, someone would surely go public.

the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.title: Nine recruitments in twenty-five years
the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.summary: The conversation in which John Kiriakou''s Athens station chief, a twenty-five-year operations officer who had reached senior intelligence service level four with nine recruitments to his name, pointed out that Kiriakou had recruited five in two years — and Kiriakou''s explanation of the knack: that he could hide his disdain for a man completely while talking about whatever interested him.

the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.title: How the CIA kills
the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.summary: John Kiriakou''s description of the methods used when the CIA is ordered to kill someone outside a war zone: a team parachuting in miles away, stealing a car, a locks-and-picks specialist opening the door and suppressed weapons inside; a snatch into a van bound for an airport or a boat; or a brush past in a market with something poisoned — a technique he says the Russians used often and taught the Bulgarians into the early 1980s.

the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.title: SEALs on loan to the CIA
the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to why the CIA did not use its own paramilitary team against Osama bin Laden: it did. The raid was a CIA operation directed by the Counterterrorism Center, and every Navy SEAL involved was temporarily a CIA contractor, on loan to the agency for the duration.

the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.title: Mark Polymeropoulos
the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.summary: The CIA officer John Kiriakou describes as a friend who was in his first tour when Aldrich Ames blew his identity, was brought in from the cold, and later became station chief in Moscow — an appointment Kiriakou characterises as a deliberate thumb in the Russians'' eye: the officer their spy had burned, put in charge of operations against them.

the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.title: Suing the CIA
the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to whether anyone has ever successfully sued the CIA in civil court: not that he knows of. He allows only what he calls small, picky victories — chiefly suing for the right to sue — and applies the same pessimism to the burned officer whose case prompted the question.

the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.title: The Armitage leak
the-ayatollah-and-the-photographs.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of who actually disclosed Valerie Plame''s identity: Richard Armitage — whom Kiriakou identifies as deputy secretary of defense — who everybody assumed would be charged under the Intelligence Identities Protection Act and who was never charged with any crime at all. Scooter Libby, he stresses, never leaked the name and was never accused of doing so; Libby fell on a perjury count.

the-backstory.title: Caleb Maupin
the-backstory.summary: American journalist and Marxist commentator, a recurring guest on John Kiriakou's radio programme The Backstory, whom Kiriakou introduces as one of the best-informed people out there. Kiriakou endorses his analysis of automation and capitalism while noting he does not agree with all of it, and proposed putting him on air opposite a libertarian economist.

the-backstory.title: Arabic and Greek
the-backstory.summary: The qualification John Kiriakou says opened the door to his transfer from CIA analysis to operations: a post in Athens wanted Greek or Arabic, and he had both — by most of his tellings the only officer in the agency who did. The chief who hired him gave the reason in one sentence: it is easier and cheaper to take a linguist and teach him operations than the other way round. The pairing also became a detection tool, since the language nobody speaks in Pakistan is Arabic.

the-backstory.title: Haiti
the-backstory.summary: A country John Kiriakou studied for the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, where he found that the seven largest merchant families — the families that run the entire Haitian economy — are white. He treats Haiti's poverty as manufactured rather than accidental, and its unrest as a story the American press declines to cover.

the-backstory.title: Abolish the CIA
the-backstory.summary: John Kiriakou's position that the CIA should be abolished because its functions are already duplicated by the other 17 U.S. intelligence agencies — analysis by the State Department, human spying by the Pentagon, technology by DARPA, NSA and the private sector.

the-backstory.title: "Admit nothing, deny everything, make counter-accusations"
the-backstory.summary: One of the twenty life lessons John Kiriakou says the CIA taught him in training, and a slogan sold on coffee mugs and t-shirts in the headquarters gift shop — by far the most popular mug in the building. It was treated at Langley as a joke that was not quite a joke; in federal prison Kiriakou used it as an operating rule, and credits it with getting him out of an investigation into a prison-yard fight with nothing given up.

the-backstory.title: Advanced Counterterrorism Operations
the-backstory.summary: The six-week specialist course John Kiriakou flew back from Athens to attend roughly eighteen months before 9/11 as one of fourteen officers selected worldwide — high-threat operations, technical collection, and a driving syllabus built around crashing through roadblocks that left the class with whiplash. By accident of timing it meant a trained cadre was ready to deploy the moment the attacks came.

the-bahraini-fire-brigade.title: A dangerous neighborhood
the-bahraini-fire-brigade.summary: The contrast John Kiriakou drew between his Gulf contacts on the second day of the 2026 Iran war — friends in Dubai who were panicked as drones struck the city's landmark towers, and the son of a senior Qatari official who simply chuckled and said 'this is life in the Middle East. We live in a dangerous neighborhood.'

the-bahraini-fire-brigade.title: Bahrain's force majeure
the-bahraini-fire-brigade.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of Bahrain declaring force majeure on its energy commitments during the 2026 Iran war — why it is catastrophic for Bahrain and irrelevant to the global oil market, since the kingdom produces and consumes about a hundred thousand barrels a day and sells only the output of a small offshore field gifted to it by Saudi Arabia.

the-bahraini-fire-brigade.title: Bahrain's naturalisation policy
the-bahraini-fire-brigade.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how the Bahraini royal family changed the sectarian arithmetic of the country over thirty years — importing Syrians and naturalising Indian and Pakistani Sunni Muslims until a population that had been two-thirds to three-quarters Shia was closer to half and half.

the-bahraini-fire-brigade.title: 2026 Iran war
the-bahraini-fire-brigade.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-bahraini-fire-brigade.title: Bahrain Posting (1994–1996)
the-bahraini-fire-brigade.summary: John Kiriakou's 1994–1996 assignment to Bahrain under U.S. State Department cover as second secretary for economic affairs — arriving with his wife Joanne and infant son Chris on August 1, 1994, into a tiny Gulf monarchy whose sectarian tensions erupted, two months later, into the first Intifada.

the-balloon-test.title: The Iowa Republican exchange
the-balloon-test.summary: The argument John Kiriakou says he had at a conservative event with the head of the Iowa Republican Party — an abortion absolutist who answered Kiriakou's challenge on Gaza by calling him pro-Hamas — and how Kiriakou ended it.

the-balloon-test.title: The Piers Morgan panel
the-balloon-test.summary: The televised debate John Kiriakou returns to most often — two against two, with Scott Horton and himself on one side and Alan Dershowitz and a senior former Israeli official on the other. Kiriakou set out his position on Hamas, October 7th and Gaza, and Piers Morgan told him at the end that he had come around and agreed. On a second appearance from the same panel he argued that Jeffrey Epstein was an Israeli access agent, provoked Dershowitz — Epstein's own attorney — into an interruption Kiriakou considers self-defeating, and got an unbothered "who knows?" from the Israeli.

the-balloon-test.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
the-balloon-test.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

the-balloon-test.title: Cleaning up after Tora Bora
the-balloon-test.summary: John Kiriakou was not at Tora Bora. He arrived in Pakistan in January 2002, two months after the bombing, and says he went specifically to clean up what the battle had left behind — scavenging material, detaining the fighters too slow to get away, and mapping the smugglers'' valleys the survivors had used to cross. In his account the clean-up was necessary because the encirclement failed: bin Laden, warned by an al-Qaeda operative working as translator to the commander of Central Command, left in the dark dressed as a woman in the back of a pickup truck, and at dawn there was nobody in Tora Bora to surrender.

the-balloon-test.title: Famine in Gaza
the-balloon-test.summary: The starvation of the civilian population of the Gaza Strip, which John Kiriakou describes as a United Nations-declared famine caused not by an absence of food but by an Israeli refusal to let food reach the people who need it; Kiriakou characterises it as a war crime, a crime against humanity and a form of genocide, attributing that characterisation to the United Nations and the International Court of Justice rather than to himself.

the-balloon-test.title: Hayden at the National Press Club
the-balloon-test.summary: John Kiriakou's account of seeing Michael Hayden, after a series of strokes, at a National Press Club event sponsored by the intelligence centre that bears his name — and the two reactions it produced in him, neither of them satisfaction alone.

the-baltimore-plot.title: The catering truck transfer
the-baltimore-plot.summary: The covert removal of Donald Trump from Air Force One at the end of a NATO summit in Turkey — boarded in front of the television cameras, driven across the tarmac inside an airport catering truck, and flown on to Britain aboard a smaller jet while the White House press corps travelled on the aircraft everyone believed he was on.

the-baltimore-plot.title: The Clinton Pakistan plane switch
the-baltimore-plot.summary: Bill Clinton''s secret transfer to an unmarked aircraft for the 2000 flight into Pakistan — the closest precedent John Kiriakou finds for the catering truck transfer, and the one that differs in the detail he thinks matters: the White House told the reporters while it was happening.

the-baltimore-plot.title: Fidel Castro
the-baltimore-plot.summary: The Cuban leader John Kiriakou uses as his standing example of a relationship the United States could have had and chose not to — a rebel who liked America and had pitched in its minor leagues, written off because Washington had already committed itself to Batista. Castro also recurs across Kiriakou's account of the CIA as the agency's most-attempted assassination target, as the man who never cashed the rent cheques for Guantánamo, and as the figure American policy is still fighting years after his death.

the-baltimore-plot.title: The Air Force One bomb threat
the-baltimore-plot.summary: The bomb threat telephoned to the classified telephone aboard Air Force One as Bill Clinton's aircraft lifted out of Athens in November 1999, disclosed by the ambassador at the embassy's after-action review — a detail John Kiriakou withheld from years of tellings of that visit until 2026.

the-baltimore-plot.title: The Qatari 747
the-baltimore-plot.summary: The Boeing 747 given to the United States by the government of Qatar to serve as Air Force One. John Kiriakou reported in July 2026 that it had been delivered to the president while he was overseas and that he declined to fly home in it, because it had not been fitted with the protective equipment — countermeasures, radar jamming — that the role requires.

the-baltimore-plot.title: Bill Clinton
the-baltimore-plot.summary: 42nd U.S. president whom John Kiriakou describes as wholly disinterested in intelligence — briefed by the CIA only twice in eight years, with Vice President Al Gore taking the daily briefing instead and relaying anything important.

the-baltimore-tunnel.title: The Taiwan blank check
the-baltimore-tunnel.summary: John Kiriakou''s reading of the Republican revolt against funding Ukraine: that most of the members refusing to write another blank check for Kyiv wanted to write it for Taipei instead, and would rather have a direct confrontation with China than a decade bogged down in Eastern Europe.

the-baltimore-tunnel.title: Elliott Abrams
the-baltimore-tunnel.summary: The Reagan-era assistant secretary of state whose 2023 appointment to a Biden administration advisory board John Kiriakou treated as proof that neoliberal and neoconservative foreign policy are the same policy with interchangeable players — a man who pleaded guilty over Iran-Contra, was pardoned, helped sell the Iraqi weapons of mass destruction case, and then served Donald Trump on Iran and Venezuela.

the-baltimore-tunnel.title: Frances Haugen
the-baltimore-tunnel.summary: The Facebook employee John Kiriakou refuses to call a whistleblower — arguing that against the legal definition, bringing to light waste, fraud, abuse, illegality or threats to public health or safety, she qualifies as a corporate spokesperson whose motive was to improve the company's bottom line, not to expose wrongdoing.

the-baltimore-tunnel.title: Gavin Newsom
