the-c-130-resettlements.summary: The CIA-trained Afghan paramilitary units whose surviving members were resettled in the United States, and John Kiriakou''s account of why so many of them have broken down: recruited without training or therapy, taken out at night to kill their own tribesmen and extended family, promised the land of milk and honey, and then met on arrival with no work permit, no treatment and no help at all.

the-c-130-resettlements.title: Savas Kalenderidis
the-c-130-resettlements.summary: Greek intelligence officer, national hero and personal friend of John Kiriakou''s, who was involved in the operation to protect the PKK founder Abdullah Öcalan at the Greek embassy in Nairobi in 1999 — an operation that ended when Turkish and Kenyan intelligence diverted part of Öcalan''s motorcade and seized him. Kiriakou flatly denies the claim that the CIA and Turkish intelligence tried to kill Kalenderidis there.

the-c-130-resettlements.title: Lindsey Graham
the-c-130-resettlements.summary: Republican senator from South Carolina who died in July 2026, and John Kiriakou's standing shorthand for the permanent war caucus — a "show horse" rather than a workhorse, a "chameleon" who "never saw a war that he didn't want to jump into with both feet," and, on posthumously released documentary footage, a man offering the US Air Force to bomb a country America was not at war with.

the-c-130-resettlements.title: Mexico City as an espionage hub
the-c-130-resettlements.summary: John Kiriakou''s assessment of Mexico City as one of the world''s principal centres of international espionage, alongside Vienna, London, Paris and Washington — driven by a gargantuan American embassy that Russian services target from next door — and his reading of why Mexico simply ignored a dossier of suspected Russian officers handed over by the Biden administration.

the-c-130-resettlements.title: Pakistani prisons
the-c-130-resettlements.summary: John Kiriakou''s flat refusal, in a discussion of Imran Khan''s detention, of the idea that a Pakistani prison offers VIP treatment to a former prime minister — grounded in his having visited many of them himself during the period when the CIA was locking people up there.

the-c-130-resettlements.title: The embassy local hire
the-c-130-resettlements.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of how a foreign service recruits inside an American embassy without ever approaching an American: by paying long-serving local staff a supplement they cannot refuse, and letting them assemble the identity of the station from fragments — most conclusively the office a new arrival names when he answers his telephone.

the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.title: The Palestinian middle class in the Gulf
the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.summary: John Kiriakou's stated puzzlement, after a career spent on and in the Middle East, at what he calls a region-wide dislike of Palestinians among Arab governments — given that Palestinians constitute the entire professional middle class of the Gulf states, and are themselves Arabs and mostly Muslims.

the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.title: Medea Benjamin's broken arm
the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Egyptian authorities breaking the arm of the CODEPINK co-founder Medea Benjamin while arresting her, as she attempted to reach the Rafah crossing to escort a food shipment into Gaza — an incident he offers as a measure of what Egyptian policing of the border looks like in practice.

the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.title: Expulsion of Palestinians from the Gulf
the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.summary: The mass expulsion of the Palestinian professional class from the Gulf Arab states in the aftermath of Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, which John Kiriakou witnessed from the region and identifies as the reason Gulf governments are willing to normalise relations with Israel. He dates the Kuwaiti decision to a wedding he attended weeks after the liberation, says Western and Egyptian pressure stopped it being total, and has repeatedly said he has never understood the grudge himself.

the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.title: The synagogue in Damascus
the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.summary: John Kiriakou's account of visiting an operating, practising Jewish synagogue in Damascus, and the forecast he attaches to it — that he would not bet money on the safety of Christians, Jews, Alawites or any other religious minority in Syria under the present government or any other, whatever else is said of Bashar al-Assad.

the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.title: The 1991 Saudi plan for Gaza
the-call-about-rebuilding-gaza.summary: A proposal John Kiriakou says he watched Ambassador Chas Freeman float to the Saudis during his first overseas tour in 1991 — that Saudi Arabia fund a port, an airport, a desalination plant and an electrical grid in Gaza. The Saudis agreed; Israel refused outright. Kiriakou raises it because the identical arrangement resurfaced in the Israeli press more than three decades later.

the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.title: Turkey and a safe zone in Iran
the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.summary: John Kiriakou''s response to the Turkish president''s suggestion that, in the event of an attack on Iran, the Turkish army would establish a safe zone inside Iranian territory — that Ankara would love nothing more, having previously taken Iraqi, Cypriot and Syrian territory, and that pan-Turkism is a subject most people are unaware of.

the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.title: Barrett Brown
the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.summary: American journalist and former Anonymous associate whom John Kiriakou describes as one of the most intelligent writers and analysts he has ever encountered, with long-standing mental health problems and a two-decade heroin addiction he has now been clear of for at least a year, expelled from the United Kingdom and relocated to Mexico.

the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.title: Censorship on the left
the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.summary: John Kiriakou''s observation that he was censored far less by Forbes and Fortune than by The Nation and Mother Jones, which he offers as an instance of a general rule that a writer''s own side censors them hardest — the counterpart to Ted Rall''s account of being made to fit a particular kind of leftism rather than any kind.

the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.title: Dr Oz and the Armenian hospices
the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.summary: John Kiriakou''s reaction to a television segment by Mehmet Oz alleging fraud by Armenian-run hospices in Los Angeles — that a man he identifies as a veteran of the Turkish special forces zeroing in on Armenians in California is not a coincidence, and that each of the administration''s appointees appears to arrive with a racial scandal of their own.

the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.title: The Iron Dome
the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.summary: Israel's air-defence system as John Kiriakou reads it — impressive against a wave of slow Iranian drones, but shown by the handful that got through, and later by Iranian ballistic missiles, to be not all it is cracked up to be; each exchange, in his account, buying Iran intelligence about the gaps.

the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.title: James Morris
the-calls-not-to-attack-iran.summary: A close friend of John Kiriakou''s who served seventeen years of a twenty-year sentence for a crime committed at sixteen, found on release that a violent felony conviction closed off employment, made his own way to Turkey and across the border into Syria, spent two years fighting alongside the Kurds against ISIS, and later took his own life.

the-can-of-ravioli.title: The colour-coded badges
the-can-of-ravioli.summary: The CIA's badge system as John Kiriakou describes it — blue for the top secret compartments everyone in the building holds, green for contractors, yellow for the language instructors cleared only to secret, red for the man in the cafeteria doughnut shop and the woman who vacuums at night — and the lettered suffixes that were dropped once the letters themselves gave the game away.

the-can-of-ravioli.title: Craig Murray
the-can-of-ravioli.summary: Former British Ambassador to Uzbekistan whom John Kiriakou cites as a whistleblower of extreme torture: during a meeting at the Uzbek intelligence service, Murray heard screaming, walked in, and saw a man being boiled in oil — reporting it cost him his career.

the-can-of-ravioli.title: Dumping cash in a Moscow bathroom
the-can-of-ravioli.summary: John Kiriakou's examples of what covert action has actually meant in practice — American commandos blowing up the Trans-Siberian oil pipeline, Afghan guerrillas hired to cross the Amu Darya and attack a refinery inside the southern USSR, and cash dumped in a Moscow bathroom to undermine the rouble.

the-can-of-ravioli.title: How Chinese intelligence recruits
the-can-of-ravioli.summary: John Kiriakou''s assessment of the Ministry of State Security''s tradecraft: very effective with anyone who simply wants money, because the money is limitless, and very bad at cultivating a source who does not yet know who is cultivating him — with the target usually being access to sophisticated technology.

the-can-of-ravioli.title: MK-ULTRA in Canada
the-can-of-ravioli.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that many MK-ULTRA experiments took place on Canadian soil, and his explanation of why: the CIA asked the Canadian intelligence service for help with its anti-Soviet, anti-Chinese remote-viewing and LSD work, and the Canadians gladly gave it.

the-can-of-ravioli.title: Pakistani corruption and democracy
the-can-of-ravioli.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment that corruption in Pakistan is so deep and so broad that a genuinely functioning democracy is almost impossible there — set against a long history of military coups, a habit of imprisoning former prime ministers, and his insistence that Imran Khan should not be in a cell.

the-capitol-hill-cocaine-ring.title: The cocaine in the West Wing
the-capitol-hill-cocaine-ring.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of how a bag of cocaine came to be found in a White House cubby in July 2023 — the phone cubbies outside every vaulted area, the fingerprints that every cleared visitor has already surrendered, and his prediction that despite an investigation requiring only a couple of hours of work, the public would never be told whose it was.

the-capitol-hill-cocaine-ring.title: Elliott Abrams
the-capitol-hill-cocaine-ring.summary: The Reagan-era assistant secretary of state whose 2023 appointment to a Biden administration advisory board John Kiriakou treated as proof that neoliberal and neoconservative foreign policy are the same policy with interchangeable players — a man who pleaded guilty over Iran-Contra, was pardoned, helped sell the Iraqi weapons of mass destruction case, and then served Donald Trump on Iran and Venezuela.

the-capitol-hill-cocaine-ring.title: Frances Haugen
the-capitol-hill-cocaine-ring.summary: The Facebook employee John Kiriakou refuses to call a whistleblower — arguing that against the legal definition, bringing to light waste, fraud, abuse, illegality or threats to public health or safety, she qualifies as a corporate spokesperson whose motive was to improve the company's bottom line, not to expose wrongdoing.

the-capitol-hill-cocaine-ring.title: Gavin Newsom
the-capitol-hill-cocaine-ring.summary: The California governor John Kiriakou described in 2023 as the consummate Democratic Party insider waiting his turn — a Pelosi relative who married into the Brown family, doing everything the Biden operation asked of him, including a pointless surrogate trip to Idaho, on the calculation that Joe Biden would not reach the nominating convention.

the-capitol-hill-cocaine-ring.title: Netanyahu and the Tel Aviv police chief
the-capitol-hill-cocaine-ring.summary: The July 2023 dismissal of Tel Aviv's police chief, which John Kiriakou identified as the moment Benjamin Netanyahu may have overstepped — arguing that the real threat to the Israeli prime minister came not from the Palestinians but from his own attempt to take over the court system, and from the strikes and demonstrations that had not subsided.

the-capitol-switchboard.title: John Kerry
the-capitol-switchboard.summary: U.S. Senator from Massachusetts; chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee during John Kiriakou's 2009 service as the committee's senior investigator; subsequently U.S. Secretary of State; characterized by Kiriakou as a coward who buckled under CIA pressure on the Dasht-i-Leili reopening and as personally fixated on his perceived theft of the Secretary of State position by Hillary Clinton; the famously thrown medals were duplicates purchased at the post exchange.

the-capitol-switchboard.title: Senate Foreign Relations Committee
the-capitol-switchboard.summary: Kiriakou was senior investigator under John Kerry — and still held the post when his own federal prosecution came to a head in January 2012.

the-capitol-switchboard.title: Congressional intelligence oversight
the-capitol-switchboard.summary: John Kiriakou''s standing criticism of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Permanent Select Committee — that unlike the armed services and foreign relations committees, they do not perform oversight at all: "They''re just cheerleaders." His illustration is a sitting committee chairman who summoned him privately, then asked whether Kiriakou would write the criticism publicly on his behalf.

the-capitol-switchboard.title: Lobbyists writing legislation
the-capitol-switchboard.summary: John Kiriakou''s first-hand account from the Senate Foreign Relations Committee: told that the committee would take part in the carbon offsets debate and protesting that he knew nothing about carbon offsets, he was told not to worry — and the next day strangers came into the office, took over most of the desks, logged on and began writing the bill.

the-capitol-switchboard.title: Whipping votes
the-capitol-switchboard.summary: John Kiriakou''s explanation of what a party whip does and why Chuck Schumer''s failure to do it mattered: a leader who tells his caucus to vote their conscience has not whipped the vote at all. Kiriakou traces the office to a figurative whip used in the 1700s and 1800s, and calls the concession very dangerous — an admission that you have lost.

the-capitol-switchboard.title: Afghan heroin policy
the-capitol-switchboard.summary: The post-2001 U.S. policy in Afghanistan of protecting, and per John Kiriakou actively encouraging, the cultivation of heroin poppy. Under the Taliban in 2000 Afghanistan produced 0% of the world's heroin; by 2009 under American occupation it produced 93%. Per a DEA officer Kiriakou consulted with on the policy paper he was preparing for Senator Kerry, the strategic rationale was that nearly all of the heroin flowed to Iran and Russia, addiction in those countries was considered desirable as a long-run societal weakener, and the same logic now operates in reverse with Chinese fentanyl flowing into the United States.

the-car-pickup-meeting.title: CIA liaison relationships
the-car-pickup-meeting.summary: John Kiriakou's critique of CIA intelligence-liaison relationships with foreign governments — sharply expanded after 9/11 — arguing that officers do not consider the long-term risk that disclosing sensitive operations to foreign services hands those governments leverage, including potential blackmail material, over the United States, and that no one left in Congress has the will to provide real oversight of the practice.

the-car-pickup-meeting.title: Romania and US military positioning
the-car-pickup-meeting.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment that Romania has become the United States' next staging option toward the Middle East, because Greece is full and Turkey is pursuing its own course.

the-car-pickup-meeting.title: Cancelling the 2026 midterms
the-car-pickup-meeting.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that the 2026 war cannot win the midterm elections for the Republicans, and his flagged-as-paranoid worry that it may instead furnish the pretext for a national emergency and a cancelled election.

the-car-pickup-meeting.title: Civilian ships and piracy
the-car-pickup-meeting.summary: Why merchant crews cannot defend themselves: by international treaty no civilian ship may carry a weapon. John Kiriakou handled international piracy as a Senate Foreign Relations Committee staffer and brought Captain Richard Phillips to testify.

the-car-pickup-meeting.title: Counterterrorism Center
the-car-pickup-meeting.summary: The CIA's Counterterrorism Center (CTC) — the unit where John Kiriakou spent the defining years of his operational career. He joined in the late 1990s as the only officer in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic, served as chief of counterintelligence in the bin Laden unit, watched the Center swell from a few hundred employees to nearly 2,000 by September 12, 2001, and it was to CTC that he walked back down in May 2002 to refuse the torture program — the moment, he says, the CIA began to turn on him.

the-car-pickup-meeting.title: David Ransom
the-car-pickup-meeting.summary: U.S. Ambassador to Bahrain during the period of John Kiriakou's posting there; characterized by Kiriakou as one of the finest people he worked for in his CIA career

the-caracas-checklist.title: Fentanyl as a weapon of mass destruction
the-caracas-checklist.summary: John Kiriakou's objection to the designation of fentanyl as a weapon of mass destruction — that a WMD is by definition a single weapon that kills large numbers at once, that no drug can be that, and that stretching the term cheapens and disables it. He notes in passing that Venezuela does not make fentanyl and that what it does ship goes to Western Europe.

the-caracas-checklist.title: The Stratfor cables on Venezuela
the-caracas-checklist.summary: Material John Kiriakou says WikiLeaks exposed on American operations against Venezuela — the training of opposition figures including Juan Guaidó and Leopoldo López, and plotting to sabotage dams inside the country to help bring down Hugo Chávez. He offers it as an example of detail so obscure that few journalists know it, and as the real reason for the pursuit of Julian Assange.

the-caracas-checklist.title: Elliott Abrams
the-caracas-checklist.summary: The Reagan-era assistant secretary of state whose 2023 appointment to a Biden administration advisory board John Kiriakou treated as proof that neoliberal and neoconservative foreign policy are the same policy with interchangeable players — a man who pleaded guilty over Iran-Contra, was pardoned, helped sell the Iraqi weapons of mass destruction case, and then served Donald Trump on Iran and Venezuela.

the-caracas-checklist.title: Maduro Capture
the-caracas-checklist.summary: CIA-driven nighttime operation in which a team of Delta Force commandos entered Venezuela and removed Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife from their beds. Per John Kiriakou, the key enabling intelligence — per a New York Times account he cited — came from a CIA asset inside Maduro''s presidential palace who called when Maduro went to sleep: ''He''s sound asleep. If you''re going to do it, do it now.'' At least eighty people were killed in the operation, including approximately thirty-five Cubans. Kiriakou compares it to the 1989 capture of Manuel Noriega, in which US forces blasted death metal at the Vatican Embassy until Noriega was asked to leave.

the-caracas-checklist.title: Russia is not the gravest threat
the-caracas-checklist.summary: John Kiriakou's rejection of the first policy speech by MI6's first woman chief, Blaise Metreweli, which named Russia and the Russo-Ukrainian war as the greatest danger to Britain and Europe. His counter-case is demographic and fiscal — Russia is practically bankrupt with a birth rate that would empty it in a century — and his own candidate for the real threat is not a state at all.

the-caracas-checklist.title: The Greenland prediction he got wrong
the-caracas-checklist.summary: John Kiriakou's account of dismissing the idea that the United States would seize Greenland on a podcast one afternoon, and hearing Stephen Miller say the opposite on CNN an hour later — after which he treated the threat to a NATO member as a legitimate problem, and looked to Emmanuel Macron rather than Keir Starmer to stop it.

the-case-against-work-camps.title: Mental health as a disciplinary problem
the-case-against-work-camps.summary: John Kiriakou has said that before his own prosecution he never gave five seconds of thought to the American prison system, and that living inside it showed him a broken one — in particular a system in which mental health is treated as a disciplinary problem rather than a medical one.

the-case-against-work-camps.title: Three square meals and a warm bed
the-case-against-work-camps.summary: John Kiriakou has said he will never forget a remark he overheard from three men playing cards in an empty television room at FCI Loretto, who counted up the meals, the bed, the clothes, the television and the medical care they were given and concluded that the place was very nearly paradise.

the-case-against-work-camps.title: The CO who wanted the CIA
the-case-against-work-camps.summary: A young correctional officer at FCI Loretto once pulled John Kiriakou aside and asked in a whisper how to get into the CIA; when Kiriakou told him he was bright and did not belong there, the man explained that both his parents and his grandfather had been correctional officers and that his wife would never leave Loretto, a town of twelve hundred people.

the-case-against-work-camps.title: Domingo's television
the-case-against-work-camps.summary: John Kiriakou has used the television rooms at FCI Loretto as his sharpest illustration of prison segregation: sets owned by racial blocs since a riot in the 1990s, a seat in front of one costing fourteen dollars, and one set left tuned to Law & Order every morning because a man named Domingo had paid four hundred dollars for it and had been gone for years.

the-case-against-work-camps.title: The chapel rule
the-case-against-work-camps.summary: The chapel and the library at FCI Loretto were the two places child molesters could be certain of safety, because a correctional officer was always present; John Kiriakou, who worked in the chapel, has described the house rule against discussing your case there and the indignation with which it was met.

the-case-against-work-camps.title: The persona in the first week
the-case-against-work-camps.summary: Five days into a sentence he had expected to serve at a minimum-security camp, John Kiriakou decided to fall back on his CIA training and adopt a deliberately aggressive exterior — reasoning that in a prison where the weak end up checking themselves into solitary for protection, he would rather be the man other people needed protection from.

the-caspian-drone-strike.title: 2026 Iran war
the-caspian-drone-strike.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-caspian-drone-strike.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
the-caspian-drone-strike.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

the-caspian-drone-strike.title: Volodymyr Zelensky
the-caspian-drone-strike.summary: Kiriakou says he was told not to discuss Zelensky's corruption publicly, and calls the Oval Office dressing-down of him set up in advance.

the-caspian-drone-strike.title: Lindsey Graham
the-caspian-drone-strike.summary: Republican senator from South Carolina who died in July 2026, and John Kiriakou's standing shorthand for the permanent war caucus — a "show horse" rather than a workhorse, a "chameleon" who "never saw a war that he didn't want to jump into with both feet," and, on posthumously released documentary footage, a man offering the US Air Force to bomb a country America was not at war with.

the-caspian-drone-strike.title: Major non-NATO ally status for Ukraine
the-caspian-drone-strike.summary: John Kiriakou''s forecast of how the Russian demand that Ukraine never join NATO can be met without leaving Ukraine unprotected: the designation of major non-NATO ally, already held by Australia, Japan, South Korea, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, which he says confers essentially the same rights without the membership.

the-caspian-drone-strike.title: Nord Stream pipeline sabotage
the-caspian-drone-strike.summary: The 2022 destruction of the Nord Stream gas pipelines, whose responsibility John Kiriakou treats as genuinely unresolved — citing Seymour Hersh's reporting that the CIA did it, a later Ukrainian special-forces claim of a sailboat-based operation carried out without Zelensky's knowledge, and a retired CIA colleague's private theory that Putin blew up his own pipeline to blame the Americans.

the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.title: Kiriakou's morning reading list
the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.summary: The specific news diet John Kiriakou reads before he opens his mouth to speak, an ideologically deliberate spread across American mainstream, American right, British mainstream, Israeli press, Arab press, and independent alt-media, framed by him as the analyst's guard against believing the outlets you agree with.

the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.title: Doing Time Like a Spy
the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.summary: Prison memoir by John Kiriakou, full title Doing Time Like a Spy: How the CIA Taught Me to Survive and Thrive in Prison; winner of two literary awards and reissued in a second edition by Simon and Schuster.

the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.title: FCI Loretto
the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.title: The Club Fed myth
the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.summary: John Kiriakou''s standing objection to the phrase ''Club Fed'' and the idea that federal prison is a soft landing for white-collar convicts: there is no such thing, he says, no golf and no gardening, only an institution designed to humiliate and emasculate and to make a man count the days.

the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.title: Communications management unit
the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.summary: The two restricted-contact units inside the American federal prison system, at Terre Haute and Marion; built for "the worst of the worst" but, in John Kiriakou's account, used to silence prisoners whose messages are inconvenient — and a practice he groups with solitary confinement as torture. He served part of his own sentence in a modified one.

the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.title: Critical Analytic Thinking
the-cat-in-the-hat-and-truck.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the foundational discipline of CIA analyst training and the most practically valuable skill he carried into civilian life: questioning all incoming information — including, especially, sources whose ideological positions align with one''s own — and arriving at conclusions from evidence rather than prior belief. Kiriakou cites his own COVID lab-leak conclusion, reached against his initial instinct, as an example of the method in practice.

the-catering-truck-transfer.title: The Clinton Pakistan plane switch
the-catering-truck-transfer.summary: Bill Clinton''s secret transfer to an unmarked aircraft for the 2000 flight into Pakistan — the closest precedent John Kiriakou finds for the catering truck transfer, and the one that differs in the detail he thinks matters: the White House told the reporters while it was happening.

the-catering-truck-transfer.title: The Baltimore plot
the-catering-truck-transfer.summary: The 1861 conspiracy to assassinate president-elect Abraham Lincoln as his train passed through Baltimore, uncovered by Pinkerton detectives — and the overnight passage in a soft felt hat and shawl that got him to his inauguration and made the press call him a coward.

the-catering-truck-transfer.title: Fidel Castro
the-catering-truck-transfer.summary: The Cuban leader John Kiriakou uses as his standing example of a relationship the United States could have had and chose not to — a rebel who liked America and had pitched in its minor leagues, written off because Washington had already committed itself to Batista. Castro also recurs across Kiriakou's account of the CIA as the agency's most-attempted assassination target, as the man who never cashed the rent cheques for Guantánamo, and as the figure American policy is still fighting years after his death.

the-catering-truck-transfer.title: The Qatari 747
the-catering-truck-transfer.summary: The Boeing 747 given to the United States by the government of Qatar to serve as Air Force One. John Kiriakou reported in July 2026 that it had been delivered to the president while he was overseas and that he declined to fly home in it, because it had not been fitted with the protective equipment — countermeasures, radar jamming — that the role requires.

the-catering-truck-transfer.title: The Air Force One bomb threat
the-catering-truck-transfer.summary: The bomb threat telephoned to the classified telephone aboard Air Force One as Bill Clinton's aircraft lifted out of Athens in November 1999, disclosed by the ambassador at the embassy's after-action review — a detail John Kiriakou withheld from years of tellings of that visit until 2026.

the-catering-truck-transfer.title: Bill Clinton
the-catering-truck-transfer.summary: 42nd U.S. president whom John Kiriakou describes as wholly disinterested in intelligence — briefed by the CIA only twice in eight years, with Vice President Al Gore taking the daily briefing instead and relaying anything important.

the-cats-of-athens.title: The Parthenon-view condo
the-cats-of-athens.summary: The eighth-floor Athens apartment John Kiriakou has been watching on the Greek property app Spitogatos, whose price fell from €600,000 to €250,000 after the city banned new Airbnb conversions — and the golden-visa buying that had emptied the residential market in the first place.

the-cats-of-athens.title: Washington, rat central
the-cats-of-athens.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the rat population of Washington, D.C. — one he saw the size of a small dog, and the night he drove to Southeast Washington at quarter to two in the morning to collect two eighteen-year-olds whose van had been stolen, and found them panicking not about the theft but about the rats eating a sleeping homeless man's toes.

the-cats-of-athens.title: The Greek brain drain
the-cats-of-athens.summary: The editorial John Kiriakou read in a Greek newspaper tracking where educated Greeks emigrate — the United States, Britain, Germany, Australia — and the line he took from it: that when fifteen hundred Greeks with master''s degrees, law degrees, MDs and PhDs move to Turkey for better opportunity, you know you are finished.

the-cats-of-athens.title: Astrology at the CIA
the-cats-of-athens.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that astrology played a role in CIA work in the 1950s and early 1960s as part of MK-ULTRA, alongside time travel and teleportation — and his explanation for why: officials with unlimited budgets and no obligation to report to the public reasoned that there was probably nothing to it, but that if there were, it would make them a star.

the-cats-of-athens.title: Carrying passports in Washington
the-cats-of-athens.summary: John Kiriakou's report in September 2025 that people in Washington had begun carrying their passports for fear of being scooped up by immigration enforcement — alongside the case of an American symphony violinist held for three weeks, and his own belief that ethnic profiling violates the Fourth Amendment.

the-cats-of-athens.title: "Christians are suckers"
the-cats-of-athens.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for how a president who does not go to church, has no spiritual adviser and could not name a line of scripture can push school prayer without cost — that he thinks most Christians are suckers, an assessment Kiriakou says he hates to make and believes anyway.

the-cave-myth.title: Bin Laden health rumors
the-cave-myth.summary: John Kiriakou's dismissal of the claim that Osama bin Laden died years before the 2011 raid. He says the CIA received a steady stream of medical rumours about him — kidney failure, dialysis in a cave, a spinal disorder — none of which turned out to be true, and that bin Laden was in fine health apart from arthritis and a hip problem until the day he died.

the-cave-myth.title: The ISI as two organizations
the-cave-myth.summary: John Kiriakou''s working model of Pakistan''s Inter-Services Intelligence during his time as CIA chief of counterterrorism operations there: one half made up of British-trained officers he calls great counterterrorism partners, and another half that created, trained, financed and armed the Taliban — a split that left him deciding case by case whom he could trust.

the-cave-myth.title: SEAL Team Six attrition
the-cave-myth.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to the claim that the Navy SEALs who killed Osama bin Laden have since been killed off: the dead came from the broader unit rather than the raid party, SEAL Team Six numbers several hundred men rather than the dozen or so people imagine, and losing a high number of them to accidents and combat is, in his phrase, very sadly common.

the-cave-myth.title: The Taliban lobbyist in Washington
the-cave-myth.summary: A story put to John Kiriakou about a Taliban delegation''s American press conference and the Washington lobbyist who represented them. Kiriakou remembered the episode and the lobbyist''s New Jersey base but not the claim about her parentage, and explained why it caused so little controversy at the time: the United States had no historical quarrel with the Taliban, and had armed and fêted some of its future members during the war against the Soviets.

the-cave-myth.title: The torture memo signature
the-cave-myth.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of how the CIA''s torture programme was authorised: a list of about ten techniques sent from headquarters through the Justice Department, the National Security Council lawyers and Condoleezza Rice to the president — who, to the surprise of the agency''s own leadership, signed it. Kiriakou recalls the deputy director saying three times in one meeting that he could not believe the president had signed the memo.

the-cave-myth.title: Abu Zubaydah
the-cave-myth.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

the-chain-of-command-argument.title: Edward Snowden
the-chain-of-command-argument.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

the-chain-of-command-argument.title: Whistleblower psychology
the-chain-of-command-argument.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of what distinguishes people who come forward: psychological studies showing whistleblowers hold a much more sharply defined sense of right and wrong than the general population, weighed against his own claim that there is no whistleblower who has not contemplated suicide in the period after going public.

the-chain-of-command-argument.title: Espionage Act
the-chain-of-command-argument.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

the-chain-of-command-argument.title: Seventy-two denied motions
the-chain-of-command-argument.summary: The count John Kiriakou gives of the pretrial motions filed in his case and denied by Judge Leonie Brinkema — seventy-two denied and none granted — which he offers as the mechanism by which a national security defendant in the Eastern District of Virginia is prevented from mounting a defence at all.

the-chain-of-command-argument.title: Julian Assange
the-chain-of-command-argument.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

the-chain-of-command-argument.title: The Guardian smear series
the-chain-of-command-argument.summary: The run of articles about Julian Assange that John Kiriakou characterised in 2018 as a pile-on based on anonymous sources leaking intelligence-agency material, and which he read as a formal psychological operation intended to weaken Assange rather than as journalism.

the-chapel-rule.title: The psychology chairman's letter
the-chapel-rule.summary: Unsure how to deal with the child molesters who made up a large share of the population at FCI Loretto, John Kiriakou wrote to a professor friend for advice; the reply, from the chairman of a university psychology department, told him that pedophiles cannot be cured and that they talk about their crimes constantly because reliving them is itself gratifying.

the-chapel-rule.title: The professor in the visiting room
the-chapel-rule.summary: John Kiriakou has credited the idea for his prison memoir to a university professor who visited him at FCI Loretto, listened to him tell stories across a visiting-room table, and told him that although the whole thing was by its nature depressing, the stories were good and there were lessons in them, and that he should write a book.

the-chapel-rule.title: Chomo
the-chapel-rule.summary: The prison term for a child molester, which John Kiriakou first heard on his first day at FCI Loretto when two skinheads at the Aryan table put it to him as the last of three vetting questions before deciding whether he could eat with them.

the-chapel-rule.title: Domingo's television
the-chapel-rule.summary: John Kiriakou has used the television rooms at FCI Loretto as his sharpest illustration of prison segregation: sets owned by racial blocs since a riot in the 1990s, a seat in front of one costing fourteen dollars, and one set left tuned to Law & Order every morning because a man named Domingo had paid four hundred dollars for it and had been gone for years.

the-chapel-rule.title: Mental health as a disciplinary problem
the-chapel-rule.summary: John Kiriakou has said that before his own prosecution he never gave five seconds of thought to the American prison system, and that living inside it showed him a broken one — in particular a system in which mental health is treated as a disciplinary problem rather than a medical one.

the-chapel-rule.title: The case against work camps
the-chapel-rule.summary: John Kiriakou, who asked to serve his own sentence at a minimum-security work camp and was sent to the prison across the street instead, came out of prison arguing that the camps should not exist at all — and, in the same breath, that some prisoners are dangerous enough that prisons certainly should.

the-chilean-newspaper-prediction.title: One hundred and twenty-three investigations
the-chilean-newspaper-prediction.summary: The figure John Kiriakou attributes to Attorney General Jeff Sessions and what he calls his big mouth: 123 active national security leak investigations under way, which Kiriakou uses to argue the Trump administration was worse for whistleblowers than Obama''s.

the-chilean-newspaper-prediction.title: Hillary in a Kamala suit
the-chilean-newspaper-prediction.summary: John Kiriakou''s assessment of the incoming Biden administration three weeks after the 2020 election: Biden as Obama 2.0, Kamala Harris as "Hillary in a Kamala suit", and a career prosecutor whose drug sentencings he says ruined thousands of lives.

the-chilean-newspaper-prediction.title: Donald Trump
the-chilean-newspaper-prediction.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

the-chilean-newspaper-prediction.title: Edward Snowden
the-chilean-newspaper-prediction.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

the-chilean-newspaper-prediction.title: Thomas Drake
the-chilean-newspaper-prediction.summary: NSA whistleblower; per John Kiriakou, the source for the statement that on the morning of September 11, 2001, NSA Director Mike Hayden told agency personnel NSA had been 'waiting for a 9/11' to implement the mass-electronic-surveillance program that NSA's founding charter forbids.

the-chinese-embassy-in-london.title: Russia is not the gravest threat
the-chinese-embassy-in-london.summary: John Kiriakou's rejection of the first policy speech by MI6's first woman chief, Blaise Metreweli, which named Russia and the Russo-Ukrainian war as the greatest danger to Britain and Europe. His counter-case is demographic and fiscal — Russia is practically bankrupt with a birth rate that would empty it in a century — and his own candidate for the real threat is not a state at all.

the-chinese-embassy-in-london.title: China as economic threat
the-chinese-embassy-in-london.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

the-chinese-embassy-in-london.title: Denied areas
the-chinese-embassy-in-london.summary: The CIA term for countries so hostile and so heavily surveilled that ordinary operational movement is impossible — the Soviet Union, Cuba, Syria, and later Russia, China, North Korea and Iran — and the reason, in John Kiriakou's account, that officers heading to one get specialist briefings, eight-hour surveillance detection routes, and that the Agency has to fall back on liaison services instead of its own sources.

the-chinese-embassy-in-london.title: MI6
the-chinese-embassy-in-london.summary: The United Kingdom''s Secret Intelligence Service, the foreign-intelligence service of the British government and the closest CIA liaison partner under the Five Eyes framework. Per John Kiriakou, MI6 was the parent organization that asked Truman after WWII to set up a ''central intelligence agency'' on the model of its own service — making the CIA in effect MI6''s little brother. Kiriakou''s stated view of the historical relationship: MI6 saw the CIA as its little brother, then after the empire fell apart as its big brother, and then after 9/11 as ''strangers'' because U.S. policy became ''simply to kill everybody.''

the-chinese-embassy-in-london.title: Nigel Farage
the-chinese-embassy-in-london.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment that Nigel Farage was a fringe joke five years ago and is no less fascistic now, only accepted — and his prediction that if Farage becomes leader of the Conservative Party it will be the end of that party as a viable political force.

the-chinese-embassy-in-london.title: Chinese overseas police stations
the-chinese-embassy-in-london.summary: John Kiriakou's account of a New York Times revelation about Chinese nationals with apparent ties to the Chinese police operating out of storefronts around Manhattan and travelling around the United States to threaten Chinese people with reprisals against relatives in Beijing — and his puzzlement that the FBI missed it.

the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.title: How Chinese intelligence recruits
the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.summary: John Kiriakou''s assessment of the Ministry of State Security''s tradecraft: very effective with anyone who simply wants money, because the money is limitless, and very bad at cultivating a source who does not yet know who is cultivating him — with the target usually being access to sophisticated technology.

the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.title: The Solomon Islands trip
the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.summary: The reporting trip John Kiriakou announced for July 2026 — ten days on Guadalcanal with Jeremy Kuzmarov of CovertAction Magazine, travelling via Fiji, to cover the dispute between the United States and China over access to Japan's Second World War military bases.

the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.title: Craig Murray
the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.summary: Former British Ambassador to Uzbekistan whom John Kiriakou cites as a whistleblower of extreme torture: during a meeting at the Uzbek intelligence service, Murray heard screaming, walked in, and saw a man being boiled in oil — reporting it cost him his career.

the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.title: Dumping cash in a Moscow bathroom
the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.summary: John Kiriakou's examples of what covert action has actually meant in practice — American commandos blowing up the Trans-Siberian oil pipeline, Afghan guerrillas hired to cross the Amu Darya and attack a refinery inside the southern USSR, and cash dumped in a Moscow bathroom to undermine the rouble.

the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.title: MK-ULTRA in Canada
the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that many MK-ULTRA experiments took place on Canadian soil, and his explanation of why: the CIA asked the Canadian intelligence service for help with its anti-Soviet, anti-Chinese remote-viewing and LSD work, and the Canadians gladly gave it.

the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.title: Pakistani corruption and democracy
the-chinese-professor-on-linkedin.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment that corruption in Pakistan is so deep and so broad that a genuinely functioning democracy is almost impossible there — set against a long history of military coups, a habit of imprisoning former prime ministers, and his insistence that Imran Khan should not be in a cell.

the-cia-and-honey-trapping.title: CIA sexpionage
the-cia-and-honey-trapping.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the CIA''s use of sex in espionage — routine from its founding through the early 1980s, including MK-Ultra and honey-pot operations — and why the agency largely abandoned it: coercion cannot build the trust a long-term source requires. Other services never stopped.

the-cia-and-honey-trapping.title: Islam in America
the-cia-and-honey-trapping.summary: John Kiriakou's response to a widely circulated clip of thousands of American Muslims at prayer, captioned as evidence that Islam is the fastest-growing religion in the United States. He notes that nothing in the clip establishes where or what the event was, and that most new American Muslims are African Americans converting — often, in his experience, in the prison system.

the-cia-and-honey-trapping.title: Jihad means to struggle
the-cia-and-honey-trapping.summary: John Kiriakou's insistence, as a graduate in Islamic theology and an Arabic speaker, that jihad does not mean and has never meant holy war. He traces the American usage to media coverage of the 1979 Iranian revolution and the embassy hostage crisis, and points out that one can declare a jihad against poverty or in favour of education.

the-cia-and-honey-trapping.title: Olof Palme assassination
the-cia-and-honey-trapping.summary: The 1986 street murder of the Swedish prime minister, which John Kiriakou revisited step by step in Stockholm with researchers who had spent years on it. His conclusion — drawn from dozens of witness reports of two-man cars with walkie-talkies, some identified as police vehicles — is that much of the surveillance that night was carried out by people who believed they were running a practice exercise, until someone walked up and shot Palme dead.

the-cia-and-honey-trapping.title: Ro Khanna
the-cia-and-honey-trapping.summary: Democratic congressman from California, whom John Kiriakou describes as one of the very few selfless people in Congress and grades highly in his case-officer rankings.

the-cia-and-honey-trapping.title: The CIA close-and-continuing-contact rule
the-cia-and-honey-trapping.summary: The CIA policy John Kiriakou has described as *"written in stone"*, every officer must report to headquarters any close and continuing contact with a foreign national, defined explicitly to include sexual relationships, so that a name trace can identify hostile intelligence approaches. Kiriakou frames the rule as the operational counter to honey-trap recruitment, and offers the case of the woman officer who slept with her own recruited source, was demoted to analyst rather than fired, and finally lost her job for hiding under her desk on 9/11.

the-cia-and-iridium.title: Phil Donahue
the-cia-and-iridium.summary: American talk-show host who, John Kiriakou discovered seven years after the fact, had been secretly paying his weekly newspaper column fee — $400 a week for nine years, routed through Reader Supported News — because Donahue had learned that Kiriakou came out of prison broke and did not want him sleeping in his car.

the-cia-and-iridium.title: Soviet Union
the-cia-and-iridium.summary: The superpower whose collapse framed the start of John Kiriakou's CIA career — it was "literally in the process of collapsing" when he joined in January 1990, ushering in a brief "peace dividend" era when the agency's new threats were environmental degradation and AIDS. Kiriakou cites Brzezinski's "Afghan trap" that lured the Soviets into Afghanistan, argues the U.S. abandoned the radicalized mujahideen the moment the Soviets were beaten, notes America then took "a vacation from history," and recalls that Jonathan Pollard's stolen documents were traded by Israel to the Soviets in exchange for Russian Jews.

the-cia-and-iridium.title: The Alaska glacier
the-cia-and-iridium.summary: The visitor centre John Kiriakou saw on a 2016 trip to Alaska with Gary Johnson, built at the foot of a glacier close enough to touch from the observation deck and by then a quarter of a mile away from it — an image he uses as the plainest available demonstration of climate change, and one he refuses to let pass as a joke.

the-cia-and-iridium.title: The armour at Union Station
the-cia-and-iridium.summary: John Kiriakou''s eyewitness account of stepping off an Amtrak train at Washington''s Union Station in August 2025 to find two armoured personnel carriers and a .50 calibre machine gun trained on the entrance — and of tourists posing for photographs with the National Guardsmen deployed in the parts of the city where, he says, there is no crime.

the-cia-and-iridium.title: The diplomatic stool collection
the-cia-and-iridium.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that visiting heads of state routinely carry their own faeces home rather than leave them in an American hotel — because, in his account, entities within the United States government will gladly collect the material for its DNA and health information, and the hotel employee who retrieves it is a CIA officer under cover.

the-cia-and-iridium.title: The Hall of States
the-cia-and-iridium.summary: The Washington office building at 444 North Capitol Street where, in John Kiriakou''s floor-by-floor description, most of the capital''s television news operations share an address — NBC and MSNBC on the ground floor, Fox on the fifth, PBS and Democracy Now on the sixth, and Newsmax in the basement in a single room.

the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.title: The Gang of Four and Gang of Eight
the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.summary: John Kiriakou''s description of how the CIA restricts notification of its most sensitive covert operations to four or eight congressional leaders, and his verdict on the practice: because a member of an intelligence committee can be an overseer without being cleared for what is being overseen, the arrangement is not oversight but, in his word, gangsterism.

the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.title: The ask-forgiveness maxim
the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.summary: The rule of thumb John Kiriakou says he was taught early in his CIA career — that it is always better to ask forgiveness than to ask permission — and which he offers as the explanation for how the agency runs legally doubtful programmes: it does what it wants, apologises if caught, and that is the end of it.

the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.title: CIA attention to West Africa
the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer on whether the CIA is likely to be operating in Burkina Faso: for all the years he was at the agency it cared very little about Africa and especially West Africa, but the presence of al-Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates plus the drug trade makes CIA and special forces involvement probable — and, he adds, the American public will not hear about it.

the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.title: CIA–FBI incompatible computer systems
the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.summary: John Kiriakou's claim that from the CIA's founding in 1947 until 2009 the computer systems of the CIA and the FBI were not compatible with one another — no message could be sent from one to the other and no intelligence shared — which he offers both as the material substrate of the interagency hatred that helped make September 11 possible, and as the gap through which James Mitchell and Bruce Jessen were able to pass Ali Soufan's FBI debriefings of Abu Zubaydah off as the fruits of torture.

the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.title: Fake CIA résumés
the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of being used as a human authenticator in the private sector: at the consulting firm he joined after leaving the CIA, every job applicant claiming agency service was sent to dinner with him, and by his count fully half of them had never set foot inside the CIA.

the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.title: Forcing Iran toward a bomb
the-cia-as-a-paramilitary-organization.summary: John Kiriakou''s argument that Western pressure risks producing the very outcome it claims to prevent: repeated Israeli assassinations of Iranian scientists and generals and strikes on Iranian sites may eventually leave Ayatollah Khamenei with no choice but to permit a defensive weapon — despite the religious prohibition Kiriakou credits him with maintaining, and despite successive American estimates that Iran is not seeking one.

the-cia-backdoor-banking.title: Astrology at the CIA
the-cia-backdoor-banking.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that astrology played a role in CIA work in the 1950s and early 1960s as part of MK-ULTRA, alongside time travel and teleportation — and his explanation for why: officials with unlimited budgets and no obligation to report to the public reasoned that there was probably nothing to it, but that if there were, it would make them a star.

the-cia-backdoor-banking.title: Carrying passports in Washington
the-cia-backdoor-banking.summary: John Kiriakou's report in September 2025 that people in Washington had begun carrying their passports for fear of being scooped up by immigration enforcement — alongside the case of an American symphony violinist held for three weeks, and his own belief that ethnic profiling violates the Fourth Amendment.

the-cia-backdoor-banking.title: "Christians are suckers"
the-cia-backdoor-banking.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for how a president who does not go to church, has no spiritual adviser and could not name a line of scripture can push school prayer without cost — that he thinks most Christians are suckers, an assessment Kiriakou says he hates to make and believes anyway.

the-cia-backdoor-banking.title: E. Jean Carroll
the-cia-backdoor-banking.summary: The plaintiff whose persistence John Kiriakou singled out for deep respect — she kept suing after the political tide turned against her, and won an award he put at eighty-three or eighty-five million dollars on a day when Donald Trump won almost everything else in the federal courts.

the-cia-backdoor-banking.title: Find a Grave
the-cia-backdoor-banking.summary: The cemetery database John Kiriakou calls literally his favourite website on the internet, which he opens during the ten-minute countdown before broadcasts and uses to decide who goes into his cemetery books — and which supplied him the story of Greta Zimmer Friedman.

the-cia-backdoor-banking.title: Greta Zimmer Friedman
the-cia-backdoor-banking.summary: The Austrian-born dental assistant John Kiriakou found listed on Find a Grave as a "pop culture icon" — the woman a sailor grabbed and kissed in Times Square on V-J Day 1945, misidentified for years as a nurse, buried at Arlington, and whose story Kiriakou tells as the reason he writes cemetery books.

the-cia-barber-shop.title: The CIA's internal social culture
the-cia-barber-shop.summary: John Kiriakou's one-word characterisation of the agency's internal culture — "incestuous" — describing a club for every conceivable interest, actively encouraged officer-to-officer romances, and a design intent that officers should have no need of friends or activities outside the building.

the-cia-barber-shop.title: Fridays at the agency
the-cia-barber-shop.summary: John Kiriakou's observation that Fridays were always very slow at the CIA, because the Middle East weekend falls on Thursday-Friday or Friday-Saturday depending on the country and the quiet propagates back to Washington — a rhythm he says bled into the United States generally.

the-cia-barber-shop.title: Abraham Accords
the-cia-barber-shop.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

the-cia-barber-shop.title: Death threats against Kiriakou
the-cia-barber-shop.summary: The threats John Kiriakou has received across two decades — first after going public about the CIA torture program, when FBI advice that at least two were credible sent his family out of the country, and later in waves tied to his opposition to Gina Haspel, his remarks about Pakistan, and his advocacy on Palestine and the Epstein case.

the-cia-barber-shop.title: Hamid Karzai
the-cia-barber-shop.summary: The president installed in Afghanistan after the American invasion, whom John Kiriakou uses as the standing illustration of what occupation actually buys: after twenty years and more than a trillion dollars, Karzai was ''little more than the mayor of Kabul'' — and did not control all of Kabul either. The line began as a joke among Senate Foreign Relations Committee staff, and Kiriakou used it to Senator John Kerry''s face ten years into the war.

the-cia-barber-shop.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle in Athens
the-cia-barber-shop.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of Kimberly Guilfoyle's appointment as American ambassador to Greece — that she got it because Donald Trump Jr. wanted her out of the way, a manoeuvre he compares to Saddam Hussein's habit of exiling successful generals as ambassadors — and his reluctant conclusion that Greece could have done worse.

the-cia-buyout-offer.title: Israel and the fear of being held back
the-cia-buyout-offer.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of why an ally that receives almost everything it asks for still spies on the United States — that the Israelis are always afraid something is being withheld, and, having nowhere to be pushed except the Mediterranean, will do anything to be certain about their own security.

the-cia-buyout-offer.title: Snowden did not defect
the-cia-buyout-offer.summary: John Kiriakou's two corrections to the treatment of Edward Snowden at Tulsi Gabbard's 2025 confirmation hearing — that "traitor" has a constitutional definition Snowden does not meet, there having been no declaration of war since December 1941, and that Snowden did not defect to Russia but was stranded in a Moscow transit lounge en route to Ecuador when John Kerry revoked his passport.

the-cia-buyout-offer.title: CIA Drug Facilitation
the-cia-buyout-offer.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the CIA''s reported involvement in facilitating the arrival of cocaine into the United States during the era that became the crack epidemic, and his own firsthand discovery — as a Senate Foreign Relations Committee investigator — that under American military control Afghanistan produced 93% of the world''s heroin. A DEA contact told him the report would never be published because ''we want Iran and Russia to be addicted to heroin. It weakens their societies.'' Kiriakou draws a direct parallel to the current fentanyl crisis: China is doing to the US what the US did to Iran and Russia.

the-cia-buyout-offer.title: Congressional intelligence oversight
the-cia-buyout-offer.summary: John Kiriakou''s standing criticism of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Permanent Select Committee — that unlike the armed services and foreign relations committees, they do not perform oversight at all: "They''re just cheerleaders." His illustration is a sitting committee chairman who summoned him privately, then asked whether Kiriakou would write the criticism publicly on his behalf.

the-cia-buyout-offer.title: Guantánamo Bay detention camp
the-cia-buyout-offer.summary: Per John Kiriakou — as chief of counterterrorism operations in Pakistan after September 11, 2001 — the Guantanamo detention facility began as a temporary holding measure intended to last two to three weeks while the CIA and Justice Department determined which federal district court should try each prisoner, not as a long-term detention infrastructure. The Rawalpindi jail had reached capacity, Pakistani intelligence demanded the prisoners be removed, and CIA headquarters directed Kiriakou to load them onto a C-12 cargo plane and fly them to Cuba.

the-cia-buyout-offer.title: Extraordinary Rendition
the-cia-buyout-offer.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the CIA practice of seizing terrorism suspects in one country and transporting them to a third country — often a country with no due-process protections — to be held, interrogated, or tortured outside U.S. legal jurisdiction. The program operated alongside the enhanced-interrogation program and was the operational mechanism by which prisoners reached secret CIA facilities and allied torture sites in countries like Bahrain. Kiriakou himself was not in the rendition line of work but became a federal felon under the Intelligence Identities Protection Act for a single confirmation of a colleague's surname to a journalist who claimed to be writing a book on the Abu Omar rendition from Milan.

the-cia-close-and-continuing-rule.title: The CIA and honey-trapping
the-cia-close-and-continuing-rule.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of why the CIA, unlike the Russians, Chinese, Israelis and French, does not run honey-trap recruitment operations. He credits an instructor's story about a 1970s attempt against an Iranian mulla, who reacted to the incriminating photographs by asking for 8×10s and wallets, as the moment the agency concluded coercion produces resentment rather than sources.

the-cia-defense.title: Rick Praau
the-cia-defense.summary: Career CIA officer, chief of operations at the Counterterrorism Center and previously of the Special Activities Division, whose retirement memoir John Kiriakou reviewed critically in Covert Action Magazine. Kiriakou's objection is not to what the book contains but to what it omits — published reports that before joining the agency its author was investigated by Miami-Dade police over seven contract killings for the Medellín cartel. The surname is given here as the source transcript's auto-captions render it and may be mis-transcribed.

the-cia-defense.title: Bureau of Prisons
the-cia-defense.summary: The federal agency that ran John Kiriakou's incarceration — and one of his most persistent post-prison targets. The BOP overrode his judge's camp recommendation by deeming him "a threat to the public safety," threatened him with "diesel therapy" until 1,600 logged phone calls and letters from a dozen House members and two senators backed it off, and, per Kiriakou, functions as "an employment agency for unemployable semi-literate rural white men" and "a dumping ground for failed medical professionals" — an agency for which a prisoner's death is cheaper than his treatment.

the-cia-defense.title: The child-trafficking misquotation
the-cia-defense.summary: A widely circulated claim that John Kiriakou said the CIA is involved in the sex trafficking of children. Kiriakou denies it flatly and traces it to a distorted account of a teaching hypothetical he uses in university lectures on ethics — a speech cleared by the CIA's Publications Review Board, whose video was attached to the original article by a writer who evidently had not watched it.

the-cia-defense.title: Giuliani Pardon Solicitation
the-cia-defense.summary: Per John Kiriakou, a meeting at the Trump International Hotel in Washington in which Rudy Giuliani's associate solicited $2 million in exchange for a presidential pardon — a story that subsequently appeared as a front-page New York Times article. Giuliani publicly denied ever meeting Kiriakou; Kiriakou sent the Times the photograph taken at the meeting that morning, and the paper published the story with the note that it had seen documentary proof.

the-cia-defense.title: The 2022 deplatforming
the-cia-defense.summary: The removal of John Kiriakou's radio programme from every major podcast platform after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, on the basis of his work for Sputnik News — preceded, he says, by a Washington Post article and a CSIS paper arguing that his weekly segment on American prison conditions was Russian propaganda weakening American democracy.

the-cia-defense.title: The German POW chess analogy
the-cia-defense.summary: The reasoning John Kiriakou gave ABC News in December 2007 for why he had believed at the time that waterboarding was necessary: he had heard of Second World War German prisoners who, over months of playing chess with their interrogators, built enough rapport to talk, and he judged that al-Qaeda prisoners were a different order of adversary who would never be seduced into cooperating.

the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.title: The CIA Insider's Guide to Surveillance and Surveillance Detection
the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.summary: Book by John Kiriakou drawing on his experience as a surveillance detection instructor at the CIA and as a private surveillance training consultant. The book covers the techniques used by intelligence professionals to identify whether they are being followed — including the four-phase surveillance detection route, concealment device placement and retrieval, and counter-surveillance strategy — adapted for use by corporate executives, journalists, and others who want to confirm whether they are being followed.

the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.title: Remains of the Day (book)
the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.summary: John Kiriakou's book, announced for publication by Simon and Schuster in March 2026, billed as a definitive guide to the historic cemeteries of Washington DC and the first in a planned series; the second installment will cover the Mafia graves of New York City.

the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.title: "The Spy Who Talked Too Much"
the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.summary: Steve Coll's New Yorker profile of John Kiriakou, written after Coll had been welcomed into his home, and which Kiriakou telephoned him from prison to complain about. Coll's defence was that authors do not write their own headlines — a defence Kiriakou concedes, while still rating Coll among the country's great investigative journalists.

the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.title: 2026 Iran war economic shock
the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.summary: John Kiriakou''s running assessment of the economic damage from the 2026 Iran war — an oil shock he says already exceeds both 1970s shocks combined, a natural-gas shock worse than the Nord Stream destruction, and a chokepoint problem that runs through fertilizer as much as fuel, since 65% of the world''s supply must transit the Strait of Hormuz. His summary: "This is an economic slowdown of choice."

the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.title: Advice to an aspiring intelligence analyst
the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to a 21-year-old student asking what to study and what to read: pick a geographic area, become the go-to person on it, and consume everything published in the field — including the journals written by people who have never made policy.

the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.title: Air wars are overrated
the-cia-insiders-guide-omnibus.summary: John Kiriakou''s summary judgement on the 2026 Iran and Lebanon campaigns, delivered as the meta-headline of the whole war: air power flattened Gaza without destroying Hamas, is bogging down against Hezbollah, and cannot produce the outcome the war requires.

the-cia-one-year-leave.title: Ray McGovern
the-cia-one-year-leave.summary: Former senior CIA analyst turned antiwar dissident, and one of John Kiriakou's closest friends — "like a brother to me." Kiriakou began working at the CIA on the Monday after the Friday McGovern retired in January 1990, so the two never overlapped inside; they became comrades in the whistleblower world instead. McGovern coined the "MICIMATT" framing Kiriakou often borrows, went into Putin's office with Oliver Stone for a 40-minute meeting, and — per Kiriakou — believes 9/11 was a conspiracy, a view Kiriakou affectionately notes is far from his own.

the-cia-one-year-leave.title: The Frank Kendall Air Force One case
the-cia-one-year-leave.summary: The 2026 Espionage Act investigation of former Secretary of the Air Force Frank Kendall, an acknowledged MAGA Republican expert whom John Kiriakou describes as having publicly warned that the Boeing 747 the government of Qatar gifted the United States for use as Air Force One was not up to the security standards a presidential aircraft requires. Kiriakou reads the resulting grand-jury proceeding as embarrassment prosecution, and expects Kendall not to be indicted, but the case illustrates the reach of Espionage Act charges Kiriakou himself faced.

the-cia-one-year-leave.title: Edward Snowden
the-cia-one-year-leave.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

the-cia-one-year-leave.title: John Kiriakou
the-cia-one-year-leave.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

the-cia-one-year-leave.title: Sam Adams Award
the-cia-one-year-leave.summary: The integrity-in-intelligence award John Kiriakou received in 2016 at American University, joining a laureate list that includes Edward Snowden, Julian Assange, and Sy Hersh. Named not for the founding father but for the CIA analyst who insisted the true enemy strength in Vietnam was double what General Westmoreland allowed to be reported, it is given by Veteran Intelligence Professionals for Sanity — a community Kiriakou describes as doubling as a support group for whistleblowers.

the-cia-one-year-leave.title: Angela Merkel
the-cia-one-year-leave.summary: German chancellor whose mobile phone the NSA was intercepting, in what John Kiriakou treats as the cleanest illustration of the two-tier American attitude to surveillance: the interception of one of Washington''s closest allies was big news, Hillary Clinton flew to Germany to apologise, and — per Kiriakou — the United States then did it again. Asked about it in Berlin, his answer was that intercepting her phone is exactly what he wants the CIA to be doing.

the-cia-performance-metric.title: Recruiting from the bottom
the-cia-performance-metric.summary: The targeting method John Kiriakou believes produced the killings of Iran''s leadership: not agents at the top of the state but destitute refugees at street level, paid a hundred dollars a month to write down when a general leaves his building and by which route. He contrasts it with the CIA''s own record in Iran, where it spent his career trying and failing to recruit inside the Ayatollah''s office, the foreign ministry and the IRGC.

the-cia-performance-metric.title: Canada as a bargaining chip
the-cia-performance-metric.summary: John Kiriakou's reading of Mark Carney's Davos speech as the moment Canada stopped pretending the United States could be trusted as a long-term partner — and his account of what wore the relationship out, including Washington's insistence that Ottawa arrest Huawei's chief financial officer on a computer-hacking charge and hold her for three years to trade.

the-cia-performance-metric.title: China's generals without combat experience
the-cia-performance-metric.summary: Presented with the observation that China's purged and reshuffled top brass are now too young to have fought in any war, John Kiriakou agreed it mattered little in the near term and a great deal in the long term — because American military planning will have to account for an adversary whose senior commanders have never been in combat.

the-cia-performance-metric.title: Ilhan Omar
the-cia-performance-metric.summary: U.S. Representative whom John Kiriakou credits with sponsoring a rewrite of the Espionage Act in two consecutive Congresses — legislation he says is dead on arrival with a Republican House because of who she is. Kiriakou has also sat at her table — in January 2026 he was one of about twenty guests at a dinner where Omar described the federal operation in Minneapolis and the budget manoeuvre that funded every part of the government except Homeland Security.

the-cia-performance-metric.title: Macron and the airplane steps
the-cia-performance-metric.summary: Asked what he thought was behind the French president's bruised appearance at Davos, John Kiriakou gave the blunt answer — "honestly, I think she hits him" — and dated his own change of mind to the footage at the top of the airplane steps.

the-cia-performance-metric.title: The Abraham Lincoln off Oman
the-cia-performance-metric.summary: The carrier battle group John Kiriakou placed in the Arabian Sea off Oman in January 2026, and the reason he said he genuinely feared the coming weeks: a belief in Washington and Jerusalem that the Iranian government needed only a gentle shove to collapse, against 150,000 members of the Revolutionary Guard who would not oblige.

the-cia-recruiting-video.title: Sheldon Adelson
the-cia-recruiting-video.summary: American casino magnate and Republican megadonor. In John Kiriakou's account Adelson sent his private jet to fly Jonathan Pollard from prison to Israel, paid out of his own pocket to move the American embassy to Jerusalem, and functions as Kiriakou's standing unit of measurement for what political money can buy — including in the negative, as the patron the Libertarian Party never had.

the-cia-recruiting-video.title: Shin Bet
the-cia-recruiting-video.summary: Israel's internal security service; per John Kiriakou, one of the two declared Israeli intelligence officers at the Washington embassy, and the service whose officer, alongside a Mossad officer, he says tried to recruit him at his first CIA liaison briefing in the spring of 1990 — an approach his colleagues told him had been made to every one of them.

the-cia-recruiting-video.title: The Kuwaiti cargo in yuan
the-cia-recruiting-video.summary: The shipment of Kuwaiti oil that John Kiriakou says the Chinese paid for in yuan rather than dollars for the first time, which he treats as the first step toward the end of the American empire.

the-cia-recruiting-video.title: The Saudi question
