Kiriakou describes him as the most admired diplomat in the building — the most powerful, important and strategic ambassador there despite operating with far smaller resources than his American, British, French and Chinese counterparts, and better than most of the American diplomats Kiriakou worked for. When Lavrov was abruptly sidelined in late 2025, Kiriakou's reading was retirement rather than disgrace.

the-crenshaw-text-messages.title: "Stefanik will not be governor"
the-crenshaw-text-messages.summary: John Kiriakou's flat, on-the-record prediction about the New York governor's race, made against a friend he describes as irrationally conservative who insisted the contest would turn on a single issue — the right to carry a gun. Kiriakou called it the most ridiculous thing he had heard the man say, and argued that Elise Stefanik's political career is finished.

the-crete-blood-feud.title: Abigail Spanberger
the-crete-blood-feud.summary: Governor of Virginia from 2025 and, before Congress, a CIA officer alongside John Kiriakou in the Counterterrorism Center — whom he calls a perfectly nice person who would have been a middle-of-the-road Republican in the 1970s and 1980s, and whose victory speech, to his surprise, said all the right things.

the-crete-blood-feud.title: Jason Miyares
the-crete-blood-feud.summary: The Cuban-born Republican attorney general of Virginia whom John Kiriakou expected to be a right-wing disaster and found instead to be excellent — a judgement he says is hard for him to make about a conservative Republican, and which he repeated on the night Miyares was unceremoniously thrown out of office.

the-crete-blood-feud.title: Joe Rogan
the-crete-blood-feud.summary: The podcast host whose show John Kiriakou finally sat for in October 2025 — an experience that began with signing a non-disclosure agreement and ended with his verdict that Rogan is "a nice guy, very down to earth, very normal." The first thing Rogan asked, walking into the studio ten minutes late: "Hey, do you know my friend Mike Baker?" Kiriakou defends Rogan as unfairly characterized as a right-winger, and had long cited the show as the venue where Zuckerberg admitted Facebook suppressed the Hunter Biden laptop story at the FBI''s behest.

the-crete-blood-feud.title: The Arlington house
the-crete-blood-feud.summary: The 1,200-square-foot house John Kiriakou bought with his Pakistan overtime and danger pay for $347,000, sold two years later for $721,000, and now values at a million — the anchor of his repeated argument that his own children can never live in the Arlington, Virginia neighbourhood they grew up in.

the-crete-blood-feud.title: The Farragut West encounter
the-crete-blood-feud.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of walking up to two National Guardsmen in the Farragut West Metro station — the safest station on the network, in his estimate — telling himself the whole way not to say anything, and then saying one sentence: "You guys should be ashamed of yourselves."

the-crete-blood-feud.title: The George Mason confrontation
the-crete-blood-feud.summary: The videotaped encounter at George Mason University in which former CIA director John Brennan poked a questioner in the chest — an incident John Kiriakou says at least a dozen friends sent him, and which showed him, for the first time in thirty-five years of knowing the man, a frightened John Brennan.

the-culling-of-friendships.title: Brian Ross
the-culling-of-friendships.summary: American investigative journalist and seven-time Emmy Award winner who was a prominent reporter at ABC News when, in December 2007, he conducted the on-camera interview with John Kiriakou that produced the first public confirmation by a U.S. official that the CIA waterboarded prisoners. Per Kiriakou, Ross called him out of the blue with the assertion that a source said Kiriakou had personally tortured Abu Zubaydah; Kiriakou's decision to give the interview anyway — driven by the conclusion that 'Brian Ross's source is at the White House and they're going to pin this on me' — became the pivot point of his entire post-CIA life.

the-culling-of-friendships.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
the-culling-of-friendships.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

the-culling-of-friendships.title: The Club Fed myth
the-culling-of-friendships.summary: John Kiriakou''s standing objection to the phrase ''Club Fed'' and the idea that federal prison is a soft landing for white-collar convicts: there is no such thing, he says, no golf and no gardening, only an institution designed to humiliate and emasculate and to make a man count the days.

the-culling-of-friendships.title: Supervised release travel restrictions
the-culling-of-friendships.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the years of court supervision that followed his prison term, in which a judge refused him permission to travel abroad to give paid speeches while he was expected to earn a living, and in which he had to surrender his passport on returning from every trip he was allowed to take.

the-culling-of-friendships.title: The Oz analogy
the-culling-of-friendships.summary: John Kiriakou's habit of explaining federal prison social structure through the HBO drama Oz, in which rival gangs are forced to share a single unit — and his identification with the show's unaffiliated Irish character, who belonged to no faction and survived by playing them off one another.

the-culling-of-friendships.title: The Virginia pardon and voting rights
the-culling-of-friendships.summary: John Kiriakou's account of applying to have his voting rights restored in Virginia after leaving prison and receiving, unasked, a full state pardon delivered by courier from the office of Governor Terry McAuliffe — followed by a courthouse clerk and a state employee who between them got him registered in time to vote.

the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.title: Craig Murray
the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.summary: Former British Ambassador to Uzbekistan whom John Kiriakou cites as a whistleblower of extreme torture: during a meeting at the Uzbek intelligence service, Murray heard screaming, walked in, and saw a man being boiled in oil — reporting it cost him his career.

the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.title: Dumping cash in a Moscow bathroom
the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.summary: John Kiriakou's examples of what covert action has actually meant in practice — American commandos blowing up the Trans-Siberian oil pipeline, Afghan guerrillas hired to cross the Amu Darya and attack a refinery inside the southern USSR, and cash dumped in a Moscow bathroom to undermine the rouble.

the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.title: How Chinese intelligence recruits
the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.summary: John Kiriakou''s assessment of the Ministry of State Security''s tradecraft: very effective with anyone who simply wants money, because the money is limitless, and very bad at cultivating a source who does not yet know who is cultivating him — with the target usually being access to sophisticated technology.

the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.title: MK-ULTRA in Canada
the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that many MK-ULTRA experiments took place on Canadian soil, and his explanation of why: the CIA asked the Canadian intelligence service for help with its anti-Soviet, anti-Chinese remote-viewing and LSD work, and the Canadians gladly gave it.

the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.title: Pakistani corruption and democracy
the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment that corruption in Pakistan is so deep and so broad that a genuinely functioning democracy is almost impossible there — set against a long history of military coups, a habit of imprisoning former prime ministers, and his insistence that Imran Khan should not be in a cell.

the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.title: Tarpon Springs
the-culture-of-secrecy-and-the-truth.summary: The Greek sponge-diving town on the Florida gulf coast that John Kiriakou calls one of his favourite places — settled for a century by divers from Kalymnos, the island immediately north of the one his own family comes from, and, in his verdict, the site of absolutely incredible Greek food.

the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.title: China as economic threat
the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.title: NSA
the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.summary: Kiriakou on the agency whose Utah facility boasts room to store every American's calls, texts and emails for the next 500 years.

the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.title: NSA Surveillance
the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.summary: ''It is part of NSA''s founding charter that it is not allowed to spy on Americans'' — Kiriakou on warrantless collection and the Bluffdale warehouse.

the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.title: The hundred and eighty-seven Israeli officers
the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.summary: The figure John Kiriakou gives for undeclared Israeli intelligence officers working clandestinely in the United States when he joined the CIA around 1990 — 187 identified by the FBI, over and above the one declared Mossad officer and one declared Shin Bet officer at the Israeli embassy.

the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.title: Alexa
the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.summary: Per John Kiriakou, Amazon''s Alexa smart speaker reports directly to the NSA — and he owns one anyway. The device recurs across his interviews as the standing example of the surveillance trade-off in modern smart-home technology, and of his own negotiated exception to it: one speaker, in one room, against the advice of every intelligence officer he has ever known.

the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.title: San Bernardino iPhone Case
the-cyber-victimhood-complaint.summary: The 2015–16 legal standoff in which Apple refused to unlock the San Bernardino shooter's iPhone for the FBI, which instead paid an Israeli firm $6 million to crack it — though, per John Kiriakou, the intelligence that could have disrupted the attack never came from the phone at all.

the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.title: Abraham Accords
the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.title: The Iron Dome
the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.summary: Israel's air-defence system as John Kiriakou reads it — impressive against a wave of slow Iranian drones, but shown by the handful that got through, and later by Iranian ballistic missiles, to be not all it is cracked up to be; each exchange, in his account, buying Iran intelligence about the gaps.

the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.title: Why Iran targets the Gulf states
the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.summary: John Kiriakou''s explanation of why Iranian missiles fell more heavily on Gulf Arab states than on Israel during the 2026 war: the Gulf has no Iron Dome, a finite missile stock has to be spent where it counts, and hosting American forces converted an uneasy coexistence into open enmity.

the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.title: American missile stockpiles
the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that the United States has run its interceptor stocks down to the point of strategic vulnerability — that the conventional wisdom in Washington was that a round of the Iran war ended because the Patriots ran out, and that a country which cannot fight a two-front war certainly cannot do it below maximum production.

the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.title: The 1991 Saudi plan for Gaza
the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.summary: A proposal John Kiriakou says he watched Ambassador Chas Freeman float to the Saudis during his first overseas tour in 1991 — that Saudi Arabia fund a port, an airport, a desalination plant and an electrical grid in Gaza. The Saudis agreed; Israel refused outright. Kiriakou raises it because the identical arrangement resurfaced in the Israeli press more than three decades later.

the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.title: Declare victory and go home
the-cyprus-fruit-relabel.summary: The exit John Kiriakou prescribed for Israel in Gaza: turn the territory back to the United Nations, declare Hamas destroyed, declare victory, then engage the Saudis on the Abraham Accords and negotiate a deal later. His reasoning was that nothing remained to destroy, that killing as many people as possible is not a viable policy, and that Israel had no other way out.

the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.title: 2026 Iran war
the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.title: Greater Israel
the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.summary: The territorial project John Kiriakou believes the Israeli government genuinely holds: the expulsion of every Palestinian, beginning in Gaza and continuing into the West Bank, pursued on a hundred- or two-hundred-year horizon in the confidence that the United States will never push back.

the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.title: Israeli Nuclear Program
the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.summary: Israel's widely assumed but officially unacknowledged nuclear arsenal; per John Kiriakou, the conventional wisdom within the CIA is that Israel possesses between 120 and 220 nuclear weapons, and the U.S. government's refusal to formally acknowledge this is driven by a specific legal obligation under the Glenn-Symington Act, which would require cutting off all foreign aid to any nuclear-armed country not party to the Non-Proliferation Treaty.

the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.title: Lebanon-Israeli Conflict
the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.summary: Per John Kiriakou, no Israeli government will allow Lebanon to flourish as a nation; he expects continued Israeli attacks and forced displacement of civilians, citing a statistic of up to 700,000 Lebanese internally displaced, and links the war to the "Greater Israel" rhetoric of US ambassador Mike Huckabee.

the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.title: Mike Huckabee
the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.summary: The United States ambassador to Israel under Donald Trump, and the subject of a public call for resignation from John Kiriakou after Huckabee received Jonathan Pollard at the American embassy. Kiriakou''s assessment separates two charges: Huckabee is not a traitor but an idiot who did not think the meeting was a big deal, and a former governor of a small state who still behaves as though he can set policy without the State Department or the National Security Council.

the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.title: Naftali Bennett
the-cyprus-naval-buildup-2026.summary: The former Israeli prime minister, cited by John Kiriakou through 2026 for the position that Turkey would be the next target after Iran — a claim Kiriakou uses to identify the second obstacle, alongside Iran, to the Greater Israel project, and which by May 2026 he was stating in his own voice as an active Israeli intention rather than a Bennett prediction.

the-dandelion-salad.title: The best meal overseas
the-dandelion-salad.summary: Asked for the best meals he had eaten abroad, John Kiriakou named first a dish cooked by a young Pakistani in a CIA guest house in Islamabad — shaved beef, a myriad of spices, hot green chillies and rice cooked in chicken stock — followed by sushi in Tokyo and the Lenten table of Clean Monday in Greece.

the-dandelion-salad.title: The Islamabad guest house
the-dandelion-salad.summary: The sixteen-room guest house in Islamabad that CIA officers took over entirely during the post-9/11 deployments — a place John Kiriakou says the agency still will not let him name, which came with breakfast, dinner and laundry for about thirty-five dollars a day against a per diem of five hundred.

the-dandelion-salad.title: A Middle East reading list
the-dandelion-salad.summary: The books and the starting point John Kiriakou recommends to anyone trying to understand the modern Middle East: begin at the end of the Second World War, not five thousand years earlier, and start with The House of Saud, the Sykes-Picot Agreement and From Beirut to Jerusalem.

the-dandelion-salad.title: Bombing the Omanis
the-dandelion-salad.summary: John Kiriakou's judgement that Iran's strikes on the Gulf states — and above all on Oman, which had been trying to broker peace — made enemies Iran did not need to make, of governments that would otherwise have sat the war out.

the-dandelion-salad.title: Bowe Bergdahl
the-dandelion-salad.summary: The American soldier who walked off his base in Afghanistan, was captured by the Haqqani network and handed to the Taliban, and was repatriated in a prisoner trade — a man John Kiriakou says was treated as a traitor although he was not one.

the-dandelion-salad.title: Chaos as the Israeli objective
the-dandelion-salad.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to whether Netanyahu''s government actually wanted an American invasion of Iran: what the Israelis want in Iran is what they got in Libya — chaos, civil war, and as many dead Iranians as possible.

the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.title: Greenland
the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.summary: The Danish territory the United States has spent years talking about acquiring; John Kiriakou reports two flatly contradictory readings from his own contacts — a White House friend who says Washington is serious and will lean on a Cold War treaty to claim it is already de facto American, and a Republican friend who says the whole thing is a grenade thrown to distract the press — and warns that taking it by force would end NATO.

the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.title: Donald Trump
the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.title: 2026 Iran war economic shock
the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.summary: John Kiriakou''s running assessment of the economic damage from the 2026 Iran war — an oil shock he says already exceeds both 1970s shocks combined, a natural-gas shock worse than the Nord Stream destruction, and a chokepoint problem that runs through fertilizer as much as fuel, since 65% of the world''s supply must transit the Strait of Hormuz. His summary: "This is an economic slowdown of choice."

the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.title: Advice to an aspiring intelligence analyst
the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to a 21-year-old student asking what to study and what to read: pick a geographic area, become the go-to person on it, and consume everything published in the field — including the journals written by people who have never made policy.

the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.title: Air wars are overrated
the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.summary: John Kiriakou''s summary judgement on the 2026 Iran and Lebanon campaigns, delivered as the meta-headline of the whole war: air power flattened Gaza without destroying Hamas, is bogging down against Hezbollah, and cannot produce the outcome the war requires.

the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.title: Asian fuel reserves, 2026
the-danish-greenland-demolition-plan.summary: The effect of the Strait of Hormuz closure on oil-importing Asian economies as John Kiriakou described it — countries counting their remaining fuel in days rather than months, with no substitute supply available, and economies he expects simply to stop.

the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.title: MOSSAD
the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.title: The Siemens control room
the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.summary: The underground surveillance facility in Dubai that John Kiriakou says he was given a tour of — built by Siemens, five storeys of monitors covering every inch of the city — and the taxi crash he watched unfold on the wall in real time.

the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.title: Five Eyes
the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.summary: The intelligence-sharing partnership of the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand

the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.title: Jonathan Pollard
the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.summary: U.S. Navy civilian intelligence analyst convicted in 1985 of spying for Israel; the canonical proven case of Israeli espionage against the United States; cited by John Kiriakou in his 2024 Piers Morgan debate with a former Mossad director who denied any Israeli spying on the U.S.

the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.title: George Tenet
the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.summary: Director of Central Intelligence from 1997 to 2004, spanning the September 11 attacks and the early enhanced-interrogation program; identified by John Kiriakou as John Brennan's institutional patron at the agency; the figure who ordered the Five Eyes intelligence services to "open the files" to each other in the early 2000s.

the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.title: Israel and the fear of being held back
the-debate-with-the-mossad-director.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of why an ally that receives almost everything it asks for still spies on the United States — that the Israelis are always afraid something is being withheld, and, having nowhere to be pushed except the Mediterranean, will do anything to be certain about their own security.

the-declination-letter.title: The rogue officer remark
the-declination-letter.summary: The answer President George W. Bush shouted to a reporter on his way to the helicopter — that if there was torture, it was the work of a rogue CIA officer — which John Kiriakou has said convinced him he was about to be made the scapegoat, and which led him to accept Brian Ross's interview offer.

the-declination-letter.title: Bankruptcy and the dropped charges
the-declination-letter.summary: The sequence John Kiriakou places at the centre of his case: that the espionage counts against him were dropped only after his legal fees had bankrupted him, which he presents as evidence that the government''s aim was attrition rather than conviction.

the-declination-letter.title: John Brennan
the-declination-letter.summary: Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President

the-declination-letter.title: Curtailment cables
the-declination-letter.summary: The career-ending requests John Kiriakou says he read coming back from the CIA's black sites — officers, doctors, psychologists and nurses asking to end their tours early rather than continue to take part in the interrogation programme — and his conclusion that if that many people were objecting in classified channels, someone would surely go public.

the-declination-letter.title: Arabic and Greek
the-declination-letter.summary: The qualification John Kiriakou says opened the door to his transfer from CIA analysis to operations: a post in Athens wanted Greek or Arabic, and he had both — by most of his tellings the only officer in the agency who did. The chief who hired him gave the reason in one sentence: it is easier and cheaper to take a linguist and teach him operations than the other way round. The pairing also became a detection tool, since the language nobody speaks in Pakistan is Arabic.

the-declination-letter.title: The Office of Security arrangement
the-declination-letter.summary: The disclosure John Kiriakou says emerged from a 2020 custody hearing: that his wife, herself a senior CIA officer, had accompanied him to the 2007 ABC News whistleblowing interview on the instruction of the CIA''s Office of Security, and had continued to report on his activities.

the-denials-after-dallas.title: Butler rally shooting
the-denials-after-dallas.summary: The July 2024 attempt on Donald Trump's life at a rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, on which John Kiriakou takes no position as to who was responsible but argues the published facts cannot be reconciled with a competent Secret Service — and that the questions it leaves open are owed an answer for the historical record whether or not anyone alive gets one.

the-denials-after-dallas.title: Secret Service
the-denials-after-dallas.summary: The U.S. agency protecting the president. John Kiriakou, who worked alongside it for 35 years, describes a culture of complacency and poor follow-up — great with guns, weak on training and follow-through — and calls the 2024 Butler rally shooting a colossal historic screw-up in which coverage of the surrounding buildings was outsourced to a county sheriff's department. He has also encountered the Service as an adversary, outside the Venezuelan embassy in Washington in 2019.

the-denials-after-dallas.title: Taking the ball and going home
the-denials-after-dallas.summary: John Kiriakou''s rule of thumb, offered after the July 2024 Butler shooting, that a failed state-run assassination is not retried: an operation with that many moving parts would not be attempted in front of thousands of people, would not be entrusted to a twenty-year-old, and once blown would be abandoned rather than repeated.

the-denials-after-dallas.title: The unsearched car at Mar-a-Lago
the-denials-after-dallas.summary: An episode John Kiriakou related in July 2024 as evidence that the Secret Service''s problem is systemic rather than confined to the Butler rally: a retired Army colonel and Republican fundraiser was asked at the Mar-a-Lago gate whether he had weapons in the car, said yes, went back to his hotel to lock them up — and later realised nobody had ever searched the vehicle.

the-denials-after-dallas.title: Watergate
the-denials-after-dallas.summary: The scandal that ended Nixon''s presidency and the standing benchmark in John Kiriakou''s vocabulary — the CIA spying on the Senate committee investigating its torture program was, to him, "a Watergate-level kind of scandal," except that this time nothing came of it. He draws one lesson from it above all others: Nixon did not fall for the burglary but for the cover-up. Watergate touches his own story directly — his lead defense attorney had been John Mitchell''s lawyer — and its cast overlapped with the agency he joined, from E. Howard Hunt to the tradecraft by which Deep Throat summoned Bob Woodward.

the-denials-after-dallas.title: JFK assassination
the-denials-after-dallas.summary: November 22, 1963 killing of President John F. Kennedy in Dallas, Texas. John Kiriakou's position, drawn from a Pakistan-station encounter with Bay of Pigs commander Jean Gately, an RFK Jr. account of CIA Director John McCone's same-day exchange with Bobby Kennedy Sr., and a White House contact's confirmation that the remaining classified Kennedy documents all contain the word "Israel," is that elements of the CIA were probably involved and that Israeli intelligence was involved as well.

the-density-of-spies-in-washington.title: The Greek colonel and China
the-density-of-spies-in-washington.summary: The arrest of a Greek colonel assigned to NATO on charges of spying for China — a case John Kiriakou calls highly unusual not because espionage arrests are rare in Greece, but because they are almost always for Russia, and which he says shows the Chinese have begun caring about NATO communications.

the-density-of-spies-in-washington.title: The operational test
the-density-of-spies-in-washington.summary: The vetting procedure John Kiriakou describes for moving a trusted source onto normal handling: put a full surveillance team on him without telling him, watch how he gets to the meeting, and then ask him to describe what he did.

the-density-of-spies-in-washington.title: The orb off Yemen
the-density-of-spies-in-washington.summary: A leaked video John Kiriakou describes as the most dramatic UFO material he has seen: two F-18s following a silver orb off the coast of Yemen, given permission to fire, and a missile that hits the object and bounces off before the orb turns ninety degrees and flies on.

the-density-of-spies-in-washington.title: Running into former sources
the-density-of-spies-in-washington.summary: John Kiriakou has twice met people he once ran as agents by accident, years after leaving the CIA — once at an airport and once in the street — and both times they came to him with a bear hug. One of them was astonished to discover he spoke English.

the-density-of-spies-in-washington.title: Sources are not traitors
the-density-of-spies-in-washington.summary: Asked whether CIA officers privately regarded their recruited agents as traitors and held them in contempt, John Kiriakou answered that they did not — because the officers believed they were the good guys, and a recruited source had become one of them.

the-density-of-spies-in-washington.title: CIA Training Doctrine
the-density-of-spies-in-washington.summary: ''Our job is to break the law'' — Kiriakou on what CIA training actually teaches, why it applies only overseas, and the ethics class that never comes.

the-desert-sunset-photograph.title: Bigger than the Russian embassy
the-desert-sunset-photograph.summary: Why American embassies in small, strategically unimportant countries are enormous: the answer John Kiriakou says he was given by a station chief on one of his first CIA trips — that the building had to be bigger than the Soviet one across town. He describes American embassies in Africa as "absolutely gigantic" for that reason alone, and calls the US embassy in Cairo an enormous facility matched by an equally enormous Russian one.

the-desert-sunset-photograph.title: "Do not ever attempt to contact me again"
the-desert-sunset-photograph.summary: The reply John Kiriakou says he received from John Kerry, then Secretary of State, after emailing him privately in the days before reporting to prison to beg that his sentence be commuted. Kiriakou had worked closely with Kerry for two and a half years; the one-line answer, sent after two or three days, was the last he ever heard from him.

the-desert-sunset-photograph.title: The airbridge
the-desert-sunset-photograph.summary: John Kiriakou''s definition of an airbridge, given when the term surfaced in reporting on German aid to Gaza: a direct path into another country''s airspace along which safety is guaranteed — his worked example being Cyprus to Gaza, with an undertaking that the Israeli Air Force will not shoot the aircraft down.

the-desert-sunset-photograph.title: Declare victory and go home
the-desert-sunset-photograph.summary: The exit John Kiriakou prescribed for Israel in Gaza: turn the territory back to the United Nations, declare Hamas destroyed, declare victory, then engage the Saudis on the Abraham Accords and negotiate a deal later. His reasoning was that nothing remained to destroy, that killing as many people as possible is not a viable policy, and that Israel had no other way out.

the-desert-sunset-photograph.title: "Every Israeli I ever knew"
the-desert-sunset-photograph.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the attitudes he encountered among Israelis he knew professionally and socially — that almost every one of them wanted the Palestinians killed or exiled — together with his description of a sensibility he says is palpable walking around Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, and his immediate self-correction when he overstated the claim.

the-desert-sunset-photograph.title: Palestine House
the-desert-sunset-photograph.summary: The Washington, DC meeting space and gallery for pro-Palestinian human rights groups, artists and musicians that John Kiriakou describes as newly opened on Capitol Hill — housed in a building donated by a Lebanese-American property developer, running programming several nights a week, and headed by Miko Peled.

the-detractors-who-died.title: Hire a lawyer first
the-detractors-who-died.summary: The single piece of practical advice John Kiriakou gives to anyone considering blowing the whistle: retain a lawyer before saying anything, and have that lawyer sitting beside you when you do.

the-detractors-who-died.title: The CIA divorce rate
the-detractors-who-died.summary: John Kiriakou's account of why marriages fail at the CIA at a rate he says exceeds that of any other part of the U.S. government — the impossibility of explaining a midnight departure to a spouse without a clearance, and the difficulty officers have switching off a professional habit of deception. He gives the figure variously as over 75 percent and upwards of 80 percent, says he was determined not to become a statistic and became one anyway, and dates the end of his first marriage to a sentence spoken in an armoured car on the way to Athens airport. Both his divorces have been costly; of the second he says the agency played an active role he is barred by court order from explaining.

the-detractors-who-died.title: Get better enough to go back
the-detractors-who-died.summary: John Kiriakou's warning that the CIA does not care whether an officer has a mental breakdown, and cares about recovery only far enough to send them overseas again — advice he says means the officer has to look after themselves.

the-detractors-who-died.title: Never meet my grandchildren
the-detractors-who-died.summary: The threat John Kiriakou says one of the prosecutors in his case made to him — that he was going to die in prison and would never meet his grandchildren — set against the forty-five years he faced under the original charges.

the-detractors-who-died.title: The standard operating procedure assignment
the-detractors-who-died.summary: The task John Kiriakou says he was given on arriving in Pakistan in January 2002 — to write a standard operating procedure for taking down an al-Qaeda safe house — the legal pad he wrote it on, the high value target list it was built around, and the first raid it produced.

the-detractors-who-died.title: They deserve an apology
the-detractors-who-died.summary: John Kiriakou's statement that he feels he owes the men his government tortured an apology, that they deserve compensation they will never receive, and that at the very least they are owed the apology.

the-difficulty-of-getting-out.title: MBS and Netanyahu asked Trump to attack Iran
the-difficulty-of-getting-out.summary: John Kiriakou's account that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu jointly went to Donald Trump and asked him to attack Iran — a move Kiriakou finds hard to reconcile with MBS's own years of work to improve Saudi relations with Tehran.

the-difficulty-of-getting-out.title: Chaos as the Israeli objective
the-difficulty-of-getting-out.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to whether Netanyahu''s government actually wanted an American invasion of Iran: what the Israelis want in Iran is what they got in Libya — chaos, civil war, and as many dead Iranians as possible.

the-difficulty-of-getting-out.title: Marco Rubio and Iran policy
the-difficulty-of-getting-out.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to who was actually driving American policy toward Iran in 2026: with the Vice President, the Director of National Intelligence and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs all reported as opposed, and with Marco Rubio holding both the State Department and the National Security Adviser''s job, the policy was Rubio''s.

the-difficulty-of-getting-out.title: The Condoleezza Rice meeting
the-difficulty-of-getting-out.summary: The nine o'clock White House appointment John Kiriakou and Cofer Black never kept on the morning of 11 September 2001. The Government Printing Office was about to issue a volume of declassified Greece-Turkey-Cyprus cables in an edition of five or ten copies; three of them named CIA sources who were still alive, and an obscure statute obliges the government to offer citizenship and resettlement to any recruited source it outs. The two men were going to ask the National Security Advisor to quietly pull three cables nobody would miss. The car was at the East entrance at 8.15.

the-difficulty-of-getting-out.title: A Middle East reading list
the-difficulty-of-getting-out.summary: The books and the starting point John Kiriakou recommends to anyone trying to understand the modern Middle East: begin at the end of the Second World War, not five thousand years earlier, and start with The House of Saud, the Sykes-Picot Agreement and From Beirut to Jerusalem.

the-difficulty-of-getting-out.title: Bombing the Omanis
the-difficulty-of-getting-out.summary: John Kiriakou's judgement that Iran's strikes on the Gulf states — and above all on Oman, which had been trying to broker peace — made enemies Iran did not need to make, of governments that would otherwise have sat the war out.

the-diplomatic-stool-collection.title: The hundred-dollar informants
the-diplomatic-stool-collection.summary: John Kiriakou''s explanation of Iran''s mass detention of some 20,000 suspected Israeli spies after the 2026 twelve-day war: that most of those rounded up were undocumented Afghan refugees, targeted by Israeli intelligence precisely because Iran had spent two years expelling them, and recruited for about $100 a month to report troop movements and the addresses of nuclear scientists and utility headquarters.

the-diplomatic-stool-collection.title: Phil Donahue
the-diplomatic-stool-collection.summary: American talk-show host who, John Kiriakou discovered seven years after the fact, had been secretly paying his weekly newspaper column fee — $400 a week for nine years, routed through Reader Supported News — because Donahue had learned that Kiriakou came out of prison broke and did not want him sleeping in his car.

the-diplomatic-stool-collection.title: Soviet Union
the-diplomatic-stool-collection.summary: The superpower whose collapse framed the start of John Kiriakou's CIA career — it was "literally in the process of collapsing" when he joined in January 1990, ushering in a brief "peace dividend" era when the agency's new threats were environmental degradation and AIDS. Kiriakou cites Brzezinski's "Afghan trap" that lured the Soviets into Afghanistan, argues the U.S. abandoned the radicalized mujahideen the moment the Soviets were beaten, notes America then took "a vacation from history," and recalls that Jonathan Pollard's stolen documents were traded by Israel to the Soviets in exchange for Russian Jews.

the-diplomatic-stool-collection.title: The Alaska glacier
the-diplomatic-stool-collection.summary: The visitor centre John Kiriakou saw on a 2016 trip to Alaska with Gary Johnson, built at the foot of a glacier close enough to touch from the observation deck and by then a quarter of a mile away from it — an image he uses as the plainest available demonstration of climate change, and one he refuses to let pass as a joke.

the-diplomatic-stool-collection.title: The armour at Union Station
the-diplomatic-stool-collection.summary: John Kiriakou''s eyewitness account of stepping off an Amtrak train at Washington''s Union Station in August 2025 to find two armoured personnel carriers and a .50 calibre machine gun trained on the entrance — and of tourists posing for photographs with the National Guardsmen deployed in the parts of the city where, he says, there is no crime.

the-diplomatic-stool-collection.title: The CIA and Iridium
the-diplomatic-stool-collection.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the Central Intelligence Agency buying the satellite telephone company Iridium when it was unprofitable and about to go out of business, because the agency needed the network — a purchase he places alongside its acquisition of Intelsat, and which he encountered personally when he had to rent the phones for Afghanistan.

the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.title: Amnesty International
the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.summary: The human rights organization whose torture report forms part of John Kiriakou's core defense — the CIA's crimes were already public knowledge before he confirmed them on ABC, and the Justice Department's own declination letter said so — and the organization whose silence during his prosecution he cannot forgive. He begged Amnesty for a one-sentence statement and got a New Yorker subscription instead; it took Ai Weiwei to change their minds, and by then he was walking out of prison.

the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.title: Daniel Hale
the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.summary: Per John Kiriakou, drone whistleblower Daniel Hale — an NSA contractor and drone targeting analyst who exposed an 80% civilian death rate in the U.S. drone program, was ordered to fire on two young girls his superior called "goats," and was sentenced to 45 months (of which Kiriakou says he actually served about 18) despite prosecutors seeking nine to eleven years.

the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.title: I want my fifty bucks back
the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.summary: What John Kiriakou says he shouted at John Fetterman from ten rows back at an Ohio State football game — and his explanation, as a Pennsylvanian furious about the senator, of why Fetterman keeps his seat anyway.

the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.title: Ian Henderson
the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.summary: The British colonial police officer who ran Bahrain's intelligence service during John Kiriakou's posting there — a man Kiriakou says even the heir presumptive to the throne was afraid to name aloud, and whom Kiriakou, seated at the crown prince's table at a dinner for George H. W. Bush, mistook for a corpse.

the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.title: Ibrahim Traoré
the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of the military ruler of Burkina Faso — a young officer who took power promising a return to democracy, and who in Kiriakou's account has grown increasingly irrational, criminalising homosexuality, abolishing the electoral commission and moving to expel foreigners.

the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle in Athens
the-disappearance-of-daniel-hale.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of Kimberly Guilfoyle's appointment as American ambassador to Greece — that she got it because Donald Trump Jr. wanted her out of the way, a manoeuvre he compares to Saddam Hussein's habit of exiling successful generals as ambassadors — and his reluctant conclusion that Greece could have done worse.

the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.title: The bunker busters as preemption
the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.summary: What John Kiriakou says friends in the CIA, the Defense Department and the White House told him about why Donald Trump broke with every previous president and struck Iran — that Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel was so certain of an Iranian nuclear attack that it was prepared to use nuclear weapons itself, and that Trump used bunker-buster bombs so that Israel would not.

the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.title: 2026 Iran war
the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.title: Iran Nuclear Assessment
the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.summary: Per John Kiriakou's assessment, the US–Israeli military campaign against Iran was a war of choice driven by Israeli political pressure rather than genuine intelligence indicating an Iranian nuclear weapons threat. The CIA produced two National Intelligence Estimates concluding Iran had no nuclear weapons program; Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei issued a fatwa in the 1980s forbidding such a program. The U.S. went to war anyway, in Kiriakou's view, after President Trump replaced the Joint Chiefs of Staff with officers willing to accept Israeli intelligence and proceed.

the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.title: AIPAC
the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.title: Bezalel Smotrich
the-dispersal-of-the-iranian-program.summary: Israeli far-right minister whom John Kiriakou, alongside Itamar Ben-Gvir, blames for leaving Israel unprepared on October 7 by insisting any attack would come from the West Bank rather than Gaza.

the-divorce-at-the-airport.title: Learning to dive in the embassy pool
the-divorce-at-the-airport.summary: John Kiriakou''s brief diving history, offered when the Nordstream sabotage discussion turned to the physics of deep water: lessons in the pool of the American embassy in 1991, one dive in the Red Sea at Sharm el-Sheikh in about 1992, and never again after that.

the-divorce-at-the-airport.title: How the CIA kills
the-divorce-at-the-airport.summary: John Kiriakou''s description of the methods used when the CIA is ordered to kill someone outside a war zone: a team parachuting in miles away, stealing a car, a locks-and-picks specialist opening the door and suppressed weapons inside; a snatch into a van bound for an airport or a boat; or a brush past in a market with something poisoned — a technique he says the Russians used often and taught the Bulgarians into the early 1980s.

the-divorce-at-the-airport.title: Mark Polymeropoulos
the-divorce-at-the-airport.summary: The CIA officer John Kiriakou describes as a friend who was in his first tour when Aldrich Ames blew his identity, was brought in from the cold, and later became station chief in Moscow — an appointment Kiriakou characterises as a deliberate thumb in the Russians'' eye: the officer their spy had burned, put in charge of operations against them.

the-divorce-at-the-airport.title: Mike Baker
the-divorce-at-the-airport.summary: Former CIA case officer and John Kiriakou's direct predecessor in Athens on the 17 November problem; "the real deal," in Kiriakou's phrase, until a botched surveillance operation got him expelled from Greece and forced out of the agency the same day he expected a commendation.

the-divorce-at-the-airport.title: Nine recruitments in twenty-five years
the-divorce-at-the-airport.summary: The conversation in which John Kiriakou''s Athens station chief, a twenty-five-year operations officer who had reached senior intelligence service level four with nine recruitments to his name, pointed out that Kiriakou had recruited five in two years — and Kiriakou''s explanation of the knack: that he could hide his disdain for a man completely while talking about whatever interested him.

the-divorce-at-the-airport.title: Qatari money in Egypt
the-divorce-at-the-airport.summary: John Kiriakou''s explanation for Qatar injecting seven and a half billion dollars into the Egyptian economy: to annoy Saudi Arabia. He describes a long, close Saudi–Egyptian relationship dating back to the mid-1960s, a terrible Qatari–Saudi one, and an Egypt happy to take the money — including the year the Egyptians thanked the Saudis for their generosity with an uninhabited island in the Red Sea.

the-dnc-in-debt.title: The stapler in the Dirksen building
the-dnc-in-debt.summary: An incident John Kiriakou witnessed while serving as a senior staff member on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee: a Democratic senator threw a stapler at a staff member in a hallway of the Dirksen Senate Office Building, swore at him, and then looked around to see who had seen it.

the-dnc-in-debt.title: 2026 Iran war
the-dnc-in-debt.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-dnc-in-debt.title: Embassy movie night
the-dnc-in-debt.summary: The weekly diversion John Kiriakou remembers from his posting to Pakistan after September 11th, when the station worked seven days a week and fourteen hours a day: on Wednesday nights the ambassador hosted a film in the embassy''s small theatre, and the audience shouted at the screen and threw popcorn at whatever they had managed to get hold of.

the-dnc-in-debt.title: Lindsey Graham
the-dnc-in-debt.summary: Republican senator from South Carolina who died in July 2026, and John Kiriakou's standing shorthand for the permanent war caucus — a "show horse" rather than a workhorse, a "chameleon" who "never saw a war that he didn't want to jump into with both feet," and, on posthumously released documentary footage, a man offering the US Air Force to bomb a country America was not at war with.

the-dnc-in-debt.title: The Espionage Act and the Rosenbergs
the-dnc-in-debt.summary: John Kiriakou''s short legislative history of the Espionage Act: written in 1917 to counter German saboteurs, slightly amended in 1950 after the execution of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, and never meaningfully updated since. It does not use the words classified information, because the classification system did not exist when it was drafted.

the-dnc-in-debt.title: The Graham Senate succession
the-dnc-in-debt.summary: John Kiriakou's comment on the appointment of Lindsey Graham's sister to serve out the remainder of his Senate term, and her announcement that she would run for a full term of her own — a candidacy whose only qualification, in Kiriakou's assessment, is her relation to the late senator.

the-dorm-as-a-reward.title: The guard booth rounds
the-dorm-as-a-reward.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of federal prison staffing from the inside: rounds required every eight or fifteen minutes and performed once an hour or two, cameras that are down half the time, and a hiring standard he says amounts to a GED and no felony convictions.

the-dorm-as-a-reward.title: Clickers and touchers
the-dorm-as-a-reward.summary: The distinction John Kiriakou says prisoners at FCI Loretto drew between convicted sex offenders who had only viewed images of children and those who had travelled across state lines to molest them, and his account of why they are all held at low security.

the-dorm-as-a-reward.title: Prince Andrew
the-dorm-as-a-reward.summary: British royal, now Andrew Mountbatten Windsor, named repeatedly by John Kiriakou as one of the un-recruitable principals whose access made Jeffrey Epstein valuable to a foreign intelligence service. Kiriakou has asked why Andrew was never charged over conduct with minors, reads his alleged provision of classified Ministry of Defence documents to Epstein as evidence of espionage rather than vanity — and expects him to face no criminal consequence at all, because the statute of limitations has run.

the-dorm-as-a-reward.title: Why he believes Epstein killed himself
the-dorm-as-a-reward.summary: John Kiriakou's stated conclusion that Jeffrey Epstein died by suicide, reasoned from his own experience of how federal prison guards actually work rather than from any view of the wider Epstein case.

the-dorm-as-a-reward.title: Bureau of Prisons
the-dorm-as-a-reward.summary: The federal agency that ran John Kiriakou's incarceration — and one of his most persistent post-prison targets. The BOP overrode his judge's camp recommendation by deeming him "a threat to the public safety," threatened him with "diesel therapy" until 1,600 logged phone calls and letters from a dozen House members and two senators backed it off, and, per Kiriakou, functions as "an employment agency for unemployable semi-literate rural white men" and "a dumping ground for failed medical professionals" — an agency for which a prisoner's death is cheaper than his treatment.

the-dorm-as-a-reward.title: Maxwell at a work camp
the-dorm-as-a-reward.summary: John Kiriakou's objection to Ghislaine Maxwell's placement in a minimum security work camp — that convicted sex offenders are, in his experience, never eligible for minimums — and his refusal, when pressed, to offer any explanation for the exception.

the-draft-argument.title: George McGovern
the-draft-argument.summary: The 1972 Democratic presidential nominee, whose landslide defeat John Kiriakou identifies as the pretext for creating superdelegates. As a George Washington University sophomore in 1983, Kiriakou wrote to McGovern offering the campus theater for a campaign launch; McGovern telephoned him personally, announced his 1984 candidacy there, and afterwards took him home for tuna sandwiches made by his wife.

the-draft-argument.title: Invasion of Grenada
the-draft-argument.summary: The 1983 American invasion of Grenada, which John Kiriakou supported as a nineteen-year-old College Democrat at George Washington University on the grounds that American medical students had to be rescued — an episode he now cites as the clearest example of how completely he once accepted the government's own account of what it was doing.

the-draft-argument.title: John Kiriakou
the-draft-argument.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

the-draft-argument.title: George Washington University
the-draft-argument.summary: The Washington university where John Kiriakou took a bachelor's degree in Middle Eastern studies and began a master's in legislative affairs, and where a professor who was in fact a CIA spotter recruited him into the agency — an institution that recurs throughout his account as the place his intelligence career began, as the venue of his first CIA tests, and later as a classroom he taught in himself.

the-draft-argument.title: Reza Pahlavi
the-draft-argument.summary: The exiled Iranian crown prince whom John Kiriakou dismisses as an Israeli-backed fantasy candidate to rule Iran — a man who has not lived there since his teens, supported mainly by Beverly Hills exiles, whom Kiriakou says 'wouldn't survive the walk from the plane to the terminal.'

the-draft-argument.title: The letter to the Shah
the-draft-argument.summary: The fan letter John Kiriakou wrote at fourteen or fifteen to the deposed Shah of Iran, objecting to how the United States had treated him — and the reply, agreeing, with an autographed photograph enclosed.

the-drone-papers.title: Daniel Hale
the-drone-papers.summary: Per John Kiriakou, drone whistleblower Daniel Hale — an NSA contractor and drone targeting analyst who exposed an 80% civilian death rate in the U.S. drone program, was ordered to fire on two young girls his superior called "goats," and was sentenced to 45 months (of which Kiriakou says he actually served about 18) despite prosecutors seeking nine to eleven years.

the-drone-papers.title: The Intercept
the-drone-papers.summary: The investigative news outlet that published Daniel Hale's drone leak; John Kiriakou notes that the same Intercept reporter, Matthew Cole, was involved in cases that led to the exposure of both Kiriakou himself and NSA leaker Reality Winner — though he insists Hale outed himself rather than being burned by the outlet.

the-drone-papers.title: Signature strikes
the-drone-papers.summary: The drone-targeting doctrine, exposed by Daniel Hale's leak, under which the U.S. kills people not for who they are but for patterns of behavior or association; John Kiriakou says operators treat any male over 12 as a legitimate target on the theory that he 'could pick up a gun.'

the-drone-papers.title: Matthew Cole
the-drone-papers.summary: American national-security journalist whose reporting tradecraft, per John Kiriakou, has led to the federal incarceration of five whistleblowers — including Kiriakou himself. In Kiriakou's account, Cole emailed him in 2010 ostensibly researching a book on the rendition of Abu Omar, asked Kiriakou to confirm the surname of a CIA officer who appeared in Kiriakou's own first book under the alias 'John', and Kiriakou's confirmation was the act of confirming a covert officer's identity for which he was eventually prosecuted under the Intelligence Identities Protection Act.

the-drone-papers.title: National Bird
the-drone-papers.summary: Award-winning documentary on the U.S. drone program featuring whistleblower Daniel Hale; John Kiriakou calls it essential viewing, noting its footage of drone operators debating on audio whether the figures in their crosshairs are children before firing.

the-drone-papers.title: RDAP program
the-drone-papers.summary: The Bureau of Prisons' Residential Drug and Alcohol Program, which can shave 12 to 18 months off a federal sentence; John Kiriakou repeatedly advises fellow whistleblowers that, combined with good behavior and a halfway house, it can turn a five-year sentence into as little as two and a half years.

the-dublin-compensation.title: Kiriakou on travel
the-dublin-compensation.summary: John Kiriakou''s own ranking of the countries he has visited: Greece his favourite and, he insists, the best food anywhere; Oman the most beautiful landscape; Syria the most extraordinary civilisation; and Chile the cheapest, illustrated by a bottle of a vineyard''s locked-away reserve that cost $8.50 on his honeymoon.

the-dublin-compensation.title: Aafia Siddiqui
the-dublin-compensation.summary: Pakistani-American neuroscientist arrested in Afghanistan and convicted in the United States of attempting to shoot FBI agents; per John Kiriakou, who covered the arrest as a terrorism consultant for ABC News and has followed the case since, she never had a gun and never fired, the bullet holes offered as proof predated her capture, and the CIA took her three children — two later recovered, the youngest never found.

the-dublin-compensation.title: The 1991 Saudi plan for Gaza
the-dublin-compensation.summary: A proposal John Kiriakou says he watched Ambassador Chas Freeman float to the Saudis during his first overseas tour in 1991 — that Saudi Arabia fund a port, an airport, a desalination plant and an electrical grid in Gaza. The Saudis agreed; Israel refused outright. Kiriakou raises it because the identical arrangement resurfaced in the Israeli press more than three decades later.

the-dublin-compensation.title: Clive Stafford Smith
the-dublin-compensation.summary: The British human rights lawyer who represents Aafia Siddiqui, described by John Kiriakou as a man who has never charged a client a dollar in his life, lives on donations, holds an OBE for his human rights work, and represented sixty-six Guantanamo detainees — securing the release of every one of them.

the-dublin-compensation.title: Hamid Karzai
the-dublin-compensation.summary: The president installed in Afghanistan after the American invasion, whom John Kiriakou uses as the standing illustration of what occupation actually buys: after twenty years and more than a trillion dollars, Karzai was ''little more than the mayor of Kabul'' — and did not control all of Kabul either. The line began as a joke among Senate Foreign Relations Committee staff, and Kiriakou used it to Senator John Kerry''s face ten years into the war.

the-dublin-compensation.title: Corkscrew landings in Afghanistan
the-dublin-compensation.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the tight spiralling helicopter approaches used to evade rocket and Stinger fire on landings in Afghanistan after 9/11, with the side doors open, and of the passengers around him being sick while he found it exhilarating.

the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.title: A Turkey–Israel confrontation
the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of what two senior Turkish foreign ministry officials told him over dinner in March 2026 about the prospect of war with Israel: that it will not happen, that Turkey would win if it did, and that Turkey would not ask NATO for help.

the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.title: 2026 Iran war
the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.title: Arming the crazies
the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the American habit of arming the most radical faction available — the Mujahideen over any other Afghan force, the White Russians over the Red — and his expectation, stated days into the 2026 war, that the United States and Israel would begin arming factions inside Iran and that the factions chosen would be the radical ones.

the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.title: Closing the Gulf embassies
the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.summary: John Kiriakou''s reading of the American decision, announced live on air on 3 March 2026, to close its embassies in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait: that in the whole of the first Gulf War no American embassy was closed except Kuwait''s own, whose diplomats were taken to Iraq as human shields, and that shutting two at once meant Washington had concluded the war was about to get very much worse.

the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.title: The referee in a Greek-Turkish war
the-east-mediterranean-gas-partnership.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment, given in Athens in 2025, that Greece cannot count on the United States taking its side against Turkey — Washington would position itself as an honest broker between the two — but that NATO support, particularly from Italy, France, Germany and Britain, would make Greece able to cope even without American leadership.

the-egyptian-berm.title: Famine in Gaza
the-egyptian-berm.summary: The starvation of the civilian population of the Gaza Strip, which John Kiriakou describes as a United Nations-declared famine caused not by an absence of food but by an Israeli refusal to let food reach the people who need it; Kiriakou characterises it as a war crime, a crime against humanity and a form of genocide, attributing that characterisation to the United Nations and the International Court of Justice rather than to himself.

the-egyptian-berm.title: Proposals to relocate the Palestinians
the-egyptian-berm.summary: John Kiriakou's account of recurring schemes to solve the Palestinian question by moving the population somewhere else — including a 1980s proposal to rename a barren diamond of land on the Saudi–Iraqi border "Palestine" and resettle everyone there — and his verdict that picking up an entire people and moving them is unprecedented and untenable.

the-egyptian-berm.title: France recognises Palestine
the-egyptian-berm.summary: Emmanuel Macron's decision in July 2025 to extend formal recognition to the Republic of Palestine and exchange ambassadors, which John Kiriakou called a turning point that could not be overstated — the first serious crack in Western support for Israel, and significant precisely because France is a historic colonial power in the Middle East with a Security Council veto.

the-egyptian-berm.title: Hostages and prisoners
the-egyptian-berm.summary: John Kiriakou's objection to the vocabulary of the Gaza war — that Israelis held by Hamas are called hostages while Palestinians held by Israel without charge are called prisoners — which he treats as one instance of a wider pattern in which allies have governments and adversaries have regimes.

the-egyptian-berm.title: The burden of peace
the-egyptian-berm.summary: John Kiriakou's rule for asymmetric wars — that in any lopsided military conflict most of the burden of making peace falls on the superior military force, which will have to make most of the concessions — together with his rejection of unconditional surrender as a war aim.

the-egyptian-berm.title: No band-aids since the early nineties
the-egyptian-berm.summary: What doctors told John Kiriakou when he visited an Afghan hospital in 2000, during the first Taliban government — that they had not seen a band-aid since the early 1990s — and his conclusion that the humanitarian carve-outs in the Clinton-era sanctions did not exist in practice.

the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.title: Jesse Jackson
the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.summary: American civil rights leader and two-time presidential candidate whose hospitalisation in November 2025 John Kiriakou discussed at length — explaining progressive supranuclear palsy, the condition Jackson was diagnosed with two years after Parkinson''s, from his own family''s experience of the same disease, and giving a poor prognosis.

the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.title: Kiriakou's acting career
the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.summary: The film role John Kiriakou took in 2025 after Tyrel Ventura wrote a part for him — a former CIA officer running a billionaire's security detail — which he shot in Mexico for a month and which made him, at sixty-odd, a member of the Screen Actors Guild.

the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.title: The conscientious objectors book
the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.summary: A long out-of-print volume of interviews with American conscientious objectors, published around 1972 and given to John Kiriakou from the personal collection of an objector he was friendly with in prison — a book whose harrowing accounts of objectors sent to real federal prisons rather than to camps convinced him that refusing to serve was often more physically dangerous than serving.

the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.title: The Giuliani–Epstein emails
the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.summary: A cache of correspondence that a former chief of business development for Giuliani Partners told John Kiriakou she holds — thousands of pages of emails between Rudy Giuliani and Jeffrey Epstein, which she says she has offered to news organisations and to congressional committees and which nobody wanted, together with her claim that a second British prince and other former heads of state are implicated.

the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.title: The mob vote for Trump
the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to a viewer asking whether he discussed politics with organised crime figures in prison: that he did, a great deal, that they love Donald Trump without qualification, and that the reason is a New York real estate developer''s unavoidable daily contact with the unions the mob controls.

the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.title: The Outer Banks seasonal workers
the-egyptian-intelligence-chiefs-son.summary: John Kiriakou''s observation, from years of family summers on the Outer Banks of North Carolina, that he never encountered an American lifeguard and almost no American shop clerks or waiters — the staff being Bulgarian, Romanian, Moldovan and otherwise Eastern European, working on the cheap, housed eight to twelve to a house and sent home at the end of the season.

the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.title: Counterterrorist driving
the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.summary: The vehicle training at the Farm — the PIT manoeuvre and how to avoid one, when to ram a roadblock and where to hit it, reversing at sixty miles an hour — conducted in a fleet of junkyard beaters the CIA bought expressly to be wrecked.

the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.title: The shooting house
the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.summary: The live-fire decision course at the Farm where a trainee has about three quarters of a second to decide whether the figure at the window is a gunman or a woman holding a baby — and where John Kiriakou says he never missed, which he connects to his own account of the temperament the CIA selects for.

the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.title: How Kiriakou went armed in Athens
the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.summary: The load John Kiriakou carried every day during his Athens tour — a 9mm in a tear-away waist pack with three magazines, a snub-nosed .38 on his ankle, about 47 rounds in total, and a buck knife his boss handed him on his first day *"just in case things go to shit"*.

the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.title: The bomb course
the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.summary: The week-long CIA explosives course at a facility in another state, where John Kiriakou learned to build a Molotov cocktail, then a detonator rig, then an ammonium nitrate bomb — his final exam, which put a van's transmission three hundred yards into the woods.

the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.title: The Farm
the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.summary: The CIA's clandestine training facility in Virginia; site of approximately 80% of all CIA operational training

the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.title: Trading informants to El Salvador
the-el-salvador-hotel-drill.summary: John Kiriakou's reaction to reports that the secretary of state had agreed to hand over American informants in El Salvador in exchange for the use of Salvadoran prisons — that it is, in plain terms, a death sentence, and that the surprise is not that people will stop cooperating but that they never seem to.

the-election-day-1992-poll.title: Quoted on NPR
the-election-day-1992-poll.summary: John Kiriakou's discovery, via a standing Google alert on his own name, that National Public Radio had cited a DeProgram discussion between him and Ted Rall in an article on Palestinians killed while waiting for food — an outlet he had walked out on years earlier.

the-election-day-1992-poll.title: The Addis Ababa zoo
the-election-day-1992-poll.summary: A visit John Kiriakou made to the zoo in Addis Ababa on a free half-day, where he watched keepers force a screaming donkey into the lion enclosure — and noted the two-tier admission price charged to foreigners.

the-election-day-1992-poll.title: The boring cover story
the-election-day-1992-poll.summary: The CIA training principle John Kiriakou says governed how officers described their jobs to strangers: pick something so dull that nobody asks a second question. His own standard answer was the foreign service, training work, and some import-export negotiation.

the-election-day-1992-poll.title: The ex-prisoner at the Bureau of Prisons
the-election-day-1992-poll.summary: John Kiriakou's approving account of the appointment of a former federal prisoner — recently released after five years on a drug conspiracy charge — as deputy director of the Bureau of Prisons, which he calls an inspired choice and one of the few things he has praised Donald Trump for.

the-election-day-1992-poll.title: The fifteen-dollar maintenance fee
the-election-day-1992-poll.summary: An appointment John Kiriakou made at his bank on the morning of a broadcast to ask for the return of a $15 monthly maintenance fee that had taken his account to minus fifteen dollars — a story he told on air as a plain statement of what his finances looked like after prison.

the-election-day-1992-poll.title: The Hannity Lockerbie exchange
the-election-day-1992-poll.summary: A televised argument in which John Kiriakou says he embarrassed Sean Hannity by pointing out that the 1986 American bombing that killed Muammar Gaddafi's daughter came three years before the Lockerbie bombing, and so could not have been revenge for it.

the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.title: Evidence of previous heroism
the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.summary: A phrase John Kiriakou attributes to Judge Leonie Brinkema at his 2013 sentencing. When his service in Pakistan and his role in the capture of Abu Zubaydah were raised in mitigation, the judge ruled — in what Kiriakou gives as her exact words — that any evidence of previous heroism is irrelevant.

the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.title: Federal plea coercion
the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that the federal justice system coerces guilty pleas by stacking charges and winning 98.2% of its cases — so that even innocent defendants take deals, as he did, told by his own attorney that the system is 'not about justice; it's about mitigating damage.'

the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.title: From the Alien and Sedition Acts to the Espionage Act
the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.summary: A lineage John Kiriakou endorsed on the In Limine podcast: that language was lifted from the Alien and Sedition Acts into the Espionage Act of 1917 during the anti-radical hysteria of that period, making a straight line from the earliest American political prosecutions to the statute used against modern whistleblowers.

the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.title: Plato Cacheris
the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.summary: Legendary Washington, D.C. defense attorney who served as John Kiriakou''s lead counsel in his 2012–2013 Espionage Act prosecution. Per Kiriakou, when discovery revealed the FBI had run a fake-diplomat sting against him, Cacheris explained the government''s posture bluntly: ''Because they have a shit case and they know it''s shit, and that''s why we''re going to trial.'' He spent most of the case urging trial, then drove to Kiriakou''s house on decision day and said ''You stupid son of a bitch — take the deal.'' Cacheris also represented FBI spy Robert Hanssen.

the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.title: The plea-hearing objection
the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.summary: John Kiriakou's account of standing up at his own plea hearing, over his lawyer's objection, to tell the judge that the statement of facts the prosecutors had written into his plea agreement was untrue — and of her reply that it was just window dressing.

the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.title: Kermit Roosevelt and Mosaddegh
the-eleven-c-one-c-plea.summary: The CIA officer John Kiriakou names as the man who ran the 1953 overthrow of Iran's Prime Minister Mosaddegh on behalf of British Petroleum — who called it the gravest mistake of his life in the only interview he ever gave, and who, according to the documents Kiriakou has since read in the archives, did not actually run it at all.

the-embassy-local-hire.title: Mexico City as an espionage hub
the-embassy-local-hire.summary: John Kiriakou''s assessment of Mexico City as one of the world''s principal centres of international espionage, alongside Vienna, London, Paris and Washington — driven by a gargantuan American embassy that Russian services target from next door — and his reading of why Mexico simply ignored a dossier of suspected Russian officers handed over by the Biden administration.

the-embassy-local-hire.title: Lindsey Graham
the-embassy-local-hire.summary: Republican senator from South Carolina who died in July 2026, and John Kiriakou's standing shorthand for the permanent war caucus — a "show horse" rather than a workhorse, a "chameleon" who "never saw a war that he didn't want to jump into with both feet," and, on posthumously released documentary footage, a man offering the US Air Force to bomb a country America was not at war with.

the-embassy-local-hire.title: Pakistani prisons
the-embassy-local-hire.summary: John Kiriakou''s flat refusal, in a discussion of Imran Khan''s detention, of the idea that a Pakistani prison offers VIP treatment to a former prime minister — grounded in his having visited many of them himself during the period when the CIA was locking people up there.

the-embassy-local-hire.title: Savas Kalenderidis
the-embassy-local-hire.summary: Greek intelligence officer, national hero and personal friend of John Kiriakou''s, who was involved in the operation to protect the PKK founder Abdullah Öcalan at the Greek embassy in Nairobi in 1999 — an operation that ended when Turkish and Kenyan intelligence diverted part of Öcalan''s motorcade and seized him. Kiriakou flatly denies the claim that the CIA and Turkish intelligence tried to kill Kalenderidis there.

the-embassy-local-hire.title: The Afghan Zero Units
the-embassy-local-hire.summary: The CIA-trained Afghan paramilitary units whose surviving members were resettled in the United States, and John Kiriakou''s account of why so many of them have broken down: recruited without training or therapy, taken out at night to kill their own tribesmen and extended family, promised the land of milk and honey, and then met on arrival with no work permit, no treatment and no help at all.

the-embassy-local-hire.title: The C-130 resettlements
the-embassy-local-hire.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that the Hmong communities of Minnesota were former CIA assets brought to the United States as refugees, and his extension of a rule Ted Rall proposed — that refugee populations end up wherever the aircraft carrying them happened to land — to the Kurds of Bismarck, North Dakota and St Louis.

the-embassy-swap.title: The bug in the bedroom
