the-embassy-swap.summary: The listening device John Kiriakou says fell out of an air conditioning vent onto his bare chest while he read in bed in Bahrain — planted, his chief told him, because he was writing the embassy's human rights report.

the-embassy-swap.title: Ian Henderson
the-embassy-swap.summary: The British colonial police officer who ran Bahrain's intelligence service during John Kiriakou's posting there — a man Kiriakou says even the heir presumptive to the throne was afraid to name aloud, and whom Kiriakou, seated at the crown prince's table at a dinner for George H. W. Bush, mistook for a corpse.

the-embassy-swap.title: The Russian soldier in Manama
the-embassy-swap.summary: The Russian soldier John Kiriakou says he met in Manama, Bahrain, who told him the Chechens were the only people on earth he was afraid of — a remark Kiriakou produced in a conversation about Chechnya's standing as a fighting nation.

the-embassy-swap.title: Amnesty International
the-embassy-swap.summary: The human rights organization whose torture report forms part of John Kiriakou's core defense — the CIA's crimes were already public knowledge before he confirmed them on ABC, and the Justice Department's own declination letter said so — and the organization whose silence during his prosecution he cannot forgive. He begged Amnesty for a one-sentence statement and got a New Yorker subscription instead; it took Ai Weiwei to change their minds, and by then he was walking out of prison.

the-embassy-swap.title: Bigger than the Russian embassy
the-embassy-swap.summary: Why American embassies in small, strategically unimportant countries are enormous: the answer John Kiriakou says he was given by a station chief on one of his first CIA trips — that the building had to be bigger than the Soviet one across town. He describes American embassies in Africa as "absolutely gigantic" for that reason alone, and calls the US embassy in Cairo an enormous facility matched by an equally enormous Russian one.

the-embassy-swap.title: I want my fifty bucks back
the-embassy-swap.summary: What John Kiriakou says he shouted at John Fetterman from ten rows back at an Ohio State football game — and his explanation, as a Pennsylvanian furious about the senator, of why Fetterman keeps his seat anyway.

the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.title: The Rashid family
the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.summary: The dynasty that controlled the Arabian peninsula before the House of Saud, and John Kiriakou''s account of meeting one of its descendants while stationed in Saudi Arabia — a man who told him the kingdom had once been theirs.

the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.title: The Saudi-administered Gaza proposal
the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.summary: An arrangement reported in the Israeli left-wing press and repeated by John Kiriakou as a possible basis for future talks: a disarmed, semi-independent Gaza policed and rebuilt by Saudi Arabia, with a port, an airport, a power grid and a sewage system.

the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.title: The Penn State textbooks
the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.summary: How a week-long high-school scholarship to Penn State sent the teenage John Kiriakou into the university bookstore to buy the textbooks for Middle East courses he was not enrolled in — the purchase he credits with turning a childhood fascination into a field of study.

the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.title: Bill Clinton
the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.summary: 42nd U.S. president whom John Kiriakou describes as wholly disinterested in intelligence — briefed by the CIA only twice in eight years, with Vice President Al Gore taking the daily briefing instead and relaying anything important.

the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.title: Church Committee
the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.summary: U.S. Senate investigative committee operating in 1975–1976 that examined domestic intelligence abuses by the CIA, FBI, and NSA; per John Kiriakou, the Church Committee — alongside the concurrent Pike Committee in the House — was the last genuine moment of legislative oversight over the intelligence community, born of a national consensus that government had gone dangerously off course. Its work led to the creation of the permanent Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, which Kiriakou says ceased to function as real oversight roughly seven years after its founding.

the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.title: Fifty new crimes a year
the-emir-of-bahrains-verdict.summary: John Kiriakou''s argument that the United States has become a carceral country by legislative accretion — fifty newly created federal crimes every year for two decades, on top of five per cent of the world''s population holding twenty-five per cent of its prisoners.

the-empire-on-the-ropes.title: 2026 Iran war economic shock
the-empire-on-the-ropes.summary: John Kiriakou''s running assessment of the economic damage from the 2026 Iran war — an oil shock he says already exceeds both 1970s shocks combined, a natural-gas shock worse than the Nord Stream destruction, and a chokepoint problem that runs through fertilizer as much as fuel, since 65% of the world''s supply must transit the Strait of Hormuz. His summary: "This is an economic slowdown of choice."

the-empire-on-the-ropes.title: Advice to an aspiring intelligence analyst
the-empire-on-the-ropes.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to a 21-year-old student asking what to study and what to read: pick a geographic area, become the go-to person on it, and consume everything published in the field — including the journals written by people who have never made policy.

the-empire-on-the-ropes.title: Air wars are overrated
the-empire-on-the-ropes.summary: John Kiriakou''s summary judgement on the 2026 Iran and Lebanon campaigns, delivered as the meta-headline of the whole war: air power flattened Gaza without destroying Hamas, is bogging down against Hezbollah, and cannot produce the outcome the war requires.

the-empire-on-the-ropes.title: Asian fuel reserves, 2026
the-empire-on-the-ropes.summary: The effect of the Strait of Hormuz closure on oil-importing Asian economies as John Kiriakou described it — countries counting their remaining fuel in days rather than months, with no substitute supply available, and economies he expects simply to stop.

the-empire-on-the-ropes.title: The CIA Insider's Guide to Surveillance and Surveillance Detection
the-empire-on-the-ropes.summary: Book by John Kiriakou drawing on his experience as a surveillance detection instructor at the CIA and as a private surveillance training consultant. The book covers the techniques used by intelligence professionals to identify whether they are being followed — including the four-phase surveillance detection route, concealment device placement and retrieval, and counter-surveillance strategy — adapted for use by corporate executives, journalists, and others who want to confirm whether they are being followed.

the-empire-on-the-ropes.title: Donald Trump
the-empire-on-the-ropes.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.title: Bahrain's force majeure
the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of Bahrain declaring force majeure on its energy commitments during the 2026 Iran war — why it is catastrophic for Bahrain and irrelevant to the global oil market, since the kingdom produces and consumes about a hundred thousand barrels a day and sells only the output of a small offshore field gifted to it by Saudi Arabia.

the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.title: Mojtaba Khamenei
the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.summary: The successor named as Iran's leader after the assassination of Ali Khamenei, and John Kiriakou's reading of the choice — that the only real objection is the shared surname, which exposes Iran to charges of hereditary succession, but that the appointment was an act of defiance aimed squarely at Donald Trump's declaration that he would choose Iran's next leader.

the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.title: The Iranians only have to survive
the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.summary: John Kiriakou's formulation of the asymmetry at the heart of the 2026 Iran war — that winning would require the United States to overthrow the Iranian government and install a pro-American, pro-Israeli replacement in Tehran, while Iran wins simply by continuing to exist. His conclusion is that Washington must either commit to killing half the population of Iran over twenty years or walk away.

the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.title: 2026 Iran war
the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.title: The Greek Orthodox Church
the-empty-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.summary: The church John Kiriakou was raised in and still belongs to — the institution behind his Greek fluency and his family''s immigrant history, a recurring thread in his accounts of Athens, Damascus, Bethlehem and Washington, and, in two cases, an actor in his own story: the church the FBI followed him into, and the priest who tried to get him a pardon.

the-epstein-birthday-book.title: The Bloomingdale precedent
the-epstein-birthday-book.summary: The scandal from Ronald Reagan's kitchen cabinet that John Kiriakou holds up as the model Donald Trump should have followed over Jeffrey Epstein — when Reagan's advisers nearly denied the friendship, were talked out of it because the denial would become the story, and issued a statement embracing it instead.

the-epstein-birthday-book.title: E. Jean Carroll
the-epstein-birthday-book.summary: The plaintiff whose persistence John Kiriakou singled out for deep respect — she kept suing after the political tide turned against her, and won an award he put at eighty-three or eighty-five million dollars on a day when Donald Trump won almost everything else in the federal courts.

the-epstein-birthday-book.title: Astrology at the CIA
the-epstein-birthday-book.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that astrology played a role in CIA work in the 1950s and early 1960s as part of MK-ULTRA, alongside time travel and teleportation — and his explanation for why: officials with unlimited budgets and no obligation to report to the public reasoned that there was probably nothing to it, but that if there were, it would make them a star.

the-epstein-birthday-book.title: Carrying passports in Washington
the-epstein-birthday-book.summary: John Kiriakou's report in September 2025 that people in Washington had begun carrying their passports for fear of being scooped up by immigration enforcement — alongside the case of an American symphony violinist held for three weeks, and his own belief that ethnic profiling violates the Fourth Amendment.

the-epstein-birthday-book.title: "Christians are suckers"
the-epstein-birthday-book.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for how a president who does not go to church, has no spiritual adviser and could not name a line of scripture can push school prayer without cost — that he thinks most Christians are suckers, an assessment Kiriakou says he hates to make and believes anyway.

the-epstein-birthday-book.title: Find a Grave
the-epstein-birthday-book.summary: The cemetery database John Kiriakou calls literally his favourite website on the internet, which he opens during the ten-minute countdown before broadcasts and uses to decide who goes into his cemetery books — and which supplied him the story of Greta Zimmer Friedman.

the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.title: Prince Andrew
the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.summary: British royal, now Andrew Mountbatten Windsor, named repeatedly by John Kiriakou as one of the un-recruitable principals whose access made Jeffrey Epstein valuable to a foreign intelligence service. Kiriakou has asked why Andrew was never charged over conduct with minors, reads his alleged provision of classified Ministry of Defence documents to Epstein as evidence of espionage rather than vanity — and expects him to face no criminal consequence at all, because the statute of limitations has run.

the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.title: The anti-semite smear
the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the professional cost of saying publicly that Israel spies on the United States: Alan Dershowitz calls him names, and the political director of the Israeli foreign minister called him a noted anti-semite.

the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.title: The Epstein statute of limitations
the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that nobody in the United States will be prosecuted over the Jeffrey Epstein case because the limitation period on the sex offences has run — a lapse he says may itself have been part of the plan, which leaves victims with civil suits against the estate, leaves the men named to social ruin rather than trial, and leaves only an improbable continuing-conspiracy theory as a route to criminal charges.

the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.title: Running into former sources
the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.summary: John Kiriakou has twice met people he once ran as agents by accident, years after leaving the CIA — once at an airport and once in the street — and both times they came to him with a bear hug. One of them was astonished to discover he spoke English.

the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.title: Sources are not traitors
the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.summary: Asked whether CIA officers privately regarded their recruited agents as traitors and held them in contempt, John Kiriakou answered that they did not — because the officers believed they were the good guys, and a recruited source had become one of them.

the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.title: The density of spies in Washington
the-epstein-files-and-the-starmer-govern.summary: John Kiriakou's claim that there are more spies in Washington DC than anywhere else in the world, that the FBI's counterintelligence division does nothing but try to root them out, and that the job cannot be finished short of becoming North Korea.

the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.title: The Saudi demand for a political appointee
the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.summary: John Kiriakou's account of a standing Saudi condition on the American embassy in Riyadh — that the ambassador must never be a career diplomat, the opposite of what most countries want, because Riyadh wants someone whose telephone call the president of the United States will take.

the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.title: Zohran Mamdani
the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of the New York mayoral candidate in September 2025 — a smart young man running a very good campaign, surrounding himself with older seasoned New Yorkers rather than going in like a bull in a china shop, and gaining rather than losing ground the more the establishment attacked him.

the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.title: Saudi Arabia as an open-air prison
the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.summary: John Kiriakou's verdict on the country he served in — 'the biggest open air prison in the world' — together with his account of what the ambassador's life there is like inside the residence and outside it, the two ambassadors he served under, and the annual migration of the entire Saudi government to Jeddah to escape the heat.

the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.title: The kafala sponsorship system
the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.summary: The Saudi sponsorship regime as John Kiriakou describes it — a Saudi national must own the majority of any company a foreigner works for, that sponsor holds the worker's passport, and a falling-out leaves the worker under effective house arrest, which he says is how South Asian women brought in as domestics are kept as sex slaves.

the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.title: The 1991 Saudi plan for Gaza
the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.summary: A proposal John Kiriakou says he watched Ambassador Chas Freeman float to the Saudis during his first overseas tour in 1991 — that Saudi Arabia fund a port, an airport, a desalination plant and an electrical grid in Gaza. The Saudis agreed; Israel refused outright. Kiriakou raises it because the identical arrangement resurfaced in the Israeli press more than three decades later.

the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.title: Aafia Siddiqui
the-eric-adams-ambassadorship.summary: Pakistani-American neuroscientist arrested in Afghanistan and convicted in the United States of attempting to shoot FBI agents; per John Kiriakou, who covered the arrest as a terrorism consultant for ABC News and has followed the case since, she never had a gun and never fired, the bullet holes offered as proof predated her capture, and the CIA took her three children — two later recovered, the youngest never found.

the-eritrea-prohibition.title: Djibouti
the-eritrea-prohibition.summary: The small Horn of Africa state a few miles across the water from Yemen that hosts Camp Lemonnier — the American drone base for the Yemen and Somalia wars, inherited from the departing French, and shared with China's only overseas military base behind a fence down the middle, in what John Kiriakou calls the worst kept secret in the world.

the-eritrea-prohibition.title: The Bab el-Mandeb
the-eritrea-prohibition.summary: The strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa through which everything leaving the Suez Canal must pass — narrower than the Strait of Hormuz, in John Kiriakou's account the one genuine American national interest in Yemen, and the reason Israel has offered diplomatic recognition to Somaliland in exchange for a military base.

the-eritrea-prohibition.title: Kiriakou's Cuba trip
the-eritrea-prohibition.summary: John Kiriakou's account of his first visit to Cuba, where his books sit in the national library and officials treated him warmly — and a Cuban vice president told him every U.S. president is 'the same,' blaming Cuba while it cannot keep the lights on. He was invited as a guest of the Havana international book fair after his first two books were translated into Spanish, and later wrote about how the U.S. embargo shapes daily life there, from a dengue-fever hospital bill he had to pay in euros to a diet dominated by squash.

the-eritrea-prohibition.title: Kiriakou on travel
the-eritrea-prohibition.summary: John Kiriakou''s own ranking of the countries he has visited: Greece his favourite and, he insists, the best food anywhere; Oman the most beautiful landscape; Syria the most extraordinary civilisation; and Chile the cheapest, illustrated by a bottle of a vineyard''s locked-away reserve that cost $8.50 on his honeymoon.

the-eritrea-prohibition.title: China's base in Djibouti
the-eritrea-prohibition.summary: Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti, the abandoned French base the Djiboutians offered to the Americans and the Chinese took a share of — split down the middle by a chain-link fence, the only Chinese military installation outside China, and the centrepiece of John Kiriakou's argument that China is not an expansionist power.

the-eritrea-prohibition.title: A virtual state of war with Venezuela
the-eritrea-prohibition.summary: John Kiriakou said in February 2025 that he was mystified by the choice of Marco Rubio as Secretary of State, describing him as a neoconservative in the mould of George W. Bush, and predicted that on Venezuela the second Trump administration would simply continue the Biden policy — which had itself continued the first Trump policy — leaving the two countries in what he called a virtual state of war.

the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.title: Lindsey Graham
the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.summary: Republican senator from South Carolina who died in July 2026, and John Kiriakou's standing shorthand for the permanent war caucus — a "show horse" rather than a workhorse, a "chameleon" who "never saw a war that he didn't want to jump into with both feet," and, on posthumously released documentary footage, a man offering the US Air Force to bomb a country America was not at war with.

the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.title: 2026 Iran war
the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.title: Embassy movie night
the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.summary: The weekly diversion John Kiriakou remembers from his posting to Pakistan after September 11th, when the station worked seven days a week and fourteen hours a day: on Wednesday nights the ambassador hosted a film in the embassy''s small theatre, and the audience shouted at the screen and threw popcorn at whatever they had managed to get hold of.

the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.title: Espionage Act
the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.title: The Graham Senate succession
the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.summary: John Kiriakou's comment on the appointment of Lindsey Graham's sister to serve out the remainder of his Senate term, and her announcement that she would run for a full term of her own — a candidacy whose only qualification, in Kiriakou's assessment, is her relation to the late senator.

the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.title: The McConnell obituary
the-espionage-act-and-the-rosenbergs.summary: A Kentucky newspaper's decision, reported by John Kiriakou in July 2026, to run an obituary of the living Senator Mitch McConnell on purpose — a response, in Kiriakou's reading, to the rapid rehabilitation of Lindsey Graham after his death, and an attempt to get the assessment on the record before the whitewashing could begin.

the-eu-whistleblower-directive.title: Blueprint for Free Speech
the-eu-whistleblower-directive.summary: The Australian non-governmental organisation that drafts whistleblower protection legislation and markets it to governments around the world, and which hired John Kiriakou in 2015 to help write Greece's law. Its board is mostly academics and transparency activists; Kiriakou credits it with successes in Canada, Zambia, Jamaica and Ukraine, and names its founder and director as Suelette Dreyfus, whom he describes as a co-founder of WikiLeaks with Julian Assange.

the-eu-whistleblower-directive.title: Kiriakou Greek whistleblower law
the-eu-whistleblower-directive.summary: A whistleblower protection law John Kiriakou says he was hired by the Greek government to write in 2015, at the invitation of Greece, after which it was passed by both the European Parliament and the Greek Parliament and became law across the European Union. Per Kiriakou, the law's first courtroom use involved a whistleblower who exposed Greece's defense minister for taking bribes from Siemens; the resulting press coverage led a consortium of Greece's four wealthiest families to ask Kiriakou to run a private equity fund for them.

the-eu-whistleblower-directive.title: Eastern District of Virginia
the-eu-whistleblower-directive.summary: The U.S. federal district covering northern Virginia — home to Langley, the Pentagon, DHS and much of the intelligence-contractor industry — which John Kiriakou calls 'the espionage court' because the Justice Department files the great majority of its national security prosecutions there and because, in his telling, no national-security defendant has ever won a case in it; Kiriakou, Julian Assange, Edward Snowden and Jeffrey Sterling were all charged there.

the-eu-whistleblower-directive.title: The solitary confinement precedents
the-eu-whistleblower-directive.summary: The legal argument John Kiriakou made repeatedly between 2020 and 2022 in defence of Julian Assange, and revived in 2025 for the Australian pilot Daniel Duggan — that no extradition to the United States can succeed once a court is asked to find that American solitary confinement is not torture, a proposition already contradicted by the United Nations, by the United States' own federal torture statute, and by a line of British and European rulings blocking extraditions on exactly that ground.

the-eu-whistleblower-directive.title: Bernie Sanders
the-eu-whistleblower-directive.summary: United States senator from Vermont. John Kiriakou, who watched him daily from the Senate Foreign Relations Committee staff, describes Sanders holding open breakfast in the Senate cafeteria for anyone who walked in — insisting only that they call him "Bernie" — and names him the one 2016 candidate willing to talk about shrinking the military.

the-eu-whistleblower-directive.title: Bill Barr
the-eu-whistleblower-directive.summary: Per Sean Davis, speaking on the same Megyn Kelly panel as Kiriakou, the attorney general under the first Trump administration, seen as competent but not fully loyal, whose relationship with Trump ended in a "breakup."

the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.title: Bureau of Prisons advisory board
the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.summary: The advisory board John Kiriakou joined at the personal invitation of the Director of the Bureau of Prisons, who told him the president had tasked him with tearing the Bureau down and rebuilding it.

the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.title: Quoted on NPR
the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.summary: John Kiriakou's discovery, via a standing Google alert on his own name, that National Public Radio had cited a DeProgram discussion between him and Ted Rall in an article on Palestinians killed while waiting for food — an outlet he had walked out on years earlier.

the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.title: The Addis Ababa zoo
the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.summary: A visit John Kiriakou made to the zoo in Addis Ababa on a free half-day, where he watched keepers force a screaming donkey into the lion enclosure — and noted the two-tier admission price charged to foreigners.

the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.title: The boring cover story
the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.summary: The CIA training principle John Kiriakou says governed how officers described their jobs to strangers: pick something so dull that nobody asks a second question. His own standard answer was the foreign service, training work, and some import-export negotiation.

the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.title: The election day 1992 poll
the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.summary: An informal show of hands taken in a CIA branch office on election day 1992, which John Kiriakou describes as the moment he discovered he had no idea of the politics of the colleagues he sat three feet away from — and that he was not, as he had assumed, the only progressive in the room.

the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.title: The fifteen-dollar maintenance fee
the-ex-prisoner-at-the-bureau-of-prisons.summary: An appointment John Kiriakou made at his bank on the morning of a broadcast to ask for the return of a $15 monthly maintenance fee that had taken his account to minus fifteen dollars — a story he told on air as a plain statement of what his finances looked like after prison.

the-f-35-shootdown.title: Air wars are overrated
the-f-35-shootdown.summary: John Kiriakou''s summary judgement on the 2026 Iran and Lebanon campaigns, delivered as the meta-headline of the whole war: air power flattened Gaza without destroying Hamas, is bogging down against Hezbollah, and cannot produce the outcome the war requires.

the-f-35-shootdown.title: F-35 avionics dispute with Israel
the-f-35-shootdown.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how Israel demanded F-35 fighters without the deliberately degraded avionics the U.S. installs on export models — and, refused, allegedly worked through American defense contractors to steal the technology instead.

the-f-35-shootdown.title: Hamas
the-f-35-shootdown.summary: The Palestinian movement behind the October 7, 2023 attack; John Kiriakou argues that a case could be made for calling it a freedom-fighting organization dedicated to the liberation of its people rather than simply a terrorist group, notes it is labeled a terrorist organization by only a small minority of UN member states, and has ruled Gaza since Israel's 2005 withdrawal.

the-f-35-shootdown.title: The house of cards theory
the-f-35-shootdown.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the strategic premise behind the 2026 Iran war — that decapitating the Iranian government would bring the whole state down — and of why it fails. To win, he argues, the United States would have to destroy the entire Iranian government and military and install a puppet; Iran wins simply by surviving.

the-f-35-shootdown.title: 2026 Iran war economic shock
the-f-35-shootdown.summary: John Kiriakou''s running assessment of the economic damage from the 2026 Iran war — an oil shock he says already exceeds both 1970s shocks combined, a natural-gas shock worse than the Nord Stream destruction, and a chokepoint problem that runs through fertilizer as much as fuel, since 65% of the world''s supply must transit the Strait of Hormuz. His summary: "This is an economic slowdown of choice."

the-f-35-shootdown.title: Advice to an aspiring intelligence analyst
the-f-35-shootdown.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to a 21-year-old student asking what to study and what to read: pick a geographic area, become the go-to person on it, and consume everything published in the field — including the journals written by people who have never made policy.

the-faisalabad-cash-run.title: Security, finance and medical
the-faisalabad-cash-run.summary: The rule John Kiriakou says CIA recruits were taught in their first week on the job — that there are exactly three offices an officer may never lie to, because those three can end a career — and the reasoning he attaches to each.

the-faisalabad-cash-run.title: Arabic and Greek
the-faisalabad-cash-run.summary: The qualification John Kiriakou says opened the door to his transfer from CIA analysis to operations: a post in Athens wanted Greek or Arabic, and he had both — by most of his tellings the only officer in the agency who did. The chief who hired him gave the reason in one sentence: it is easier and cheaper to take a linguist and teach him operations than the other way round. The pairing also became a detection tool, since the language nobody speaks in Pakistan is Arabic.

the-faisalabad-cash-run.title: Bankruptcy and the dropped charges
the-faisalabad-cash-run.summary: The sequence John Kiriakou places at the centre of his case: that the espionage counts against him were dropped only after his legal fees had bankrupted him, which he presents as evidence that the government''s aim was attrition rather than conviction.

the-faisalabad-cash-run.title: Curtailment cables
the-faisalabad-cash-run.summary: The career-ending requests John Kiriakou says he read coming back from the CIA's black sites — officers, doctors, psychologists and nurses asking to end their tours early rather than continue to take part in the interrogation programme — and his conclusion that if that many people were objecting in classified channels, someone would surely go public.

the-faisalabad-cash-run.title: The bowl of dates
the-faisalabad-cash-run.summary: The detail John Kiriakou uses to compress his argument about interrogation: that the intelligence the CIA''s contractors reported as the fruit of waterboarding had in fact been obtained by an FBI agent who offered Abu Zubaydah a bowl of dates.

the-faisalabad-cash-run.title: The hooding dispute
the-faisalabad-cash-run.summary: The argument John Kiriakou says he had with a subordinate at a CIA safe house in Pakistan on the night of the Abu Zubaydah raid, over hoods placed on captured prisoners; both men reported each other to headquarters, and Kiriakou was the one reprimanded.

the-false-volunteer.title: Surveillance detection route
the-false-volunteer.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

the-false-volunteer.title: Abu Zubaydah
the-false-volunteer.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

the-false-volunteer.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
the-false-volunteer.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

the-false-volunteer.title: Bureau of Prisons advisory board
the-false-volunteer.summary: The advisory board John Kiriakou joined at the personal invitation of the Director of the Bureau of Prisons, who told him the president had tasked him with tearing the Bureau down and rebuilding it.

the-false-volunteer.title: The Green Line in Nicosia
the-false-volunteer.summary: The division of Nicosia between the Republic of Cyprus and the Turkish-occupied north, which John Kiriakou toured in July 2026 and described as maintained through deliberate humiliation rather than any interest in settlement.

the-false-volunteer.title: Edward Snowden
the-false-volunteer.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

the-families-of-the-captured.title: Prisoner disposition from Pakistan
the-families-of-the-captured.summary: How captured prisoners were routed out of Pakistan in John Kiriakou's account — cooperation recorded in his reporting, headquarters consulted by telephone, most men flown to Guantanamo on a C-12, and the ones judged important enough sent, as he puts it, a different way.

the-families-of-the-captured.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
the-families-of-the-captured.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

the-families-of-the-captured.title: Tora Bora
the-families-of-the-captured.summary: Mountainous cave complex in eastern Afghanistan that served as an al-Qaeda redoubt after the September 11 attacks. Per John Kiriakou — chief of counterterrorism operations in Pakistan at the time — the CIA killed al-Qaeda military-affairs chief Mohammed Atef there in October 2001, and Tora Bora was the backdrop to the hunt for the senior al-Qaeda leadership that culminated in the capture of Abu Zubaydah. Kiriakou also recounts an Egyptian al-Qaeda fighter he later recruited who survived a cruise-missile strike on a Tora Bora cave — one of only two who came out alive, his ears bleeding, describing the explosion as the most hideous sound he had ever heard.

the-families-of-the-captured.title: The first prisoner who cooperated
the-families-of-the-captured.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the first al-Qaeda prisoner in Pakistan who agreed to talk to him, the reason the man gave — that he was a prisoner and got nothing out of refusing — and the intelligence that followed: a foot-by-foot description of his crossing from Afghanistan and the locations of safe houses that were then raided.

the-families-of-the-captured.title: Afghan heroin policy
the-families-of-the-captured.summary: The post-2001 U.S. policy in Afghanistan of protecting, and per John Kiriakou actively encouraging, the cultivation of heroin poppy. Under the Taliban in 2000 Afghanistan produced 0% of the world's heroin; by 2009 under American occupation it produced 93%. Per a DEA officer Kiriakou consulted with on the policy paper he was preparing for Senator Kerry, the strategic rationale was that nearly all of the heroin flowed to Iran and Russia, addiction in those countries was considered desirable as a long-run societal weakener, and the same logic now operates in reverse with Chinese fentanyl flowing into the United States.

the-families-of-the-captured.title: Abu Zubaydah
the-families-of-the-captured.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.title: Tarpon Springs
the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.summary: The Greek sponge-diving town on the Florida gulf coast that John Kiriakou calls one of his favourite places — settled for a century by divers from Kalymnos, the island immediately north of the one his own family comes from, and, in his verdict, the site of absolutely incredible Greek food.

the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.title: Craig Murray
the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.summary: Former British Ambassador to Uzbekistan whom John Kiriakou cites as a whistleblower of extreme torture: during a meeting at the Uzbek intelligence service, Murray heard screaming, walked in, and saw a man being boiled in oil — reporting it cost him his career.

the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.title: Dumping cash in a Moscow bathroom
the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.summary: John Kiriakou's examples of what covert action has actually meant in practice — American commandos blowing up the Trans-Siberian oil pipeline, Afghan guerrillas hired to cross the Amu Darya and attack a refinery inside the southern USSR, and cash dumped in a Moscow bathroom to undermine the rouble.

the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.title: How Chinese intelligence recruits
the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.summary: John Kiriakou''s assessment of the Ministry of State Security''s tradecraft: very effective with anyone who simply wants money, because the money is limitless, and very bad at cultivating a source who does not yet know who is cultivating him — with the target usually being access to sophisticated technology.

the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.title: MK-ULTRA in Canada
the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that many MK-ULTRA experiments took place on Canadian soil, and his explanation of why: the CIA asked the Canadian intelligence service for help with its anti-Soviet, anti-Chinese remote-viewing and LSD work, and the Canadians gladly gave it.

the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.title: Pakistani corruption and democracy
the-family-that-spans-the-spectrum.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment that corruption in Pakistan is so deep and so broad that a genuinely functioning democracy is almost impossible there — set against a long history of military coups, a habit of imprisoning former prime ministers, and his insistence that Imran Khan should not be in a cell.

the-farm.title: Doing Time Like a Spy
the-farm.summary: Prison memoir by John Kiriakou, full title Doing Time Like a Spy: How the CIA Taught Me to Survive and Thrive in Prison; winner of two literary awards and reissued in a second edition by Simon and Schuster.

the-farm.title: Surveillance detection route
the-farm.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

the-farm.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
the-farm.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

the-farm.title: The asset recruitment cycle
the-farm.summary: The four-step professional standard John Kiriakou says governed CIA operations before September 11 — spot, assess, develop, recruit — and without which an officer did not get promoted. He calls it the asset acquisition cycle as often as the recruitment cycle. Spotting looks for access, not rank; assessment looks for a vulnerability, a word he insists is less ugly than it sounds; development is months or years of friendship bought on an unlimited expense account; and the recruitment itself rests not on money, revenge or ideology but on the target believing the officer is his best friend. Threats are forbidden — partly on ethics, partly because the target may come to the next meeting with a gun.

the-farm.title: Asset acquisition cycle
the-farm.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

the-farm.title: The operational cable
the-farm.summary: The written product of every CIA field meeting — drafted the same day, printed and handed to the instructors at the Farm, who critiqued the prose, the conduct of the meeting and what the officer had been wearing.

the-farragut-west-encounter.title: The mobile passport lane
the-farragut-west-encounter.summary: John Kiriakou's report of flying home from Spain during the longest government shutdown in American history — ridiculous security lines, and an immigration officer who said four words, "Look at the camera. Welcome home," which Kiriakou attributes to the man not being paid.

the-farragut-west-encounter.title: Abigail Spanberger
the-farragut-west-encounter.summary: Governor of Virginia from 2025 and, before Congress, a CIA officer alongside John Kiriakou in the Counterterrorism Center — whom he calls a perfectly nice person who would have been a middle-of-the-road Republican in the 1970s and 1980s, and whose victory speech, to his surprise, said all the right things.

the-farragut-west-encounter.title: Jason Miyares
the-farragut-west-encounter.summary: The Cuban-born Republican attorney general of Virginia whom John Kiriakou expected to be a right-wing disaster and found instead to be excellent — a judgement he says is hard for him to make about a conservative Republican, and which he repeated on the night Miyares was unceremoniously thrown out of office.

the-farragut-west-encounter.title: Joe Rogan
the-farragut-west-encounter.summary: The podcast host whose show John Kiriakou finally sat for in October 2025 — an experience that began with signing a non-disclosure agreement and ended with his verdict that Rogan is "a nice guy, very down to earth, very normal." The first thing Rogan asked, walking into the studio ten minutes late: "Hey, do you know my friend Mike Baker?" Kiriakou defends Rogan as unfairly characterized as a right-winger, and had long cited the show as the venue where Zuckerberg admitted Facebook suppressed the Hunter Biden laptop story at the FBI''s behest.

the-farragut-west-encounter.title: The Arlington house
the-farragut-west-encounter.summary: The 1,200-square-foot house John Kiriakou bought with his Pakistan overtime and danger pay for $347,000, sold two years later for $721,000, and now values at a million — the anchor of his repeated argument that his own children can never live in the Arlington, Virginia neighbourhood they grew up in.

the-farragut-west-encounter.title: The Crete blood feud
the-farragut-west-encounter.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of the mass shooting on Crete as neither terrorism nor politics but a family feud that boiled over — an answer he gives smiling, because in his account every Greek already knows that on Crete everybody is armed and everybody is angry with somebody.

the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.title: The Colombian air bridge through Venezuela
the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.summary: What John Kiriakou says his own Senate Foreign Relations Committee investigation found about drug trafficking through Venezuela — that it exists, that it consists of Colombian aircraft landing there en route to Africa, and that there is no evidence Nicolás Maduro controls it or knows when and where it happens.

the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.title: Venezuela Boat Strikes
the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.summary: September 2025 U.S. military strike on a boat in the Caribbean that killed 11 people the White House called drug traffickers; John Kiriakou calls it piracy on the high seas followed by mass murder, arguing the victims were never charged with a crime and that the boat's unusual passenger count undercuts the drug-trafficking story.

the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.title: The plot to divert Maduro's plane
the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.summary: The reported CIA attempt to recruit Nicolás Maduro's pilot so that a flight carrying him into exile in Havana would instead land at Key West, where the DEA would seize him — a Noriega repeat that prompted John Kiriakou to ask why a government pursuing regime change should care where the deposed ruler goes.

the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.title: There are denials and then there are denials
the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.summary: John Kiriakou's rule for reading official statements — that 'we have no such plans' is not a denial, because nothing counts as a plan until a head of government signs off on it, leaving a government free to discuss and even prepare something it can still credibly say it has no plans for.

the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.title: Abraham Accords
the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.title: The CIA's internal social culture
the-fentanyl-from-cocaine-claim.summary: John Kiriakou's one-word characterisation of the agency's internal culture — "incestuous" — describing a club for every conceivable interest, actively encouraged officer-to-officer romances, and a design intent that officers should have no need of friends or activities outside the building.

the-fifteen-dollar-maintenance-fee.title: Bankruptcy and the dropped charges
the-fifteen-dollar-maintenance-fee.summary: The sequence John Kiriakou places at the centre of his case: that the espionage counts against him were dropped only after his legal fees had bankrupted him, which he presents as evidence that the government''s aim was attrition rather than conviction.

the-fifteen-dollar-maintenance-fee.title: The Addis Ababa zoo
the-fifteen-dollar-maintenance-fee.summary: A visit John Kiriakou made to the zoo in Addis Ababa on a free half-day, where he watched keepers force a screaming donkey into the lion enclosure — and noted the two-tier admission price charged to foreigners.

His own standard answer was the foreign service, training work, and some import-export negotiation.

the-fifteen-dollar-maintenance-fee.title: The election day 1992 poll
the-fifteen-dollar-maintenance-fee.summary: An informal show of hands taken in a CIA branch office on election day 1992, which John Kiriakou describes as the moment he discovered he had no idea of the politics of the colleagues he sat three feet away from — and that he was not, as he had assumed, the only progressive in the room.

the-fifteen-dollar-maintenance-fee.title: The ex-prisoner at the Bureau of Prisons
the-fifteen-dollar-maintenance-fee.summary: John Kiriakou's approving account of the appointment of a former federal prisoner — recently released after five years on a drug conspiracy charge — as deputy director of the Bureau of Prisons, which he calls an inspired choice and one of the few things he has praised Donald Trump for.

the-fifteen-minute-call.title: The SHU loophole
the-fifteen-minute-call.summary: John Kiriakou''s warning about the American assurances given to British courts in the Julian Assange extradition case: prosecutors promised not to place him in a communications management unit but said nothing about the Special Housing Unit, and in Kiriakou''s account a prison need only cite an overheard threat to hold a man in solitary indefinitely.

the-fifteen-minute-call.title: The glass-eating prisoner
the-fifteen-minute-call.summary: A case John Kiriakou cites from a 2015 New York Times Magazine investigation of federal solitary confinement: a prisoner held in the Special Housing Unit at the federal supermax in Florence, Colorado for roughly eighteen years who smashed his narrow cell window and ate the broken glass so that he would be taken to a hospital and could speak to another human being.

the-fifteen-minute-call.title: The modified CMU
the-fifteen-minute-call.summary: The communications restrictions imposed on John Kiriakou at FCI Loretto after his Letter from Loretto was published by the Huffington Post. Staff called it a modified communications management unit: a five-day delay on incoming and outgoing email, live monitoring of his telephone calls rather than recording, and a prohibition on speaking Greek to his family.

the-fifteen-minute-call.title: Communications management unit
the-fifteen-minute-call.summary: The two restricted-contact units inside the American federal prison system, at Terre Haute and Marion; built for "the worst of the worst" but, in John Kiriakou's account, used to silence prisoners whose messages are inconvenient — and a practice he groups with solitary confinement as torture. He served part of his own sentence in a modified one.

the-fifteen-minute-call.title: The Bureau of Prisons answers to no one
the-fifteen-minute-call.summary: John Kiriakou''s summary of what he calls the hardest lesson of his incarceration: that the Bureau of Prisons sits under the Justice Department but is accountable to nobody in practice, disregarding what sentencing judges order and what its own prosecutors have agreed, and placing prisoners wherever it chooses.

the-fifteen-minute-call.title: The sixty-five-cent arrangement
the-fifteen-minute-call.summary: The deal John Kiriakou struck with the chaplain at FCI Loretto: rather than keep his 65-cents-an-hour janitor''s wage, he asked to be kept on the books while the money went to the next man on the list, and to stop coming to work — which is how he found the time to write Doing Time Like a Spy.

the-filibuster-and-harry-reids-lesson.title: Cancelling the 2026 midterms
the-filibuster-and-harry-reids-lesson.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that the 2026 war cannot win the midterm elections for the Republicans, and his flagged-as-paranoid worry that it may instead furnish the pretext for a national emergency and a cancelled election.

the-filibuster-and-harry-reids-lesson.title: Jake Tapper
the-filibuster-and-harry-reids-lesson.summary: CNN anchor who drove to FCI Loretto to interview the imprisoned John Kiriakou — and who asked President Obama at a press conference why he had insisted on prosecuting a man who exposed a crime, a question Obama answered by walking away from the podium. Tapper's visit was the head of a media wave that began with a smuggled-out letter on the Huffington Post, and it became Kiriakou's protection inside; even a guard known as a psychopath left him alone rather than find CNN parked beside his car.

the-filibuster-and-harry-reids-lesson.title: Abraham Accords
the-filibuster-and-harry-reids-lesson.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." the-filibuster-and-harry-reids-lesson.summary: John Kiriakou's one-word characterisation of the agency's internal culture — "incestuous" — describing a club for every conceivable interest, actively encouraged officer-to-officer romances, and a design intent that officers should have no need of friends or activities outside the building.

the-filibuster-and-harry-reids-lesson.title: CIA liaison relationships
the-filibuster-and-harry-reids-lesson.summary: John Kiriakou's critique of CIA intelligence-liaison relationships with foreign governments — sharply expanded after 9/11 — arguing that officers do not consider the long-term risk that disclosing sensitive operations to foreign services hands those governments leverage, including potential blackmail material, over the United States, and that no one left in Congress has the will to provide real oversight of the practice.

the-filibuster-and-harry-reids-lesson.title: Civilian ships and piracy
the-filibuster-and-harry-reids-lesson.summary: Why merchant crews cannot defend themselves: by international treaty no civilian ship may carry a weapon. John Kiriakou handled international piracy as a Senate Foreign Relations Committee staffer and brought Captain Richard Phillips to testify.

the-first-prisoner-who-cooperated.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

the-first-prisoner-who-cooperated.title: The families of the captured
the-first-prisoner-who-cooperated.summary: John Kiriakou's statement that the wives and children of men captured in the post-9/11 raids in Pakistan were separated from them and sent back to their home countries — and that the prisoners were not told, and were left believing their wives were still in American custody.

the-first-prisoner-who-cooperated.title: Afghan heroin policy
the-first-prisoner-who-cooperated.summary: The post-2001 U.S. policy in Afghanistan of protecting, and per John Kiriakou actively encouraging, the cultivation of heroin poppy. Under the Taliban in 2000 Afghanistan produced 0% of the world's heroin; by 2009 under American occupation it produced 93%. Per a DEA officer Kiriakou consulted with on the policy paper he was preparing for Senator Kerry, the strategic rationale was that nearly all of the heroin flowed to Iran and Russia, addiction in those countries was considered desirable as a long-run societal weakener, and the same logic now operates in reverse with Chinese fentanyl flowing into the United States.

the-first-prisoner-who-cooperated.title: Tora Bora
the-first-prisoner-who-cooperated.summary: Mountainous cave complex in eastern Afghanistan that served as an al-Qaeda redoubt after the September 11 attacks. Per John Kiriakou — chief of counterterrorism operations in Pakistan at the time — the CIA killed al-Qaeda military-affairs chief Mohammed Atef there in October 2001, and Tora Bora was the backdrop to the hunt for the senior al-Qaeda leadership that culminated in the capture of Abu Zubaydah. Kiriakou also recounts an Egyptian al-Qaeda fighter he later recruited who survived a cruise-missile strike on a Tora Bora cave — one of only two who came out alive, his ears bleeding, describing the explosion as the most hideous sound he had ever heard.

the-fletc-badge.title: The Bureau of Prisons polos
the-fletc-badge.summary: What John Kiriakou says he saw on the morning of 6 January 2021 while parking on Capitol Hill for a meeting with his attorney Bruce Fein — a group of men stripping off Bureau of Prisons logo polo shirts and pulling on black ones — and the sentence he says he shouted at them.

the-fletc-badge.title: Letters the cabinet ignored
the-fletc-badge.summary: John Kiriakou's account, from his years on the staff of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, of what happened to congressional oversight letters sent to cabinet secretaries and agency directors — mostly nothing — and why he expects the same of demands made from the minority side of the aisle.

the-fletc-badge.title: Ali from Newark
the-fletc-badge.summary: The Black shot caller at FCI Loretto, near the end of a twenty-five-year drug sentence, who came to embrace John Kiriakou at the close of his term and tell him how much he respected him — a friendship possible only because Kiriakou had decided on arrival to ignore the prison's racial divisions.

the-fletc-badge.title: Bezalel Smotrich
the-fletc-badge.summary: Israeli far-right minister whom John Kiriakou, alongside Itamar Ben-Gvir, blames for leaving Israel unprepared on October 7 by insisting any attack would come from the West Bank rather than Gaza.

the-fletc-badge.title: Candace Owens
the-fletc-badge.summary: The commentator whose claims about the killing of Charlie Kirk John Kiriakou has publicly declined to accept. He credits her reach and her intelligence and rejects her method, citing an earlier occasion — a conference call he says he was on — at which she claimed irrefutable proof that the Italian government had stolen the 2020 election and that its release would return Donald Trump to office.

the-fletc-badge.title: Clyde Hall
the-fletc-badge.summary: The imprisoned Ohio congressman John Kiriakou says served at his prison a few years before him, whose remark on release — that he had made some of the best friends of his life inside — Kiriakou thought insane at the time and came to understand after his own sentence.

the-flynn-charges.title: The attribution problem in the DNC hack
the-flynn-charges.summary: Asked in 2017 whether he had any confidence in the intelligence community's assessments of Russian interference, John Kiriakou said he had none — objecting that no one had ever defined what was meant by hacking, that the published evidence told the public nothing, and that an agency asking to be taken at its word should not be.

the-flynn-charges.title: The Washington Post editorial on the cover-up
the-flynn-charges.summary: In May 2017 John Kiriakou pointed to an editorial in a newspaper he says he generally hates, which advised Donald Trump to save himself by adopting Ronald Reagan's Iran-Contra posture — on the principle that it is never the crime that brings a president down but the cover-up, a principle Kiriakou illustrated with the conviction of Scooter Libby.

the-flynn-charges.title: Domingo's television
the-flynn-charges.summary: John Kiriakou has used the television rooms at FCI Loretto as his sharpest illustration of prison segregation: sets owned by racial blocs since a riot in the 1990s, a seat in front of one costing fourteen dollars, and one set left tuned to Law & Order every morning because a man named Domingo had paid four hundred dollars for it and had been gone for years.

the-flynn-charges.title: Mental health as a disciplinary problem
the-flynn-charges.summary: John Kiriakou has said that before his own prosecution he never gave five seconds of thought to the American prison system, and that living inside it showed him a broken one — in particular a system in which mental health is treated as a disciplinary problem rather than a medical one.

the-flynn-charges.title: The 2017 European tour
the-flynn-charges.summary: In May 2017 John Kiriakou spent a week speaking about national security whistleblowing in Iceland, Germany, Luxembourg, Belgium and Ireland, addressing the German Parliament and sharing panels with serving European ministers — an audience he contrasted sharply with his reception in the United States, and one he found newly willing to break with Washington because it was, in his word, panic-stricken about Donald Trump.

the-flynn-charges.title: The Ai Weiwei encounter in Berlin
the-flynn-charges.summary: John Kiriakou met the artist Ai Weiwei by pure chance on a Berlin street while dragging a suitcase to the airport after a board meeting — an encounter that led to a tour of Ai Weiwei's studio and a signed iPhone case bearing the Lego portrait the artist had made of him for an exhibition at Alcatraz.

the-forged-award-certificate.title: The Grasshopper
the-forged-award-certificate.summary: A recruited terrorist source John Kiriakou ran under a cryptonym, who called him after midnight on a dedicated burner, met him behind a church with a paper bag of his wife's gold jewellery, and was given five thousand dollars from station funds as what the chief of station called an early Christmas bonus.

the-forged-award-certificate.title: Asset acquisition cycle
the-forged-award-certificate.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

the-forged-award-certificate.title: Walk-in
the-forged-award-certificate.summary: In John Kiriakou's telling, someone who walks into an embassy offering information; 95% are lunatics or liars, some are 'intelligence peddlers' or hostile 'probes,' and about 1% are 'the real McCoy' — a framework he used to see through a supposed 'walk-in' tip during the Abu Zubaydah hunt. A genuine walk-in — a witness to a terrorist assassination — was later hypnotized by CIA psychologists in a London hotel room and read back a stolen van's license plate, verifying his account.

the-forged-award-certificate.title: CIA operational psychologists
the-forged-award-certificate.summary: The branch of the CIA's psychological staff that John Kiriakou says he worked with directly as a case officer — not the analysts who profile foreign leaders, but the clinicians who vet a prospective recruit for insanity or invention, and advise an officer on exactly how hard a source can be pushed before he breaks.

the-forged-award-certificate.title: Intelligence peddlers
the-forged-award-certificate.summary: John Kiriakou''s breakdown of who actually walks into an American embassy offering information: the overwhelming majority are fabricators or probes, a few per cent are peddlers selling the same nugget to five embassies in a month, and about one per cent are the real thing.

the-forged-award-certificate.title: Surveillance detection route
the-forged-award-certificate.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

the-forty-seven-suffix.title: The hierarchy of charges
the-forty-seven-suffix.summary: How federal prisoners ranked one another by offence, in John Kiriakou's account — RICO at the top, usually with a murder conspiracy attached; wealthy white-collar convicts despised as soft; and arson, insurance fraud and mortgage fraud attracting no interest at all.

the-forty-seven-suffix.title: The golf course deed forgery
the-forty-seven-suffix.summary: The property fraud John Kiriakou encountered at FCI Loretto — a prisoner who forged papers transferring ownership of a golf course to himself and then began charging people rent — and the place such crimes occupy in the prison's own hierarchy of offences.

the-forty-seven-suffix.title: Ali from Newark
the-forty-seven-suffix.summary: The Black shot caller at FCI Loretto, near the end of a twenty-five-year drug sentence, who came to embrace John Kiriakou at the close of his term and tell him how much he respected him — a friendship possible only because Kiriakou had decided on arrival to ignore the prison's racial divisions.

the-forty-seven-suffix.title: Say five years
the-forty-seven-suffix.summary: The first piece of prison advice John Kiriakou says he was given — from a Bonanno family captain, walking laps of the snowed-in basketball court at FCI Loretto — to tell anyone who asked that he was serving five years rather than the thirty months he actually had.

the-forty-seven-suffix.title: The quarterback with a personal chef
the-forty-seven-suffix.summary: The former New York Giants quarterback John Kiriakou says lived in the next row of cells at FCI Loretto — serving a long sentence for a Ponzi scheme, paying every prison gang $500 a month for his safety, and employing another prisoner to cook him three meals a day from food stolen out of the cafeteria.

the-forty-seven-suffix.title: The question about the showers
the-forty-seven-suffix.summary: The single thing John Kiriakou says he most wanted to know before going to prison, and the lunch his attorneys arranged with a former George Washington University professor — himself recently released — to answer it.

the-four-day-old-new-york-times.title: Edward Snowden
the-four-day-old-new-york-times.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

the-four-day-old-new-york-times.title: Kermit Roosevelt and Mosaddegh
the-four-day-old-new-york-times.summary: The CIA officer John Kiriakou names as the man who ran the 1953 overthrow of Iran's Prime Minister Mosaddegh on behalf of British Petroleum — who called it the gravest mistake of his life in the only interview he ever gave, and who, according to the documents Kiriakou has since read in the archives, did not actually run it at all.

the-four-day-old-new-york-times.title: Make it the blip
the-four-day-old-new-york-times.summary: Having stayed up all night reading law review journals and concluded that he had broken no law, John Kiriakou telephoned his attorneys at six in the morning to say he wanted to go to trial. They drove to his house, told him he was facing twelve to eighteen years, and the lawyer he respected most gave him the sentence that changed his mind.

the-four-day-old-new-york-times.title: Plato Kacheris
the-four-day-old-new-york-times.summary: A spelling variant of the name of John Kiriakou's lead defence attorney, who appears in the auto-generated transcripts as both "Kacheris" and "Cacheris". The article on him is at Plato Cacheris.

the-four-day-old-new-york-times.title: The Colonial Pipeline hack
the-four-day-old-new-york-times.summary: Days after the May 2021 ransomware attack that shut the East Coast's main fuel pipeline, John Kiriakou said an FBI contact told him the bureau was fairly confident the Russian government was not behind it — and turned the episode into an indictment of the National Security Agency for watching Americans instead of defending them.

the-four-day-old-new-york-times.title: The nineteen intelligence agencies
the-four-day-old-new-york-times.summary: Asked how many American intelligence agencies there are, John Kiriakou put the number at about nineteen, said there are no genuinely secret ones left, and argued that the sprawl is empire-building by the Pentagon — before asking why the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Commerce need intelligence agencies at all.

the-four-question-torture-exam.title: Liberty University
the-four-question-torture-exam.summary: Evangelical university in Lynchburg, Virginia — the largest in the world — where John Kiriakou taught for several years as an adjunct professor of intelligence studies in the Jesse Helms School of Government. He says he warned the school he disagreed with it on 95% of the issues and was hired anyway, on the dean's reasoning that "torture's not Christian"; he enjoyed the post while clashing constantly with the institution over the treatment of Middle Eastern Christians.

the-four-question-torture-exam.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
the-four-question-torture-exam.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

the-four-question-torture-exam.title: Agent payment mechanics
the-four-question-torture-exam.summary: How the CIA physically pays a recruited agent — cash every month, a receipt signed with any alias the agent chooses, and a polygraph regime built around the assumption that the officer handling the money is the person most likely to steal it.

the-four-question-torture-exam.title: Allen Dulles
the-four-question-torture-exam.summary: Long-serving CIA director whom John Kiriakou calls a 'monster' and a 'very dark figure in American history' — a United Fruit board member who ran the agency that overthrew Guatemala's Árbenz, who went to Truman's house to talk him out of criticising the CIA, and who stayed in touch with the men Kiriakou believes killed John F. Kennedy.

the-four-question-torture-exam.title: Church Committee
the-four-question-torture-exam.summary: U.S. Senate investigative committee operating in 1975–1976 that examined domestic intelligence abuses by the CIA, FBI, and NSA; per John Kiriakou, the Church Committee — alongside the concurrent Pike Committee in the House — was the last genuine moment of legislative oversight over the intelligence community, born of a national consensus that government had gone dangerously off course. Its work led to the creation of the permanent Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, which Kiriakou says ceased to function as real oversight roughly seven years after its founding.

the-four-question-torture-exam.title: The CIA's internal social culture
the-four-question-torture-exam.summary: John Kiriakou's one-word characterisation of the agency's internal culture — "incestuous" — describing a club for every conceivable interest, actively encouraged officer-to-officer romances, and a design intent that officers should have no need of friends or activities outside the building.

the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.title: Venezuela regime change (2026)
the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.summary: John Kiriakou''s assessment of the American operation that removed Venezuela''s president — a clear violation of international law, since none of the three recognised grounds for one state attacking another applied, but not a violation of US law, which since 1985 has expressly permitted special forces to cross borders and seize people for trial. His reluctant conclusion at the time: "as much as I hate admitting it, this regime change seems to be working right now."

the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.title: Hamid Karzai
the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.summary: The president installed in Afghanistan after the American invasion, whom John Kiriakou uses as the standing illustration of what occupation actually buys: after twenty years and more than a trillion dollars, Karzai was ''little more than the mayor of Kabul'' — and did not control all of Kabul either. The line began as a joke among Senate Foreign Relations Committee staff, and Kiriakou used it to Senator John Kerry''s face ten years into the war.

the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.title: María Corina Machado
the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.summary: The Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate whom John Kiriakou rates no higher than Juan Guaidó: a figure in a permanently divided right-wing opposition who commands no armies and no troops. He reads the prize itself as part of the propaganda campaign against Maduro, and expects that if Maduro leaves the next leader of Venezuela will be a senior military officer rather than a civilian politician.

the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.title: Maduro Capture
the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.summary: CIA-driven nighttime operation in which a team of Delta Force commandos entered Venezuela and removed Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife from their beds. Per John Kiriakou, the key enabling intelligence — per a New York Times account he cited — came from a CIA asset inside Maduro''s presidential palace who called when Maduro went to sleep: ''He''s sound asleep. If you''re going to do it, do it now.'' At least eighty people were killed in the operation, including approximately thirty-five Cubans. Kiriakou compares it to the 1989 capture of Manuel Noriega, in which US forces blasted death metal at the Vatican Embassy until Noriega was asked to leave.

the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.title: The assassination approval process
the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.summary: Why John Kiriakou thinks arranging the death of a foreign leader is far harder for the CIA than the public assumes. It is not the 1960s: there is congressional oversight, and before any proposal reaches the president''s signature it must clear layers of lawyers at the Justice Department''s Office of Legal Counsel, the National Security Council and the agency''s own General Counsel. Pressuring a leader into flight, he notes, is both easier and more legal.

the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.title: The Mariel boatlift comparison
the-four-requirements-of-a-coup.summary: John Kiriakou''s rebuttal to the claim that Venezuela emptied its prisons and mental institutions into the United States: nothing of the kind has been shown to have happened, and the episode being described actually belongs to Cuba, which did exactly that during the Mariel boatlift.

the-fox-news-military-analyst.title: Fake CIA résumés
the-fox-news-military-analyst.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of being used as a human authenticator in the private sector: at the consulting firm he joined after leaving the CIA, every job applicant claiming agency service was sent to dinner with him, and by his count fully half of them had never set foot inside the CIA.

the-fox-news-military-analyst.title: Hugh Francis Redmond
the-fox-news-military-analyst.summary: The first CIA officer to die in the line of duty, per John Kiriakou — a Special Activities Division officer sent to Shanghai in 1946 under cover as an ice cream machine salesman, arrested by the Chinese communists in 1951, held and tortured for nineteen years, and declared a suicide by Beijing in 1970. The CIA denied he had ever worked for it until his name was declassified and added to the Wall of Honor.

the-fox-news-military-analyst.title: Robert David Steele
the-fox-news-military-analyst.summary: The former intelligence officer and podcaster whose death during the COVID-19 pandemic John Kiriakou was asked to explain. Kiriakou, who had appeared on his show, calls him a sweet man who died of the disease, and offers a blunt assessment of his work: he did not believe most of the conspiracy theories he promoted, but they brought him an audience.

the-fox-news-military-analyst.title: The applicant who invented a CIA career
the-fox-news-military-analyst.summary: The job interview John Kiriakou conducted in the private sector at which he took a candidate to lunch, asked two questions any real CIA officer could answer, and was told: "I''m really sorry. I really need this job."

the-fox-news-military-analyst.title: Bin Laden health rumors
the-fox-news-military-analyst.summary: John Kiriakou's dismissal of the claim that Osama bin Laden died years before the 2011 raid. He says the CIA received a steady stream of medical rumours about him — kidney failure, dialysis in a cave, a spinal disorder — none of which turned out to be true, and that bin Laden was in fine health apart from arthritis and a hip problem until the day he died.

the-fox-news-military-analyst.title: CIA attention to West Africa
the-fox-news-military-analyst.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer on whether the CIA is likely to be operating in Burkina Faso: for all the years he was at the agency it cared very little about Africa and especially West Africa, but the presence of al-Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates plus the drug trade makes CIA and special forces involvement probable — and, he adds, the American public will not hear about it.

the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.title: The resort with no air conditioning
the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.summary: The Baja California resort where John Kiriakou spent a month filming in 2025 — built in the 1960s as a commune by long-haired left-wing Angelenos funded by Thomas Hart Benton's daughter, a dozen buildings on the southernmost tip of the peninsula, no air conditioning, and nothing whatsoever to do unless you dive.

the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.title: The tarantula on the mini fridge
the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.summary: The wildlife of the Baja resort as John Kiriakou catalogued it — rattlesnakes everywhere, an emailed instruction never to go barefoot, shoes shaken out before every midnight walk to the mini fridge kept outdoors, a flashlight in hand, and one night at three in the morning a tarantula sitting on the fridge itself.

the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.title: Where he slept in Afghanistan
the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.summary: John Kiriakou's inventory of his own Afghan accommodation across a decade of trips — a shared tent on the first visits, a tent of his own once ("living high on the hog"), the officers' quarters at Bagram once the American foothold was serious, and a three-star Afghan hotel when he returned as a private citizen to get the Kite Runner children out.

the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.title: Abigail Spanberger
