the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.summary: Governor of Virginia from 2025 and, before Congress, a CIA officer alongside John Kiriakou in the Counterterrorism Center — whom he calls a perfectly nice person who would have been a middle-of-the-road Republican in the 1970s and 1980s, and whose victory speech, to his surprise, said all the right things.

the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.title: Destroying the Dome of the Rock
the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.summary: John Kiriakou's agreement with Tucker Carlson that a Zionist extremist plan to demolish the Dome of the Rock and build a third temple would be the event that starts the Third World War — and his additional prediction that it would also be the beginning of the end for the Israeli government and all of its support.

the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.title: Jason Miyares
the-fox-that-ate-the-scraps.summary: The Cuban-born Republican attorney general of Virginia whom John Kiriakou expected to be a right-wing disaster and found instead to be excellent — a judgement he says is hard for him to make about a conservative Republican, and which he repeated on the night Miyares was unceremoniously thrown out of office.

the-frank-kendall-air-force-one-case.title: The CIA one-year leave
the-frank-kendall-air-force-one-case.summary: The administrative fact about CIA departures John Kiriakou uses to knock down the *"once CIA, always CIA"* line on social media. Officers who resign are placed on a mandatory one-year leave without pay during which their security clearances remain intact so the agency can pull them back for an operation or a source that will only speak to them. Only at the anniversary is the badge formally shredded and the resignation becomes real.

the-frank-kendall-air-force-one-case.title: Espionage Act
the-frank-kendall-air-force-one-case.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

the-french-human-sources.title: Torture as a recruiting tool
the-french-human-sources.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that interrogations, drone strikes and targeted killings have generated more enemies than they removed — supported by the arithmetic he uses, from an al-Qaeda core of a few hundred in Afghanistan to an ISIS he numbered at some thirty-five thousand, by the fighters he personally captured who told him they had no quarrel with America until a drone killed their families, and by his answer to the charge that it was his disclosure rather than the programme that put Americans at risk.

the-french-human-sources.title: CIA–FBI interagency rivalry and 9/11
the-french-human-sources.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the historical CIA–FBI rivalry, dating to J. Edgar Hoover's opposition to the 1947 National Security Act, and how it manifested before September 11 when Cofer Black's Counterterrorism Center withheld from the FBI that hijackers Nawaf al-Hazmi and Khalid al-Mihdhar had been granted U.S. visas.

the-french-human-sources.title: Economic roots of terrorism
the-french-human-sources.summary: John Kiriakou's argument, drawn from interrogating young al-Qaeda fighters in Pakistan, that jihadi recruitment is driven by poverty and hopelessness rather than religion — illiterate villagers paid $300 a month who could not find the U.S. on a map and had never read the Quran.

the-french-human-sources.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
the-french-human-sources.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

the-french-human-sources.title: National Security Agency
the-french-human-sources.summary: The U.S. signals-intelligence agency. John Kiriakou notes it was never created by an act of Congress and that its own charter forbids collection on Americans — a rule that, when he entered government, meant heads rolled over accidental intercepts, and which he says has since been inverted into total collection stored in Utah for 500 years.

the-french-human-sources.title: Origins of al-Qaeda
the-french-human-sources.summary: John Kiriakou''s position on where al-Qaeda came from: bad American foreign policy decisions led to it indirectly, but not by design. He rejects the deliberate-creation theory on the grounds that it is unnecessary — a state willing to kill does not need to manufacture a pretext first.

the-french-in-the-streets.title: Albright in Pyongyang
the-french-in-the-streets.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Bill Clinton's stated regret over the final week of his presidency — that he wished he had pursued diplomatic relations with North Korea instead of Israeli-Palestinian peace — and of Madeleine Albright being in Pyongyang rather than at the talks.

the-french-in-the-streets.title: Failure to accept responsibility
the-french-in-the-streets.summary: The federal sentencing enhancement that John Kiriakou says explains why 98 per cent of federal criminal cases end in a plea bargain: a defendant who refuses a deal, goes to trial and loses has time added to the sentence for failing to accept responsibility.

the-french-in-the-streets.title: Nationalizing the midterms
the-french-in-the-streets.summary: John Kiriakou's recurring comparison between contemporary party messaging and Newt Gingrich's 1994 Contract with America, including his advice that Speaker Mike Johnson should keep Gingrich on his couch and ask him nightly how the 1994 midterms were nationalised.

the-french-in-the-streets.title: The nine-dollar-eighty-three premium
the-french-in-the-streets.summary: John Kiriakou's own Affordable Care Act premium, which he gives as $9.83 a month, and the doctor who asked him why he carried the plan at all. Offered during a October 2025 discussion of the government shutdown and the expiring Obamacare subsidies.

the-french-in-the-streets.title: Ted Rall
the-french-in-the-streets.summary: American editorial cartoonist and two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist; co-host with John Kiriakou of the daily news-commentary podcast "Deprogram," launched in September 2025 and by late 2025 running every weekday morning.

the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.title: Tulsi Gabbard
the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.summary: U.S. Director of National Intelligence; a longtime family friend of John Kiriakou's, who has known her since she was 12; Kiriakou calls her appointment "an inspired choice" despite disagreeing with her decision to join the Republican Party, and says she appears to have given up her opposition to Section 702 surveillance to secure Senate confirmation.

the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.title: Section 702
the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.summary: Section of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act under which the U.S. government conducts warrantless electronic surveillance; per John Kiriakou the principal post-9/11 mechanism by which the CIA, NSA, and FBI surveil American citizens; renewed by Congress every two years over the objection of a small bipartisan minority; the subject of an estimated 200,000+ illegal FBI database queries — per the Brennan Center for Justice, including ~78,000 misused queries over a two-year window; the disclosure that Edward Snowden made public in summer 2013.

the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.title: FISA
the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.summary: The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, the U.S. legal framework governing surveillance warrants for foreign-intelligence purposes. Per John Kiriakou, FISA is dangerously easy to abuse — he cites Carter Page, whose life was ruined and who was driven into bankruptcy after the Steele dossier was used to support four FISA applications against him. Kiriakou groups FISA with the Patriot Act and Section 702 as the legal architecture stripping Americans of constitutional protections, opposed by only a handful of legislators.

the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.title: NSA Surveillance
the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.summary: ''It is part of NSA''s founding charter that it is not allowed to spy on Americans'' — Kiriakou on warrantless collection and the Bluffdale warehouse.

the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.title: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.summary: The intelligence-community layer created in 2004, which John Kiriakou argues should never have existed. He traces its origin to George Tenet's failures over 9/11 and Iraq, notes it grew from sixteen employees to roughly twenty-four thousand, and points out that most agencies nominally under it are Defense Department bodies over which it controls nothing but the budget.

the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.title: Patriot Act
the-gabbard-confirmation-fight.summary: U.S. law passed after the September 11 attacks that vastly expanded domestic surveillance authority. Per John Kiriakou, the Patriot Act ''opened up everything'' — and he disputes the common belief that 9/11 was required to pass it: ''You underestimate Congress. They didn''t need a catastrophe — they would just pass it because they can.'' He ties it to NSA bulk-collection programs that vacuum up every phone call, text, email, and piece of metadata from Americans, in violation of the NSA''s own charter.

the-gamma-globulin-shot.title: Typhoid fever in Bangkok
the-gamma-globulin-shot.summary: The illness John Kiriakou calls the sickest he has ever been — typhoid fever caught in Bangkok in 2002, which he had assumed the inoculation would prevent, and which put him in hospital twice. The doctor''s correction: the shot does not stop you catching typhoid, only makes it slightly less virulent when you do.

the-gamma-globulin-shot.title: The Puerto Rico thirds
the-gamma-globulin-shot.summary: The division of Puerto Rican opinion John Kiriakou says was given to him on the island by a mid-level government official — a third for independence, a third for statehood, a third for leaving things exactly as they are — and the official's conclusion that because of it, nothing will ever change. Kiriakou has repeated the split in his own voice as an argument that Puerto Rico is a colony but not a settler colony, and doubts statehood will ever come.

the-gamma-globulin-shot.title: Why Maxwell took the Fifth
the-gamma-globulin-shot.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of Ghislaine Maxwell's silence before Congress — not that she was protecting anyone, but that nobody had offered her anything. His precedent is Oliver North, whose congressional immunity made his testimony unusable and kept him out of prison altogether.

the-gamma-globulin-shot.title: Kiriakou on travel
the-gamma-globulin-shot.summary: John Kiriakou''s own ranking of the countries he has visited: Greece his favourite and, he insists, the best food anywhere; Oman the most beautiful landscape; Syria the most extraordinary civilisation; and Chile the cheapest, illustrated by a bottle of a vineyard''s locked-away reserve that cost $8.50 on his honeymoon.

the-gamma-globulin-shot.title: Acts of Service
the-gamma-globulin-shot.summary: The Doja Cat song that John Kiriakou discovered, through a Cameo request, had become the soundtrack to a genre of montage about him. The clips set to it use footage from before his weight loss — he lost 77 pounds by 2007 and 115 pounds from 2022 — and he says he cannot watch them.

the-gamma-globulin-shot.title: Kiriakou's volunteer trip to Guatemala
the-gamma-globulin-shot.summary: A visit John Kiriakou made to Guatemala to volunteer for a couple of weeks at an orphanage, which he recounts as the closing evidence in his argument about the 1954 coup: the orphanage was ringed by a twenty-foot concrete wall, and he could barely sleep for the gunfire outside.

the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.title: The ask-forgiveness maxim
the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.summary: The rule of thumb John Kiriakou says he was taught early in his CIA career — that it is always better to ask forgiveness than to ask permission — and which he offers as the explanation for how the agency runs legally doubtful programmes: it does what it wants, apologises if caught, and that is the end of it.

the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.title: The North Korea SEAL Team Six operation
the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.summary: The 2018 mission in which American special forces attempted to plant an eavesdropping device on North Korean soil, killed a boatload of fishermen and withdrew without planting it — which John Kiriakou uses to call Donald Trump a liar, because such an operation requires the president's signature on a finding, and to note that Congress was never told.

the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.title: The CIA as a paramilitary organization
the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.summary: John Kiriakou''s periodisation of the CIA''s mission — spying and analysis until Vietnam, restored after the Church and Pike hearings of 1975, and converted immediately after September 11 into a paramilitary body that he says it has remained ever since. His objection is stated without hedging: drawing up a kill list every Tuesday and dispatching officers to carry it out is not intelligence, it is murder.

the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.title: Hamid Karzai
the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.summary: The president installed in Afghanistan after the American invasion, whom John Kiriakou uses as the standing illustration of what occupation actually buys: after twenty years and more than a trillion dollars, Karzai was ''little more than the mayor of Kabul'' — and did not control all of Kabul either. The line began as a joke among Senate Foreign Relations Committee staff, and Kiriakou used it to Senator John Kerry''s face ten years into the war.

the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.title: Aafia Siddiqui
the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.summary: Pakistani-American neuroscientist arrested in Afghanistan and convicted in the United States of attempting to shoot FBI agents; per John Kiriakou, who covered the arrest as a terrorism consultant for ABC News and has followed the case since, she never had a gun and never fired, the bullet holes offered as proof predated her capture, and the CIA took her three children — two later recovered, the youngest never found.

the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.title: The 1991 Saudi plan for Gaza
the-gang-of-four-and-gang-of-eight.summary: A proposal John Kiriakou says he watched Ambassador Chas Freeman float to the Saudis during his first overseas tour in 1991 — that Saudi Arabia fund a port, an airport, a desalination plant and an electrical grid in Gaza. The Saudis agreed; Israel refused outright. Kiriakou raises it because the identical arrangement resurfaced in the Israeli press more than three decades later.

the-general-assembly-circus.title: 2026 Iran war
the-general-assembly-circus.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-general-assembly-circus.title: Acts of Service
the-general-assembly-circus.summary: The Doja Cat song that John Kiriakou discovered, through a Cameo request, had become the soundtrack to a genre of montage about him. The clips set to it use footage from before his weight loss — he lost 77 pounds by 2007 and 115 pounds from 2022 — and he says he cannot watch them.

the-general-assembly-circus.title: Kiriakou on soccer
the-general-assembly-circus.summary: John Kiriakou's public reversal on football, a sport he had dismissed since his teens on the strength of a Saturday Night Live joke about a match between Yemen and Saudi Arabia being decided early by an insurmountable one-nil lead. Watching the 2026 World Cup, he concluded he had been wrong.

the-general-assembly-circus.title: Strait of Hormuz
the-general-assembly-circus.summary: The shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Persian Gulf, and the centre of gravity of the 2026 Iran war in John Kiriakou''s account — a strait whose only navigable deep water lies on the Iranian side of the maritime border, closed not by Iran''s aggression but, as he insists, by the American and Israeli attack that provoked it: "The Strait of Hormuz was open. We''re the ones that forced the closure."

the-general-assembly-circus.title: The 2026 World Cup final
the-general-assembly-circus.summary: Spain''s victory over Argentina in a final John Kiriakou described as dirty on the losers'' part and notable for a red card, and the awkwardness that followed: Donald Trump, who had exerted considerable influence over FIFA and whose country was hosting, had to present the trophy to a nation whose leadership he had spent weeks publicly attacking. The Spanish press cropped him out of the celebration photographs.

the-general-assembly-circus.title: Russia was always the same enemy
the-general-assembly-circus.summary: John Kiriakou''s observation, from inside the CIA, that the collapse of the Soviet Union changed nothing about how the agency worked on Russia. The marching orders given to his colleagues on the Russia account were not to change policy at all: Russia was treated as the same enemy it had been as the Soviet Union, with a brief exception during the Yeltsin presidency.

the-general-assembly-workaround.title: Ireland recognizes Palestine
the-general-assembly-workaround.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the American reaction to Ireland''s recognition of Palestine, which he says he witnessed the aftermath of while in the country: the CIA was indifferent, but the State Department was apoplectic — not about Ireland itself, but about the precedent, which Kiriakou says other European states promptly began to follow.

the-general-assembly-workaround.title: CIA attention to West Africa
the-general-assembly-workaround.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer on whether the CIA is likely to be operating in Burkina Faso: for all the years he was at the agency it cared very little about Africa and especially West Africa, but the presence of al-Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates plus the drug trade makes CIA and special forces involvement probable — and, he adds, the American public will not hear about it.

the-general-assembly-workaround.title: CIA–FBI incompatible computer systems
the-general-assembly-workaround.summary: John Kiriakou's claim that from the CIA's founding in 1947 until 2009 the computer systems of the CIA and the FBI were not compatible with one another — no message could be sent from one to the other and no intelligence shared — which he offers both as the material substrate of the interagency hatred that helped make September 11 possible, and as the gap through which James Mitchell and Bruce Jessen were able to pass Ali Soufan's FBI debriefings of Abu Zubaydah off as the fruits of torture.

the-general-assembly-workaround.title: Fake CIA résumés
the-general-assembly-workaround.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of being used as a human authenticator in the private sector: at the consulting firm he joined after leaving the CIA, every job applicant claiming agency service was sent to dinner with him, and by his count fully half of them had never set foot inside the CIA.

the-general-assembly-workaround.title: Forcing Iran toward a bomb
the-general-assembly-workaround.summary: John Kiriakou''s argument that Western pressure risks producing the very outcome it claims to prevent: repeated Israeli assassinations of Iranian scientists and generals and strikes on Iranian sites may eventually leave Ayatollah Khamenei with no choice but to permit a defensive weapon — despite the religious prohibition Kiriakou credits him with maintaining, and despite successive American estimates that Iran is not seeking one.

the-general-assembly-workaround.title: Freemasons and Opus Dei at the CIA
the-general-assembly-workaround.summary: John Kiriakou's characterisation of the affinity networks at the top of the CIA — a great many senior officers who are Freemasons, and periods in which most of the leadership belonged to Opus Dei and attended the same church in Great Falls, Virginia. He rejects the idea that these are plots, describing them instead as accidental clusters of men who look out for one another.

the-george-mason-confrontation.title: Abigail Spanberger
the-george-mason-confrontation.summary: Governor of Virginia from 2025 and, before Congress, a CIA officer alongside John Kiriakou in the Counterterrorism Center — whom he calls a perfectly nice person who would have been a middle-of-the-road Republican in the 1970s and 1980s, and whose victory speech, to his surprise, said all the right things.

the-george-mason-confrontation.title: Jason Miyares
the-george-mason-confrontation.summary: The Cuban-born Republican attorney general of Virginia whom John Kiriakou expected to be a right-wing disaster and found instead to be excellent — a judgement he says is hard for him to make about a conservative Republican, and which he repeated on the night Miyares was unceremoniously thrown out of office.

the-george-mason-confrontation.title: Joe Rogan
the-george-mason-confrontation.summary: The podcast host whose show John Kiriakou finally sat for in October 2025 — an experience that began with signing a non-disclosure agreement and ended with his verdict that Rogan is "a nice guy, very down to earth, very normal." The first thing Rogan asked, walking into the studio ten minutes late: "Hey, do you know my friend Mike Baker?" Kiriakou defends Rogan as unfairly characterized as a right-winger, and had long cited the show as the venue where Zuckerberg admitted Facebook suppressed the Hunter Biden laptop story at the FBI''s behest.

the-george-mason-confrontation.title: The Arlington house
the-george-mason-confrontation.summary: The 1,200-square-foot house John Kiriakou bought with his Pakistan overtime and danger pay for $347,000, sold two years later for $721,000, and now values at a million — the anchor of his repeated argument that his own children can never live in the Arlington, Virginia neighbourhood they grew up in.

the-george-mason-confrontation.title: The Crete blood feud
the-george-mason-confrontation.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation of the mass shooting on Crete as neither terrorism nor politics but a family feud that boiled over — an answer he gives smiling, because in his account every Greek already knows that on Crete everybody is armed and everybody is angry with somebody.

the-george-mason-confrontation.title: The Farragut West encounter
the-george-mason-confrontation.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of walking up to two National Guardsmen in the Farragut West Metro station — the safest station on the network, in his estimate — telling himself the whole way not to say anything, and then saying one sentence: "You guys should be ashamed of yourselves."

the-giuliani-epstein-emails.title: Jesse Jackson
the-giuliani-epstein-emails.summary: American civil rights leader and two-time presidential candidate whose hospitalisation in November 2025 John Kiriakou discussed at length — explaining progressive supranuclear palsy, the condition Jackson was diagnosed with two years after Parkinson''s, from his own family''s experience of the same disease, and giving a poor prognosis.

the-giuliani-epstein-emails.title: Kiriakou's acting career
the-giuliani-epstein-emails.summary: The film role John Kiriakou took in 2025 after Tyrel Ventura wrote a part for him — a former CIA officer running a billionaire's security detail — which he shot in Mexico for a month and which made him, at sixty-odd, a member of the Screen Actors Guild.

the-giuliani-epstein-emails.title: The conscientious objectors book
the-giuliani-epstein-emails.summary: A long out-of-print volume of interviews with American conscientious objectors, published around 1972 and given to John Kiriakou from the personal collection of an objector he was friendly with in prison — a book whose harrowing accounts of objectors sent to real federal prisons rather than to camps convinced him that refusing to serve was often more physically dangerous than serving.

the-giuliani-epstein-emails.title: The Egyptian intelligence chief''s son
the-giuliani-epstein-emails.summary: A coincidence John Kiriakou reported from Oxford, Ohio in November 2025: his own son''s marketing professor turned out to be the son of Muhammad Farag, head of the Egyptian intelligence service some thirty-five years earlier, whom Kiriakou had met in Cairo when the professor was a boy of seven or eight — and the two families went out to dinner together.

the-giuliani-epstein-emails.title: The mob vote for Trump
the-giuliani-epstein-emails.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to a viewer asking whether he discussed politics with organised crime figures in prison: that he did, a great deal, that they love Donald Trump without qualification, and that the reason is a New York real estate developer''s unavoidable daily contact with the unions the mob controls.

the-giuliani-epstein-emails.title: The Outer Banks seasonal workers
the-giuliani-epstein-emails.summary: John Kiriakou''s observation, from years of family summers on the Outer Banks of North Carolina, that he never encountered an American lifeguard and almost no American shop clerks or waiters — the staff being Bulgarian, Romanian, Moldovan and otherwise Eastern European, working on the cheap, housed eight to twelve to a house and sent home at the end of the season.

the-glass-eating-prisoner.title: The SHU loophole
the-glass-eating-prisoner.summary: John Kiriakou''s warning about the American assurances given to British courts in the Julian Assange extradition case: prosecutors promised not to place him in a communications management unit but said nothing about the Special Housing Unit, and in Kiriakou''s account a prison need only cite an overheard threat to hold a man in solitary indefinitely.

the-glass-eating-prisoner.title: The Bureau of Prisons answers to no one
the-glass-eating-prisoner.summary: John Kiriakou''s summary of what he calls the hardest lesson of his incarceration: that the Bureau of Prisons sits under the Justice Department but is accountable to nobody in practice, disregarding what sentencing judges order and what its own prosecutors have agreed, and placing prisoners wherever it chooses.

the-glass-eating-prisoner.title: The fifteen-minute call
the-glass-eating-prisoner.summary: How Marty Gottesfeld, held in the communications management unit at Terre Haute, allocated the single fifteen-minute telephone call he was permitted each week: an email to his wife, his two attorneys and John Kiriakou, with the call going to whoever answered first.

the-glass-eating-prisoner.title: The modified CMU
the-glass-eating-prisoner.summary: The communications restrictions imposed on John Kiriakou at FCI Loretto after his Letter from Loretto was published by the Huffington Post. Staff called it a modified communications management unit: a five-day delay on incoming and outgoing email, live monitoring of his telephone calls rather than recording, and a prohibition on speaking Greek to his family.

the-glass-eating-prisoner.title: The sixty-five-cent arrangement
the-glass-eating-prisoner.summary: The deal John Kiriakou struck with the chaplain at FCI Loretto: rather than keep his 65-cents-an-hour janitor''s wage, he asked to be kept on the books while the money went to the next man on the list, and to stop coming to work — which is how he found the time to write Doing Time Like a Spy.

the-glass-eating-prisoner.title: Evidence of previous heroism
the-glass-eating-prisoner.summary: A phrase John Kiriakou attributes to Judge Leonie Brinkema at his 2013 sentencing. When his service in Pakistan and his role in the capture of Abu Zubaydah were raised in mitigation, the judge ruled — in what Kiriakou gives as her exact words — that any evidence of previous heroism is irrelevant.

the-golf-course-deed-forgery.title: The forty-seven suffix
the-golf-course-deed-forgery.summary: The last two digits of a federal prisoner number that, according to John Kiriakou, mark the holder as a member of an organised gang — and which the Italians at FCI Loretto carried along with MS-13, the Bloods, the Crips and the Mexican Mafia.

the-golf-course-deed-forgery.title: The hierarchy of charges
the-golf-course-deed-forgery.summary: How federal prisoners ranked one another by offence, in John Kiriakou's account — RICO at the top, usually with a murder conspiracy attached; wealthy white-collar convicts despised as soft; and arson, insurance fraud and mortgage fraud attracting no interest at all.

the-golf-course-deed-forgery.title: The quarterback with a personal chef
the-golf-course-deed-forgery.summary: The former New York Giants quarterback John Kiriakou says lived in the next row of cells at FCI Loretto — serving a long sentence for a Ponzi scheme, paying every prison gang $500 a month for his safety, and employing another prisoner to cook him three meals a day from food stolen out of the cafeteria.

the-golf-course-deed-forgery.title: Ali from Newark
the-golf-course-deed-forgery.summary: The Black shot caller at FCI Loretto, near the end of a twenty-five-year drug sentence, who came to embrace John Kiriakou at the close of his term and tell him how much he respected him — a friendship possible only because Kiriakou had decided on arrival to ignore the prison's racial divisions.

the-golf-course-deed-forgery.title: Clyde Hall
the-golf-course-deed-forgery.summary: The imprisoned Ohio congressman John Kiriakou says served at his prison a few years before him, whose remark on release — that he had made some of the best friends of his life inside — Kiriakou thought insane at the time and came to understand after his own sentence.

the-golf-course-deed-forgery.title: Say five years
the-golf-course-deed-forgery.summary: The first piece of prison advice John Kiriakou says he was given — from a Bonanno family captain, walking laps of the snowed-in basketball court at FCI Loretto — to tell anyone who asked that he was serving five years rather than the thirty months he actually had.

the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.title: "I had no intent"
the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.summary: The formula John Kiriakou used in the days around his January 2013 sentencing to describe his own guilty plea — that he had committed the act charged but had neither the intent to commit a crime nor the intent to harm the officer he named, having believed the man was retired and available to be interviewed.

the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.title: The weight of the government
the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.summary: John Kiriakou's comparison, made on the eve of his imprisonment, between the danger of his overseas career — including two attempts on his life by different terrorist groups — and being prosecuted at home, which he says none of it prepared him for.

the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.title: Espionage Act
the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.title: Official leaks
the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.summary: The category of disclosure John Kiriakou says is both the largest and the only one that is never prosecuted — trial balloons and opinion-shaping put out by the White House, the National Security Council and the Pentagon, with the president himself as the most prolific leaker in Washington.

the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.title: The second officer in the same case
the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.summary: A document John Kiriakou says his attorneys discovered shortly before his January 2013 sentencing, showing that a second CIA officer had given the same reporter the names of ten undercover officers along with information on counterterrorist operations and the flight plans of the aircraft serving a secret prison — and was never investigated or prosecuted, which Kiriakou takes as proof that his own case was about whistleblowing rather than disclosure.

the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.title: Zero Dark Thirty
the-government-is-the-biggest-leaker.summary: 2012 film dramatizing the CIA hunt for Osama bin Laden, criticized on release for suggesting torture produced the intelligence that led to his capture. John Kiriakou surveys the mixed critical reception — praise from Time and the New Yorker for its craft, condemnation from journalist Michael Wolff and director Kathryn Bigelow's critics for what they called pro-torture propaganda — and notes his friend Senator John McCain said the film left him "sick... because it is wrong."

the-graham-senate-succession.title: Lindsey Graham
the-graham-senate-succession.summary: Republican senator from South Carolina who died in July 2026, and John Kiriakou's standing shorthand for the permanent war caucus — a "show horse" rather than a workhorse, a "chameleon" who "never saw a war that he didn't want to jump into with both feet," and, on posthumously released documentary footage, a man offering the US Air Force to bomb a country America was not at war with.

the-graham-senate-succession.title: The McConnell obituary
the-graham-senate-succession.summary: A Kentucky newspaper's decision, reported by John Kiriakou in July 2026, to run an obituary of the living Senator Mitch McConnell on purpose — a response, in Kiriakou's reading, to the rapid rehabilitation of Lindsey Graham after his death, and an attempt to get the assessment on the record before the whitewashing could begin.

the-graham-senate-succession.title: The Qatari 747
the-graham-senate-succession.summary: The Boeing 747 given to the United States by the government of Qatar to serve as Air Force One. John Kiriakou reported in July 2026 that it had been delivered to the president while he was overseas and that he declined to fly home in it, because it had not been fitted with the protective equipment — countermeasures, radar jamming — that the role requires.

the-graham-senate-succession.title: John Larson
the-graham-senate-succession.summary: The twenty-eight-year congressman from Connecticut's first district whose primary defeat John Kiriakou reads as a verdict on both the Democratic Party's campaign theory and the age of its incumbents.

the-graham-senate-succession.title: 2026 Iran war
the-graham-senate-succession.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-graham-senate-succession.title: Embassy movie night
the-graham-senate-succession.summary: The weekly diversion John Kiriakou remembers from his posting to Pakistan after September 11th, when the station worked seven days a week and fourteen hours a day: on Wednesday nights the ambassador hosted a film in the embassy''s small theatre, and the audience shouted at the screen and threw popcorn at whatever they had managed to get hold of.

the-grand-mosque-cover-story.title: The Convenient Terrorist
the-grand-mosque-cover-story.summary: Book co-written by John Kiriakou and former Guantanamo guard Joe Hickman on the case of Abu Zubaydah, split half and half between the hunt and capture on one side and the detention on the other; Kiriakou dates the decision to write it to a declassified CIA inspector-general report that told him the intelligence he had risked his life on was false.

the-grand-mosque-cover-story.title: CIA crimes reports against Kiriakou
the-grand-mosque-cover-story.summary: The referral mechanism by which the Central Intelligence Agency asked the Justice Department to investigate John Kiriakou, used not once but repeatedly — by his account after every op-ed, television interview and university speech he gave following his 2007 disclosure of the torture program. The Justice Department declined every time, and Kiriakou treats the pattern as retaliation conducted through a lawful channel.

the-grand-mosque-cover-story.title: False flags are too hard
the-grand-mosque-cover-story.summary: John Kiriakou''s practical objection to the idea that governments routinely stage false flag operations: they exist, and at the operational level the CIA used them constantly, but the bigger the operation the harder it is to run — too many moving parts, too many people who must buy into the conspiracy, and too much incompetence in government to keep any of it straight. He couples the objection with the observation that a government which is not transparent has no standing to complain about public suspicion.

the-grand-mosque-cover-story.title: Abu Zubaydah
the-grand-mosque-cover-story.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

the-grand-mosque-cover-story.title: Guantanamo Bay
the-grand-mosque-cover-story.summary: U.S. naval base in Cuba; site of CIA detention operations during the post-9/11 enhanced interrogation program; briefly served by John Kiriakou as interim Chief during the summer of 2002.

the-grand-mosque-cover-story.title: Origins of al-Qaeda
the-grand-mosque-cover-story.summary: John Kiriakou''s position on where al-Qaeda came from: bad American foreign policy decisions led to it indirectly, but not by design. He rejects the deliberate-creation theory on the grounds that it is unnecessary — a state willing to kill does not need to manufacture a pretext first.

the-grasshopper.title: The forged award certificate
the-grasshopper.summary: A recruited source John Kiriakou says he brought to tears twice — first by telling him his reporting had gone directly to the president of the United States, then by presenting him with an award certificate Kiriakou had made himself in Word with clip art, the agency seal, and a forged signature of the director, which he then took back for safekeeping on the grounds that being seen with it would get the man killed.

the-grasshopper.title: Prince Muhammad bin Naif
the-grasshopper.summary: Saudi prince, former head of Saudi intelligence and briefly crown prince, described by John Kiriakou as the golden boy of the royal family and the West's preferred successor. He survived an al-Qaeda assassin who detonated a bomb concealed inside his own body at an open house in Riyadh, was decorated at CIA headquarters for surviving it, and was then overthrown and placed under arrest by Muhammad bin Salman.

the-grasshopper.title: Asset acquisition cycle
the-grasshopper.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

the-grasshopper.title: Exchange of bona fides
the-grasshopper.summary: The challenge-and-response protocol taught on the first day of CIA operational training, by which two intelligence officers who have never met establish that they are on the same side — a fixed nonsense phrase answered by a fixed nonsense phrase. Per John Kiriakou it is drilled hard enough that forgetting it under pressure, a staple of spy films, does not happen; if one side does not have the bona fides, "anything goes."

the-grasshopper.title: Agent inducements
the-grasshopper.summary: The non-cash things the CIA can offer a recruited agent — a child's university place anywhere in America, treatment at a top hospital for a sick spouse, or a carefully staged personal gift — and the standing arrangements with universities and large corporations that make them possible.

the-grasshopper.title: The beer and the couch
the-grasshopper.summary: What John Kiriakou says he did with the CIA''s spot-assessment training after leaving the agency. He still sizes up strangers within moments of meeting them, but the question is no longer what they can do for him: it is whether he would want to have a beer with them, and whether, if he were down on his luck, they would let him sleep on their couch.

the-greek-brain-drain.title: The Parthenon-view condo
the-greek-brain-drain.summary: The eighth-floor Athens apartment John Kiriakou has been watching on the Greek property app Spitogatos, whose price fell from €600,000 to €250,000 after the city banned new Airbnb conversions — and the golden-visa buying that had emptied the residential market in the first place.

the-greek-brain-drain.title: The cats of Athens
the-greek-brain-drain.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for why there are no rats in Athens — the enormous population of street cats that tourists feed at restaurant tables — offered as a contrast to Washington, where he says the rats are the size of small dogs.

the-greek-brain-drain.title: Washington, rat central
the-greek-brain-drain.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the rat population of Washington, D.C. — one he saw the size of a small dog, and the night he drove to Southeast Washington at quarter to two in the morning to collect two eighteen-year-olds whose van had been stolen, and found them panicking not about the theft but about the rats eating a sleeping homeless man's toes.

the-greek-brain-drain.title: Astrology at the CIA
the-greek-brain-drain.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that astrology played a role in CIA work in the 1950s and early 1960s as part of MK-ULTRA, alongside time travel and teleportation — and his explanation for why: officials with unlimited budgets and no obligation to report to the public reasoned that there was probably nothing to it, but that if there were, it would make them a star.

the-greek-brain-drain.title: Carrying passports in Washington
the-greek-brain-drain.summary: John Kiriakou's report in September 2025 that people in Washington had begun carrying their passports for fear of being scooped up by immigration enforcement — alongside the case of an American symphony violinist held for three weeks, and his own belief that ethnic profiling violates the Fourth Amendment.

the-greek-brain-drain.title: "Christians are suckers"
the-greek-brain-drain.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for how a president who does not go to church, has no spiritual adviser and could not name a line of scripture can push school prayer without cost — that he thinks most Christians are suckers, an assessment Kiriakou says he hates to make and believes anyway.

the-greek-colonel-and-china.title: The density of spies in Washington
the-greek-colonel-and-china.summary: John Kiriakou's claim that there are more spies in Washington DC than anywhere else in the world, that the FBI's counterintelligence division does nothing but try to root them out, and that the job cannot be finished short of becoming North Korea.

the-greek-colonel-and-china.title: The operational test
the-greek-colonel-and-china.summary: The vetting procedure John Kiriakou describes for moving a trusted source onto normal handling: put a full surveillance team on him without telling him, watch how he gets to the meeting, and then ask him to describe what he did.

the-greek-colonel-and-china.title: Running into former sources
the-greek-colonel-and-china.summary: John Kiriakou has twice met people he once ran as agents by accident, years after leaving the CIA — once at an airport and once in the street — and both times they came to him with a bear hug. One of them was astonished to discover he spoke English.

the-greek-colonel-and-china.title: Sources are not traitors
the-greek-colonel-and-china.summary: Asked whether CIA officers privately regarded their recruited agents as traitors and held them in contempt, John Kiriakou answered that they did not — because the officers believed they were the good guys, and a recruited source had become one of them.

the-greek-colonel-and-china.title: The orb off Yemen
the-greek-colonel-and-china.summary: A leaked video John Kiriakou describes as the most dramatic UFO material he has seen: two F-18s following a silver orb off the coast of Yemen, given permission to fire, and a missile that hits the object and bounces off before the orb turns ninety degrees and flies on.

the-greek-colonel-and-china.title: Prince Andrew
the-greek-colonel-and-china.summary: British royal, now Andrew Mountbatten Windsor, named repeatedly by John Kiriakou as one of the un-recruitable principals whose access made Jeffrey Epstein valuable to a foreign intelligence service. Kiriakou has asked why Andrew was never charged over conduct with minors, reads his alleged provision of classified Ministry of Defence documents to Epstein as evidence of espionage rather than vanity — and expects him to face no criminal consequence at all, because the statute of limitations has run.

the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.title: The Rwanda deportations
the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.summary: The British policy of removing asylum seekers to Rwanda for resettlement, which John Kiriakou cited in 2023 as evidence that the United Kingdom belongs on the list of countries with entrenched right-wing governments — a policy he called right-wing extremist and probably illegal.

the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.title: The Israeli electorate shift
the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.summary: John Kiriakou's structural explanation for why he does not expect Israeli politics to swing back — that the influx of Russian and Ukrainian Jewish immigrants over the preceding ten or fifteen years has moved the electorate so far right that a viable socialist movement or Labour party is, in his view, gone for good.

the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.title: Netanyahu and the Tel Aviv police chief
the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.summary: The July 2023 dismissal of Tel Aviv's police chief, which John Kiriakou identified as the moment Benjamin Netanyahu may have overstepped — arguing that the real threat to the Israeli prime minister came not from the Palestinians but from his own attempt to take over the court system, and from the strikes and demonstrations that had not subsided.

the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.title: Rebetiko music
the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.summary: The Greek genre born in the prisons and opium dens of Constantinople that John Kiriakou reaches for when he is feeling particularly down — one half of a listening diet he describes as classic rock and Greek folk, the music his parents and grandparents played, and which he names as what would bring back his memories if he ever lost them.

the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.title: The Jenin incursion
the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.summary: The Israeli military operation in Jenin of early July 2023, which John Kiriakou cited by its casualty figures — nine Palestinians dead and about a hundred wounded before the withdrawal — and which he called only the very beginning of what the most right-wing government in Israeli history would do.

the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.title: Elliott Abrams
the-greek-neo-nazi-seats.summary: The Reagan-era assistant secretary of state whose 2023 appointment to a Biden administration advisory board John Kiriakou treated as proof that neoliberal and neoconservative foreign policy are the same policy with interchangeable players — a man who pleaded guilty over Iran-Contra, was pardoned, helped sell the Iraqi weapons of mass destruction case, and then served Donald Trump on Iran and Venezuela.

the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.title: Bigger than the Russian embassy
the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.summary: Why American embassies in small, strategically unimportant countries are enormous: the answer John Kiriakou says he was given by a station chief on one of his first CIA trips — that the building had to be bigger than the Soviet one across town. He describes American embassies in Africa as "absolutely gigantic" for that reason alone, and calls the US embassy in Cairo an enormous facility matched by an equally enormous Russian one.

the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.title: Declare victory and go home
the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.summary: The exit John Kiriakou prescribed for Israel in Gaza: turn the territory back to the United Nations, declare Hamas destroyed, declare victory, then engage the Saudis on the Abraham Accords and negotiate a deal later. His reasoning was that nothing remained to destroy, that killing as many people as possible is not a viable policy, and that Israel had no other way out.

the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.title: "Do not ever attempt to contact me again"
the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.summary: The reply John Kiriakou says he received from John Kerry, then Secretary of State, after emailing him privately in the days before reporting to prison to beg that his sentence be commuted. Kiriakou had worked closely with Kerry for two and a half years; the one-line answer, sent after two or three days, was the last he ever heard from him.

the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.title: "Every Israeli I ever knew"
the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the attitudes he encountered among Israelis he knew professionally and socially — that almost every one of them wanted the Palestinians killed or exiled — together with his description of a sensibility he says is palpable walking around Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, and his immediate self-correction when he overstated the claim.

the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.title: Palestine House
the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.summary: The Washington, DC meeting space and gallery for pro-Palestinian human rights groups, artists and musicians that John Kiriakou describes as newly opened on Capitol Hill — housed in a building donated by a Lebanese-American property developer, running programming several nights a week, and headed by Miko Peled.

the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.title: Sanctions and the Russian adjustment
the-greek-offer-for-the-bamiyan-buddhas.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of why sanctions stopped hurting Russia: Sergey Lavrov''s admission that Moscow was caught off balance by the speed of the American response, the three or four weeks that shock lasted, and the discovery that Russia did not need the United States or its banking system once India and China agreed to buy whatever oil it had.

the-greek-turn-toward-israel.title: Ireland recognizes Palestine
the-greek-turn-toward-israel.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the American reaction to Ireland''s recognition of Palestine, which he says he witnessed the aftermath of while in the country: the CIA was indifferent, but the State Department was apoplectic — not about Ireland itself, but about the precedent, which Kiriakou says other European states promptly began to follow.

the-greek-turn-toward-israel.title: The University of Salamanca professorship
the-greek-turn-toward-israel.summary: John Kiriakou's teaching post in the graduate intelligence studies programme at the University of Salamanca, where he lectures on introductory intelligence studies and the history of terrorism, at an institution he describes as older than Spain itself.

the-greek-turn-toward-israel.title: CIA attention to West Africa
the-greek-turn-toward-israel.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer on whether the CIA is likely to be operating in Burkina Faso: for all the years he was at the agency it cared very little about Africa and especially West Africa, but the presence of al-Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates plus the drug trade makes CIA and special forces involvement probable — and, he adds, the American public will not hear about it.

the-greek-turn-toward-israel.title: CIA–FBI incompatible computer systems
the-greek-turn-toward-israel.summary: John Kiriakou's claim that from the CIA's founding in 1947 until 2009 the computer systems of the CIA and the FBI were not compatible with one another — no message could be sent from one to the other and no intelligence shared — which he offers both as the material substrate of the interagency hatred that helped make September 11 possible, and as the gap through which James Mitchell and Bruce Jessen were able to pass Ali Soufan's FBI debriefings of Abu Zubaydah off as the fruits of torture.

the-greek-turn-toward-israel.title: Fake CIA résumés
the-greek-turn-toward-israel.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of being used as a human authenticator in the private sector: at the consulting firm he joined after leaving the CIA, every job applicant claiming agency service was sent to dinner with him, and by his count fully half of them had never set foot inside the CIA.

the-greek-turn-toward-israel.title: Forcing Iran toward a bomb
the-greek-turn-toward-israel.summary: John Kiriakou''s argument that Western pressure risks producing the very outcome it claims to prevent: repeated Israeli assassinations of Iranian scientists and generals and strikes on Iranian sites may eventually leave Ayatollah Khamenei with no choice but to permit a defensive weapon — despite the religious prohibition Kiriakou credits him with maintaining, and despite successive American estimates that Iran is not seeking one.

the-green-room-with-hayden.title: Hayden at the National Press Club
the-green-room-with-hayden.summary: John Kiriakou's account of seeing Michael Hayden, after a series of strokes, at a National Press Club event sponsored by the intelligence centre that bears his name — and the two reactions it produced in him, neither of them satisfaction alone.

the-green-room-with-hayden.title: Cleaning up after Tora Bora
the-green-room-with-hayden.summary: John Kiriakou was not at Tora Bora. He arrived in Pakistan in January 2002, two months after the bombing, and says he went specifically to clean up what the battle had left behind — scavenging material, detaining the fighters too slow to get away, and mapping the smugglers'' valleys the survivors had used to cross. In his account the clean-up was necessary because the encirclement failed: bin Laden, warned by an al-Qaeda operative working as translator to the commander of Central Command, left in the dark dressed as a woman in the back of a pickup truck, and at dawn there was nobody in Tora Bora to surrender.

the-green-room-with-hayden.title: Saddam and the journalists
the-green-room-with-hayden.summary: John Kiriakou's comparison, drawn from fifteen years working the Iraq target at the CIA, between a dictator who hated the press and did not kill it and a government that he says kills journalists deliberately and in numbers.

the-green-room-with-hayden.title: The balloon test
the-green-room-with-hayden.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that Israel had warning of the 7 October 2023 attack — that settlers along the Gaza line had reported training for months, that balloons were sent over as a probe in the days beforehand, and that nothing was done.

the-green-room-with-hayden.title: The book the publisher sat on
the-green-room-with-hayden.summary: The manuscript John Kiriakou says he delivered to his publisher three years before August 2025 and had still not seen printed, and the email he finally sent telling them it was time to fish or cut bait.

the-green-room-with-hayden.title: The Iowa Republican exchange
the-green-room-with-hayden.summary: The argument John Kiriakou says he had at a conservative event with the head of the Iowa Republican Party — an abortion absolutist who answered Kiriakou's challenge on Gaza by calling him pro-Hamas — and how Kiriakou ended it.

the-greenland-prediction.title: Five Eyes
the-greenland-prediction.summary: The intelligence-sharing partnership of the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand

the-greenland-prediction.title: Greenland
the-greenland-prediction.summary: The Danish territory the United States has spent years talking about acquiring; John Kiriakou reports two flatly contradictory readings from his own contacts — a White House friend who says Washington is serious and will lean on a Cold War treaty to claim it is already de facto American, and a Republican friend who says the whole thing is a grenade thrown to distract the press — and warns that taking it by force would end NATO.

the-greenland-prediction.title: The Caracas checklist
the-greenland-prediction.summary: The sequence of steps John Kiriakou says an operation to overthrow the Venezuelan government would run through — pressure Maduro into flight, secure the presidential palace, co-opt or bombard the military, take the television and radio stations, hold the main intersections of the capital — and his insistence that none of it is the hard part.

the-greenland-prediction.title: Central Intelligence Agency
the-greenland-prediction.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

the-greenland-prediction.title: David Hicks
the-greenland-prediction.summary: Australian national captured in Afghanistan in late 2001 and held at Guantanamo, whose case John Kiriakou uses as the measure of what the Australian government can achieve for one of its citizens when it decides to act — and therefore as the indictment of its slowness over Julian Assange.

the-greenland-prediction.title: French intelligence (DGSE)
the-greenland-prediction.summary: The French foreign intelligence service; characterized as exceptionally talented, exceptionally aggressive, and routinely lethal in the conduct of its operations

the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.title: Deep state
the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.summary: John Kiriakou''s position on the deep state — that it is not a right-wing trope but an accurate description of something he served inside for fifteen years at the CIA and two more on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee staff. He is indifferent to the label ("call it the state, call it the federal bureaucracy") and insists on the substance: "It''s there to stay. It''s not going anywhere."

the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.title: Bob Grenier
the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.summary: Career CIA officer who served as station chief in Islamabad before, during, and after 9/11; later associate deputy director of operations for policy support and Iraq Mission Manager; John Kiriakou's boss and, for one year, his supervisor as executive assistant.

the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.title: John Brennan
the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.summary: Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President

the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.title: The MI5 model
the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.summary: The proposal John Kiriakou says was already being discussed with the British in 1992 or 1993 — an American domestic intelligence service on the MI5 pattern, without arrest powers, feeding what it collected on citizens to the FBI — and which he believes the post-January 6 legislation would finally deliver.

the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.title: Jim Pavitt
the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.summary: Long-serving CIA Deputy Director for Operations during the early post-9/11 period; characterized by John Kiriakou as "a legendary officer and a really great guy"; mocked John Brennan openly within the agency for Brennan's recurring stated ambition to head his own intelligence agency.

the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.title: The Taliban
the-grenier-counterinsurgency-op-ed.summary: The Afghan movement John Kiriakou describes as loyal to nobody and, in 2001, genuinely baffled by the American invasion: its leadership held that sheltering al-Qaeda was a cultural obligation to a guest rather than an alliance, that it had never taken up arms against the United States, and that Washington was welcome to fight al-Qaeda on Afghan soil. He supported the Doha peace process but judged the Biden-era power-sharing letter an abandonment, arguing that any deal without guarantees on women, girls'' education and the vote returns the country to the 1990s.

the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.title: The ATF funding rider
the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.summary: The provision John Kiriakou describes as the reason no American felon has had firearm rights restored since the 1990s: a Clinton-era law permitting non-violent, non-drug felons to apply to the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms, paired in the same statute with a bar on any federal money being spent to investigate the applications.

the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.title: Barrett Brown
the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.summary: American journalist and former Anonymous associate whom John Kiriakou describes as one of the most intelligent writers and analysts he has ever encountered, with long-standing mental health problems and a two-decade heroin addiction he has now been clear of for at least a year, expelled from the United Kingdom and relocated to Mexico.

the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.title: Censorship on the left
the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.summary: John Kiriakou''s observation that he was censored far less by Forbes and Fortune than by The Nation and Mother Jones, which he offers as an instance of a general rule that a writer''s own side censors them hardest — the counterpart to Ted Rall''s account of being made to fit a particular kind of leftism rather than any kind.

the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.title: Dr Oz and the Armenian hospices
the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.summary: John Kiriakou''s reaction to a television segment by Mehmet Oz alleging fraud by Armenian-run hospices in Los Angeles — that a man he identifies as a veteran of the Turkish special forces zeroing in on Armenians in California is not a coincidence, and that each of the administration''s appointees appears to arrive with a racial scandal of their own.

the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.title: The Iron Dome
the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.summary: Israel's air-defence system as John Kiriakou reads it — impressive against a wave of slow Iranian drones, but shown by the handful that got through, and later by Iranian ballistic missiles, to be not all it is cracked up to be; each exchange, in his account, buying Iran intelligence about the gaps.

the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.title: James Morris
the-guantanamo-airfare-catch.summary: A close friend of John Kiriakou''s who served seventeen years of a twenty-year sentence for a crime committed at sixteen, found on release that a violent felony conviction closed off employment, made his own way to Turkey and across the border into Syria, spent two years fighting alongside the Kurds against ISIS, and later took his own life.

the-guard-booth-rounds.title: Why he believes Epstein killed himself
the-guard-booth-rounds.summary: John Kiriakou's stated conclusion that Jeffrey Epstein died by suicide, reasoned from his own experience of how federal prison guards actually work rather than from any view of the wider Epstein case.

the-guard-booth-rounds.title: The dorm as a reward
the-guard-booth-rounds.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation that moving a federal prisoner from a cell to a dormitory is a privilege earned over time, and why Ghislaine Maxwell's rapid promotion to dormitory living made no sense to him.

the-guard-booth-rounds.title: Clickers and touchers
the-guard-booth-rounds.summary: The distinction John Kiriakou says prisoners at FCI Loretto drew between convicted sex offenders who had only viewed images of children and those who had travelled across state lines to molest them, and his account of why they are all held at low security.

the-guard-booth-rounds.title: Prince Andrew
the-guard-booth-rounds.summary: British royal, now Andrew Mountbatten Windsor, named repeatedly by John Kiriakou as one of the un-recruitable principals whose access made Jeffrey Epstein valuable to a foreign intelligence service. Kiriakou has asked why Andrew was never charged over conduct with minors, reads his alleged provision of classified Ministry of Defence documents to Epstein as evidence of espionage rather than vanity — and expects him to face no criminal consequence at all, because the statute of limitations has run.

the-guard-booth-rounds.title: The blacked-out grand jury minutes
the-guard-booth-rounds.summary: John Kiriakou on the 119 pages of grand jury minutes released in the Epstein document tranches with every single word blacked out, despite two federal judges having ordered their release.

the-guard-booth-rounds.title: The letter to Larry Nassar
the-guard-booth-rounds.summary: The letter from Jeffrey Epstein to the convicted USA Gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar that John Kiriakou singled out from the released documents, in which Epstein wrote that he would have gone home by the time it arrived and blamed everything on Donald Trump.

the-guardian-smear-series.title: Assange and solitary confinement
the-guardian-smear-series.summary: John Kiriakou's 2018 argument that Julian Assange's isolation inside the Ecuadorian embassy amounted to solitary confinement — a practice the United Nations classes as torture — and that everybody breaks under it eventually, however strong they are.

the-guardian-smear-series.title: "Ecuador is open for business"
the-guardian-smear-series.summary: The Wall Street Journal headline John Kiriakou says appeared the day after he hand-delivered a letter to Ecuador's ambassador in Washington asking that Julian Assange's internet access be restored, and which made him fear Assange was about to be used as a bargaining chip.

the-guardian-smear-series.title: The chain of command argument
the-guardian-smear-series.summary: John Kiriakou's standing rejection of the advice given to new intelligence officers — that evidence of waste, fraud, abuse or illegality should be taken up the chain of command — supported by the fates of Thomas Drake, William Binney, Kirk Wiebe and Diane Roark, and by the fact that his own chain of command had created the torture programme.

the-guardian-smear-series.title: "Embrace it and keep telling it"
the-guardian-smear-series.summary: The advice John Kiriakou says he was given days after his arrest — that he could not hide from the prosecution but had to embrace it, and had to keep telling his side of the story until it became the side of record, because the government would eventually move on to its next target.

the-guardian-smear-series.title: Julian Assange
the-guardian-smear-series.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

the-guardian-smear-series.title: Seventy-two denied motions
the-guardian-smear-series.summary: The count John Kiriakou gives of the pretrial motions filed in his case and denied by Judge Leonie Brinkema — seventy-two denied and none granted — which he offers as the mechanism by which a national security defendant in the Eastern District of Virginia is prevented from mounting a defence at all.

the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.title: Volodymyr Zelensky
the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.summary: Kiriakou says he was told not to discuss Zelensky's corruption publicly, and calls the Oval Office dressing-down of him set up in advance.

the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.title: Lindsey Graham
the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.summary: Republican senator from South Carolina who died in July 2026, and John Kiriakou's standing shorthand for the permanent war caucus — a "show horse" rather than a workhorse, a "chameleon" who "never saw a war that he didn't want to jump into with both feet," and, on posthumously released documentary footage, a man offering the US Air Force to bomb a country America was not at war with.

the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.title: Major non-NATO ally status for Ukraine
the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.summary: John Kiriakou''s forecast of how the Russian demand that Ukraine never join NATO can be met without leaving Ukraine unprotected: the designation of major non-NATO ally, already held by Australia, Japan, South Korea, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, which he says confers essentially the same rights without the membership.

the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.title: Nord Stream pipeline sabotage
the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.summary: The 2022 destruction of the Nord Stream gas pipelines, whose responsibility John Kiriakou treats as genuinely unresolved — citing Seymour Hersh's reporting that the CIA did it, a later Ukrainian special-forces claim of a sailboat-based operation carried out without Zelensky's knowledge, and a retired CIA colleague's private theory that Putin blew up his own pipeline to blame the Americans.

the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.title: Operation Spiderweb
the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.summary: The Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's strategic bomber fleet in June 2025, which John Kiriakou calls a brilliant operation and — against Volodymyr Zelensky's account — one Ukraine could not have run alone. Eighteen months of preparation, drones smuggled across eleven time zones by human couriers, and command from Kyiv all required outside help, he argues; and Donald Trump's uncharacteristic public silence afterwards is his evidence that Washington was in on it.

the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.title: Russia-Ukraine war origins
the-gur-sbu-gun-battle.summary: John Kiriakou's account that the war began in 2014, not 2022 — rooted in broken U.S. promises that NATO would not expand to Russia's borders, the 2014 removal of a pro-Russian Ukrainian leader, and the seizure of Crimea; he says Russia is now winning and has no reason to negotiate.

the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.title: Composition of the Saudi military
the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.summary: John Kiriakou's long-standing claim that there are almost no Saudi nationals in the Saudi armed forces below the most senior ranks, and that the rank and file are Pakistanis hired from among Pakistan's poor. He treats it as a standing joke in the Gulf and as a limit on what Saudi Arabia can contribute to any war with Iran.

the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.title: 2026 Iran war economic shock
the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.summary: John Kiriakou''s running assessment of the economic damage from the 2026 Iran war — an oil shock he says already exceeds both 1970s shocks combined, a natural-gas shock worse than the Nord Stream destruction, and a chokepoint problem that runs through fertilizer as much as fuel, since 65% of the world''s supply must transit the Strait of Hormuz. His summary: "This is an economic slowdown of choice."

the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.title: Advice to an aspiring intelligence analyst
the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to a 21-year-old student asking what to study and what to read: pick a geographic area, become the go-to person on it, and consume everything published in the field — including the journals written by people who have never made policy.

the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.title: Air wars are overrated
the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.summary: John Kiriakou''s summary judgement on the 2026 Iran and Lebanon campaigns, delivered as the meta-headline of the whole war: air power flattened Gaza without destroying Hamas, is bogging down against Hezbollah, and cannot produce the outcome the war requires.

the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.title: Asian fuel reserves, 2026
the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.summary: The effect of the Strait of Hormuz closure on oil-importing Asian economies as John Kiriakou described it — countries counting their remaining fuel in days rather than months, with no substitute supply available, and economies he expects simply to stop.

the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.title: The CIA Insider's Guide to Surveillance and Surveillance Detection
the-hajj-ban-as-leverage.summary: Book by John Kiriakou drawing on his experience as a surveillance detection instructor at the CIA and as a private surveillance training consultant. The book covers the techniques used by intelligence professionals to identify whether they are being followed — including the four-phase surveillance detection route, concealment device placement and retrieval, and counter-surveillance strategy — adapted for use by corporate executives, journalists, and others who want to confirm whether they are being followed.

the-hall-of-states.title: Phil Donahue
the-hall-of-states.summary: American talk-show host who, John Kiriakou discovered seven years after the fact, had been secretly paying his weekly newspaper column fee — $400 a week for nine years, routed through Reader Supported News — because Donahue had learned that Kiriakou came out of prison broke and did not want him sleeping in his car.

the-hall-of-states.title: The Washington Post under Bezos
the-hall-of-states.summary: John Kiriakou''s running account of the decline of a newspaper he subscribes to and no longer recognises — an editorial board he says has gone wholly right-wing and obsequious to its owner, foreign bureaus and sports and local coverage cut back, a comment of his own rejected for criticising Jeff Bezos, and his own short list of what he would want the paper to be instead.

the-hall-of-states.title: Soviet Union
the-hall-of-states.summary: The superpower whose collapse framed the start of John Kiriakou's CIA career — it was "literally in the process of collapsing" when he joined in January 1990, ushering in a brief "peace dividend" era when the agency's new threats were environmental degradation and AIDS. Kiriakou cites Brzezinski's "Afghan trap" that lured the Soviets into Afghanistan, argues the U.S. abandoned the radicalized mujahideen the moment the Soviets were beaten, notes America then took "a vacation from history," and recalls that Jonathan Pollard's stolen documents were traded by Israel to the Soviets in exchange for Russian Jews.

the-hall-of-states.title: The Alaska glacier
the-hall-of-states.summary: The visitor centre John Kiriakou saw on a 2016 trip to Alaska with Gary Johnson, built at the foot of a glacier close enough to touch from the observation deck and by then a quarter of a mile away from it — an image he uses as the plainest available demonstration of climate change, and one he refuses to let pass as a joke.

the-hall-of-states.title: The armour at Union Station
the-hall-of-states.summary: John Kiriakou''s eyewitness account of stepping off an Amtrak train at Washington''s Union Station in August 2025 to find two armoured personnel carriers and a .50 calibre machine gun trained on the entrance — and of tourists posing for photographs with the National Guardsmen deployed in the parts of the city where, he says, there is no crime.

the-hall-of-states.title: The CIA and Iridium
the-hall-of-states.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the Central Intelligence Agency buying the satellite telephone company Iridium when it was unprofitable and about to go out of business, because the agency needed the network — a purchase he places alongside its acquisition of Intelsat, and which he encountered personally when he had to rent the phones for Afghanistan.

the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.title: The Saudi request on Gaddafi
the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.summary: John Kiriakou's account of an approach by Saudi Arabia to the CIA asking that Muammar Gaddafi be overthrown by any means necessary, with Riyadh offering to pay for everything — a request he says was declined, and which lapsed only when Gaddafi announced he would turn his attention from the Middle East to African unity.

the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.title: Quoted on NPR
the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.summary: John Kiriakou's discovery, via a standing Google alert on his own name, that National Public Radio had cited a DeProgram discussion between him and Ted Rall in an article on Palestinians killed while waiting for food — an outlet he had walked out on years earlier.

the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.title: The Addis Ababa zoo
the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.summary: A visit John Kiriakou made to the zoo in Addis Ababa on a free half-day, where he watched keepers force a screaming donkey into the lion enclosure — and noted the two-tier admission price charged to foreigners.

the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.title: The boring cover story
the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.summary: The CIA training principle John Kiriakou says governed how officers described their jobs to strangers: pick something so dull that nobody asks a second question. His own standard answer was the foreign service, training work, and some import-export negotiation.

the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.title: The election day 1992 poll
the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.summary: An informal show of hands taken in a CIA branch office on election day 1992, which John Kiriakou describes as the moment he discovered he had no idea of the politics of the colleagues he sat three feet away from — and that he was not, as he had assumed, the only progressive in the room.

the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.title: Air India Flight 182
the-hannity-lockerbie-exchange.summary: The 1985 bombing of a Boeing 747 over the Atlantic, which John Kiriakou has attributed to the government of India in the course of arguing that state sponsorship of terrorism is not confined to the countries formally designated for it.

the-hardtalk-interview.title: Espionage Act
the-hardtalk-interview.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

the-hardtalk-interview.title: Senate Torture Report
the-hardtalk-interview.summary: The December 2014 executive summary of the U.S. Senate Select Committee on Intelligence's study of the CIA's post-9/11 detention and interrogation program; the first public disclosure of techniques including rectal feeding with hummus, sexual assault with broomsticks, and prolonged sleep deprivation.

the-hardtalk-interview.title: David Petraeus
the-hardtalk-interview.summary: Retired U.S. Army general and director of the CIA who, per John Kiriakou, confirmed the names of ten covert CIA operatives to his biographer and girlfriend and was never criminally charged — a contrast Kiriakou cites repeatedly as proof that his own prosecution under the Intelligence Identities Protection Act was selective. Kiriakou''s explanation for the disparity: Petraeus had not blown the whistle on the torture program and embarrassed the agency.

the-hardtalk-interview.title: John Brennan
the-hardtalk-interview.summary: Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President

the-hardtalk-interview.title: The philosophy class
