the-isi-as-two-organizations.summary: Pakistani politician; twice Prime Minister of Pakistan; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as personally corrupt and married to an even more corrupt husband

the-isi-as-two-organizations.title: Bin Laden health rumors
the-isi-as-two-organizations.summary: John Kiriakou's dismissal of the claim that Osama bin Laden died years before the 2011 raid. He says the CIA received a steady stream of medical rumours about him — kidney failure, dialysis in a cave, a spinal disorder — none of which turned out to be true, and that bin Laden was in fine health apart from arthritis and a hip problem until the day he died.

the-isi-as-two-organizations.title: Fake CIA résumés
the-isi-as-two-organizations.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of being used as a human authenticator in the private sector: at the consulting firm he joined after leaving the CIA, every job applicant claiming agency service was sent to dinner with him, and by his count fully half of them had never set foot inside the CIA.

the-isi-mossad-relationship.title: Pakistani troops for Gaza
the-isi-mossad-relationship.summary: The proposal, floated by Israel and Saudi Arabia in late 2025, to send some 20,000 Pakistani peacekeepers into Gaza — which John Kiriakou thought might be a good idea on cultural and religious grounds, and thought Israel would never permit, because a country that will not let journalists in will not let foreign Muslim troops in either.

the-isi-mossad-relationship.title: Pacific island peacekeepers
the-isi-mossad-relationship.summary: John Kiriakou's observation that small Pacific states such as Fiji supply a disproportionate share of the world's peacekeeping forces because the pay makes up a large part of their national budgets — and his argument that this makes them cultural strangers wherever they deploy.

the-isi-mossad-relationship.title: Abraham Accords
the-isi-mossad-relationship.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

the-isi-mossad-relationship.title: The Imran Khan apology demand
the-isi-mossad-relationship.summary: The demand issued by Imran Khan's party in late October 2025 that John Kiriakou apologise in writing to Khan, to the party and to the Pakistani people over a single sentence he had given an Indian outlet — that India would win a conventional war because it has five times the population — together with his refusal, the death threats, his lawyer's advice, and the blanket policy on South Asian media he adopted afterwards.

the-isi-mossad-relationship.title: There are denials and then there are denials
the-isi-mossad-relationship.summary: John Kiriakou's rule for reading official statements — that 'we have no such plans' is not a denial, because nothing counts as a plan until a head of government signs off on it, leaving a government free to discuss and even prepare something it can still credibly say it has no plans for.

the-isi-mossad-relationship.title: The CIA's internal social culture
the-isi-mossad-relationship.summary: John Kiriakou's one-word characterisation of the agency's internal culture — "incestuous" — describing a club for every conceivable interest, actively encouraged officer-to-officer romances, and a design intent that officers should have no need of friends or activities outside the building.

the-islamabad-guest-house.title: The best meal overseas
the-islamabad-guest-house.summary: Asked for the best meals he had eaten abroad, John Kiriakou named first a dish cooked by a young Pakistani in a CIA guest house in Islamabad — shaved beef, a myriad of spices, hot green chillies and rice cooked in chicken stock — followed by sushi in Tokyo and the Lenten table of Clean Monday in Greece.

the-islamabad-guest-house.title: The dandelion salad
the-islamabad-guest-house.summary: The meal John Kiriakou assembled in the yard at FCI Loretto from foraged dandelions, commissary olive oil and sea salt, instant rice, a bouillon cube, peanuts, borrowed Sazón and a bag of chicken — which he calls the single most satisfying meal of his twenty-three months in prison.

the-islamabad-guest-house.title: Narcotics under cover
the-islamabad-guest-house.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to whether a CIA officer under cover may take drugs when an asset offers them: yes. The rule he describes begins with qat in Yemen and extends to cocaine in Latin America, on the ground that refusing can be a matter of life and death.

the-islamabad-guest-house.title: Qat in Yemen
the-islamabad-guest-house.summary: The afternoon shrub-chewing habit of Yemen, and the special dispensation the CIA had to issue so that its officers could take part in it. John Kiriakou explains that no source could be developed in a qat-chewing country by an officer who would not chew.

the-islamabad-guest-house.title: Spies traded home
the-islamabad-guest-house.summary: What happens to intelligence officers and agents after they are exchanged and sent back, in John Kiriakou''s account: not usually execution, but a career that is irreparably damaged, because every service you would want to hide from now knows exactly who you are.

the-islamabad-guest-house.title: A Middle East reading list
the-islamabad-guest-house.summary: The books and the starting point John Kiriakou recommends to anyone trying to understand the modern Middle East: begin at the end of the Second World War, not five thousand years earlier, and start with The House of Saud, the Sykes-Picot Agreement and From Beirut to Jerusalem.

the-israeli-electorate-shift.title: Netanyahu and the Tel Aviv police chief
the-israeli-electorate-shift.summary: The July 2023 dismissal of Tel Aviv's police chief, which John Kiriakou identified as the moment Benjamin Netanyahu may have overstepped — arguing that the real threat to the Israeli prime minister came not from the Palestinians but from his own attempt to take over the court system, and from the strikes and demonstrations that had not subsided.

the-israeli-electorate-shift.title: The Greek neo-Nazi seats
the-israeli-electorate-shift.summary: John Kiriakou''s tally of the June 2023 Greek parliamentary election, which he treats as the most disturbing case of a Europe-wide trend: eight parties won seats, six of them right-wing, four of them right-wing extremist, and two of them neo-Nazi parties taking thirteen seats between them.

the-israeli-electorate-shift.title: The Jenin incursion
the-israeli-electorate-shift.summary: The Israeli military operation in Jenin of early July 2023, which John Kiriakou cited by its casualty figures — nine Palestinians dead and about a hundred wounded before the withdrawal — and which he called only the very beginning of what the most right-wing government in Israeli history would do.

the-israeli-electorate-shift.title: The Rwanda deportations
the-israeli-electorate-shift.summary: The British policy of removing asylum seekers to Rwanda for resettlement, which John Kiriakou cited in 2023 as evidence that the United Kingdom belongs on the list of countries with entrenched right-wing governments — a policy he called right-wing extremist and probably illegal.

the-israeli-electorate-shift.title: Elliott Abrams
the-israeli-electorate-shift.summary: The Reagan-era assistant secretary of state whose 2023 appointment to a Biden administration advisory board John Kiriakou treated as proof that neoliberal and neoconservative foreign policy are the same policy with interchangeable players — a man who pleaded guilty over Iran-Contra, was pardoned, helped sell the Iraqi weapons of mass destruction case, and then served Donald Trump on Iran and Venezuela.

the-israeli-electorate-shift.title: Frances Haugen
the-israeli-electorate-shift.summary: The Facebook employee John Kiriakou refuses to call a whistleblower — arguing that against the legal definition, bringing to light waste, fraud, abuse, illegality or threats to public health or safety, she qualifies as a corporate spokesperson whose motive was to improve the company's bottom line, not to expose wrongdoing.

the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.title: The "spell your name" briefing
the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.summary: The first time John Kiriakou dealt with the Israeli services: eight weeks into his CIA career, giving the junior slot in a liaison briefing on Saddam Hussein''s state of mind, he was interrupted by a Mossad representative who asked him to spell his name and then told him he was Jewish. Kiriakou''s reply — that he was not recruitable — became one of his recurring illustrations of the liaison relationship.

the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.title: The Jerusalem harassment campaign
the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of what happened to a CIA colleague and his wife during a declared two-year State Department rotation in Jerusalem: furniture rearranged after one embassy party, all three toilets in the house defecated in after another, and, before they left, the family dog''s tail cut off and bandaged. Kiriakou presents the three break-ins as routine rather than exceptional.

the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.title: Gulf secret prisons for hire
the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.summary: Asked whether the CIA knew of Gulf royals operating underground torture facilities and secret prisons, John Kiriakou answered that it did — one hundred per cent — then refused to give details, saying he would risk returning to prison. He described the arrangement instead: the United States sought out these countries precisely because they had no parliament and no free press to answer to, and paid for the use of their cells.

the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.title: AIPAC
the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.title: CIA attention to West Africa
the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer on whether the CIA is likely to be operating in Burkina Faso: for all the years he was at the agency it cared very little about Africa and especially West Africa, but the presence of al-Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates plus the drug trade makes CIA and special forces involvement probable — and, he adds, the American public will not hear about it.

the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.title: CIA–FBI incompatible computer systems
the-israeli-listening-devices-ban.summary: John Kiriakou's claim that from the CIA's founding in 1947 until 2009 the computer systems of the CIA and the FBI were not compatible with one another — no message could be sent from one to the other and no intelligence shared — which he offers both as the material substrate of the interagency hatred that helped make September 11 possible, and as the gap through which James Mitchell and Bruce Jessen were able to pass Ali Soufan's FBI debriefings of Abu Zubaydah off as the fruits of torture.

the-israelis-are-free-agents.title: Alan Dershowitz
the-israelis-are-free-agents.summary: American attorney and Harvard Law professor; John Kiriakou describes debating him on Piers Morgan's show over Jeffrey Epstein, telling Dershowitz he would have wanted to see him "hanging from a tree" had he sought leniency for Epstein as an Israeli spy — and cites attorney David Boies's on-air statement that Dershowitz was far more than Epstein's lawyer, also serving as his publicist, friend, and a guest on Epstein's island.

the-israelis-are-free-agents.title: Jeffrey Epstein
the-israelis-are-free-agents.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

the-israelis-are-free-agents.title: Jonathan Pollard
the-israelis-are-free-agents.summary: U.S. Navy civilian intelligence analyst convicted in 1985 of spying for Israel; the canonical proven case of Israeli espionage against the United States; cited by John Kiriakou in his 2024 Piers Morgan debate with a former Mossad director who denied any Israeli spying on the U.S.

the-israelis-are-free-agents.title: Signal and the parking lot
the-israelis-are-free-agents.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how a clandestine source is actually contacted — an innocuous telephone question with a pre-agreed answer standing for a time and a place fixed in advance, and a physical signal such as the flowerpot on Bob Woodward's balcony — offered as the reason investigators looking for an email trail between a service and its agent will not find one.

the-israelis-are-free-agents.title: Epstein and more than one service
the-israelis-are-free-agents.summary: John Kiriakou's revision of his own position after the release of a further tranche of Epstein documents — that while he continues to believe Jeffrey Epstein was working for the Israelis, the papers indicate he was probably also working for the British, probably for the Americans, and possibly for the Germans.

the-israelis-are-free-agents.title: The Israelis were off limits
the-israelis-are-free-agents.summary: John Kiriakou's flat denial, given on a televised panel, that the CIA collected against Israel in return — 'the Israelis were off limits to us at the CIA. We were not permitted' — and Alan Dershowitz's refusal to believe it.

the-israelis-were-off-limits.title: The counterintelligence report that stopped
the-israelis-were-off-limits.summary: John Kiriakou's account of an annual FBI assessment of the worst counterintelligence threats to the United States that named Russia, China and Israel every year, reported each time by Newsweek's Jeff Stein — until, he says, Dianne Feinstein changed the rules so that the report no longer had to be issued.

the-israelis-were-off-limits.title: The hundred and eighty-seven Israeli officers
the-israelis-were-off-limits.summary: The figure John Kiriakou gives for undeclared Israeli intelligence officers working clandestinely in the United States when he joined the CIA around 1990 — 187 identified by the FBI, over and above the one declared Mossad officer and one declared Shin Bet officer at the Israeli embassy.

the-israelis-were-off-limits.title: The Israelis are free agents
the-israelis-were-off-limits.summary: John Kiriakou's formulation of Israel as an intelligence partner whose cooperation is conditional rather than allied — friendly when it suits, and equally willing to deal with Russia, China or Germany — offered as the reason an Israeli-run source could end up passing American information to a service hostile to the United States, and given each time with an acknowledgement that saying it brings him threats.

the-israelis-were-off-limits.title: Alan Dershowitz
the-israelis-were-off-limits.summary: American attorney and Harvard Law professor; John Kiriakou describes debating him on Piers Morgan's show over Jeffrey Epstein, telling Dershowitz he would have wanted to see him "hanging from a tree" had he sought leniency for Epstein as an Israeli spy — and cites attorney David Boies's on-air statement that Dershowitz was far more than Epstein's lawyer, also serving as his publicist, friend, and a guest on Epstein's island.

the-israelis-were-off-limits.title: MOSSAD
the-israelis-were-off-limits.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

the-israelis-were-off-limits.title: Alexander Acosta and the sweetheart deal
the-israelis-were-off-limits.summary: The US attorney who gave Jeffrey Epstein his 2006 non-prosecution agreement and later said he had been ordered to — a chain of command John Kiriakou traces upward to an attorney general famous for his powerlessness, and therefore to somebody above him whom nobody has ever named.

the-istanbul-peace-talks.title: Kiriakou's Ukraine settlement prediction
the-istanbul-peace-talks.summary: The endgame John Kiriakou forecast in June 2025 and calls deliberately unbold: Russia keeps the disputed eastern territories and Crimea, Ukraine never joins NATO but probably joins the European Union, and Moscow gets ninety per cent of what it wanted. The one demand he expects Russia to trade away is denazification, which he reads as propaganda rather than policy.

the-istanbul-peace-talks.title: Assange and the European Court of Human Rights
the-istanbul-peace-talks.summary: The last legal avenue John Kiriakou identified for Julian Assange in 2022 — three precedents in which the Strasbourg court refused to let Britain extradite mentally ill defendants to American solitary confinement — and the procedural trap that made it useless: Britain said the appeal need not halt the extradition.

the-istanbul-peace-talks.title: Pan Quake
the-istanbul-peace-talks.summary: An open-source, nonprofit, advertising-free social media platform hosted in Iceland on geothermal power and built on a content blockchain, conceived by Suzie Dawson and promoted by John Kiriakou as a brand ambassador from 2021. Kiriakou described its offshore incorporation and subscription model as deliberate defences against the attacks he expected from the CIA and NSA, and later said its Icelandic bank account was frozen at the FBI's request over the platform's association with Julian Assange supporters.

the-istanbul-peace-talks.title: Russia-Ukraine war origins
the-istanbul-peace-talks.summary: John Kiriakou's account that the war began in 2014, not 2022 — rooted in broken U.S. promises that NATO would not expand to Russia's borders, the 2014 removal of a pro-Russian Ukrainian leader, and the seizure of Crimea; he says Russia is now winning and has no reason to negotiate.

the-istanbul-peace-talks.title: Sealing the courtroom
the-istanbul-peace-talks.summary: The physical measures John Kiriakou describes as accompanying a classified-information trial: plastic sheeting and duct tape over the windows so lasers cannot read the vibrations, white noise in the vestibule, and the clearing of everyone but the judge, jury, bailiff, clerk, lawyers and defendant.

the-istanbul-peace-talks.title: The jury consultant's advice
the-istanbul-peace-talks.summary: What John Kiriakou''s jury consultant told him about a national security trial in the Eastern District of Virginia: that in any other district in America he would say fight and win, but in that one, "buddy, you don''t have a prayer. Take the deal."

the-italian-schoolchildren.title: Embassy movie night
the-italian-schoolchildren.summary: The weekly diversion John Kiriakou remembers from his posting to Pakistan after September 11th, when the station worked seven days a week and fourteen hours a day: on Wednesday nights the ambassador hosted a film in the embassy''s small theatre, and the audience shouted at the screen and threw popcorn at whatever they had managed to get hold of.

the-italian-schoolchildren.title: The stapler in the Dirksen building
the-italian-schoolchildren.summary: An incident John Kiriakou witnessed while serving as a senior staff member on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee: a Democratic senator threw a stapler at a staff member in a hallway of the Dirksen Senate Office Building, swore at him, and then looked around to see who had seen it.

the-italian-schoolchildren.title: 2026 Iran war
the-italian-schoolchildren.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-italian-schoolchildren.title: Lindsey Graham
the-italian-schoolchildren.summary: Republican senator from South Carolina who died in July 2026, and John Kiriakou's standing shorthand for the permanent war caucus — a "show horse" rather than a workhorse, a "chameleon" who "never saw a war that he didn't want to jump into with both feet," and, on posthumously released documentary footage, a man offering the US Air Force to bomb a country America was not at war with.

the-italian-schoolchildren.title: The DNC in debt
the-italian-schoolchildren.summary: John Kiriakou''s July 2026 summary of the Democratic National Committee''s finances, drawn from New York Times reporting: two million dollars in debt against Republican reserves of $130 million, vendors asked to hold their invoices until after the elections, the party headquarters pledged as loan collateral, and a chairman who threw his phone at a junior aide.

the-italian-schoolchildren.title: The Espionage Act and the Rosenbergs
the-italian-schoolchildren.summary: John Kiriakou''s short legislative history of the Espionage Act: written in 1917 to counter German saboteurs, slightly amended in 1950 after the execution of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, and never meaningfully updated since. It does not use the words classified information, because the classification system did not exist when it was drafted.

the-january-6-pipe-bomber.title: Coffee with a cabinet member
the-january-6-pipe-bomber.summary: John Kiriakou's disclosure that he had coffee with a member of the cabinet who told him to be patient about his pardon — and told him to watch what he said. He reports the meeting while stating plainly that there is nothing further he can do to make his case, and that he is not confident the outcome will be decided on justice.

the-january-6-pipe-bomber.title: Ed Martin and the pardon file
the-january-6-pipe-bomber.summary: The US pardon attorney whose office John Kiriakou directed supporters to write to, and the message a mutual friend brought back from him: that he was the third person that day to call about Kiriakou, that Kiriakou should relax, and that his file was literally on Martin''s desk. Kiriakou''s advice to letter-writers was to send physical mail rather than email.

the-january-6-pipe-bomber.title: Lincoln's candlelight pardons
the-january-6-pipe-bomber.summary: The historical contrast John Kiriakou drew while discussing a mass grant of clemency: stories of Abraham Lincoln staying up late into the night pardoning Civil War deserters by candlelight, on the principle that nobody should be executed for cowardice — set against a modern president who Kiriakou says has pardoned more people than anyone in American history, whenever the mood strikes him.

the-january-6-pipe-bomber.title: Pardons nobody asked for
the-january-6-pipe-bomber.summary: Two cases John Kiriakou cites of people pardoned without applying: the Binance founder, who said publicly that he had never met the president, never asked for a pardon and never applied for one; and Darryl Strawberry, a New York Mets great with tax and drug problems behind him. Kiriakou raises both while waiting, unsuccessfully, for a pardon he has actively sought for years.

the-january-6-pipe-bomber.title: Sergey Lavrov
the-january-6-pipe-bomber.summary: Russian foreign minister, and previously Russian ambassador to the United Nations during John Kiriakou's assignment there, where the two worked the same Security Council. Kiriakou describes him as the most admired diplomat in the building — the most powerful, important and strategic ambassador there despite operating with far smaller resources than his American, British, French and Chinese counterparts, and better than most of the American diplomats Kiriakou worked for. When Lavrov was abruptly sidelined in late 2025, Kiriakou's reading was retirement rather than disgrace.

the-january-6-pipe-bomber.title: "Stefanik will not be governor"
the-january-6-pipe-bomber.summary: John Kiriakou's flat, on-the-record prediction about the New York governor's race, made against a friend he describes as irrationally conservative who insisted the contest would turn on a single issue — the right to carry a gun. Kiriakou called it the most ridiculous thing he had heard the man say, and argued that Elise Stefanik's political career is finished.

the-jay-jones-texts.title: Jason Miyares
the-jay-jones-texts.summary: The Cuban-born Republican attorney general of Virginia whom John Kiriakou expected to be a right-wing disaster and found instead to be excellent — a judgement he says is hard for him to make about a conservative Republican, and which he repeated on the night Miyares was unceremoniously thrown out of office.

the-jay-jones-texts.title: Abigail Spanberger
the-jay-jones-texts.summary: Governor of Virginia from 2025 and, before Congress, a CIA officer alongside John Kiriakou in the Counterterrorism Center — whom he calls a perfectly nice person who would have been a middle-of-the-road Republican in the 1970s and 1980s, and whose victory speech, to his surprise, said all the right things.

the-jay-jones-texts.title: Joe Rogan
the-jay-jones-texts.summary: The podcast host whose show John Kiriakou finally sat for in October 2025 — an experience that began with signing a non-disclosure agreement and ended with his verdict that Rogan is "a nice guy, very down to earth, very normal." The first thing Rogan asked, walking into the studio ten minutes late: "Hey, do you know my friend Mike Baker?" Kiriakou defends Rogan as unfairly characterized as a right-winger, and had long cited the show as the venue where Zuckerberg admitted Facebook suppressed the Hunter Biden laptop story at the FBI''s behest.

the-jay-jones-texts.title: Winsome Earle-Sears and the machine gun
the-jay-jones-texts.summary: John Kiriakou's verdict on the lieutenant governor of Virginia who ran for the top job in 2025 — that she is a nut, that her earlier campaign photographs showed her smiling and holding a machine gun, and that at the gubernatorial debate she had to be repeatedly slapped down for talking over her opponent.

the-jay-jones-texts.title: Destroying the Dome of the Rock
the-jay-jones-texts.summary: John Kiriakou's agreement with Tucker Carlson that a Zionist extremist plan to demolish the Dome of the Rock and build a third temple would be the event that starts the Third World War — and his additional prediction that it would also be the beginning of the end for the Israeli government and all of its support.

the-jay-jones-texts.title: No declaration of war since 1941
the-jay-jones-texts.summary: John Kiriakou's answer to whether Congress will assert its authority over military action against Venezuela — an unqualified no, resting on the fact that the last declaration of war was on 8 December 1941 and that even the Gulf War was fought on an authorisation to use force rather than a declaration.

the-jenin-incursion.title: Netanyahu and the Tel Aviv police chief
the-jenin-incursion.summary: The July 2023 dismissal of Tel Aviv's police chief, which John Kiriakou identified as the moment Benjamin Netanyahu may have overstepped — arguing that the real threat to the Israeli prime minister came not from the Palestinians but from his own attempt to take over the court system, and from the strikes and demonstrations that had not subsided.

the-jenin-incursion.title: The Israeli electorate shift
the-jenin-incursion.summary: John Kiriakou's structural explanation for why he does not expect Israeli politics to swing back — that the influx of Russian and Ukrainian Jewish immigrants over the preceding ten or fifteen years has moved the electorate so far right that a viable socialist movement or Labour party is, in his view, gone for good.

the-jenin-incursion.title: The Greek neo-Nazi seats
the-jenin-incursion.summary: John Kiriakou''s tally of the June 2023 Greek parliamentary election, which he treats as the most disturbing case of a Europe-wide trend: eight parties won seats, six of them right-wing, four of them right-wing extremist, and two of them neo-Nazi parties taking thirteen seats between them.

the-jenin-incursion.title: The Rwanda deportations
the-jenin-incursion.summary: The British policy of removing asylum seekers to Rwanda for resettlement, which John Kiriakou cited in 2023 as evidence that the United Kingdom belongs on the list of countries with entrenched right-wing governments — a policy he called right-wing extremist and probably illegal.

the-jenin-incursion.title: Elliott Abrams
the-jenin-incursion.summary: The Reagan-era assistant secretary of state whose 2023 appointment to a Biden administration advisory board John Kiriakou treated as proof that neoliberal and neoconservative foreign policy are the same policy with interchangeable players — a man who pleaded guilty over Iran-Contra, was pardoned, helped sell the Iraqi weapons of mass destruction case, and then served Donald Trump on Iran and Venezuela.

the-jenin-incursion.title: Frances Haugen
the-jenin-incursion.summary: The Facebook employee John Kiriakou refuses to call a whistleblower — arguing that against the legal definition, bringing to light waste, fraud, abuse, illegality or threats to public health or safety, she qualifies as a corporate spokesperson whose motive was to improve the company's bottom line, not to expose wrongdoing.

the-jerusalem-bluff.title: Abu Omar rendition
the-jerusalem-bluff.summary: The CIA's kidnapping of a Milan cleric, Abu Omar, who was sent to Egypt to be tortured; John Kiriakou calls it a case that ought to be taught at the CIA as how not to run a rendition, and it is what ultimately sent him to prison, after he confirmed a former colleague's surname to a journalist claiming to be writing a book about it.

the-jerusalem-bluff.title: Brian Ross
the-jerusalem-bluff.summary: American investigative journalist and seven-time Emmy Award winner who was a prominent reporter at ABC News when, in December 2007, he conducted the on-camera interview with John Kiriakou that produced the first public confirmation by a U.S. official that the CIA waterboarded prisoners. Per Kiriakou, Ross called him out of the blue with the assertion that a source said Kiriakou had personally tortured Abu Zubaydah; Kiriakou's decision to give the interview anyway — driven by the conclusion that 'Brian Ross's source is at the White House and they're going to pin this on me' — became the pivot point of his entire post-CIA life.

the-jerusalem-bluff.title: Gavin Newsom
the-jerusalem-bluff.summary: The California governor John Kiriakou described in 2023 as the consummate Democratic Party insider waiting his turn — a Pelosi relative who married into the Brown family, doing everything the Biden operation asked of him, including a pointless surrogate trip to Idaho, on the calculation that Joe Biden would not reach the nominating convention.

the-jerusalem-bluff.title: Human Rights Watch
the-jerusalem-bluff.summary: The organization whose 2005 report that the CIA was torturing its prisoners — two years before John Kiriakou''s ABC interview — anchors his defense that he confirmed rather than revealed the program. It is also the middle link in the chain that ended in his arrest: working with the John Adams Project, Human Rights Watch employed the investigator who carried a classified name from journalist Matthew Cole to the Guantánamo defense attorneys, and when the FBI walked that chain backwards it arrived at Kiriakou''s door.

the-jerusalem-bluff.title: Jim Jordan
the-jerusalem-bluff.summary: Republican congressman from Ohio and chairman of the House Judiciary Committee. John Kiriakou describes a genuinely divided view of him: one of only four members of Congress he names as a friend of whistleblowers, and simultaneously the chairman whose Weaponization subcommittee he says is a partisan counterfeit of the Church Committee — with the whole question settled against Jordan by the Ohio State wrestlers who told him their team doctor was abusing them.

the-jerusalem-bluff.title: Jon Ossoff
the-jerusalem-bluff.summary: United States senator from Georgia, whom John Kiriakou places among the rare honest figures on Capitol Hill and grades at the top of his case-officer rankings. Kiriakou also notes a family connection to the wartime liberation of Greece.

the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.title: The Israeli listening devices ban
the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.summary: Why Mossad and Shin Bet representatives were barred from CIA headquarters, per John Kiriakou: the gifts they brought to liaison meetings kept turning up with listening devices and batteries embedded inside, so the agency stopped admitting them and rented meeting space in Virginia instead.

the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.title: The "spell your name" briefing
the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.summary: The first time John Kiriakou dealt with the Israeli services: eight weeks into his CIA career, giving the junior slot in a liaison briefing on Saddam Hussein''s state of mind, he was interrupted by a Mossad representative who asked him to spell his name and then told him he was Jewish. Kiriakou''s reply — that he was not recruitable — became one of his recurring illustrations of the liaison relationship.

the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.title: Gulf secret prisons for hire
the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.summary: Asked whether the CIA knew of Gulf royals operating underground torture facilities and secret prisons, John Kiriakou answered that it did — one hundred per cent — then refused to give details, saying he would risk returning to prison. He described the arrangement instead: the United States sought out these countries precisely because they had no parliament and no free press to answer to, and paid for the use of their cells.

the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.title: The minister of Awqaf compliment
the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.summary: The moment John Kiriakou calls the highlight of his Bahrain tour and freely describes as an ego booster: interpreting for Ambassador David Ransom''s first courtesy call on the only Bahraini cabinet member who did not speak fluent English, and being complimented on his Arabic on the way out — something he says he still thinks about thirty years later.

the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.title: CIA attention to West Africa
the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer on whether the CIA is likely to be operating in Burkina Faso: for all the years he was at the agency it cared very little about Africa and especially West Africa, but the presence of al-Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates plus the drug trade makes CIA and special forces involvement probable — and, he adds, the American public will not hear about it.

the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.title: CIA–FBI incompatible computer systems
the-jerusalem-harassment-campaign.summary: John Kiriakou's claim that from the CIA's founding in 1947 until 2009 the computer systems of the CIA and the FBI were not compatible with one another — no message could be sent from one to the other and no intelligence shared — which he offers both as the material substrate of the interagency hatred that helped make September 11 possible, and as the gap through which James Mitchell and Bruce Jessen were able to pass Ali Soufan's FBI debriefings of Abu Zubaydah off as the fruits of torture.

the-job-in-the-medical-practice.title: Seven cell phones
the-job-in-the-medical-practice.summary: John Kiriakou's account of why his first marriage ended — that his wife, a ballet teacher, knew only that he worked for the CIA, and that a career in which one of seven cell phones rang at midnight and he left speaking Arabic for a day at a time could not survive the questions it produced.

the-job-in-the-medical-practice.title: The hundred-city tour
the-job-in-the-medical-practice.summary: The year-long, hundred-city speaking tour John Kiriakou described beginning in early 2026 — opening in Belfast, Dublin and Manchester, returning to Scotland and northern England, then the United States and Canada, Australia and New Zealand, continental Europe, the Persian Gulf and East Asia.

the-job-in-the-medical-practice.title: The Nation of Islam at Loretto
the-job-in-the-medical-practice.summary: The largest Muslim faction at FCI Loretto — African American converts to the Nation of Islam — two of whom walked into John Kiriakou's cell in his first days holding their own newspaper, in which Louis Farrakhan had called him a hero of the Muslim people for opposing torture. They told him he would have no trouble with them; one declined the handshake he offered, on the ground that he does not shake hands with the white devil. The Aryans, meanwhile, had decided he was a CIA assassin who killed Muslims. Kiriakou kept his mouth shut and let both beliefs stand.

the-job-in-the-medical-practice.title: Seventy-two denied motions
the-job-in-the-medical-practice.summary: The count John Kiriakou gives of the pretrial motions filed in his case and denied by Judge Leonie Brinkema — seventy-two denied and none granted — which he offers as the mechanism by which a national security defendant in the Eastern District of Virginia is prevented from mounting a defence at all.

the-job-in-the-medical-practice.title: The legal bills
the-job-in-the-medical-practice.summary: The cost of John Kiriakou's defence, which he has given variously as more than half a million dollars, approaching a million, and more than a million — a figure he treats not as a hardship but as the mechanism of the prosecution itself, since bankruptcy is what makes a defendant accept a plea.

the-job-in-the-medical-practice.title: The professor and the Ellsberg profile
the-job-in-the-medical-practice.summary: The story John Kiriakou says his CIA recruiter told him — that in 1971, as founder of the unit producing long-distance psychological profiles of foreign leaders, he was handed a file on Daniel Ellsberg, refused to profile an American citizen, and later discovered his boss had done it anyway under his name, which he testified to before the Watergate Committee.

the-jury-consultants-advice.title: Sealing the courtroom
the-jury-consultants-advice.summary: The physical measures John Kiriakou describes as accompanying a classified-information trial: plastic sheeting and duct tape over the windows so lasers cannot read the vibrations, white noise in the vestibule, and the clearing of everyone but the judge, jury, bailiff, clerk, lawyers and defendant.

the-jury-consultants-advice.title: The swimming pool substitution
the-jury-consultants-advice.summary: John Kiriakou''s illustration of how classified words are handled at trial: prosecutors and judge agree in advance to replace them with harmless unclassified substitutes, so that "Vault 7" becomes "swimming pool" — and the jury, told the real words are too secret for their ears, concludes the defendant must be guilty.

the-jury-consultants-advice.title: Assange and the European Court of Human Rights
the-jury-consultants-advice.summary: The last legal avenue John Kiriakou identified for Julian Assange in 2022 — three precedents in which the Strasbourg court refused to let Britain extradite mentally ill defendants to American solitary confinement — and the procedural trap that made it useless: Britain said the appeal need not halt the extradition.

the-jury-consultants-advice.title: Eastern District of Virginia
the-jury-consultants-advice.summary: The U.S. federal district covering northern Virginia — home to Langley, the Pentagon, DHS and much of the intelligence-contractor industry — which John Kiriakou calls 'the espionage court' because the Justice Department files the great majority of its national security prosecutions there and because, in his telling, no national-security defendant has ever won a case in it; Kiriakou, Julian Assange, Edward Snowden and Jeffrey Sterling were all charged there.

the-jury-consultants-advice.title: Julian Assange
the-jury-consultants-advice.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

the-jury-consultants-advice.title: FISA court
the-jury-consultants-advice.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the secret Foreign Intelligence Surveillance court — created under Carter, sitting atop the Justice Department, issuing warrants that are never public — which he says was abused against Carter Page as part of what he believes was John Brennan's plan to deny Trump the presidency.

the-kafala-sponsorship-system.title: Saudi Arabia as an open-air prison
the-kafala-sponsorship-system.summary: John Kiriakou's verdict on the country he served in — 'the biggest open air prison in the world' — together with his account of what the ambassador's life there is like inside the residence and outside it, the two ambassadors he served under, and the annual migration of the entire Saudi government to Jeddah to escape the heat.

the-kafala-sponsorship-system.title: The Saudi demand for a political appointee
the-kafala-sponsorship-system.summary: John Kiriakou's account of a standing Saudi condition on the American embassy in Riyadh — that the ambassador must never be a career diplomat, the opposite of what most countries want, because Riyadh wants someone whose telephone call the president of the United States will take.

the-kafala-sponsorship-system.title: The Eric Adams ambassadorship
the-kafala-sponsorship-system.summary: The September 2025 proposal, floated by Steve Witkoff, to remove Eric Adams from the New York mayoral race by offering him the embassy in Riyadh — which John Kiriakou thought likely to be attempted, on the reasoning that Donald Trump is not stupid, knows Adams cannot win, and would gain by forcing Zohran Mamdani to spend money.

the-kafala-sponsorship-system.title: The 1991 Saudi plan for Gaza
the-kafala-sponsorship-system.summary: A proposal John Kiriakou says he watched Ambassador Chas Freeman float to the Saudis during his first overseas tour in 1991 — that Saudi Arabia fund a port, an airport, a desalination plant and an electrical grid in Gaza. The Saudis agreed; Israel refused outright. Kiriakou raises it because the identical arrangement resurfaced in the Israeli press more than three decades later.

the-kafala-sponsorship-system.title: Aafia Siddiqui
the-kafala-sponsorship-system.summary: Pakistani-American neuroscientist arrested in Afghanistan and convicted in the United States of attempting to shoot FBI agents; per John Kiriakou, who covered the arrest as a terrorism consultant for ABC News and has followed the case since, she never had a gun and never fired, the bullet holes offered as proof predated her capture, and the CIA took her three children — two later recovered, the youngest never found.

the-kafala-sponsorship-system.title: Clive Stafford Smith
the-kafala-sponsorship-system.summary: The British human rights lawyer who represents Aafia Siddiqui, described by John Kiriakou as a man who has never charged a client a dollar in his life, lives on donations, holds an OBE for his human rights work, and represented sixty-six Guantanamo detainees — securing the release of every one of them.

the-kenya-mission.title: United States–DRC relations
the-kenya-mission.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of why American policy toward the Democratic Republic of the Congo is quietly comfortable while the east of the country is in chaos: the United States buys as much Congolese rare earth metal as can be dug out of the ground, and the central government''s weakness against Rwanda is a problem Donald Trump claimed to have solved for the purposes of a Nobel Peace Prize case, with a peace Kiriakou says lasted a couple of weeks.

the-kenya-mission.title: Senate Foreign Relations Committee
the-kenya-mission.summary: Kiriakou was senior investigator under John Kerry — and still held the post when his own federal prosecution came to a head in January 2012.

the-kenya-mission.title: 2026 Iran war
the-kenya-mission.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

the-kenya-mission.title: Arming the crazies
the-kenya-mission.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the American habit of arming the most radical faction available — the Mujahideen over any other Afghan force, the White Russians over the Red — and his expectation, stated days into the 2026 war, that the United States and Israel would begin arming factions inside Iran and that the factions chosen would be the radical ones.

the-kenya-mission.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
the-kenya-mission.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

the-kenya-mission.title: Chaos as the Israeli objective
the-kenya-mission.summary: John Kiriakou''s answer to whether Netanyahu''s government actually wanted an American invasion of Iran: what the Israelis want in Iran is what they got in Libya — chaos, civil war, and as many dead Iranians as possible.

the-kerry-yacht-tax.title: Cleaning up after Tora Bora
the-kerry-yacht-tax.summary: John Kiriakou was not at Tora Bora. He arrived in Pakistan in January 2002, two months after the bombing, and says he went specifically to clean up what the battle had left behind — scavenging material, detaining the fighters too slow to get away, and mapping the smugglers'' valleys the survivors had used to cross. In his account the clean-up was necessary because the encirclement failed: bin Laden, warned by an al-Qaeda operative working as translator to the commander of Central Command, left in the dark dressed as a woman in the back of a pickup truck, and at dawn there was nobody in Tora Bora to surrender.

the-kerry-yacht-tax.title: "Do not ever attempt to contact me again"
the-kerry-yacht-tax.summary: The reply John Kiriakou says he received from John Kerry, then Secretary of State, after emailing him privately in the days before reporting to prison to beg that his sentence be commuted. Kiriakou had worked closely with Kerry for two and a half years; the one-line answer, sent after two or three days, was the last he ever heard from him.

the-kerry-yacht-tax.title: Hayden at the National Press Club
the-kerry-yacht-tax.summary: John Kiriakou's account of seeing Michael Hayden, after a series of strokes, at a National Press Club event sponsored by the intelligence centre that bears his name — and the two reactions it produced in him, neither of them satisfaction alone.

the-kerry-yacht-tax.title: John Kerry
the-kerry-yacht-tax.summary: U.S. Senator from Massachusetts; chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee during John Kiriakou's 2009 service as the committee's senior investigator; subsequently U.S. Secretary of State; characterized by Kiriakou as a coward who buckled under CIA pressure on the Dasht-i-Leili reopening and as personally fixated on his perceived theft of the Secretary of State position by Hillary Clinton; the famously thrown medals were duplicates purchased at the post exchange.

the-kerry-yacht-tax.title: Letters the cabinet ignored
the-kerry-yacht-tax.summary: John Kiriakou's account, from his years on the staff of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, of what happened to congressional oversight letters sent to cabinet secretaries and agency directors — mostly nothing — and why he expects the same of demands made from the minority side of the aisle.

the-kerry-yacht-tax.title: Saddam and the journalists
the-kerry-yacht-tax.summary: John Kiriakou's comparison, drawn from fifteen years working the Iraq target at the CIA, between a dictator who hated the press and did not kill it and a government that he says kills journalists deliberately and in numbers.

the-kgb-denial-cables.title: Richard Welch
the-kgb-denial-cables.summary: CIA Athens station chief assassinated December 23, 1975; the first victim of [Revolutionary Organization 17 November](/wiki/revolutionary-organization-17-november)

the-kgb-denial-cables.title: Ukraine as a proxy war
the-kgb-denial-cables.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment, given two months into the 2022 Russian invasion, that the United States was funding a proxy war it knew Ukraine could not win in order to bog Russia down — and that the outcome was already fixed, so peace talks should happen at once.

the-kgb-denial-cables.title: American media consolidation
the-kgb-denial-cables.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of why American news coverage is uniform: the entire national media is owned by six corporations or oligarchs, a number the Warner Brothers sale would reduce to five. He attributes the consolidation to profit rather than politics, and describes the practical consequence as an audience that turns on a cable channel believing it is being educated when it is being propagandised — with independent media the only alternative and almost nobody with the time to find it.

the-kgb-denial-cables.title: The CIA and Hollywood
the-kgb-denial-cables.summary: The CIA''s standing arrangement with the film industry, as John Kiriakou describes it: a branch inside the Office of Public Affairs whose only job is to cooperate with Hollywood studios, on the model the FBI has run since the 1950s, so that what comes out of Hollywood carries a pro-agency message. Kiriakou notes it is technically illegal for the CIA to propagandise the American public and says that is exactly what happens every time an agency-linked film is released.

the-kgb-denial-cables.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
the-kgb-denial-cables.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

the-kgb-denial-cables.title: Jeffrey Epstein
the-kgb-denial-cables.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

the-killing-of-alex-pretty.title: Canada as a bargaining chip
the-killing-of-alex-pretty.summary: John Kiriakou's reading of Mark Carney's Davos speech as the moment Canada stopped pretending the United States could be trusted as a long-term partner — and his account of what wore the relationship out, including Washington's insistence that Ottawa arrest Huawei's chief financial officer on a computer-hacking charge and hold her for three years to trade.

the-killing-of-alex-pretty.title: China's generals without combat experience
the-killing-of-alex-pretty.summary: Presented with the observation that China's purged and reshuffled top brass are now too young to have fought in any war, John Kiriakou agreed it mattered little in the near term and a great deal in the long term — because American military planning will have to account for an adversary whose senior commanders have never been in combat.

the-killing-of-alex-pretty.title: Ilhan Omar
the-killing-of-alex-pretty.summary: U.S. Representative whom John Kiriakou credits with sponsoring a rewrite of the Espionage Act in two consecutive Congresses — legislation he says is dead on arrival with a Republican House because of who she is. Kiriakou has also sat at her table — in January 2026 he was one of about twenty guests at a dinner where Omar described the federal operation in Minneapolis and the budget manoeuvre that funded every part of the government except Homeland Security.

the-killing-of-alex-pretty.title: Macron and the airplane steps
the-killing-of-alex-pretty.summary: Asked what he thought was behind the French president's bruised appearance at Davos, John Kiriakou gave the blunt answer — "honestly, I think she hits him" — and dated his own change of mind to the footage at the top of the airplane steps.

the-killing-of-alex-pretty.title: The Abraham Lincoln off Oman
the-killing-of-alex-pretty.summary: The carrier battle group John Kiriakou placed in the Arabian Sea off Oman in January 2026, and the reason he said he genuinely feared the coming weeks: a belief in Washington and Jerusalem that the Iranian government needed only a gentle shove to collapse, against 150,000 members of the Revolutionary Guard who would not oblige.

the-killing-of-alex-pretty.title: The Arlington house
the-killing-of-alex-pretty.summary: The 1,200-square-foot house John Kiriakou bought with his Pakistan overtime and danger pay for $347,000, sold two years later for $721,000, and now values at a million — the anchor of his repeated argument that his own children can never live in the Arlington, Virginia neighbourhood they grew up in.

the-kiriakou-children.title: I should have gone to film school
the-kiriakou-children.summary: One of the two answers John Kiriakou gives when asked whether, knowing what he knows now, he would join the CIA again. He is candid that he has answered the question differently over the years — sometimes yes, because the agency can only be changed from inside, and sometimes that he should have gone to film school, which he insists is not a joke.

the-kiriakou-children.title: Kiriakou's writing process
the-kiriakou-children.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of how he actually writes — books in waves over roughly nine months, op-eds in forty-five minutes to an hour once an idea has sat for a few days, and a habit of getting up at two in the morning to write one because he cannot sleep. He wrote *Remains of the Day* in six weeks during COVID, losing whole evenings to it: "I look at the clock again, it''s 2:00 in the morning. I''m like, oh my god, what happened?"

the-kiriakou-children.title: Remains of the Day (book)
the-kiriakou-children.summary: John Kiriakou's book, announced for publication by Simon and Schuster in March 2026, billed as a definitive guide to the historic cemeteries of Washington DC and the first in a planned series; the second installment will cover the Mafia graves of New York City.

the-kiriakou-children.title: The beer and the couch
the-kiriakou-children.summary: What John Kiriakou says he did with the CIA''s spot-assessment training after leaving the agency. He still sizes up strangers within moments of meeting them, but the question is no longer what they can do for him: it is whether he would want to have a beer with them, and whether, if he were down on his luck, they would let him sleep on their couch.

the-kiriakou-children.title: The Pentagon press contract
the-kiriakou-children.summary: A contract John Kiriakou says every news outlet covering the Pentagon was required to sign in mid-2026, undertaking to publish no information that had not been officially provided by the department. Almost nobody signed: by his count Newsmax, One America News, a Turkish paper, a Hungarian paper and a couple of bloggers.

the-kiriakou-children.title: Coffee with a cabinet member
the-kiriakou-children.summary: John Kiriakou's disclosure that he had coffee with a member of the cabinet who told him to be patient about his pardon — and told him to watch what he said. He reports the meeting while stating plainly that there is nothing further he can do to make his case, and that he is not confident the outcome will be decided on justice.

the-knesset-death-penalty-law.title: The logic of radicalization
the-knesset-death-penalty-law.summary: John Kiriakou''s explanation of why an isolated state escalates rather than moderates: it stops caring what anyone else thinks, concludes it can count on no one, and does things its own way. He applies it to Israel''s 2026 death penalty law and judges the law a serious mistake in Zionism''s own terms.

the-knesset-death-penalty-law.title: Israel's rightward shift
the-knesset-death-penalty-law.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for why Israeli politics moved sharply right over roughly two decades — that immigration from Russia, Ukraine and the United States brought in a conservatism the Israeli electorate had not seen before, displacing the socialist politics of the earlier European arrivals.

the-knesset-death-penalty-law.title: Itamar Ben-Gvir
the-knesset-death-penalty-law.summary: Israel's far-right Minister of National Security; John Kiriakou cites him as a convicted hate-crime felon placed in charge of security in Gaza and the West Bank over his victims, blames his insistence that any attack would come from the West Bank for diverting forces before October 7, and cites the death-penalty law passed under his portfolio for Palestinian detainees as the first reinstatement of capital punishment in Israel since it was abolished in 1956, excepting only the execution of Adolf Eichmann.

the-knesset-death-penalty-law.title: Antisemitism and anti-Zionism
the-knesset-death-penalty-law.summary: The conflation of criticism of the Israeli state with hatred of Jews, which John Kiriakou describes as a worldwide confusion and, according to a young Israeli he spoke to, an explicit lesson of the Israeli school system; a subject Kiriakou says he personally struggles with.

the-knesset-death-penalty-law.title: The empire on the ropes
the-knesset-death-penalty-law.summary: John Kiriakou's answer to whether the American empire is finished — that it is on the ropes but certainly not over — and, in the same exchange, his first unqualified statement that Israeli tactics were inspired by Nazi Germany, a comparison he says he hesitated for years to make.

the-knesset-death-penalty-law.title: Ted Rall
the-knesset-death-penalty-law.summary: American editorial cartoonist and two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist; co-host with John Kiriakou of the daily news-commentary podcast "Deprogram," launched in September 2025 and by late 2025 running every weekday morning.

the-knight-ridder-panel.title: Espionage Act
the-knight-ridder-panel.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

the-knight-ridder-panel.title: Jake Tapper
the-knight-ridder-panel.summary: CNN anchor who drove to FCI Loretto to interview the imprisoned John Kiriakou — and who asked President Obama at a press conference why he had insisted on prosecuting a man who exposed a crime, a question Obama answered by walking away from the podium. Tapper's visit was the head of a media wave that began with a smuggled-out letter on the Huffington Post, and it became Kiriakou's protection inside; even a guard known as a psychopath left him alone rather than find CNN parked beside his car.

the-knight-ridder-panel.title: Julian Assange
the-knight-ridder-panel.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

the-knight-ridder-panel.title: Eastern District of Virginia
the-knight-ridder-panel.summary: The U.S. federal district covering northern Virginia — home to Langley, the Pentagon, DHS and much of the intelligence-contractor industry — which John Kiriakou calls 'the espionage court' because the Justice Department files the great majority of its national security prosecutions there and because, in his telling, no national-security defendant has ever won a case in it; Kiriakou, Julian Assange, Edward Snowden and Jeffrey Sterling were all charged there.

the-knight-ridder-panel.title: A Middle East reading list
the-knight-ridder-panel.summary: The books and the starting point John Kiriakou recommends to anyone trying to understand the modern Middle East: begin at the end of the Second World War, not five thousand years earlier, and start with The House of Saud, the Sykes-Picot Agreement and From Beirut to Jerusalem.

the-knight-ridder-panel.title: Acts of Service
the-knight-ridder-panel.summary: The Doja Cat song that John Kiriakou discovered, through a Cameo request, had become the soundtrack to a genre of montage about him. The clips set to it use footage from before his weight loss — he lost 77 pounds by 2007 and 115 pounds from 2022 — and he says he cannot watch them.

the-kosovo-objection.title: The hundred-drachma coins
the-kosovo-objection.summary: How demonstrators in Athens broke the windows of the American embassy during John Kiriakou's posting there in 1999 — with hundred-drachma coins the size of an Eisenhower dollar, worth about a quarter, followed by paint-filled balloons fired from slingshots.

the-kosovo-objection.title: The Yugo factory argument
the-kosovo-objection.summary: The dinner-table confrontation in which one of John Kiriakou's uncles in Greece demanded to know why the United States had bombed the Yugo factory — an accusation Kiriakou could answer only technically, because he thought the 1999 bombing of Yugoslavia was wrong in the first place.

the-kosovo-objection.title: Drunken border guards
the-kosovo-objection.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for how quiet frontiers become shooting wars — bored, drinking troops with nothing to do and no supervision — which he applies to the Thailand-Cambodia clashes, to the India-China line, and to why Vladimir Putin objects to a NATO country on his border.

the-kosovo-objection.title: Trump's NATO reversal
the-kosovo-objection.summary: John Kiriakou's explanation for Donald Trump's turn from hostility to enthusiasm for NATO — that he genuinely expected Vladimir Putin to do as he was told, and embraced the alliance out of anger when Putin would not settle the war in Ukraine, because the alternative was standing alone.

the-kosovo-objection.title: Ali from Newark
the-kosovo-objection.summary: The Black shot caller at FCI Loretto, near the end of a twenty-five-year drug sentence, who came to embrace John Kiriakou at the close of his term and tell him how much he respected him — a friendship possible only because Kiriakou had decided on arrival to ignore the prison's racial divisions.

the-kosovo-objection.title: Bezalel Smotrich
the-kosovo-objection.summary: Israeli far-right minister whom John Kiriakou, alongside Itamar Ben-Gvir, blames for leaving Israel unprepared on October 7 by insisting any attack would come from the West Bank rather than Gaza.

the-kurd-from-terre-haute.title: Communications management unit
the-kurd-from-terre-haute.summary: The two restricted-contact units inside the American federal prison system, at Terre Haute and Marion; built for "the worst of the worst" but, in John Kiriakou's account, used to silence prisoners whose messages are inconvenient — and a practice he groups with solitary confinement as torture. He served part of his own sentence in a modified one.

the-kurd-from-terre-haute.title: Julian Assange
the-kurd-from-terre-haute.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

the-kurd-from-terre-haute.title: J. Edgar Hoover
the-kurd-from-terre-haute.summary: The FBI's founding director — 48 years in the chair — whose opposition nearly strangled the CIA at birth. Per John Kiriakou, Truman lifted Hoover's objection to the National Security Act of 1947 by disingenuously assuring him the CIA would be a division of the FBI; the lie seeded the two agencies' permanent mutual hatred. Kiriakou also credits Hoover with perfecting the annual ritual the CIA later copied — scaring Congress witless and demanding budget increases — and with controlling Hollywood's FBI image so tightly that no film could be made without his approval.

the-kurd-from-terre-haute.title: RDAP
the-kurd-from-terre-haute.summary: The Bureau of Prisons' Residential Drug and Alcohol Program, which takes a year off a federal sentence on completion — the single most valuable piece of advice John Kiriakou says he gives to people facing prison time, alongside good-conduct credit and halfway-house conversion.

the-kurd-from-terre-haute.title: The mailroom standoff
the-kurd-from-terre-haute.summary: Told at FCI Loretto that he had no right to write to journalists, John Kiriakou printed the Bureau of Prisons regulations in the law library and laid them out in the mailroom until the staff gave up and sent the letter.

the-kurd-from-terre-haute.title: The Walmart phone call
the-kurd-from-terre-haute.summary: John Kiriakou''s account, from a White House friend, that Jared Kushner personally telephoned the chief executive of Walmart to find a job for a woman whose life sentence Donald Trump had commuted, and rang back every six months to check on her.

the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.title: The Saudi question
the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.summary: John Kiriakou''s challenge to the premise of the Abraham Accords: that after a lifetime working in the Middle East he is unable to identify anything Saudi Arabia would actually gain from recognising Israel.

the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.title: Sheldon Adelson
the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.summary: American casino magnate and Republican megadonor. In John Kiriakou's account Adelson sent his private jet to fly Jonathan Pollard from prison to Israel, paid out of his own pocket to move the American embassy to Jerusalem, and functions as Kiriakou's standing unit of measurement for what political money can buy — including in the negative, as the patron the Libertarian Party never had.

the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.title: Shin Bet
the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.summary: Israel's internal security service; per John Kiriakou, one of the two declared Israeli intelligence officers at the Washington embassy, and the service whose officer, alongside a Mossad officer, he says tried to recruit him at his first CIA liaison briefing in the spring of 1990 — an approach his colleagues told him had been made to every one of them.

the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.title: The CIA recruiting video
the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.summary: The Agency recruiting video John Kiriakou says he watched with dismay, in which a woman described herself as an autistic, depressed, anxious lesbian who had found a home at the CIA — and his reaction that this was not the CIA he joined.

the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.title: Kissinger and the petrodollar
the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.summary: John Kiriakou's endorsement of the theory that Henry Kissinger deliberately structured the 1970s petrodollar to tie the U.S. to Middle Eastern oil — creating a standing rationale for policing the region, even as America exports its own fracked oil.

the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.title: Henry Kissinger
the-kuwaiti-cargo-in-yuan.summary: The former secretary of state John Kiriakou calls the biggest living war criminal — "the butcher of Cyprus, the butcher of Chile" — and blames, via the declassified record, for keeping the Greek junta in power. Kiriakou met him once as a new CIA officer, jokes that your natural impulse on meeting him "should be to become involuntarily violent," and marvels that both parties treat him as a foreign policy god. Yet he concedes the dark craftsman his due: Kissinger had goals, realpolitik was real, and it was Kissinger who got Nixon to China.

the-la-times-iran-op-ed.title: The Office of Security arrangement
the-la-times-iran-op-ed.summary: The disclosure John Kiriakou says emerged from a 2020 custody hearing: that his wife, herself a senior CIA officer, had accompanied him to the 2007 ABC News whistleblowing interview on the instruction of the CIA''s Office of Security, and had continued to report on his activities.

the-la-times-iran-op-ed.title: Abu Omar rendition
the-la-times-iran-op-ed.summary: The CIA's kidnapping of a Milan cleric, Abu Omar, who was sent to Egypt to be tortured; John Kiriakou calls it a case that ought to be taught at the CIA as how not to run a rendition, and it is what ultimately sent him to prison, after he confirmed a former colleague's surname to a journalist claiming to be writing a book about it.

the-la-times-iran-op-ed.title: Intelligence Identities Protection Act
the-la-times-iran-op-ed.summary: U.S. law enacted in 1982 that makes it a crime to knowingly disclose the identity of a covert intelligence officer; per John Kiriakou, his 2012 prosecution under the act arose from confirming a single surname of a former CIA colleague to a journalist — a confirmation that was never published. The name passed through a chain from journalist to Human Rights Watch to Guantanamo defense attorneys before reaching a judge and ultimately the FBI, which traced it back to Kiriakou.

the-la-times-iran-op-ed.title: The custody standoff
the-la-times-iran-op-ed.summary: The week John Kiriakou used his CIA surveillance training to find his own sons after his ex-wife hid them in breach of a custody order — ending with him carrying his eight-year-old out of a Greek Orthodox church during the consecration, a felony charge that was dropped, and a hostage-style handover at a diner on the state line.

the-la-times-iran-op-ed.title: The Greek community of Warren, Ohio
the-la-times-iran-op-ed.summary: The Greek-American community John Kiriakou's mother and first wife both came from — overwhelmingly from the island of Chios, closely enough knit that his divorce started a fistfight in a coffee house between men who had never met him.

the-la-times-iran-op-ed.title: Mary Jane Stevens
the-la-times-iran-op-ed.summary: The lawyer who represented John Kiriakou through his custody dispute — who told him to wait for Monday and go to court, was ignored, and then got the assurance from a hostile police chief that let him walk into the hearing without being arrested.

the-lafayette-square-tents.title: The National Guard in Washington
the-lafayette-square-tents.summary: John Kiriakou's response to the August 2025 federalisation of the District of Columbia police — a decision he says was taken without informing the mayor or the police chief, in a city where crime was falling, and which he expected to expire after three days for want of congressional authorisation.

the-lafayette-square-tents.title: The third-term workaround
the-lafayette-square-tents.summary: John Kiriakou's constitutional argument that Donald Trump cannot reach a third term by running as vice president and having J.D. Vance resign — because a vice president barred from the presidency cannot assume it, so the speakership takes precedence.

the-lafayette-square-tents.title: Cleaning up after Tora Bora
the-lafayette-square-tents.summary: John Kiriakou was not at Tora Bora. He arrived in Pakistan in January 2002, two months after the bombing, and says he went specifically to clean up what the battle had left behind — scavenging material, detaining the fighters too slow to get away, and mapping the smugglers'' valleys the survivors had used to cross. In his account the clean-up was necessary because the encirclement failed: bin Laden, warned by an al-Qaeda operative working as translator to the commander of Central Command, left in the dark dressed as a woman in the back of a pickup truck, and at dawn there was nobody in Tora Bora to surrender.

the-lafayette-square-tents.title: Hayden at the National Press Club
the-lafayette-square-tents.summary: John Kiriakou's account of seeing Michael Hayden, after a series of strokes, at a National Press Club event sponsored by the intelligence centre that bears his name — and the two reactions it produced in him, neither of them satisfaction alone.

the-lafayette-square-tents.title: Saddam and the journalists
the-lafayette-square-tents.summary: John Kiriakou's comparison, drawn from fifteen years working the Iraq target at the CIA, between a dictator who hated the press and did not kill it and a government that he says kills journalists deliberately and in numbers.

the-lafayette-square-tents.title: The balloon test
the-lafayette-square-tents.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that Israel had warning of the 7 October 2023 attack — that settlers along the Gaza line had reported training for months, that balloons were sent over as a probe in the days beforehand, and that nothing was done.

the-lake-michigan-sightings.title: The pilot who saw it drink
the-lake-michigan-sightings.summary: The F-14 pilot John Kiriakou met at his godfather's Alexandria restaurant in the late 1970s, who described following a cigar-shaped object that submerged, stayed under and came back up — and being told by other pilots that they had all seen the same thing.

the-lake-michigan-sightings.title: The New Jersey drones
the-lake-michigan-sightings.summary: John Kiriakou''s shifting account of the New Jersey drone flap: his state trooper friend''s report of a missing Defense or Energy Department convoy load, and the 60 Minutes segment in which Air Force generals concluded the drones were hostile and probably Chinese.

the-lake-michigan-sightings.title: Kiriakou's UFO sighting
the-lake-michigan-sightings.summary: The object John Kiriakou and his father watched from the side of Route 60 in Amish country, western Pennsylvania, on a Friday night in 1981 — three flashes of white light, then a silent orange trapezoid hanging a couple of thousand feet up, which left at a speed he had never seen before or since.

the-lake-michigan-sightings.title: Langley
the-lake-michigan-sightings.summary: The Virginia location of CIA headquarters and, in John Kiriakou''s usage, shorthand for the agency''s permanent power. It''s where he worked as the CIA''s lone Iraq-Kuwait analyst — told to start on Iraq "because nothing ever happened there" — where a cafeteria conversation invited him into the torture program, where he walked past the Kryptos sculpture every day for fifteen years without solving it, and the place agencies return to after apologizing to Congress, "where of course nothing ever changes." When a host suggested the real government of America is out in Langley and Washington''s white marble is for show, Kiriakou''s answer was: "that''s about the shape of it."

the-lake-michigan-sightings.title: Area 58
the-lake-michigan-sightings.summary: The claim John Kiriakou says was put to him by a man who presents as entirely serious and is writing a book about it: that beyond Area 51 there is an Area 58 — seven more, and that much more secret — containing an underground bunker where alien craft land, known to those involved as the embassy because it is where the United States liaises with the aliens.

the-lake-michigan-sightings.title: CIA and the UFO question
the-lake-michigan-sightings.summary: John Kiriakou's consistent answer that UFOs and alien technology are a Pentagon matter, not a CIA one — though he says nearly every former fighter-pilot friend of his has seen something inexplicable, sometimes emerging from the ocean.

the-land-bridge-precedents.title: Phil Donahue
the-land-bridge-precedents.summary: American talk-show host who, John Kiriakou discovered seven years after the fact, had been secretly paying his weekly newspaper column fee — $400 a week for nine years, routed through Reader Supported News — because Donahue had learned that Kiriakou came out of prison broke and did not want him sleeping in his car.

the-land-bridge-precedents.title: Soviet Union
the-land-bridge-precedents.summary: The superpower whose collapse framed the start of John Kiriakou's CIA career — it was "literally in the process of collapsing" when he joined in January 1990, ushering in a brief "peace dividend" era when the agency's new threats were environmental degradation and AIDS. Kiriakou cites Brzezinski's "Afghan trap" that lured the Soviets into Afghanistan, argues the U.S. abandoned the radicalized mujahideen the moment the Soviets were beaten, notes America then took "a vacation from history," and recalls that Jonathan Pollard's stolen documents were traded by Israel to the Soviets in exchange for Russian Jews.

the-land-bridge-precedents.title: The Alaska glacier
the-land-bridge-precedents.summary: The visitor centre John Kiriakou saw on a 2016 trip to Alaska with Gary Johnson, built at the foot of a glacier close enough to touch from the observation deck and by then a quarter of a mile away from it — an image he uses as the plainest available demonstration of climate change, and one he refuses to let pass as a joke.

the-land-bridge-precedents.title: The armour at Union Station
the-land-bridge-precedents.summary: John Kiriakou''s eyewitness account of stepping off an Amtrak train at Washington''s Union Station in August 2025 to find two armoured personnel carriers and a .50 calibre machine gun trained on the entrance — and of tourists posing for photographs with the National Guardsmen deployed in the parts of the city where, he says, there is no crime.

the-land-bridge-precedents.title: The CIA and Iridium
the-land-bridge-precedents.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the Central Intelligence Agency buying the satellite telephone company Iridium when it was unprofitable and about to go out of business, because the agency needed the network — a purchase he places alongside its acquisition of Intelsat, and which he encountered personally when he had to rent the phones for Afghanistan.

the-land-bridge-precedents.title: The diplomatic stool collection
the-land-bridge-precedents.summary: John Kiriakou''s confirmation that visiting heads of state routinely carry their own faeces home rather than leave them in an American hotel — because, in his account, entities within the United States government will gladly collect the material for its DNA and health information, and the hotel employee who retrieves it is a CIA officer under cover.

the-lapis-lazuli-paperweight.title: Cleaning up after Tora Bora
the-lapis-lazuli-paperweight.summary: John Kiriakou was not at Tora Bora. He arrived in Pakistan in January 2002, two months after the bombing, and says he went specifically to clean up what the battle had left behind — scavenging material, detaining the fighters too slow to get away, and mapping the smugglers'' valleys the survivors had used to cross. In his account the clean-up was necessary because the encirclement failed: bin Laden, warned by an al-Qaeda operative working as translator to the commander of Central Command, left in the dark dressed as a woman in the back of a pickup truck, and at dawn there was nobody in Tora Bora to surrender.
