zero-dark-thirty.title: John Kiriakou
zero-dark-thirty.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

zero-dark-thirty.title: Espionage Act
zero-dark-thirty.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

zero-dark-thirty.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
zero-dark-thirty.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

zero-dark-thirty.title: The HardTalk interview
zero-dark-thirty.summary: The first interview John Kiriakou gave after leaving prison, on the BBC programme he describes as hard-hitting and mean-spirited, in which a host pressing him to show remorse drew the formulation he has used ever since: it is not a crime to reveal a crime.

zero-dark-thirty.title: Tony Mendez
zero-dark-thirty.summary: The CIA exfiltration specialist who got the American diplomats sheltering in the Canadian embassy out of revolutionary Tehran in 1979 by inventing a fake science-fiction film production — the operation dramatised in *Argo*. John Kiriakou calls him "a giant in the history of the CIA", says the same of his wife, and rates the operation among the greatest the agency has ever carried out.

zohran-mamdani.title: The Eric Adams ambassadorship
zohran-mamdani.summary: The September 2025 proposal, floated by Steve Witkoff, to remove Eric Adams from the New York mayoral race by offering him the embassy in Riyadh — which John Kiriakou thought likely to be attempted, on the reasoning that Donald Trump is not stupid, knows Adams cannot win, and would gain by forcing Zohran Mamdani to spend money.

zohran-mamdani.title: The Saudi demand for a political appointee
zohran-mamdani.summary: John Kiriakou's account of a standing Saudi condition on the American embassy in Riyadh — that the ambassador must never be a career diplomat, the opposite of what most countries want, because Riyadh wants someone whose telephone call the president of the United States will take.

zohran-mamdani.title: 2026 Iran war
zohran-mamdani.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

zohran-mamdani.title: Aafia Siddiqui
zohran-mamdani.summary: Pakistani-American neuroscientist arrested in Afghanistan and convicted in the United States of attempting to shoot FBI agents; per John Kiriakou, who covered the arrest as a terrorism consultant for ABC News and has followed the case since, she never had a gun and never fired, the bullet holes offered as proof predated her capture, and the CIA took her three children — two later recovered, the youngest never found.

zohran-mamdani.title: Acts of Service
zohran-mamdani.summary: The Doja Cat song that John Kiriakou discovered, through a Cameo request, had become the soundtrack to a genre of montage about him. The clips set to it use footage from before his weight loss — he lost 77 pounds by 2007 and 115 pounds from 2022 — and he says he cannot watch them.

zohran-mamdani.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
zohran-mamdani.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

zunzuneo.title: USAID as a CIA cover vehicle
zunzuneo.summary: John Kiriakou's account of USAID's use by the CIA as a channel for covert operations and money laundering rather than as an undercover posting for individual officers — including a declassified 1972 exchange in which Henry Kissinger confirmed the CIA had paid Laotian mercenaries through USAID payroll checks.

zunzuneo.title: Concealment of the CIA budget
zunzuneo.summary: John Kiriakou''s description of how the CIA hides its spending: there is no publicly available written CIA budget, and individual line items are distributed across unrelated federal departments under invented cover programmes — a practice he says persists unchanged, and which once repeatedly exposed the agency to Senator William Proxmire''s Golden Fleece Award.

zunzuneo.title: John Kiriakou
zunzuneo.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

zunzuneo.title: William Proxmire
zunzuneo.summary: Democratic senator from Wisconsin, elected in the special election following Joseph McCarthy's death, whose monthly Golden Fleece Award targeted wasteful federal spending. John Kiriakou describes Proxmire as a recurring irritant to the CIA — which, he says, repeatedly saw its concealed budget line items exposed to ridicule because the cover stories invented to hide them looked exactly like waste.

zunzuneo.title: Bluffdale NSA Data Center
zunzuneo.summary: The NSA's purpose-built facility in the Utah desert, characterized by John Kiriakou as having storage capacity for every phone call, text message, and email of every American for the next 500 years.

zunzuneo.title: Donald Trump
zunzuneo.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.
